## Codebase Patterns
- Activity-fanout hooks on the funnel consumer: piggyback on the existing `SetOnChange` per-edit callback rather than introducing a parallel NATS subscription. The callback already runs inside the consumer's ack flow with broadcast / websocket fan-out alongside it; adding a third "watch fanout" branch keeps every cross-cutting subscriber on one ordered stream and avoids duplicate JetStream consumer durables. Keep the work light (one `WatchersFor` lookup + N notification inserts) — heavy lifting belongs on a separate worker. ChangeEvent grew `ActorID` + `OntologyAPIName` (omitempty) to carry per-batch context downstream; future hooks (audit fanout, ledger projection, etc.) inherit them for free.
- Object→watch RID convention: `oss.FormatObject` builds object RIDs as `ri.phonograph2-objects.main.object.<primaryKey>` and the SPA stamps that exact string into `watches.target_rid` via `__rid`. Any backend that needs to match a per-objectType edit against the watches table MUST use a single `ComputeTargetRID(objectType, primaryKey)` helper that mirrors `FormatObject`. `pkg/notifications.ComputeTargetRID` is the canonical helper; if `oss.FormatObject` ever changes shape, change both. `objectType` is currently a no-op argument (parking for the day RIDs become objectType-scoped) — keep it on the signature so future changes don't ripple through every caller.
- `target_rid = ANY($1)` for batched watcher fan-out: PostgreSQL array overlap is the right primitive when you have N targets and want one round-trip. Backed by the existing `watches_target_idx` (migration 000078) so cardinality scales linearly. The MemoryStore impl keeps a `wanted` set + linear scan — fine for tests, never the production path. Returns `map[targetRID][]userID` so callers iterate without nil-checking each bucket; absent keys mean "zero watchers" (no empty-slice defensive coding).
- SMTPMailer disabled-state convention: zero-value `SMTPMailer{}` (Host=="") MUST silently no-op on Send rather than dialing a phantom server. Move the gate inside the mailer so the call site stays branch-free — `fanout.WithMailer(mailer, resolver)` always wires it, and a deployment without `WEAVE_SMTP_HOST` set just hands in a mailer whose Send returns nil. Tests inject the underlying `func(addr, auth, from, to, msg) error` via a private `sendMail` field — no test smtp server, no goroutine leaks. RFC 5322 envelope is built by hand: From / To / Subject / MIME-Version: 1.0 / Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8 / blank line / body, every separator CRLF.
- env-driven optional integration: `WEAVE_<FEATURE>_<KEY>` for everything optional that ships with a sensible-disabled default. SMTP follows `WEAVE_SMTP_HOST/PORT/FROM/USER/PASS`; absent HOST = disabled, absent USER = unauthenticated relay. The build helper returns nil when the disabled-state condition fires so the caller's `if mailer := buildSMTPMailerFromEnv(); mailer != nil` reads naturally. Same shape for any future "deployment may or may not have a connector to X" wiring.
- RTL drag/drop with clientX/Y: `fireEvent.{dragStart,dragOver,drop}(target, { clientX })` does NOT propagate coordinates into the synthetic React event. Use `createEvent.<type>(target, { dataTransfer })` then `Object.defineProperty(ev, 'clientX'/'clientY', { value: N })` before `fireEvent(target, ev)`. Pair with a `getBoundingClientRect = () => ({ x,y,left,top,right,bottom,width,height,toJSON })` stub on the grid container so the handler's `e.clientX - rect.left` is deterministic. `fireDragWithCoords` in `web/src/components/dashboards/__tests__/DashboardEditorPage.test.tsx` is prior art — copy into any future spatial-DnD test (kanban, gantt resize, dashboard widget move-resize, etc.).
- New apierror status code: add a constructor in `pkg/apierror/error.go` next to the existing `NewNotFound` / `NewBadRequest` family — use uppercase-snake `ErrorCode` (e.g. `WEAVE_VALIDATION_ENUM`), pick an http.Status* constant, and the wire format / WriteJSON path picks it up automatically. No extra plumbing needed.
- Surfacing typed `*apierror.APIError` from action validation: return the APIError directly from the validator (e.g. `validateValueTypeConstraints`); Prepare wraps it with `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` so `errors.As` still finds it. Handlers MUST then check `errors.As(err, &apiErr *apierror.APIError)` BEFORE wrapping into the legacy `ActionFailed` 400 — otherwise the typed status code + structured Parameters are lost.
- `BatchError` (pkg/actions/executor.go) needs a `Cause error` field + `Unwrap()` method to propagate typed errors from Prepare through `ApplyBatchAtomic`. Without it the batch path collapses every prepare failure into a generic 400, masking 422/409/403 distinctions. Update both BatchError construction sites (publish failure + per-action prepare failure) when adding a new typed validation error.
- Typed constraint errors (`types.EnumViolationError`): when ValidateConstraints needs to surface structured detail (allowed values, rejected value), define a typed error in `pkg/types/constraints.go` with public fields, return it from the relevant branch, and keep `Error()` returning the legacy string. Callers detect via `errors.As` and ignore the string. Don't try to parse fields out of `err.Error()` — that path always loses fidelity.
- Goja sandbox recipe (reusable for derived props / formulas): call `vm.Set(name, goja.Undefined())` then `vm.GlobalObject().Delete(name)` for each denied host global; add watchdog goroutine that does `vm.Interrupt(...)` when `context.Done()` fires.
- Read-only object views in Goja: implement `goja.DynamicObject` and keep a reference to the owning `*goja.Runtime` so `Get` can return `runtime.ToValue(v)` from the same VM — returning values from a different runtime crashes Goja.
- Goja `Callable` from `goja.AssertFunction` is a Go `func(this Value, args ...Value) (Value, error)`; do NOT try to `.Get("call")` and re-invoke — just call it directly.
- `properties` table columns land via an ALTER with `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ... NOT NULL DEFAULT ...`; matching `pg_repository.go` helpers must add the column to INSERT, SELECT (ListProperties + GetProperty) and UPDATE paths, in that order.
- `Property` model (pkg/oms/models.go) is the canonical wire shape; adding an omitempty JSON-tagged field is non-breaking for every existing test.
- `pkg/oss.WireObject.MarshalJSON` flattens Properties to the row's top level alongside `__primaryKey` / `__apiName`; HTTP tests of loadObjects must decode rows as `map[string]interface{}` and read fields directly, not as `row.Properties[...]`.
- Goja exports whole-number JS arithmetic results as Go `int64` and fractional ones as `float64`. Tests on derived-property numerics should accept either (via a `toFloat64` helper) rather than assert a single concrete type.
- Executor-level "load base object fields" is a single `bleve.DocIDQuery` with `Fields=["*"]` and `Size=len(pks)`. Batch once per withProperties invocation and share across DPs — per-row Bleve queries were the original pattern and are materially slower at scale.
- New OMS resource types with their own table: DON'T extend `oms.Repository`. ~15 mock implementations across pkg/{oms,oss,links,actions,index,automate,ai}, test/{northwind,chinook,e2e,fixtures,integration} would need new stubs. Instead add a narrow interface in the same package (e.g. `ComputedPropertyStore`) and expose CRUD directly on `*PGRepository`.
- TTL-cache tests: inject a clock via `SetNowFunc(func() time.Time)` + an advance helper. Matches `oms.CachedRepository.nowFunc` convention and keeps time-based tests deterministic without calling `time.Sleep`.
- JSONB round-trip in pgx: stage through `[]byte` (`var aggJSON []byte` → `json.Unmarshal`). Passing the struct directly to `rows.Scan` will fail.
- Adding a new BaseType: update (1) `allBaseTypes` map + slice in pkg/types/basetype.go, (2) the count + slice in `TestBaseType_AllDefined`, (3) per-language maps in pkg/sdkgen/typemap.go (ts/python/go). Coerce/Validate have catch-all default branches so opaque types need no work there.
- Content-addressed blob storage: hash + write in one pass via `io.MultiWriter(tempFile, sha256.New())`, then CAS under a mutex — `os.Stat` the destination; if present drop the temp and reuse, else `os.MkdirAll` + `os.Rename`. Never hash a second time from disk.
- Path-traversal guard for FS-backed stores: clean the input (`filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(p))`), reject if it starts with `..` or is absolute, then verify `filepath.Abs(resolved)` is under `filepath.Abs(root)+sep`. Single choke point — duplicate nowhere.
- Multipart upload size cap: wrap `r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, max)` BEFORE `ParseMultipartForm`, then check `errors.As(err, &maxErr)` against `*http.MaxBytesError` to distinguish "too large" from generic parse errors. The cap applies to the WHOLE request body (parts + boundary + form fields), so set the limit slightly above the per-file budget if you need exact per-file enforcement.
- New global blob-style API endpoints (no {ontology} segment) belong inside the `r.Group(... auth.MiddlewareFull ...)` block in cmd/server/main.go but mount conditionally: `if deps.MediaStore != nil && deps.MediaCatalog != nil { ... }`. Pattern matches attachment / transactions / sqlqueries — degraded mode (no PG) silently skips registration so unit tests on NewFullRouter don't need to wire every dep.
- Catalog stores (oms.MediaAssetStore, oms.ComputedPropertyStore) MUST be served by the uncached `*PGRepository`, not the `oms.CachedRepository` decorator — the cache wraps the metadata Repository interface only. In main.go, capture `pgRepo := oms.NewPGRepository(pool)` BEFORE wrapping so you can hand the bare repo to deps.MediaCatalog / deps.ComputedPropertyStore.
- Web fetch path (`pkg api/client.ts`) is JSON-only — it hard-codes `Content-Type: application/json` and `JSON.stringify(body)`. Anything that needs multipart/binary or upload progress bypasses `request<T>()` and uses XMLHttpRequest (fetch has no standardized upload-progress event). Grab the access token from `useAuthStore.getState().accessToken` and set `Authorization: Bearer <token>` manually; reuse `ApiRequestError` from `api/client.ts` so error shapes stay uniform.
- react-dropzone in jsdom: the hidden file input is exposed via `getInputProps()`. Tests should drop files by `Object.defineProperty(input, 'files', { value: [file] })` + `fireEvent.change(input)` instead of constructing a DataTransfer (jsdom lacks it). Wrap state-changing calls in `act(async () => {...})` so React flushes the dropzone's internal state update.
- Parameterized BaseType additions (Array/Struct/Union): no migration needed. `Property.TypeConfig` is JSONB and `DataTypeJSON` merges unknown keys through, so adding a `Variants []DataType` / similar field on `pkg/types.DataType` is a wire-only change. Only 4 places need editing: (1) new constant + `allBaseTypes` entry, (2) `json:"xxx,omitempty"` DataType field, (3) Coerce+Validate branches, (4) sdkgen typemap (ts/python/go).
- Union-typed values are tagged on the wire. Two accepted shapes: `{__type: "<variant>", value: <v>}` (universal wrapper — coerce emits this form) OR `{__type: "<variant>", ...structFields}` (flattened tagged struct — read path recognizes it via "key count != 2" heuristic). Validate trusts the `__type` hint when present; untagged values are tried variant-by-variant in declared order. Put specific variants first — `fmt.Sprintf`-backed String coerce is greedy.
- Recursive UI components using self-referential data: label each level with a dot-separated path prop ('', '0', '0.1', ...) so aria-labels stay unique and tests can address any depth via `struct field name 0.1` / `data-testid="struct-fields-0.1"`. Root gets its own sentinel testid (e.g. `struct-fields-root`). Validators walk the same tree recursively — keep "this subtree is valid" one function that short-circuits on first bad leaf.
- Nullable text column in Go: `NULLIF($N, '')` on INSERT / UPDATE + `COALESCE(col, '')` on SELECT keeps the Go model a plain `string` (no `sql.NullString`) while the DB carries proper NULLs so partial indexes `WHERE col IS NOT NULL`, self-referential FKs and data-quality checks still work. Every `COALESCE(description, '')` in pg_repository.go is prior art — follow the same shape for any new nullable text.
- Optional field on Update DTO: use `*string` (or `*bool` etc) so callers can distinguish three states — omit=preserve, `""`=clear, `"X"`=assign. Bare `string` collapses "omit" and "clear" into one, silently nuking existing data whenever a client sends a partial update. `UpdateLinkTypeRequest.IsRequired *bool` is prior art.
- Self-referential FK in schema: prefer NULLable-without-REFERENCES for pair-authoring workflows where both sides are created separately (A↔B bidirectional links, parent/child before-both-exist, etc). Handler-layer validation enforces symmetry invariants; the DB accepts a temporary dangling reference during authoring. REFERENCES would require deferred constraints or a magic create-order — more surface area than it's worth when validation is already centralized.
- Adding a new route to `cmd/server` is a 3-step sync: (1) `RegisterRoutes` in `cmd/server/routes.go`, (2) matching `paths:` entry in `api/openapi.yaml`, (3) copy canonical to embedded: `cp api/openapi.yaml cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml`. The `TestContract_*` trio fails otherwise with a precise "missing entries" diagnostic — friendly, non-ambiguous.
- Direction-aware edge lookups (forward source-keyed vs reverse target-keyed) need SEPARATE store primitives — `ListLinkEdgesWithProperties(sourcePKs)` and `ListLinkEdgesWithPropertiesByTarget(targetPKs)`. Emulating reverse by filtering a forward call silently returns wrong rows. Pattern generalizes to any adjacency-list traversal where direction matters.
- Optional executor-level enrichment hooks (`SetEdgePropertiesProvider`, etc.) should be setter-injected rather than constructor args. Keeps the "no provider wired" path zero-cost, makes degraded-mode test routers trivial, and lets new hooks ship without disrupting existing NewExecutor callers.
- Adding a "richer" parallel column on top of a legacy single-value column (e.g. `primary_key_props JSONB` next to `primary_key_prop TEXT`): KEEP the legacy column and backfill it from `richer[0]` on every write. The legacy column stays the lowest-common-denominator handle for ~all downstream consumers (Bleve doc IDs, FK lookups, mock repos), the new column carries the full model. Single decodePrimaryKeyProps-style helper at every Scan site falls back to wrapping legacy in a one-element slice — keeps the read path tolerant of partially-migrated rows without scattering nil-checks.
- Composite-key URL routing (`/objects/{objectType}/{key1}:{key2}`): chi treats `:` as opaque path char. NO router changes needed; handler reads the raw segment and `oms.ParseCompositeKey(raw, expected)` is the canonical splitter, gated on `expected > 1` so single-PK ObjectTypes keep colon-bearing keys (e.g. RIDs) intact.
- Single-parent inheritance "diamond detection" reduces to chain-cycle detection. `extends_rid` is one column → only A→B→A loops are reachable; `oms.ValidateInheritanceCandidate(repo, otRID, parentRID)` walks the candidate parent's chain checking the visited set (seeded with `otRID`) and returns `oms.ErrInheritanceCycle` on the first repeat. The read-side resolver (`ResolveInheritedObjectType`) carries the same guard so stale data can't spin the merge forever.
- Inheritance import remap: when CreateOntology copies object types into a fresh ontology, ExtendsRID may point at any other type in the same import — including one that appears later in the slice. Pre-allocate new RIDs for the whole slice into otRIDMap BEFORE the create loop so parent pointers can be remapped regardless of declaration order. Same shape works for any future self-referential field on a row that imports as a batch.
- pkg/oms needs to call into pkg/actions (e.g. polymorphic invoke forwarding to the ActionExecutor): declare a NARROW interface in pkg/oms (`oms.InterfaceMethodActionDispatcher`), keep pkg/oms free of any pkg/actions import, and put the concrete adapter inside `cmd/server/`. Same trick as `pgEdgePropertiesResolver` from US-210 — keeps the dependency direction clean AND makes degraded-mode test routers trivial (no dispatcher wired ⇒ resolution still works, execution just skipped).
- When a handler under test relies on `mockRepo` methods that other tests stubbed as "return nil/createErr", promote them to real in-memory implementations (e.g. add an `interfaceAttachments []ObjectTypeInterface` slice in `handlers_test.go` so `AttachInterface` / `ListObjectTypeInterfaces` actually persist). Zero-arg stubs silently hide missing data and your new test passes by accident. The promotion is additive — existing tests that only read nil stay green.
- NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb columns: read path MUST `COALESCE(col, '{}'::jsonb)` AND write path MUST substitute '{}' for nil json.RawMessage — pgx encodes nil json.RawMessage as the string "null", which the JSONB column happily accepts but breaks the "empty ⇒ nil-on-the-wire" round-trip. Single normalise/decode helper pair (see `pkg/oms/function.go` normaliseSignatureForWrite + signatureFromBytes) keeps both sides honest.
- Idempotent CHECK constraint additions in migrations: ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT has no IF NOT EXISTS for CHECKs (unlike COLUMNS), so wrap with `DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = '...') THEN ALTER ... END IF; END$$;`. Prior art: `migrations/000040_function_signature_runtime.up.sql` for `functions_runtime_check`.
- Typed parameter-validation errors for HTTP handlers: define a struct error (`oms.FunctionParamError{Parameter, Code, Reason}`) so the handler can `errors.As` and emit a structured 400 with `parameter`+`code`+`reason` instead of a free-form message string. Convention: `Code` ∈ a small closed enum (`missing_required`, `type_mismatch`, `unknown_parameter`, `default_invalid`); SDKs key off `code` and ignore the human `reason`. Same shape used by `types.EnumViolationError` (US-052) — the validator owns both the legacy `Error()` string AND the public fields, so callers that haven't migrated to `errors.As` keep seeing a sensible message.
- "No-contract opts out of validation" semantic: when the declared signature is empty (nil / "{}"), the validator MUST pass every input through unchanged — including unknown keys. This matches the principle that a Function without a signature is "untyped" and the executor will receive whatever the caller sent. Once a signature exists, it becomes the gate. Making the empty case strict (reject unknowns even with no contract) breaks every legacy function authored before signatures landed; making it permissive when the signature IS declared loses the whole point. Test both directions.
- Cross-package sentinel errors for HTTP status dispatch: when the runtime package (e.g. `pkg/functions`) has a cyclic dep (it imports pkg/oss, which imports pkg/oms), place the sentinels in a leaf subpackage with ZERO repo imports — `pkg/functions/fnerrors.ErrTimeout` / `ErrMemoryLimit`. Both the runtime (wrapping goja interrupts) and the handler (`errors.Is` branch into 408 / 429) can import the leaf without forming a cycle. Tag `vm.Interrupt(reasonConst)` with small package-private string constants, then discriminate via `*goja.InterruptedError.Value()` in the wrapping helper. Beats string-matching error messages and survives downstream format changes.
- Rolling-window per-key limiter: a `[]time.Time` FIFO per key with lazy forward-scan eviction on each Allow is ~20 lines of Go and the right shape for "per minute" PRD language. Token-bucket from `golang.org/x/time/rate` gives you rps-style semantics which is wrong for monthly/per-minute caps. Always include zero-value passthrough (`limit<=0 || window<=0` → true) + nil-receiver safety so misconfigured / degraded-mode wiring never silently throttles. `SetNowFunc(fn func() time.Time)` for deterministic window-eviction tests — same convention as `oms.CachedRepository.nowFunc` + `pkg/oss/computed.Resolver`.
- Handler-side context deadline is the portable guarantee: wrapping `r.Context()` with `context.WithTimeout` AROUND `executor.Execute(...)` enforces the CPU ceiling regardless of which FunctionExecutor is wired (in-process Goja, HTTP, remote-runtime, mock). The runtime-internal watchdog (if any) is belt-and-braces; the handler's wrap is what you test. Post-call dispatch: `errors.Is(err, fnerrors.ErrTimeout) || errors.Is(execCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded)` → 408 — the second branch catches executors that honour ctx but don't explicitly propagate the sentinel (they return `ctx.Err()` = `context.DeadlineExceeded`, which is neither ErrTimeout nor its wrap).
- Atomic-commit-then-publish for write paths with async fanout: when the HTTP action writes to PG AND publishes to NATS (with the NATS consumer fanning out into Bleve / link edges / etc.), the tx MUST wrap the PG writes and the publish MUST come AFTER `tx.Commit`. Rollback on any intermediate failure; accept that a post-commit publish failure leaves PG state but never publishes — the consumer will simply never see a batch it doesn't know about. Do NOT try to reverse a committed tx on publish error; that's a known edge case and the correct HTTP response is a structured `BatchError{Phase:"publish"}` even though some state is persisted. Concrete pattern: `defer tx.Rollback(ctx)` then explicit `tx.Commit(ctx)` (Rollback becomes a no-op after Commit). Prior art: `pkg/actions.(*Executor).commitBatchAtomicTx` (US-238), mirrors the read-only tx shape from `sqlqueries.PGEngine.Execute`.
- Distinguishing two 429 causes (quota vs memory): same HTTP status, different `errorName` (`FunctionQuotaExceeded` vs `FunctionMemoryLimitExceeded`). SDKs key off errorName for retry/backoff decisions — quota is "retry after cool-off", memory is "fix the function". Pattern-match parallel to `FunctionParamError.Code` from US-216. Humans read the message; machines read the errorName.
- JSONB membership queries with pgx: the PostgreSQL `?` operator (does array contain value) conflicts with pgx's `?` placeholder-escape convention. Double it (`approvers ?? $1`) — pgx rewrites `??` to a literal `?` in the statement sent to PG. Same rule for `?&` / `?|` (becomes `??& $1` / `??| $1`). Prior art: `pg_repository_approvals.ListActionApprovals` approver membership filter (US-243).
- Caller-scoped list filters (mine=true, role-intersect, OR-of-identity): keep the store filter narrow (single-string membership) and apply the caller's identity OR post-store. `userCanApprove(user, approvers)` already codifies the identity rule for approve/reject — reusing it from the list handler avoids re-inventing JSONB array-overlap (`?|`) at the store layer. Bounded `Limit` parameter means the post-filter doesn't dominate cost. Pattern generalises to any "queue of items the caller has permission on" enumeration.
- Realm extraction from RIDs for tenant-keyed anything: the `ri.{service}.{realm}.{resourceType}.{uuid}` format is self-describing, so `rid.Parse(fn.RID).Realm` is the canonical quota/rate-limit/audit key for ontology resources. Falls back to `"main"` on parse failure so even legacy / malformed rows stay enforceable. Centralise in a tiny `realmFromRID(rid string) string` helper and reuse across Function exec, Action exec, Automation exec — all resource-bearing RIDs carry the realm.
- NDJSON streaming endpoints (`?stream=1` opt-in, `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson`): pre-execution gates (validation, 404, quota, no-executor) MUST stay regular JSON HTTP errors — by the time the executor fails the response headers are already on the wire and 4xx/5xx is impossible. Reserve in-band terminal `{"error": {"code","reason"}}` lines for post-dispatch failures only. Two error channels means SDKs need TWO try/except scopes: one around the generator-returning call (HTTP errors), one inside the loop (in-band errors). `Cache-Control: no-cache` + `X-Accel-Buffering: no` headers are mandatory for nginx/Cloudflare passthrough. `enc := json.NewEncoder(w)` adds the trailing newline automatically — do NOT manually append `\n`. Always pair `enc.Encode()` with a `flusher, _ := w.(http.Flusher); if flusher != nil { flusher.Flush() }` — `httptest.ResponseRecorder` doesn't implement Flusher (the handler is still correct without flushing; tests just see all lines at end-of-response).
- SDK iterator methods (`execute_stream`, etc.): make the entry point a regular `def` that fires the HTTP request and returns a generator — NOT a `def`-with-`yield` (lazy generator). Eager firing means HTTP errors raise at the call site BEFORE the user's `for` loop, which is the intuitive Python contract. Pattern: `status, headers, lines = transport.stream_lines(...)`; if status non-2xx, raise typed error eagerly; else `return _consume_ndjson(status, lines)` where the helper IS the generator. Test it: a stub that returns 400 must raise WeaveError BEFORE the test's `for` loop runs.
- Context-propagated call stack for cross-function invariants (depth + cycle): put the stack accessors and the sentinel errors in a ZERO-DEPENDENCY leaf subpackage (e.g. `pkg/functions/fncall`) so any layer above the runtime — HTTP handlers, test harnesses, SDKs binding — can push a frame with `fncall.WithFrame(ctx, ref)` without forming an import cycle. The top-level caller should seed the stack with the function's own ref BEFORE entering `runtime.Execute`; otherwise `A→B→A` detection slips by one level because A isn't on the stack during its own top-level run. `WithFrame` must allocate a fresh slice each push — append-mutate on the parent corrupts unrelated branches of the context tree when goroutines race.
- Host bindings that throw JS errors (like `weave.callFunction` cycle/depth rejections) want `panic(vm.NewGoError(fmt.Errorf("%w: ...", sentinel)))` — the `%w` wrap is what keeps `errors.Is(err, sentinel)` true upstream through goja's `*Exception` wrap + the runtime's own `wrapGojaError` "execution error: %w" re-wrap. Goja preserves the Go error inside the thrown JS exception and exposes it on the returned error chain, so two layers of `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` still unwrap cleanly. Verify with an explicit `errors.Is` test — a non-wrapping `fmt.Errorf("cycle: %v", ref)` would pass string-match tests but silently break sentinel dispatch the first time a caller adds `errors.Is` branches.
- Cache key canonicalisation for `map[string]interface{}` params: `json.Marshal` sorts top-level map keys alphabetically but inherits Go's nondeterministic iteration for nested values, so `{a:{x:1,y:2}}` can hash differently across runs. Walk the structure recursively (sort keys at every nesting level, encode arrays positionally) BEFORE hashing — `pkg/functions/cache.canonicalJSON` is prior art. nil and empty `map[string]interface{}{}` should hash to the same byte string (`sha256("{}")`) so callers don't need a special case for "no params". Same trick applies to any deterministic-hash use case: dedup keys, idempotency tokens, request-fingerprint logs.
- Pointer-typed boolean field on Update DTO (`Pure *bool`, `IsRequired *bool`): the only safe shape for ANY toggleable optional setting on an Update request. Bare `bool` collapses "omit ⇒ preserve" and "send false ⇒ disable" into one, silently disabling the feature whenever a partial update doesn't mention the field. Same shape used by `UpdateFunctionRequest.Runtime *string` (US-217) and `UpdateLinkTypeRequest.IsRequired *bool` (US-210). Adding a new toggleable setting? Pointer it.
- New optional `OMSHandler.SetXxx` hooks (FunctionExecutor / FunctionQuotaLimiter / FunctionResultCache / LinkPropertyStore / etc.): follow the trio — (1) narrow interface in `pkg/oms` (one/two methods), (2) concrete impl in a leaf subpackage with no `pkg/oms` import, (3) setter on `OMSHandler`. Production wiring in `cmd/server` passes the concrete impl which satisfies the interface implicitly; degraded-mode test routers leave the hook unset and exercise the "no Xxx wired" path. Keeps the dep direction clean (`cmd/server → pkg/functions/* + pkg/oms`, never the reverse) and the cascade-stub problem from extending `oms.Repository` doesn't apply.
- Per-rule function dispatch without a new dispatcher interface method: shallow-copy the `*oms.ActionType`, override `FunctionRID` with the rule's value, then call the existing `FunctionDispatcher.Dispatch(ctx, &atCopy, params)`. Keeps the GojaDispatcher / HTTPDispatcher / RoutingDispatcher signatures untouched (they all key off `at.FunctionRID`) and a future per-rule extension can add a real method later if needed. The original ActionType pointer is never mutated — `atCopy := *actionType` is a value copy. Same pattern usable any time you need to "redirect" an existing dispatcher without surgery.
- Rule slice → edits slice 1:1 invariant: `ExecuteRules` historically returned exactly one edit per rule, and `validateInterfaceRules` indexed `edits[i]` to read the rule's resolved ObjectType. Once a rule type can produce ZERO edits (executeFunction skipped) or MANY edits (executeFunction dispatched), the parallelism breaks. Cleanest fix is to NOT depend on it: `validateInterfaceRules` reads `resolveObjectTypeParam(params)` directly — same source `executeRule` uses for the interface-rule branch — so the validator and the edit producer can never drift. Any new validator that needs the resolved ObjectType for an interface/dynamic rule should follow this and walk params, not edits.
- Bitemporal validity-range backbone for "time-travel" history queries: each `(key, version)` row carries a half-open `[valid_from, valid_to)` interval. Snapshot reads collapse to `WHERE valid_from <= asOf AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > asOf)` — no window function at read time. Stamp `valid_from = recorded_at` at the INSERT site (DEFAULT can't reference another column in PG) and close the prior version's `valid_to` in a follow-up UPDATE filtered by `version < new.version AND valid_to IS NULL` so the close-out is idempotent / safe for re-runs. Migration uses `DO $$ ... END$$` guard + LEAD-window UPDATE to backfill existing rows; the guard makes re-applying a no-op. DELETE rows participate in the snapshot scan and are filtered out at the read layer (caller treats absence as "did not exist at asOf").
- "Composite ObjectSet types reject asOf" is the right v1 scope for time-travel: filter / union / intersect / searchAround need per-instant Bleve indexes that don't exist, so reject them with `TimeTravelUnsupportedObjectSet` 400 upfront rather than producing wrong answers. Future stories can add filter-over-snapshot semantics, but v1 scoping to base-only keeps the contract honest.
- Frozen-membership snapshot pattern (US-224 "save ObjectSet for later comparison"): execute the source ObjectSet ONCE at create time, persist `(definition, objectType, primaryKeys, truncated, createdBy, createdAt)` in one row, render `row.PrimaryKeys` through the LIVE Bleve index on read using the same WireObject envelope `loadObjects` produces. PK membership is frozen; property values are live. Per-row property snapshots are a separate concept (covered by US-223 time-travel); conflating them in v1 is premature. When the OMS-side store wants JSONB but the handler wants typed Go structs (`*Definition`), put the json marshal/unmarshal in the cmd/server adapter so the OMS never imports the handler package and the handler never imports `encoding/json` for the row.
- Adding a new ObjectSet type is a 4-step sync: (1) new case in `Definition.Type` + Validate branch in `pkg/oss/objectset/definition.go`, (2) new dispatch case + execute* method in `pkg/oss/objectset/executor.go::execute`, (3) extend `ObjectSetDefinition.type` enum + any new props in `api/openapi.yaml`, (4) `cp api/openapi.yaml cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml`. The contract trio (AllRoutesDocumented + NoOrphanedSpecPaths + EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical) only catches route changes, but the schema enum drift will appear in downstream SDK-gen / API consumers. Prior art: US-225 adding `sample`.
- Multi-hop traversal operators (searchAround path, any future graph walker): thread (currentType, currentPKs) through each step, dedupe PKs between hops (`dedupeStrings` helper — first-seen order preserved), and prefer `DirectionalLinkTargetTypeResolver` with a fallback to forward-only `LinkTargetTypeResolver`. ExpectedObjectType is an assertion (validated against resolver) not a declaration; silently passes when the resolver returns "". Empty mid-path PK sets should still walk the type chain to the end so `result.ObjectType` is stable for callers. US-226 added `Path []PathStep` inside searchAround rather than a new type — schema extension is lighter than a new dispatch case.
- HyperLogLog approximateDistinct (axiomhq/hyperloglog): always construct the sketch with `hyperloglog.NewSketch(precision, true)` (sparse=true) — sparse mode gives EXACT counts for low cardinality so small-dataset tests that asserted equality against the pre-HLL facet implementation stay green. Feed string values directly as `[]byte(v)`; non-string fields go through `fmt.Sprint` so numeric / bool distinct still works. Scan cap is shared with exactDistinct (`e.MaxDocScanSize`) and the caller propagates the `truncated` flag into APPROXIMATE accuracy. Precision bounds [4,18] must be validated at dispatch time — axiomhq's `NewSketch` panics outside that range, so rejecting pre-call gives a clean 400.
- Hierarchical aggregation extension (`subAggregations []SubAggregationSpec`): keep the field on `AggregationRequest` itself rather than `AggregationSpec` — sub-aggregations are bucket-scoped, not metric-scoped. Each named child reuses `Engine.AggregateWithQuery(idx, scope, childReq)` recursively, so depth is unbounded and validation is shared (duplicate-name + non-empty-name check at every level). Attach to leaf rows of `recursiveGroupBy` AND to the top-level `AggregationResponse` (when no outer groupBy). Intermediate groupBy levels must propagate `subRow.SubAggregations` upward in the merged-row build — otherwise nested results vanish on multi-level groupBy + subs combinations. Wire propagation is bracketed by 3 places: (1) `AggregationRequest`/`AggregationRow`/`AggregationResponse` JSON shape, (2) `objectset.AggregateObjectSetRequest` mirror struct + handler plumbing, (3) OpenAPI schema (`SubAggregationSpec` component + `subAggregations` arrays in two requests + `subAggregations` map on row/response).
- Cross-cutting post-aggregation transforms (Having, future Limit/OrderBy/Threshold): hook at the TAIL of `Engine.AggregateWithQuery` — the single recursive entry for simple, grouped, and every sub-aggregation level. Add the field to both `AggregationRequest` AND `SubAggregationSpec`, forward it in `runSubAggregations`, and the hook fires at every depth for free. Export the transform (`aggregation.ApplyHaving`) and call it from `pkg/oss/objectset/handler_aggregate_derived.go` too — the derived-field aggregation path is a parallel implementation that doesn't go through the Engine. Full wiring is 4 places: (1) two struct fields + forward in runSubAggregations, (2) validation + filter call at entry, (3) objectset handler plumbing for both Bleve and derived paths, (4) OpenAPI schema (new component + array on three requests). Missing metrics should DROP rows, not pass — silent typo hiding is worse than an empty result.
- `CGO_ENABLED=0` is a hard Dockerfile invariant — any new dependency MUST be pure-Go or the production build breaks. Verify with `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` before committing. uber/h3-go (cgo-only) was ruled out in US-230 in favour of mmcloughlin/geohash (pure Go) for this reason. If a future PRD asks specifically for H3 resolution semantics and CGO is acceptable for that deployment, the Dockerfile will need `apk add gcc musl-dev` + `CGO_ENABLED=1` — a deliberate choice, not a default.
- New GroupBy type extension (geohash, future grid-like groupers): (1) add dispatch case in `Engine.getGroupEntries`, (2) new `getXxxEntries` that walks Bleve hits once with `Size=e.MaxDocScanSize`, buckets doc IDs by key, and returns a `groupEntry{value, scopeQuery=DocIDQuery}` per bucket — same shape as `getDurationEntries`, (3) declare the groupBy-specific tuning knobs as pointer fields on `GroupBySpec` (e.g. `Precision *int`) so absent=default is distinguishable from zero, (4) extend OpenAPI enum + schema props + embedded copy. Bleve's MaxDocScanSize naturally bubbles APPROXIMATE accuracy — no custom truncation plumbing. The derived-aggregation path in `handler_aggregate_derived.go` only supports `exact` groupBy, so new types silently reject there — that's fine.
- Bleve geopoint field retrieval shape: searchReq with `Fields=["..."]` returns the geopoint as `[]float64{lon, lat}` — note the ORDER (lon first, lat second) and the concrete `[]float64` type (NOT `[]interface{}`). Decoder helpers must handle `[]float64` as a primary case; `[]interface{}` + `map[string]interface{}` are fallback shapes for non-Bleve-fed callers. See `pkg/oss/aggregation/geohash.go::decodeGeopoint` for the canonical shape-tolerant decoder — accepts lat/lng/lon/latitude/longitude key variants.
- Cube/Rollup are "meta-groupBys" that expand into N subsets then reuse `recursiveGroupBy` per subset. Hook the expansion BEFORE the recursion (branch at `AggregateWithQuery` dispatch), never inside `recursiveGroupBy` — that way null-bucket handling, ordering, truncation propagation, and sub-aggregation attachment all just work. Non-grouped dimensions on a cube/rollup row are ABSENT from `row.Group` (key absence = aggregated, matches SQL GROUPING() semantics). Export the combination generator (`aggregation.ExpandGroupByCombinations(n, cube, rollup)`) so the derived-field aggregation path in `pkg/oss/objectset` can reuse it without duplication. Cube on N dims = O(2^N) — document the fan-out, consider a hard cap if a future story sees N>8.
- `bleve.NewFuzzyQuery` vs `MatchQuery.SetFuzziness`: distinct primitives with distinct inputs. MatchQuery runs the text analyser on the value (lowercase, tokenise) then applies per-term fuzziness; FuzzyQuery treats the value as a single PRE-ANALYSED term and does one Levenshtein lookup. For single-token matches ("Kafka matches Kafca") FuzzyQuery is the right primitive — cheaper, sharper, no tokenisation surprises. For multi-word user input (containsAnyTerm "hello worlld") MatchQuery.SetFuzziness is correct. The `where.fuzzy` operator added in US-232 lowercases the input (`strings.ToLower`) before handing it to FuzzyQuery so it matches the default analyser's indexed form — skipping that step silently returns zero hits on any mixed-case query.
- Query-string overrides for request-body fields: the search `?fuzziness=N` override pattern is worth repeating. Parse the query param; if it's a valid integer within range REPLACE `body.Fuzzy` entirely (explicit 0 means "disable, set to nil"); if parse fails OR out of range return a typed 400 (`InvalidFuzziness`). If the query param is absent, still validate `body.Fuzzy.MaxEdits` for the same bounds — otherwise callers can bypass validation by sending a junk body. Single source of truth for the upper bound: `where.MaxFuzziness`.
- Bleve (v2.5.7) phrase-with-slop requires a CUSTOM `query.Query` + wrapping searcher. Bleve hardcodes slop=0 at every `NewPhraseSearcher` / `NewMultiPhraseSearcher` call site — `findPhrasePaths` accepts `remainingSlop` internally but it's always 0 from the public API. Pattern: build `ConjunctionSearcher` of per-term `TermSearcher`s (every phrase term must be present) then wrap with a searcher whose `Next()` calls `dm.Complete(scratch)` and validates the position map against a Lucene-style slop budget (`|expected - actual|` summed across adjacent terms ≤ slop, where `expected = prevPos + 1`). MUST set `options.IncludeTermVectors = true` INSIDE the Searcher builder before constructing TermSearchers — options are captured at construction, not runtime. Slop=0 + multi-term should still delegate to `bleve.NewMatchPhraseQuery` (optimised path, identical semantics); the custom searcher only engages when slop > 0. Single-term phrases collapse to a plain `TermSearcher` (no conjunction wrap). Add `q.(*ExpectedType)` assertion tests as cheap insurance against a future contributor "simplifying" away the optimised path. See `pkg/oss/where/phrase_slop_query.go` — US-233.
- Lucene-style phrase-slop syntax (`"quick fox"~2`): only treat the LAST `~<digits>` suffix as slop (`strings.LastIndex + all-digit-tail check`), so phrases legitimately containing `~` survive the round-trip (regression test: `"foo~bar"~1` parses as phrase=`foo~bar`, slop=1). First iteration that used `strings.Split("~")` broke on this. Accept an unquoted bare string as a phrase with slop=0 so callers can always use the operator symmetrically, and accept both `'...'`/`"..."` as the quote delimiter.
- Per-column type cascade for tabular schema inference (US-290 pkg/pipeline/schema): track ONE running candidate per column with single-pass narrow + widen-to-string sticky. Numeric promotion (integer→long→double) is the only loosen-without-conflict edge in the lattice; everything else conflicts to string. integer/long split on `strconv.ParseInt(s, 10, 64)` + `[-2^31, 2^31)` range. Conservative-by-default date/timestamp parsing: accept ONLY ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD + RFC3339-with-space-separator); slash-separated forms are locale-ambiguous, leave them to the UI override. JSON path needs `json.Decoder.UseNumber()` — default loses integer-vs-double at decode time. Backfill missing JSON keys with null observations on prior rows when a key first appears mid-stream so cross-row Nullable inference is honest.
- csv.NewReader sample-window detection: read N rows, attempt ONE more `Read()` and check `errors.Is(err, io.EOF)` to distinguish "actually done" from "had more rows than the budget". `FieldsPerRecord=-1` + manual padding/trimming + a WarningCount counter is the right shape for "tolerate ragged rows but flag them" — the default behaviour hard-fails on the first ragged row. bufio.Scanner default 64KiB line cap also bites NDJSON real-world rows fast; lift to 1MiB via `scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 64*1024), 1024*1024)`.
- HTTP body cap via `http.MaxBytesReader` BEFORE `json.NewDecoder.Decode` for any inline-blob endpoint (paste-a-CSV, upload-an-image-as-base64, etc.). The decoder reads incrementally so the cap fires the moment input exceeds the budget; `errors.As(err, &maxErr *http.MaxBytesError)` distinguishes too-large from generic parse errors → distinct typed errorName for the SDK. Same pattern as US-204 multipart upload; this is the single-Reader analogue.
- `bleve.NewRegexpQuery` is vellum-FSA backed — matches the FULL indexed term (no substring), accepts the `^` start anchor as a no-op (FSA is already anchored), but REJECTS `$` and other zero-width assertions at search time with "zero width assertions not allowed". Pre-validate the pattern with `regexp/syntax.Parse(p, syntax.Perl)` so malformed input (e.g. unbalanced parens) fails at convert time with a clean message instead of at search time. Pre-lowercase the pattern (`strings.ToLower`) for the same reason `fuzzy`/`startsWith`/`wildcard` do — the standard analyser indexes lowercased tokens, so `^A.*` becomes `^a.*` and matches `alice`. Tests should use anchorless or `^`-prefixed patterns; document the `$` rejection as a known bleve limitation rather than working around it. Backtracking is structurally impossible (RE2/FSA), so the "catastrophic backtracking" risk is mostly theoretical — but cap pattern length (`MaxRegexPatternLength=1024`) AND wrap the search call in `context.WithTimeout(ctx, 500ms)` so a malicious pattern that compiles cheaply but iterates a huge term dictionary still gets cancelled.
- Detecting a where-clause-tree property (regex presence, geo presence, etc.) for service-layer dispatch decisions: walk the tree with a tiny recursive helper (`HasRegexClause`) and pass it the SAME `*WhereClause`. Handle `and`/`or` (array-of-WhereClause Value) and `not` (BOTH single-object and array forms — the converter accepts both). Don't try to inline the walk at every call site — it duplicates the and/or/not parsing logic, which is exactly the kind of subtle drift that breaks when a new boolean operator is added.
- Index manager dual API (`Search` + `SearchInContext`): bleve's `Index.SearchInContext(ctx, req)` honours ctx cancellation INSIDE the term iterator, so a deadline imposed by the caller propagates through FSA traversal without needing a goroutine wrapper. Add the context-aware variant alongside the non-context version when adding the first deadline-sensitive caller (regex search), keep the bare `Search(req)` for callers that don't care — migrating every call site at once is unnecessary churn. Same shape mirrored in `pkg/index/manager.go::Search` + `SearchInContext`.
- "Query string overrides body" pattern, generalised: parse `?<name>=<value>`, validate, build the equivalent body shape, REPLACE the body field. Fuzziness (US-232) overrides `body.Fuzzy`; regex (US-234) overrides `body.Where`. The override semantics keep simple URL-only invocations working without the caller having to JSON-encode a where clause. When the param is absent, the body field is used as-is; when present, the param wins. Document the override clearly in the OpenAPI parameter description so SDK callers understand they can't combine the two — composition is via the structured body form.
- `?regex=field:pattern` shorthand splits on the FIRST colon (`strings.IndexByte`) so patterns containing colons (`^foo:bar`, namespace-prefixed values) survive the round-trip. Reject `field:` (empty pattern) and `:pattern` (empty field) at parse time with an `InvalidRegex` 400 — both are user errors that produce confusing zero-result searches if accepted silently.
- WireObject envelope key convention: `__<key>` (double underscore) is reserved for core Foundry object metadata (`__rid`, `__primaryKey`, `__apiName`). `_<key>` (single underscore) is the feature-scoped envelope namespace — `_highlights` (US-235), `_computed_at` (US-202), `_markings` (US-051 / US-052). Any new feature-scoped key added to WireObject.MarshalJSON should follow the single-underscore convention. Pair MarshalJSON emission with an UnmarshalJSON branch + a shape-coercion helper (see `decodeHighlights`) so SDKs can decode the same type we emit; `json.Unmarshal` of `map[string][]string` via `map[string]interface{}` surfaces nested `[]interface{}`, so the coercion helper is load-bearing, not cosmetic. Never emit an empty map (`len(map) > 0` gate in MarshalJSON) — downstream SDKs test for key presence to decide whether the feature ran.
- Adding a new Bleve analyzer (CJK, future stemmers, etc.): 3-line change in pkg/index — (1) side-effect import of the analyzer package (must live in non-test code so production picks it up), (2) new exported `AnalyzerXxx = "<bleve-name>"` constant in `mapping_builder.go`, (3) branch in the SHARED `fieldMappingFor` helper that sets `fm.Analyzer = AnalyzerXxx` when the hint matches. Both `BuildMapping` (oms.Property path) and `Manager.buildMapping` (index.Property path) inherit the new analyzer for free. ObjectType opts in via existing `TypeConfig.analyzer` JSON hint — no migration / OpenAPI change needed (typeConfig is `additionalProperties:true`). Pure-Go-only constraint: gojieba and other cgo-bound CJK libraries are BANNED by the CGO_ENABLED=0 Dockerfile invariant; use bleve's built-in `cjk` (bigram) or `github.com/wangbin/jiebago` (dictionary-based, pure Go) for Chinese-segmentation needs.
- Bleve facet mechanics for `/search?facets=` (US-236): `searchReq.AddFacet(name, bleve.NewFacetRequest(field, size))` then read via `result.Facets[name].Terms.Terms()` — each `*search.TermFacet` exposes `.Term` (string) and `.Count` (int). Default analyser on string text fields STEMS terms (English stemmer), so a facet bucket on a plain-text `owner` field returns `alic` / `new` instead of `alice` / `news`. Facet-first fields (category, owner, objectType, status) should be indexed with `index.Property.Analyzer = "not_analyzed"` (keyword field — case-sensitive, exact match) so bucket values match source strings. For a zero-match field still emit `[]FacetBucket{}` (non-nil) so the response JSON key set stays stable across requests — `nil` marshals to `null` and forces callers into presence checks. `index.Property.Analyzer` is the direct struct field (populated from OMS `TypeConfig.analyzer` via `AnalyzerFromTypeConfig`); tests feeding `EnsureIndex` directly should set `Analyzer:"not_analyzed"` rather than constructing a TypeConfig blob.
- "Atomic decide" for single-row state-machine endpoints (approval queues, lock acquisition, idempotent toggles): drive the transition with `UPDATE … SET status=$2 … WHERE id=$1 AND status='<source-state>'` and read `rowsAffected`. ==1 ⇒ success. ==0 ⇒ id missing OR row already left the source state — disambiguate with one fallback `SELECT status FROM ... WHERE id=$1` and return distinct typed errors (ErrNotFound vs ErrAlreadyDecided). Single round-trip on the happy path; never lets two concurrent approvers both flip a PENDING row to two different terminal states. Prior art: `pkg/permissionrequests` `pgPermissionRequestsStore.Decide` (US-339), `pkg/comments` `classifyMutationResult` (US-334).
- "Existence not disclosed to strangers" for shared-but-private read endpoints: when a row has multiple legitimate readers (requester + approver + admin) but cross-user reads are private, return 404 (NOT 403) to non-authorized readers. 403 leaks the fact that the id exists, which is real information disclosure — an attacker can iterate ids and observe 403/404 distinguishability to enumerate the table. 404 collapses both branches to one response and the legitimate readers' paths still work. `pkg/permissionrequests.Get` (US-339) + `pkg/dashboards.Get` (US-329) + `pkg/savedsearches.Get` (US-311) all use the same shape.
- "Server-force the safe filter" for non-admin list endpoints: when the same endpoint serves admin (sees everything) and regular-user (sees only own) callers, do NOT trust a `mine=` query param to scope non-admin reads. Detect the privilege state server-side, and if the caller is non-privileged AND `mine=` was not explicitly set, FORCE `requested_by = user.ID` into the store filter. Non-trusted query params can produce silent enumeration leaks if you forget. The handler-side test case to add: a viewer with someone else's `mine=false` query string still gets only their own rows. Prior art: `pkg/permissionrequests.List` (US-339).
- Loading skeleton vs spinner (US-353): any page/section that **撑出固定布局**（卡片网格、表格、列表、侧栏）应当用形状匹配的 `Skeleton*` 占位（`web/src/components/common/Skeleton.tsx`：`Skeleton`/`SkeletonText`/`SkeletonCard`/`SkeletonTable`/`SkeletonList`），而**不**是居中 `<LoadingSpinner>`。骨架在加载阶段就把 page chrome 搭起来，数据填充时只是 inner content swap，CLS ≈ 0。LoadingSpinner 留给"按钮内 spinner / modal action / 一次性 mutate"这类无固定尺寸的进度反馈。a11y 不变量：每个原语只暴露**一个**外层 `role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-busy="true" aria-label="..."`，内部所有装饰条 `aria-hidden="true"`——`getAllByRole('status').toHaveLength(1)` 是回归测试。视觉层面复用 `styles/index.css` 既有 `@keyframes shimmer` + `background-size: 200% 100%`，颜色绑定项目 amber 主色 `rgba(245,158,11,*)`。骨架形状跟具体页面绑定（`SkeletonCard` = OntologyCard 形状，`SkeletonTable` 列宽阶梯 70%/90%/40% 模拟"主键短/中字段满/时间戳短"），不要参数化成 generic shape——丢掉了"骨架揭示页面布局"的核心价值。
- Cross-action parameter passing (saga compensators, side-effect actions, revert paths): `actions.ValidateParameters` rejects UNKNOWN keys, so handing a primary action's param bag to a different action type silently trips "unknown parameter" inside Prepare. ALWAYS filter down to the callee's declared `ParameterDef.ID` set before calling Prepare. `prepareCompensator` (US-239) is prior art; any future cross-action param-passing should mirror it. Pair with `resolveActionType(ctx, ontologyRID, ridOrName)` = GetActionType first, fall back to ListActionTypes scan — production PG repo answers by RID; `mockOmsRepo.GetActionType` stubs return (nil,nil) so the fallback is what makes tests work without maintaining a second lookup path.
- Polling-REST connector design (pkg/pipeline/connector/rest, US-294): keep transport behind a tiny `HTTPDoer { Do(req) }` interface — production wires `*http.Client` with `cfg.effectiveTimeout()`, tests wire `httptest.Server.Client()`, and the connector itself stays net/http stdlib only. `(rows, nextCursor, hasMore, err)` shape matches JDBC (US-292) + S3 (US-293). Cursor wire format is strategy-specific (decimal page/offset for `PaginationPage`/`PaginationOffset`, opaque API token verbatim for `PaginationCursor`, rejected for `PaginationNone`) — DON'T base64-wrap when the state is single-field; that's S3's pattern because S3 carries multi-field `{queue, listToken}`. Numeric API cursors (`"next": 42` integer) round-trip as decimal text via `float64 == float64(int64(v))` check so the request's `?cursor=42` param matches what the API emitted. Records-array path uses strict `walkPath` (missing key = error); cursor-token path uses tolerant `walkPathOptional` (missing key OR null OR empty string all collapse to `""` = end-of-stream). PageSize forwarding for cursor pagination: only when explicitly set (>0), so APIs that don't accept a size param aren't poked with one. `MaxPages` safety cap on full-page-always sources prevents runaway loops; `Pagination.MaxPages=0` defaults to `DefaultMaxPages=100000`. Per-request 4KiB body preview via `io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 4096)` for typed `*HTTPError{Status, Body}` so 4xx/5xx diagnostics survive without unbounded buffering.
- Detached-goroutine async handler pattern (US-240 async apply, future long-running jobs): the HTTP handler MUST NOT hand the request context to the detached worker — `r.Context()` is cancelled the instant the response flushes, so `executor.Apply(r.Context(), ...)` would abort immediately. Use `context.Background()` as the base, then port over only the bits the worker still needs — auth identity via `copyAuthContext` (a tiny `auth.WithUser(bg, auth.UserFromContext(src))` helper) so downstream ActionLog / rate-limit / quota keys keep working. Same shape applies to any "return 202 then process" endpoint; the cancellation-decoupling step is easy to forget and produces the "job instantly FAILED with 'context canceled'" bug. Handler returns 202 Accepted + {jobId} before the goroutine starts; the store row is created synchronously inside the request so pollers never hit a 404 race.
- New persistent-job-style store (US-240 action_jobs, future async/export/bulk-import): the PG CRUD adapter belongs in `cmd/server/` (not `pkg/oms/`), because `pkg/actions` already imports `pkg/oms` — putting action-scoped types in `pkg/oms` would form a cycle. Same shape as `pgEdgePropertiesResolver` / `interface_method_dispatcher`. The narrow interface stays in the owning package (`pkg/actions/async_job.go::ActionJobStore`), the in-memory test double stays in the test file, and the PG impl is a thin `*pgxpool.Pool` wrapper in `cmd/server/action_job_store.go` wired via `deps.ActionExecutor.SetActionJobStore(...)`. Degraded mode (no PG) silently skips the wire, and the handler checks `executor.ActionJobStore() != nil` before routing to the async path — falling back to sync when no store is available keeps the endpoint contract stable for test harnesses.
- Dynamic partial-UPDATE SQL (US-240 UpdateActionJob, any future PATCH-shaped endpoint): build a `[]string` of `col = $N` fragments plus a `[]interface{}` of args, appending only for fields the caller set (`upd.Status != ""`, `upd.Progress != nil`, etc.) — then `strings.Join(sets, ", ")`. Always append `"updated_at = NOW()"` unconditionally so every row gets its clock bumped. The three-state update shape (`*int` for Progress, `*string` for ErrorMessage, empty-string-means-skip for Status) mirrors the pointer-field convention from `UpdateLinkTypeRequest.IsRequired *bool` (US-210) — callers distinguish omit / zero-value / explicit value without an extra `fieldsSet` enum. The id argument goes last so `$N = len(args)` addresses it regardless of which columns were touched.
- JS shim state that changes per-invocation rides on ctx, not on the Runtime. `FunctionCaller` is stateless-per-process so it lives on the runtime (`SetFunctionCaller`); `ProgressReporter` (US-241) is scoped to one action-job and rides on ctx via `functions.WithProgressReporter` + `ProgressReporterFromContext`. Setting per-request state on the shared Runtime would either force per-request runtime construction (Goja init is the hot path) or race across concurrent dispatches. Register the Goja method unconditionally; inside the callback read from ctx; no-op when the ctx value is absent.
- Multi-feature JS global pattern: when one global (e.g. `weave`) carries multiple independent methods whose dependencies differ, DON'T early-return the whole global on the first missing dep. Build the global unconditionally, then attach each method based on its own precondition. Prior art: `registerWeaveShim` always creates `weave` + adds `reportProgress` (ctx-driven) but only adds `callFunction` when `r.functionCaller != nil`. The old "one guard for everything" pattern silently disabled every feature the moment one dep was missing. Tests that asserted `typeof weave === "undefined"` must migrate to `typeof weave.<method> === "undefined"`.
- Ephemeral NATS vs JetStream: telemetry / progress events that can be reconciled via a polling endpoint (GET /actions/jobs/{id}) belong on plain `nats.Conn.Publish(subject, data)` — no replay cost, no OBJECT_EDITS pollution. JetStream is for events the consumer MUST not miss (edit batches, audit). Rule of thumb: "is there a canonical read path that fills in missed events?" → plain NATS; else JetStream. US-241 `actions.progress.<jobId>` subject is the reference pattern.
- ObjectSet membership in the WebSocket hot path: walk the `*objectset.Definition` tree with a pure-data recursive matcher (per-event `objectType + primaryKey + properties`). Cheaper than `executor.Execute` per change event and keeps the hub free of index/link resolver/executor dependencies. Two-step contract: a `supportedDefinitionType(def)` validator runs at SUBSCRIBE time to reject executor-only operators (`searchAround`, `nearestNeighbors`, `sample`, `interfaceBase`, `interfaceLinkSearchAround`, `methodInput`, `reference`, `asBaseObjectTypes`) with a precise error; the matcher fails CLOSED on those types so a future regression never silently admits events. Validator MUST recurse — a `union` whose grandchild is `searchAround` is rejected at the parent, not just the top-level type. Pattern in `pkg/subscriptions/objectset.go` for US-304.
- Incremental aggregation in the WebSocket hot path: keep a per-primaryKey snapshot of the LAST-seen properties on the subscription so each change event can REVERT the prior contribution before applying the new one. Min/Max use a count-by-value multiset (`map[float64]int64`) so removing a row that produced the current extremum doesn't silently wedge — recompute from the remaining keys on next read. Initial state seeds once via a Bleve full scan with `Fields=["*"]` then incrementalises forever after. Hub.readPump's "one response per request" contract is widened by treating `resp.Type == ""` as a "handler-pushed-its-own-sequence" sentinel so handlers that need subscribed → initial-snapshot ordering can c.send themselves. Pattern in `pkg/subscriptions/aggregation.go` for US-305.
- "Impact" / "what did X affect?" endpoints (US-301 action impact, future pipeline-run impact, dataset impact) reduce to a one-hop downstream lineage query keyed by an upstream RID — DON'T introduce a parallel impact_edges table. Reuse `LineageStore.ListDownstreamLineage(rid, limit)` written by US-299 and add a thin handler that validates the RID prefix, optionally enriches with the underlying row (e.g. ActionLog parsed from suffix), and flattens edges into `{rid, objectType, primaryKey, operation, timestamp}`. Truncation flag fires at impactPageLimit=200, matching `pkg/lineage` page semantics so callers can rely on identical truncation contracts across both surfaces. Top-level path (`/api/v2/actions/{rid}/impact`, NOT nested under `{ontology}`) when the RID is self-describing.
- Control-flow ActionRule types (`if` / `foreach` / `switch` — US-244): extend the existing flat `Rule` struct rather than introducing a new discriminated union. JSON unmarshal of a struct with lots of `omitempty` pointer/slice fields is free for rules that don't use the new fields (unused fields stay zero), and `ParseRules` needs no changes. ExecuteRules becomes a tiny dispatch: if `isControlFlowRule(rule.Type)`, recurse through `executeControlFlowRule` with `depth+1`; else call the existing single-edit `executeRule`. Keeps the file linear and avoids a parallel `ControlFlowRule` type that'd force every caller to switch on two disjoint shapes.
- `MaxRuleNestingDepth` is bumped ONCE per control-flow wrapper, NOT per simple rule. A `createObject` body inside a `foreach` inside an `if` counts as depth=2. Simple rules contribute 0 so an ActionType with 100 sibling `createObject` rules under one `foreach` is depth=1 — the cap protects against pathological recursion, not list length. Enforce at entry to each control-flow rule via `if depth >= MaxRuleNestingDepth { return err }`, increment before recursing into the body — comparing against `>=` means the depth-at-max test (exactly 5 wrappers) passes and the 6th-level test rejects.
- CDC receiver shape (US-291 pkg/pipeline/cdc): pull-style narrow `Source` interface (`Next(ctx) ([]byte, error)` + `CommitWatermark(ctx, LSN)` + `Close`) so the Receiver loop owns back-pressure — no goroutine sits between Source and consumer holding events. Stateful Decoder on top of `pglogrepl.Parse` caches Relation messages by RelationID, stamps txn LSN/CommitTime onto every emitted ChangeEvent, signals commit boundary on CommitMessage so caller flushes per-transaction. Commit-then-publish ORDER REVERSES for CDC: publish ALL pending batches first, THEN `source.CommitWatermark` (commit-before-publish loses batches on receiver crash because PG GCs the WAL beyond confirmed_flush_lsn). Per-ontology batch grouping during a transaction (`pending map[ontology]*EditBatch`) so multi-ontology commits split into one EditBatch per ontology on flush — funnel.EditBatch carries one OntologyAPIName for the whole batch. CDC edits stamp `Source: EditSourceIngest` + `UserID: "cdc"` so the funnel consumer's user-edit-wins conflict resolver (US-021) refuses to overwrite a concurrent user write made after the CDC event.
- pgoutput TupleData column types are a 4-way enum (`n` NULL / `u` unchanged-TOAST / `t` text / `b` binary). NULL needs an in-process sentinel (otherwise empty-string vs absent-key vs explicit-NULL collapse ambiguously); unchanged-TOAST must be ABSENT from the column map (the funnel consumer treats absent keys as "no change", which is the correct semantic). REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT means UPDATE/DELETE old tuples carry only key columns — the OldTupleType byte ('K' key vs 'O' full) tells you which; decoder must skip non-key columns when keysOnly=true so Before honestly reports "we have the key, we don't have the old non-key values" rather than emitting fake NULLs. Centralise in one `tupleToMap` choke point.
- `pglogrepl` typed messages have unexported `baseMessage` fields — `&pglogrepl.RelationMessage{}` literals don't dispatch through a type switch unless you also call `m.SetType(pglogrepl.MessageTypeRelation)` to populate the embedded type byte. Without it the dispatch falls into `default:` and silently drops the message. Same SetType call needed for every typed message used in tests.
- "Over-fetch by 1" cursor pagination is the simplest single-key pagination shape: query `LIMIT pageSize+1` rows ordered by the cursor column DESC; if you got `pageSize+1` rows, the LAST returned row's cursor key is the next-page token and you trim it off the response. No separate count query, no "is there more?" predicate. Token shape: `base64.RawURLEncoding(strconv.FormatInt(version, 10))` so future migrations can swap the underlying cursor (composite key, opaque row id, etc.) without breaking SDKs. Decode rejects non-base64 / non-numeric / `<=0` with a typed 400. Empty page returns `data: []` (non-nil array) — `var result []T` + `httputil.WriteJSON` would marshal as `null` and break SDKs that do `data.flatMap` / `data.length`. Pattern in `pkg/oss/handlers_activity.go` for US-312; reusable for any "key DESC + before-cursor" surface (audit feed, notification list, action-log tail).
- "Reset internal state when a prop changes" in React: do NOT use `useEffect` + `setState` — the `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint rule will block it for good reason (cascading renders). Two correct alternatives: (1) wrap the resettable content in a child component and pass `key={parentKey}` so React unmounts/remounts when the key changes — costs zero state-management code, (2) compare during render and call setState directly: `if (currentKey !== prevKey) { setPrevKey(currentKey); setReset(true); }` — React allows render-phase setState as long as it's idempotent. Often the right answer is to just NOT reset — if the user-selected tab / view should persist across siblings, leave the state alone and let the React Query queryKey tuple do the segmentation. US-312 ObjectDetail dropped its tab-reset effect for exactly that reason: per-row Activity browsing is a more useful flow than forcing every row click back to Properties.
- `pgconn.ReceiveMessage` on a replication stream returns `*pgproto3.CopyData` (NOT `*pgconn.CopyDataResponse` — that type doesn't exist). Branch on the first byte: `pglogrepl.PrimaryKeepaliveMessageByteID` ('k') reply in-line if requested, `pglogrepl.XLogDataByteID` ('w') unwrap to XLogData and surface its WALData payload upward.
- Replication DSN ergonomics: REQUIRE the operator to include `replication=database` in the connection string explicitly — silently appending the flag would trip anyone who copies a CDC DSN into a non-CDC tool. The pgconn.Connect error when the flag is missing is informative enough that operators self-diagnose. Same principle for any future "this DSN MUST opt into special mode" connector.
- Param-scoped variables for loop bodies: shallow-clone the parent params map (`cloneParams`) and set `<itemVariable>` / `<indexVariable>` on the child copy. Child-rule mutations never leak back into parent scope and every iteration starts from a clean projection of the parent. Same trick generalises to any future scope-introducing rule (e.g. `let`, `try/catch`). Never mutate the incoming `params` map in place — tests that share a `params` map across iterations would observe cross-talk.
- Condition eval reuses the existing `toFloat64` / `jsonEqual` helpers from `criteria.go` to keep the numeric-comparison semantics identical to SubmissionCriteria. A separate `valuesEqual` wraps: numeric-aware short-circuit first (so `float64(1)` compares equal to `int(1)` and `json.Number("1")`), then string/bool exact match, then JSON-marshal fallback for composite types. Duplicating the helper would let the two predicate surfaces drift — both are called on the same parameter map.
- `foreach` requires `[]interface{}` specifically (JSON-decoded array shape). Typed slices like `[]string` coming from a non-JSON caller would silently fail the assertion, so clean-error on mismatch rather than reflecting. Production parameters arrive via `json.Unmarshal` into `map[string]interface{}`, so the `[]interface{}` assertion matches the 99% case.
- DAG executor coordinator pattern (US-288, applies to any future graph runner: `pkg/pipeline.RunDAG`, future US-289 scheduler, async batch jobs): one `runState` struct owns nodeByName / dependents / remaining-indegree / results / sem / wg / runCtx / inflight / firstErr / aborted, then split the public entry into ~10 small methods (prepareDAG / normalizeOptions / newRunState / scheduleReady / dispatch / runWorker / executeWithRetries / coordinate / handleEvent / handleFailure / dispatchNewlyReady / finalizeStatuses / buildResult). Keeps each function under cyclo=15 (golangci-lint floor) without sacrificing readability. The buffered-channel semaphore (`make(chan struct{}, N)`) is the natural Parallelism limiter — `defer func(){<-sem}()` makes release exception-safe and avoids the `golang.org/x/sync/semaphore` dep.
- DAG runner failure-policy three-way: abort cancels runCtx (workers see ctx.Done()), continue marks transitive descendants Skipped via BFS over `dependents` so other branches finish, retry retries-then-aborts (Attempts == 1+MaxRetries when exhausted, then fall through to abort behavior — NOT a third independent policy that loops forever). Per-node NodeStatus enum (pending → running → {success | failed | skipped | canceled}); the `running` state is what lets `finalizeStatuses` distinguish "kicked off, ctx aborted before completion" (canceled) from "never reached" (skipped). The continue-policy BFS must check `Status == Pending` before overwriting so a sibling path that succeeded earlier isn't downgraded.
- Worker-coordinator deadlock under Parallelism=1: with 2+ root nodes dispatched simultaneously and a buffered-channel semaphore, only ONE root grabs the semaphore — the others block. Tests that funnel cancellation through ONE specific node (`if node.Name == "in1" { cancel() }`) deadlock 50% of the time when the OTHER root acquires sem first and waits forever on `<-ctx.Done()`. Two safe patterns: (1) trigger cancellation from EVERY worker (`cancel()` at the top of fn, fires on whichever root runs), (2) external trigger via a `started` chan + a goroutine that calls cancel after the first worker reports running. The production runner is correct — this is a test-author trap.
- apierror response shape on the wire is FLAT — `errorName` / `errorCode` / `errorInstanceId` / `parameters` are top-level JSON keys, NOT nested under an `error` envelope. Handler unit tests that assert on the error payload should read `body["errorName"]` directly. Wrong shape (`body["error"].(map)["errorName"]`) silently passes the structural Unmarshal but the .(map) assertion produces a nil map and the assertion fails late with a confusing "errorName=<nil>". Prior art: pkg/featureflags / pkg/tenants / pkg/aip handler tests.
- Pluggable LLM-backend pattern (US-279 AIP Threads): a 2-method `Provider` interface (`Name() string`, `Complete(ctx, req) (resp, err)`) plus a thread-safe `Registry` keyed by name covers Mock + OpenAI + Anthropic + any future backend in one shape. The handler dispatches via `Registry.Get(thread.Provider)`; ErrProviderNotConfigured is the standard sentinel for "name not registered" so tests can exercise the AIPProviderNotConfigured 500 path without standing up real backends. Providers that need shape-shifting between roles (Anthropic hoists `system` out of the messages array; OpenAI keeps it inline) reshape INSIDE `Complete` so the wire `ChatRequest` stays uniform — pushing the split up to the handler would break the Mock provider and force every caller to know provider quirks. Adding a fourth provider is one new file + one branch in `BuildRegistry`.
- Cross-package admin CRUD without OpenAPI: `cmd/server/contract_test.go::newContractTestRouter` wires only the deps it needs to exercise documented routes, so any handler gated on `if deps.XStore != nil { ... }` in `cmd/server/main.go` stays invisible to the contract trio when the corresponding deps field is left unset. featureflags (`/api/admin/feature-flags`), tenant_quotas (`/api/admin/tenant-quotas`), and aip-threads (`/api/v2/aip/threads`) all use this pattern — none of them appear in `api/openapi.yaml` and the contract test still passes. The trade-off is that SDK consumers can't auto-generate clients for these endpoints; weigh that against the per-deployment optionality.
- Stable-ID session row decoupled from rotating refresh_token_id: give the session its own UUID PK and carry `refresh_token_id` as a mutable column pointing at the CURRENT chain member. RefreshHandler.Lookup(plain)+Rotate → Sessions.RotateRefreshToken(oldRecID, newRecID, now) keeps the binding live across rotations so DELETE /sessions/{id} always revokes the chain's leading token with one `RefreshStore.Revoke(id, "session_revoked")` call. ON DELETE SET NULL on the FK lets us keep the session row visible in the list after rotation cleanup even if the referenced refresh_tokens row gets removed. `RotateRefreshToken(oldID, newID, when)` with no-op on missing rows means the wire-once-in-main.go flag can be flipped without breaking pre-existing logins that never got a session row.
- Two-step PG delete for 404-vs-403 discrimination: `SELECT user_id FROM t WHERE id=$1` then compare + `DELETE` — avoids UPDATE-RETURNING gymnastics, keeps the sentinel errors clean (ErrSessionNotFound for unknown id, ErrSessionForbidden for non-owner). Works equally well in MemorySessionStore and PGSessionStore. Prior art generalises to any resource where 404 and 403 need to be distinguishable at the HTTP layer (api keys, user-role grants, etc.).
- Soft-delete with tombstones-in-List for threaded discussion (US-334 comments, future watches/reactions): the row STAYS in place after deletion (`deleted_at` set) so reply chains keep their parent reference; List MUST surface tombstones so the SPA can render `[deleted]` placeholders rather than visually orphaning the replies. Body redaction belongs in the SELECT projection (`CASE WHEN deleted_at IS NULL THEN body ELSE '' END`) NOT in a `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` filter — filtering hides the row entirely and breaks reply rendering. Pair with `classifyMutationResult(pool, ctx, id, author, rowsAffected)` post-UPDATE: 0 rows affected ⇒ SELECT one row to disambiguate ErrNotFound (missing or already soft-deleted) vs ErrForbidden (live but author mismatch). Same shape used by `pgCommentsStore.Update / Delete`; reusable for any "owned resource with soft-delete + author-only mutation" surface. Memory store mirrors the SELECT projection via a `publicView(c)` helper that redacts Body when DeletedAt != nil.
- Wire-time optional feature inside auth middleware group: feature handlers that need `UserFromContext` (session list, /me, future per-user admin) register INSIDE the `r.Group(func(api chi.Router)` block in main.go and are gated on their store being non-nil. Degraded-mode routers (no PG) get no route registration, and contract tests wire nothing so the new routes don't appear — same pattern as MFA (US-253) and service accounts (US-249). The session delete's refresh-revoke short-circuit (`h.deps.RefreshService != nil && row.RefreshTokenID != ""`) keeps behaviour coherent when the two stores are wired independently.
- Wire-level `Sessions` on every token-minting handler, not just login: LoginHandler + MFAHandler.Verify BOTH create rows; RefreshHandler BOTH rebinds (`RotateRefreshToken`). Any future token-issuing surface (OIDC callback, SAML ACS) needs the same three-line insert so the device appears in /sessions. Missing any mint path means users see stale inventory. Refresh handler uses `RefreshService.Lookup(plain)` BEFORE `Rotate` to capture oldRec — Rotate consumes the plain token internally so a second Lookup afterwards would miss.
- Background scheduler with cron-style cadence (US-252 LDAP sync, future periodic jobs): wrap a `time.Ticker` in a Start(ctx)/Stop() lifecycle, run an IMMEDIATE first cycle in the goroutine BEFORE `range t.C` so the bootstrap completes at boot rather than after the first interval, dispatch on `select { ctx.Done | s.stopCh | t.C }`. `Stop()` closes `stopCh` then waits on `doneCh` (set on `defer close(doneCh)` in the goroutine) — idempotent + waits for the in-flight cycle to drain. Don't reach for `robfig/cron` unless the PRD specifically requires cron expressions; a `time.Duration` interval covers "configurable interval" cleanly and is much easier to test deterministically.
- Audit-row-written-even-on-failure pattern: when a long-running op writes a durable audit row at the end (sync run, batch import, etc.), wrap the success/failure path in a single `finish(err)` closure that stamps `FinishedAt` + `ErrorMessage` and calls the persistence method BEFORE returning. Otherwise an early `return err` skips the audit insert and operators see "the job stopped silently". Same shape as the commit-then-publish pattern from US-238, applied to local persistence rather than NATS.
- Soft-disable for sync'd identities (US-252 ldap orphan disable): scope the disable predicate to `WHERE ldap_dn IS NOT NULL` so locally-provisioned password users (admins, breakglass accounts) are NEVER touched by a directory pull. Stable correlation key is the directory DN, NOT the email — emails change in AD when users marry / re-org; DNs don't. The `ldap_dn` column is the bookkeeping handle; the `id` column stays the canonical Weave user id (`user:<email>`) so role/permission grants are unaffected when a directory user appears. Re-enable on directory-return is one UPDATE branch in UpsertSyncedUser: `SET disabled_at = NULL, last_synced_at = $now` — don't model it as a separate action, every successful sync of a user implicitly says "active right now".
- Adding a new rule-type category ({if, foreach, switch} as a set): (1) extend `Rule` with the new fields (all omitempty), (2) add `isControlFlowRule` predicate, (3) add recursive dispatch + depth guard in `executeRulesWithDepth`, (4) tests cover happy paths per type + depth-at-max + depth-exceeded + JSON round-trip. The single-edit `executeRule` stays untouched — its contract is still "one rule → one funnel.Edit" and control-flow rules that expand to 0..N edits live in a parallel function that returns `[]funnel.Edit`. Prior art: US-244 extension on top of US-222's executeFunction skip.
- Integrating a JSON Schema library (US-245 santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v5): PIN `jsonschema.NewCompiler().Draft = jsonschema.Draft7` explicitly — the default is the latest draft which changes `exclusiveMinimum` / `dependencies` / `$ref` semantics and silently shifts customer-authored schema behaviour. Compile output is cacheable keyed by the raw schema bytes (one row = one immutable schema per ActionType). `*jsonschema.ValidationError` is a nested tree — walk to leaves (`len(Causes) == 0`) to extract per-field detail; the root envelope carries the generic "doesn't validate" wrapper. `InstanceLocation` is a JSON Pointer; convert to dot-delimited field paths (`/items/0/price` → `items.0.price`) at the API boundary. Pair every typed validator with a `TestHandler_Apply_*_EmitsWire<status>` test that decodes the wire JSON to verify the error-chain-unwrap path actually fires — unit tests on the typed error struct alone don't verify the handler reaches `typedAPIError(err)`. Pure Go (no CGO) → safe under the `CGO_ENABLED=0` Dockerfile invariant from US-230.
- OAuth refresh-token rotation: revoke BEFORE issuing the new pair so a concurrent replay sees the old token already consumed; if the new mint fails the user is one-token-down (recoverable UX) rather than two-tokens-up (security incident). Public-vs-confidential client gate keys off `len(app.ClientSecretHash) > 0` on the registered Application row — gating on "did the request supply a secret?" lets a confidential client downgrade itself by simply omitting the secret. Scope narrowing on refresh MUST reject any requested scope outside the original grant (returns `ErrScopeNotGranted` → RFC 6749 §5.2 `invalid_scope`); the `client_credentials` path's `intersectStringSlice` silently drops unknowns, which is the wrong semantics for refresh — keep the two narrowing helpers separate.
