Canonical scope catalogue (`pkg/developer/oauth_scopes.go::ScopeRead/Write/Admin` + `KnownScopes()` + `IsKnownScope`) is additive, not enforcement: existing custom scopes stay valid, and `IsKnownScope` is opt-in for future strict-validator wiring at the application-create surface.
- External identity-provider integration (OIDC in US-246, SAML next): (1) split the handler into narrow `Exchanger` / `Verifier` interfaces so the real library types (`*oauth2.Config`, `*oidc.IDTokenVerifier`) satisfy them implicitly and tests can stub either half; (2) use `oidctest.Server` (discovery + JWKS only, no token endpoint) + a stub Exchanger — trying to stand up a real token endpoint is 3x the test scaffolding for 0x more coverage; (3) key upsert on email, NOT `sub` — email is stable across IdP migrations, sub is provider-scoped; (4) NEVER touch PasswordHash on IdP callback, hybrid password+SSO orgs need both auth paths on the same user; (5) discovery (`oidc.NewProvider`) is an HTTP GET at boot — wrap in log-warn-and-continue so a misconfigured IdP doesn't take down the whole server; (6) state cookie MUST be HttpOnly+SameSite=Lax, Strict breaks the inbound-redirect flow; (7) boot-time wiring lives in `cmd/server/main.go` alongside the other `ServerDeps` deps, gated on both `Enabled` flag AND successful discovery.
- Triple-pointer field (`ExpiresAt **time.Time`) on partial-update DTOs: needed when the column is nullable AND callers need three distinct states (omit = preserve, `null` = clear to NULL, value = overwrite). Single-pointer (`*bool` / `*string`) covers the two-state case, but a nullable time (or any nullable pointer-typed column) needs the extra indirection because the wire form is already `*time.Time`. Document the three states in a struct-tag comment so future readers don't silently collapse two of them. Prior art: `ServiceAccountUpdate.ExpiresAt **time.Time` (US-249).
- Soft-delete + recreate-under-same-name pattern: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_xxx_name_active ON xxx (name) WHERE disabled_at IS NULL` scopes the uniqueness invariant to active rows. Tombstones survive in place as an audit trail; a new row with the same name INSERTs without collision the moment the prior row is soft-deleted. Translate SQLSTATE 23505 into a domain error (`ErrXxxNameConflict`) so the HTTP handler emits a clean 409 without string-matching pgx's wrapped error. Prior art: `idx_api_keys_prefix` (US-010), `idx_service_accounts_name_active` (US-249).
- `Foo` / `fooFor(w, r, id)` split in admin CRUD handlers: the outer `Delete` / `Update` / `Get` is a thin `chi.URLParam` extractor; the `*For` helper carries ALL the logic AND the `UserFromContext == nil ⇒ 401` auth gate. Tests call the `*For` variant directly to bypass chi's URL routing without losing the auth check. Putting the auth gate in the wrapper instead of the helper silently skips it for test-only callers — a bug to avoid when wiring a new admin handler. Prior art: `api_key_handlers.go::DeleteFor`, `service_account_handlers.go::deleteFor` (US-249).
- SAML 2.0 SP integration (US-248): (1) DON'T call `*saml2.SAMLServiceProvider.Metadata()` for the SP descriptor — it insists on an SP encryption certificate (returns `ErrSaml{Message: "empty SP encryption certificate"}`) which a "validate-only, no AuthnRequest signing" SP doesn't need. Build the `types.EntityDescriptor` literal directly (`SPSSODescriptor` + `AssertionConsumerServices`) and `xml.MarshalIndent` it — gosaml2's exported types carry the right struct tags. (2) ACS handler MUST accept the IdP-initiated SSO case where neither the form's RelayState NOR the relay-state cookie is present — only fail the relay check when one side is set without the other. The signature/audience/expiry checks inside `RetrieveAssertionInfo` are what gate access in that flow. (3) IdP cert PEM accepts multiple concatenated CERTIFICATE blocks (key rotation overlap) — `pem.Decode` in a loop, parse each via `x509.ParseCertificate`, hand the slice to `dsig.MemoryX509CertificateStore{Roots: ...}`. (4) Email/displayName extraction walks a configurable candidate list with sensible defaults: `email` → `mail` → `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress` for email; `displayName` → `name` → xmlsoap claim URI for name. The first non-empty wins; falls back to NameID for email. Operators override per-attribute (Azure AD, ADFS, Okta all ship attributes under different names). (5) Same handler-deps shape as OIDCHandler — Users/Resolver/Signer/RefreshService/MarkingRepo — and the same upsert-on-email + preserve-PasswordHash invariant so password+SSO orgs work identically. (6) Three routes mounted inside the JWTSigner-gated block: `GET /api/auth/saml/metadata` (SP descriptor XML), `GET /api/auth/saml/login` (mint relay-state cookie + redirect to IdP SSO URL), `POST /api/auth/saml/acs` (verify + mint Weave session). Boot-time degraded-mode wiring matches OIDC: misconfig logs a warning, handler stays nil, routes skip registration.
- Compare-and-swap rotation on a same-table self-FK (US-250 `Rotate`): wrap `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` + INSERT successor + UPDATE predecessor in one `tx.Begin` / `tx.Commit` pair so two concurrent callers can't both see `successor_id = NULL` at SELECT time and race each other's UPDATE. Without the row-level lock the later UPDATE silently wins and orphans the first successor. Pair with a typed sentinel (`ErrAPIKeyAlreadyRotated`) so the handler can 409 rather than string-matching. Use `REFERENCES ... ON DELETE SET NULL` for the self-FK — CASCADE would nuke the predecessor tombstone when the successor is revoked, destroying the audit trail. Same shape generalises to any "A supersedes B" state machine on a single table (workflow versions, config revisions, policy rotations).
- "Grace period overlap" for credential rotation (US-250): model both credentials as FULL rows in the canonical table; the predecessor carries a nullable `rotates_at` that doubles as the grace-period cut-off. During `[now, rotates_at)` BOTH rows authenticate; past `rotates_at` the middleware rejects the predecessor via `IsRotationExpired(now)`. Use INCLUSIVE comparison (`!now.Before(rotatesAt)`) — exclusive leaves a one-nanosecond window where the key is neither in-grace nor rotation-expired. Dispatch errors separately: `APIKeyExpired` (absolute expiry past) vs `APIKeyRotated` (grace elapsed) so SDKs give actionable messages ("rotate your integration" vs "your integration is broken"). Applies to any long-lived credential needing overlap rollover (OAuth client secrets, signing keys, session tokens).
- DB-backed role registry alongside a static permission matrix (US-251): the `roles` table seeds the five built-ins with `builtin=true` so identity rows exist, but `role_permissions` for built-ins is INTENTIONALLY left empty — the static matrix in `pkg/auth/permissions.go` (`RolePermissions()`) remains the authoritative source for what the resolver grants. Pattern: handler `Get`/`List` responses MUST fall back to `RolePermissions(role.Name)` when `role.Builtin && len(dbPerms) == 0` so the wire response matches what the resolver actually honours; `permissionsForRole(r, repo, role)` helper centralises this so every list/get path sees the same view. Never try to pre-seed `role_permissions` rows for built-ins — that duplicates the matrix and adds a drift hazard. Built-in role protection at the handler (DELETE + PUT permissions both 409 `BuiltinRoleProtected`) keeps the matrix as the only source of truth for the five seeded roles; custom roles live entirely in `role_permissions`.
- Narrow UserRoleRevoker interface instead of widening `UserRepository` (US-251): adding `RevokeUserRole` to the full `UserRepository` interface would cascade into every in-memory stub across the codebase (role_resolver_test.go, refresh_handler_test.go, oidc_handler_test.go, saml_handler_test.go, ...). Declare a single-method interface inside `user_role_handlers.go`, make `*PGUserRepository` implement it directly, and accept a type assertion (`revoker, _ := deps.UserRepo.(UserRoleRevoker)`) in the wiring — production path gets the real impl, degraded-mode test routers get nil and the handler emits a clean 500 `RevokeUnsupported`. Same shape used by `UserRoleHandler` construction; the general principle is "new cross-cutting behaviour on an existing wide interface = new narrow interface, not a method addition", which matches the US-249 ServiceAccountRepository decision tree.
- Composite admin CRUD feature with three parallel handlers (US-251 groups + roles + user-roles): each handler lives in its own file (`group_handlers.go`, `role_handlers.go`, `user_role_handlers.go`) with its own `*For` split, its own fake repo, and its own test file — NO shared abstraction. The three feature surfaces share the `withAdmin` test helper, `PermUserManage` gate, and `audit.Record` shape, but duplication is cheaper than a premature "AdminCRUDHandler" abstraction. Wire all three conditionally in `cmd/server/main.go` — degraded mode (no PG) leaves any of the three repos nil and that handler's routes simply don't mount; the contract test's chi.Walk never sees them because `newContractTestRouter` doesn't populate those deps either. Pattern generalises: whenever a user story adds 3+ related-but-independent CRUD surfaces, keep them parallel not nested.
- Optional permission list on POST /api/admin/roles: when Create accepts a bootstrapping `permissions []string` alongside the role identity, the handler must call `SetPermissions` AFTER `Create` succeeds (not inside a tx — the two calls aren't batched at the store layer and scope creep there is not worth it). If `SetPermissions` fails mid-flight the role is created but empty; the next PUT /permissions reconciles. Alternative "atomic" semantics would require either a compound store method or a tx-aware repo; both add surface area that the current usage volume doesn't justify. Pattern generalises to any "create-plus-optional-associated-list" endpoint: create the row, then optionally populate, and document that partial failure leaves the base row.
- Pre-flight challenge for two-step auth (US-253 MFA, future device-confirm flow): step 1 returns 202 Accepted + opaque single-use challenge token (32-byte random base64url) backed by an in-memory store with TTL (5min default) + delete-on-consume. Step 2 takes the challenge token + the user's response, validates atomically, and mints the final session. Server-side store beats signed JWT challenges by avoiding key-rotation concerns and getting replay protection for free. Multi-replica deployments need a shared backing store (Redis); document the constraint. Always include a defensive re-check at step 2 ("did the precondition still hold?") so admin-side state changes between steps invalidate in-flight challenges. The login-handler MFA branch MUST sit AFTER VerifyPassword (don't leak "this user has MFA" via timing on bad-password attempts) and BEFORE refresh-token mint (don't waste a slot on attempts that may not complete).
- TOTP integration (pquerna/otp v1.4.0, pure Go, CGO-free): `totp.Generate({Issuer, AccountName, Period:30, Digits:6, Algorithm:SHA1})` for setup, `totp.ValidateCustom(code, secret, now, {Period:30, Skew:1, ...})` for verify (explicit Skew=1 = ±30s tolerance — the bare `totp.Validate` hides this and a future library upgrade could change it). QR PNG render: `otp.NewKeyFromURL(otpURL).Image(256, 256)` returns `image.Image`; `png.Encode` then `base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString` for the JSON wire (no `data:` prefix, SPA wraps it). Don't change Period/Digits/Algorithm post-launch — existing enrolled users' codes stop working.
- Bulk-revoke-by-user is the single shape every SSO/admin logout flow reduces to: `RefreshService.RevokeAllForUser(userID, reason)` + `SessionStore.DeleteAllForUser(userID)`, where `reason` is the audit-trail differentiator (`logout`, `oidc_back_channel_logout`, `saml_slo`, `reuse_detected`, `admin_force_logout`, ...). The two-call shape is intentional: refresh tokens revoke (audit row + UPDATE) lives in `refresh_tokens`, sessions delete (DELETE) lives in `sessions`; coupling them at the API layer is fine because the failure mode (one succeeds, the other doesn't) is recoverable via re-issue. Don't add a "logout user" compound store method — every future bulk-logout trigger reuses the existing pair with a fresh reason string; no new abstraction needed. Prior art: US-255 OIDC back-channel + SAML SLO handlers, US-006 LogoutHandler.
- Reusing OIDC `Verifier` across login + back-channel logout: go-oidc's `*oidc.IDTokenVerifier.Verify` validates JWT signature/iss/aud/exp identically for id_tokens and logout_tokens — the differentiating bits (events claim shape, sub-or-sid presence, no-nonce rule) are application-level. Wire ONE Verifier in main.go and hand the same instance to both `NewOIDCHandler` and `NewOIDCBackChannelLogoutHandler` so JWKS rotation applies to both surfaces in lockstep without a second `oidc.NewProvider(ctx, issuer)` discovery hit. Same shape for SAML: a single gosaml2-backed verifier implements BOTH `SAMLAssertionVerifier` (for ACS / login) AND `SAMLLogoutVerifier` (for SLO / logout) so one instance powers both endpoints.
- "Unknown subject = 200 OK" for IdP-driven logout (OIDC back-channel + SAML SLO): the spec / common interpretation says an SP MUST return success for unknown subjects so an attacker who has somehow obtained the ability to sign logout tokens can't probe which subjects map to local users. Always emit 200/StatusSuccess regardless of whether the subject lookup found a row to revoke. Test it explicitly — silently letting an unknown-user path 404 is a subtle leak that's invisible from the happy path.
- OIDC test fixtures MUST set `exp` claim by default. go-oidc's IDTokenVerifier requires it (zero-time = expired) and back-channel logout tokens that omit it (RFC says exp is RECOMMENDED not REQUIRED) get rejected with the cryptic "token is expired (Token Expiry: 0001-01-01...)" message. Make `goodLogoutClaims()` / equivalent test helpers stamp `exp = time.Now().Add(5*time.Minute).Unix()` unless the caller overrides — saves 30 minutes of debugging across every future contributor.
- Extending an existing narrow verifier interface with an orthogonal feature: ALWAYS define a SECOND narrow interface rather than adding methods to the first. The concrete impl satisfies both implicitly; existing test stubs don't grow no-op methods; tests for the new feature stub ONLY the new interface. US-255 added `SAMLLogoutVerifier` (ValidateLogoutRequest + BuildLogoutResponse) alongside the pre-existing `SAMLAssertionVerifier` — the production `gosamlVerifier` got two new methods, the existing `stubSAMLVerifier` (used by 9 ACS tests) stayed untouched. Same anti-pattern as widening `oms.Repository` (15+ mock files) but at handler-collaborator scope.
- Post-read-filter composition of value-level engines: US-257 column masking (`masking.Engine`) runs AFTER the query-time row filters (security / rls / markings) — it rewrites WireObject.Properties in place via `applyColumnMasking`. Pipeline order in every read path: `applyPolicyFilter → applyMarkingFilter → applyPropertyVisibility → applyColumnMasking`. Each hook is a single line per read path (GetObject / ListObjects / SearchObjects / linkedObjects / GetLinkedObject); adding a new hook is trivial. Short-circuit on nil engine / zero transforms keeps the no-mask path allocation-free. Mutating the map in place (instead of returning a new WireObject like `FilterProperties` does) is the right call for value rewriting — masking keeps every key, so there's no reason to allocate.
- Class-based theme switch under Tailwind v4 (US-344): default `@variant dark` is media-query (prefers-color-scheme); JS-driven toggles need `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));` at the top of the stylesheet so `dark:bg-...` utilities follow an explicit `<html class="dark">`. Token inversion shadows the @theme defaults under `:where(.light) { --color-bg-*, --color-text-*, --color-border }` — accents stay constant so brand colour reads identically in both modes. Bootstrap path: `applyThemeToDocument(readPersistedTheme())` from main.tsx BEFORE `createRoot().render()` to avoid a one-frame light↔dark flash for users whose persisted choice differs from the default. Hook (`useTheme`) returns `{ theme, toggleTheme, setTheme }`; binary-state buttons use `aria-pressed` (not `role="switch"`) so screenreaders announce the state correctly. Same recipe applies to any future palette mode (high-contrast, sepia, etc.) — add `:where(.<mode>) { ... }` overrides and a third theme value.
- "AppliesTo" semantic flip across security surfaces: in RLS (US-256) the predicate is ADDED for applicable callers (RESTRICTION); in column masking (US-257) the caller inside AppliesTo is EXEMPTED (the list is an ALLOW list, mask applies to everyone else). Same struct shape (`{Roles, Groups, Users}`), opposite interpretation — document in each package doc so authors don't get confused when using both. Admin UI should make the semantic explicit per surface.
- Structural-typing interface reuse across engine packages: `cmd/server/groupLookupFromRepo` satisfies BOTH `rls.GroupMembershipLookup` AND `masking.GroupMembershipLookup` because Go interfaces match by method set. Any future engine needing "user → groups" declares its own narrow interface in its package with the SAME `UserGroups(ctx, userID) ([]string, error)` signature; one adapter in cmd/server feeds every engine from one wiring point. No per-package adapter needed — keeps `cmd/server` lean and avoids a cascade of identical 10-line adapters.
- AND-composition of orthogonal security engines at `ServiceImpl.compilePolicyQuery`: each engine (US-046 `security.Engine`, US-256 `rls.Engine`, future cell-level/column-level engines) independently returns `(query.Query, error)` or `(nil, nil)` — the outer helper wraps every non-nil output in `bleve.NewConjunctionQuery` so all surfaces enforce simultaneously without knowing about each other. Nil-at-the-boundary is the contract: degenerate MatchAll wrappers MUST be collapsed to nil inside the engine so the outer composer doesn't generate a pointless conjunction. When adding a new security engine: (1) narrow interface + nil-return for "no filter", (2) SetXxxEngine on ServiceImpl, (3) one branch in compilePolicyQuery that AND-joins it in. Same shape on the ObjectSet executor's `policyQueryAdapter`. Multiple OR-combined within an engine (union of applicable RLS policies) vs AND-combined across engines (every security surface restricts) is the default RLS semantics — `DisjunctionQuery(...).SetMin(1)` for the within-engine union, `ConjunctionQuery(a,b)` for cross-engine intersection.
- "Non-applicable policy adds no filter" is the right permissive semantics for role/group-targeted RLS. When a row_policy lists `AppliesTo.Roles=["eu-reader"]` and the caller holds `["viewer"]`, the policy contributes nothing (returns nil, no filter) — the caller sees whatever they'd have seen without any RLS. Alternative "no applicable policy ⇒ deny all" is too surprising (one admin edit silently wipes everyone else's visibility); admins who want strict deny layer an explicit catch-all deny policy. Same default implied by the PRD phrasing "filter visible objects based on user attributes": filters are additive, not default-deny.
- Predicate JSON over a mini-DSL: stuff `where.WhereClause` JSON into a JSONB column and run it through `where.ConvertToBleveQuery` at compile time. This gives admins every search primitive (eq / range / contains / wildcard / regex / phrase / geo / ...) without growing a domain DSL, and keeps validation in one place (the converter rejects unknown clause types). `pkg/rls.RowPolicy.Predicate json.RawMessage` (US-256) is prior art.
- Admin-handler post-write `engine.Reload(ctx)` as single-replica cache invalidation: every mutating endpoint (Create/Update/Delete) calls `engine.Reload` after the store write succeeds so the query-time cache stays fresh without waiting for server reboot. The pattern is single-machine honest — multi-replica deployments need a pub/sub broadcast (NATS subject) to notify peers. Document the constraint in the handler comment when you adopt this.
- Per-row security engines indexed by (objectTypeRID → primaryKey → masks): for US-258 cell-level security the engine's in-memory cache is a two-level map keyed first by ObjectType RID then by primary key. Reload rebuilds the whole index in one pass (store returns ORDER BY created_at so iteration is stable). Size() is the only convenience accessor and sums across all PKs for one OT — a per-PK Size would invite callers to reach into engine internals. `Compile` takes (user, otRID, pk) and returns nil on three short-circuit paths (nil user / admin / no masks on cell), keeping the caller's per-row hot path allocation-free when no cell masks apply. Reusing `masking.MaskRule` + `masking.AppliesTo` + `masking.ApplyTransforms` means one rule vocabulary spans column-level (US-257) and cell-level (US-258) — admins don't have to remember which surface accepts which rule names.
- Composing two layered masking engines in ServiceImpl: column-level masking runs first (broad per-OT/property rules), cell-level masking runs AFTER on the same Properties map. Both mutate in place, so the LAST write wins — this is the right shape for "cell rules sharpen column defaults": a column-wide `partial` on SSN becomes a row-specific `redact` for the one sensitive customer. Document the order-invariant in a test that pins the wire shape (prior art: `TestCellMask_ComposesWithColumnMask`). Never invert the order — running cell first would have column silently overwrite cell's sharper rule.
- Stringifying `WireObject.PrimaryKey` for per-row lookup keys: PrimaryKey is typed `interface{}` but in practice FormatObject stores a string. Use a tiny `stringifyPrimaryKey(pk interface{}) string` helper that short-circuits on `string` and falls through to `fmt.Sprintf("%v", pk)` for future composite-key shapes. Empty string (nil PK) skips the engine call — no legit row has an empty PK, so skipping is safer than looking up "".
- Adding versioned-history to a localStorage-backed entity (US-332 SavedObjectSet, future saved searches / dashboard layouts / pivot configs): keep the original "current state" field on the parent (`def`) AND add `versions[]` + `activeVersionId`; every write path that selects/changes the active version mirrors the chosen version's payload back onto the parent's "current state" field. Existing readers (`s.def` everywhere) stay untouched; version-aware code reads `versions` + `activeVersionId` directly. Refuse-the-last-version + auto-elect-on-active-drop keeps `versions.length >= 1 && activeVersionId is valid` invariant trivially true at every persist. Legacy migration belongs at the read boundary (`readSaved`) — lift unversioned entries into a single-version array in-memory, persist on next write. One choke point at read time beats a "data migration" pass.
- Non-ontology-scoped admin pages (`/admin/markings`, future `/admin/users`, `/admin/api-keys`, …) sit at the top level of the React router, NOT under `/admin/:ontology/...`. Gate with `PermissionRoute permission="user.manage"` rather than `AdminGuard` — `AdminGuard` resolves scoped ontology permissions via `:ontology` URL param, which these pages don't have. Sidebar MUST expose the entry in BOTH the `activeOntology ? [...] : []` ternary branches; otherwise the page is reachable by URL but not discoverable from the Dashboard. Prior art: US-259 MarkingAdminPage.
- Admin-surface repo extension without widening the hot-path interface: when an existing narrow repo interface (e.g. `MarkingRepository`) is referenced by many stubbed mocks (request-hot-path tests), DON'T add the new admin-only methods to it — cascades into every mock. Declare a SECOND narrow interface in the same package (e.g. `MarkingGrantAdminRepository` with `ListGrantsByMarking` + `ListGrantsByUser`), have the concrete `*PG<Foo>Repository` implement both, and wire BOTH fields on `ServerDeps` to the SAME instance in main.go. Degraded-mode routers leave the admin field nil; the handler emits a structured 500 `<Resource>LookupUnsupported` on the list-grants endpoints. Same playbook as `UserRoleRevoker` (US-251) and `MarkingGrantAdminRepository` (US-259).
- Nullable-timestamp auto-expiration (US-260 `user_markings.expires_at`, future "grant-until-X" surfaces): NULLable `expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ` (no default) + partial index `WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL`. Read paths add `AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > NOW())` — no background sweep required. Go side uses `*time.Time` (pgx maps NULL↔nil natively, no `sql.NullTime`). Re-grant escalates from `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` to `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET expires_at = EXCLUDED.expires_at` so the same POST handles "extend access" and "promote to permanent" (passing nil clears the timer). Dual-knob admin body (`expiresAt` RFC3339 + convenience `expiresInDays` int): convenience wins when both present; negative days → typed 400; `omitempty` on wire so permanent grants omit the field.
- Per-LinkType post-write enrichment hooks (US-261 marking propagation, future link-time auto-tagging, link-time provenance stamping, etc.): the right place is the funnel consumer's `applyLinkCreate`, NOT the action executor or any pre-publish path. Reasons: (1) all link writes — admin ad-hoc, action rules, ingest replays — funnel through `LINK_CREATE` edits, so the hook fires uniformly; (2) the consumer already has Bleve fetch + index helpers (`fetchDocument`, `IndexDocument`) so the rewrite-target-after-link-write loop is ~10 lines; (3) pre-publish hooks would need every action to know about the policy and replay would skip them. Keep the hook best-effort: log+swallow propagation errors so a misconfigured policy or transient Bleve hiccup never aborts the LINK_CREATE itself — the edge is the source of truth, propagation is enrichment. Pattern is: (a) narrow interface in `pkg/funnel` returning `(payload, found, err)` with found=false treated as a soft skip; (b) concrete adapter in `cmd/server/` so pkg/funnel doesn't import RID-resolution code from elsewhere; (c) setter on Consumer (`SetLinkPropagationResolver`) so degraded-mode test routers no-op; (d) ontologyAPIName + per-objectType API names threaded through so the helper can scope Bleve calls correctly. The same shape ports to "auto-tag child objects on parent's category", "stamp link timestamp into target", "trigger downstream embedding on link" — anywhere a link should fan out to per-object state without growing the action-executor surface.
- Bleve-returned `_markings` field shape is shape-tolerant: bleve stores arrays as `[]interface{}`, but a single-element array can come back as a bare `string`, and an empty array is absent entirely. Any code that reads `_markings` from `searchReq.Fields=["*"]` MUST handle all three: `string`, `[]string`, `[]interface{}` (with non-string entries silently dropped). One `decodeMarkings(map[string]interface{}) []string` helper is the single choke point — duplicate it nowhere. Same shape applies to any other multi-valued reserved field that may someday be read back via `searchReq.Fields`.
- Adding a new nullable TEXT-enum field to BOTH object_types + properties at once (classification / sensitivity / policy-label / …): one migration covers both tables, shape is `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS <col> TEXT` (nullable, no default). The minimum working set on pg_repository.go is 5+4 paths: `object_types` needs Create INSERT + Get SELECT + List SELECT + ListInterfaceObjectTypes SELECT + Update UPDATE; `properties` needs Create INSERT + List SELECT + Get SELECT + Update UPDATE. Every path uses `NULLIF($N, '')` on write and `COALESCE(col, '')` on read so the Go model stays plain `string`. Miss any one path → you'll see a "wrote it, list still empty" silent bug. Prior art: US-262 classification, US-260 expires_at applied this pattern to `user_markings`.
- Enum-backed dropdowns: put the canonical list in ONE place and consume it everywhere. Backend owns the truth (`pkg/oms.KnownClassifications()` + `IsKnownClassification`) and the frontend mirrors via `CLASSIFICATION_VALUES` + `Classification` type. `IsKnown*` MUST accept empty string as a legal value when the field is optional — otherwise every handler gets a redundant `s == "" || IsKnown(s)` pattern; centralising that asymmetry in the predicate keeps callers clean. For the UI, assert the full option set (`['', 'A', 'B', ...]`) in one test — adding a new label then produces one test failure instead of N silent-drift bugs.
- Runtime "scan-content-then-tag-marking" hooks (US-263 PII auto-detect, future "auto-classify by content"): hook at `pkg/funnel/Consumer.applyBatchWithHistory` AFTER `resolveConflicts`/`preserveEditOnlyFields`/`filterWritableProperties` and BEFORE `applyBatchEdits` so the detector sees the FINAL property set the index will store. Wrong order = the user-edit-merge-back can introduce PII fields after the detector ran ⇒ silent miss. Detector interface stays minimal (`DetectPII(props) bool`); skip non-string values + DELETE/link edits; dedupe against existing `edit.Markings` before append. Hook is unconditionally wired in `cmd/server/main.go` because the cost is constant pure-Go regex per edit (no PG / NATS dep) — degraded-mode test routers naturally skip it. Same setter pattern as `SetLinkPropagationResolver` / `SetEditOnlyField`. Once tagged, never auto-untag — fail-secure, admin uses `revokeMarkingFor` to remove.
- Regex-PII detector design choices (`pkg/security/pii`): SSN restricted to `XXX-XX-XXXX` (bare `\d{9}` flood-tags order numbers / postal+ext); credit card MUST be Luhn-validated (the regex alone false-positives every long numeric ID); phone format-permissive (parens / dashes / dots / +CC); email standard `\b...@...\.[a-z]{2,}\b` with `(?i)` for embedded matches. Skip non-string values entirely (numbers / bools come back from Bleve as native types — `fmt.Sprint`-ing them to scan would invite catastrophic false positives). Pure-Go (no CGO) keeps US-230's `CGO_ENABLED=0` Dockerfile invariant intact.
- Partial-update tri-state collision with "always-on dropdown" UX: `*string` on the DTO means nil=preserve / ""=clear / value=assign, but a React `<select>` is ALWAYS on-screen with some value loaded. The right default is "Edit form sends current form value as-is" — if user left the unspecified sentinel, that's "" ⇒ intentional clear; if user kept the loaded value, server sees the same value ⇒ no-op. Don't try to send undefined-when-unchanged unless the UI has an explicit "keep current" affordance; you'll just confuse future readers. The tri-state shape survives because SDK callers (scripts, CI-driven migrations) can still omit the field to preserve.
- HTTP-layer context carriers for service-layer audit/telemetry (US-264 ClientInfo): when a service method needs request-scoped metadata (caller IP, User-Agent, trace header, …) without taking an `*http.Request` dependency, define a tiny struct + `WithX`/`FromContext` helpers in a leaf package (pkg/audit/context.go) and attach a chi middleware that stamps the struct onto the request context. Empty-value guard inside `WithX` keeps non-HTTP callers (unit tests, background jobs) from polluting the context tree with zero-valued entries. Unique empty-struct key (`type clientInfoKey struct{}`) avoids string-based collisions. Same shape generalises to any cross-cutting context carrier — request-ID, locale, trace-context extensions.
- Service-layer read-path audit hooks (US-264 DataAccessAuditor): package the "check flag on the ObjectType → optionally emit audit row" logic into a small helper type with a nil-safe receiver (`*DataAccessAuditor`). Call sites inside ServiceImpl drop a single line at the very END of the read path after all filtering/masking has run — so the audit reflects the row set the caller ACTUALLY saw, not the pre-policy set. The ObjectType is already loaded earlier in every read path (OMS lookup for policy + marking), so the flag check is free. Errors from `audit.Record` are SWALLOWED — a failed audit must never turn a 200 into a 500; operators monitor audit write health separately.
- objectset.Handler doesn't have the *ObjectType on hand (it works with api-name strings from the executor result), so the audit sink must be a narrow interface implemented by an adapter in cmd/server that owns the OMS repo (`loadObjectSetAuditAdapter`). Keeps `pkg/oss/objectset` free of any `pkg/oms` / `pkg/audit` import, matches the same pattern used by `newPropertyFilterAdapter` / `newHistorySnapshotAdapter` / `newObjectSetSnapshotAdapter`. Never widen the handler itself to accept an OMS repo — the adapter-in-cmd-server indirection keeps the handler testable in isolation.
- Audit-tail fan-out (SIEM exporter, future write-through replicator): decorate the base `audit.Store` with a `TeeStore{inner, exporter}` at wire time. Insert MUST hit the inner store first and propagate its error AS IS — losing observability is strictly better than losing the audit trail itself. Only on inner success does the event flow to the exporter, and even then via a detached `go func` with `context.Background()` so a cancelled HTTP request never races the committed insert. Log-and-swallow in the goroutine — no error path should bubble back to the caller. Nil exporter is a passthrough so degraded-mode wiring is one line in cmd/server. Reusable for any fire-and-forget write-through (metrics sinks, webhook forwarders, replay queues). Prior art: `pkg/audit/export.TeeStore` (US-265).
- BatchedExporter with RetryPolicy pattern (US-265): buffer-on-Enqueue + drain-on-threshold-or-explicit-Flush, with exponential backoff (`InitialBackoff * Multiplier^n` capped at `MaxBackoff`) around each attempt. Three invariants worth stressing: (1) ALWAYS clear the buffer after a flush attempt regardless of outcome — callers must not see the same failing batch replayed at every Enqueue; return `*ExportError{Exporter, Attempts, Err}` so operators can distinguish "flaked and gave up" from "recovered". (2) Backoff wait MUST be ctx-aware (`time.NewTimer` + `select { <-ctx.Done(): | <-t.C }`), else a cancelled request hangs for the full cumulative backoff. Tests inject a synchronous `sleepFunc` to observe the schedule without actually sleeping. (3) Zero RetryPolicy defaults to `MaxAttempts=1` (no retry) + BatchSize<=0 defaults to 1 (immediate flush) — mis-configured wirings must still make forward progress, never silently hang or swallow events. Same shape reusable for any retry-with-backoff queue sink.
- Pluggable-SDK pattern for cloud dependencies under CGO_ENABLED=0 (US-265 S3Uploader): define the transport client as a narrow two-method interface inside the exporter package (`S3Uploader.PutObject(ctx, bucket, key, body)`) instead of importing aws-sdk-go-v2 directly. Operators who need S3 wire a tiny adapter in their cmd/server (`func(ctx, b, k, body) error { _, err := s3c.PutObject(ctx, &s3.PutObjectInput{...}); return err }`). Keeps go.mod lean, the Dockerfile invariant intact, and tests use a trivial in-memory fake. Same shape works for Kinesis / Firehose / Cloud Pub-Sub / anywhere a hyperscaler SDK would otherwise explode the dependency tree. Ship a "not-wired: falling back to disabled" warn so a naive `WEAVE_AUDIT_EXPORT_KIND=s3` gets a clear log line rather than a silent no-op.
- Tamper-proof hash chain on an append-only audit table (US-266): store three columns alongside the event — `chain_seq BIGSERIAL` (monotonic ordering handle), `prev_hash TEXT` (pointer to previous row's entry_hash), `entry_hash TEXT` (sha256 over canonical envelope including prev_hash). Chain invariant: flipping any byte of any row changes every downstream entry_hash + the daily root hash, so tampering is detectable end-to-end. Canonicalise the envelope (sorted JSON keys + RFC3339Nano UTC timestamps + parse-and-re-emit of JSONB values) so PG round-trip doesn't break the hash — JSONB normalises whitespace on read-back and the hash must be stable under that. Serialise inserts across pool connections with `pg_advisory_xact_lock(<const>)` inside a tx: SELECT tail entry_hash FOR tailHash, compute new entry_hash over envelope+tailHash, INSERT. Advisory lock is transaction-scoped (auto-released on commit/rollback) so no cleanup needed, and doesn't block unrelated workloads. VerifyChain does three sequential checks per row — chain_seq contiguity, prev_hash == previous row's entry_hash, entry_hash == recompute(prev_hash, row) — and returns a typed `*ChainVerificationError{Index, EventID, ChainSeq, Reason}` at the first divergence so operator dashboards can point at the exact row.
- Append-only daily root-hash anchor file: every UTC day's chain is collapsed to one sha256 over concatenated entry_hashes (newline-delimited for defence against accidental prefix-match) and appended as `<YYYY-MM-DD>\t<hex>\n` to a file opened `O_APPEND|O_CREATE|O_WRONLY` at mode 0600. Publisher wakes up on `Start(ctx)` (immediate yesterday-anchor cycle + interval ticker), accepts `SetNowFunc` for deterministic tests, and NO-OPs on empty days so the file only accumulates evidence for days that actually produced events. Verification tool cross-checks each parsed `RootFileEntry` against a recomputed root over the live DB chain grouped by UTC day — any mismatch surfaces a `root mismatch on 2026-04-18` error with both the anchored hex and the recomputed hex so operators can tell "entries were tampered" from "entries were deleted" at a glance. Keep the publisher concern OUT of the audit Store Insert path — async anchor cadence beats synchronous "hash-every-row-in-memory" at any non-trivial volume.
- `pg_advisory_xact_lock` vs `FOR UPDATE` for serialisation (US-266): `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE LIMIT 1` locks only the matched row, which does NOT prevent a second connection from INSERTing between the SELECT and the INSERT (their SELECT sees the same tail, produces the same prev_hash, and creates a fork in the chain). Use `pg_advisory_xact_lock($const)` to serialise the whole chain-write region across connections; it auto-releases at tx boundary, doesn't touch row visibility, and costs O(1). The same pattern applies to any "compute from current tail then append" sequence where row-level locks aren't enough (e.g. per-table monotonic-version columns, per-tenant sequence counters).
- Streaming-zip HTTP handlers (US-268 export, future bulk-download / backup): headers go on the wire BEFORE `zip.Writer.Create` returns its first byte, so a mid-stream error can NEVER be converted to a structured 500 — all pre-flight checks (auth, body parse, source-not-configured gate) MUST run before the first `w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/zip")`. Audit rows for the request ALSO need to land synchronously before the stream starts for the same reason. Inside the stream: log-and-return on error (truncated body on the wire is the only failure mode), NEVER try to emit JSON after zip bytes have flowed. `zip.NewWriter(w).Close()` is load-bearing — skipping it leaves a corrupt archive even if every inner Create succeeded.
- Narrow-sources-with-adapters pattern for multi-subsystem data aggregation (US-268 Exporter): when a feature needs data from 5+ orthogonal subsystems (user repo, audit store, media catalog, media blobs, ...), define ONE narrow interface per source in the owning leaf package, keep the package free of the underlying subsystem imports, and push translation into thin adapters in `cmd/server/<feature>_<role>.go`. Each source is independently optional — a nil source produces an absent/empty field so degraded deployments still emit a useful response. Constructor is `New<Feature>()` with NO source args; caller sets fields directly (`e.Profile = ...`). Same shape generalises to any "multi-subsystem read pipeline" — cross-service audit reports, compliance-control-evidence bundles, cross-ontology migrations. Prior art: `pkg/gdpr.Exporter` source fields + `cmd/server/gdpr_export.go` adapters.
- Sanitising untrusted filenames before zip write: `path.Base(name)` strips directory prefixes, `strings.TrimLeft(base, ".")` kills "../" leftovers, then scrub residual separators (`ReplaceAll "/" "_"` + `"\\" "_"`). Empty / "." / ".." falls back to a sentinel like "blob" so the archive layout stays deterministic. Applying to the RID path segment too catches the rare case of a manual test fixture with slashes. NEVER trust the catalog — a compromised DB row can otherwise place bytes anywhere the consumer's unzip routine extracts to.
- Start(ctx)/Stop() scheduler race (US-269, also latent in LDAPSyncScheduler / RootHashPublisher): inside `Stop` the shape `s.stopCh = nil` races with the goroutine's `case <-s.stopCh:` read — if Stop runs before the goroutine enters select, the goroutine observes nil and waits forever, leaving Stop blocked on doneCh. Fix: allocate `stopCh := make(chan struct{})` + `doneCh := make(chan struct{})` as LOCALS in Start, assign them to the struct fields under the lock, AND capture the locals inside the goroutine closure. The goroutine reads only its captured local copies so Stop's mutations can't affect it. Cheaper than sync.Once + atomic flags and keeps the Start/Stop API unchanged. Only matters under back-to-back Start→Stop (typical production uptime never exercises it; unit tests that start-then-stop-immediately surface it every run).
- Archive-and-delete retention (US-269) pattern: when a long-running table needs TTL eviction with optional cold-storage archive, the right pipeline is (a) `ListBefore(cutoff, cursor, limit)` with a monotonic cursor over an immutable append-only column (chain_seq for audit, id for any other append-only table), (b) `Archive(batch)` on each page to an idempotent external sink, (c) single `DeleteBefore(cutoff)` at the end. Archive failure aborts BEFORE delete so the next run retries the same rows. DB rows survive on failure; the sink is idempotent so re-archiving a partial run only creates a new object (dedup at query time). Same shape reusable for: object_history retention, action_jobs archival, attachment GC, any temporal-expiry table.
- Grafana dashboard as versioned repo asset (US-272): drop the JSON under `grafana/dashboards/<name>.json` (schemaVersion≥30 for Grafana 9+), pair with `grafana/provisioning/datasources/<ds>.yml` (uid-pinned + `editable: false`) and `grafana/provisioning/dashboards/<loader>.yml` (file-provider `options.path` is the CONTAINER path, not the repo path — docker-compose volume mount does the bridging). Always template the datasource as `${datasource}` variable of type `datasource` so the JSON is portable across dev/stage/prod without a sed copy. `clamp_min(denominator, 1)` on every "fraction of total" PromQL query kills the NaN cold-start gap. Compose syntax is CI-validated with `docker compose config --quiet` (nonzero exit on any schema drift). Dashboard tests should match panels by "title OR any target.expr contains the ID" — substring on the expected metric inside at least one target is the real invariant; requiring full-title stability over a copyedit produces brittle red CI for no benefit.
- Cross-cutting OpenTelemetry coverage without per-method instrumentation (US-271): HTTPMiddleware + pgx.QueryTracer are the two choke points that cover "every handler" and "every repo method" respectively — install once in `NewFullRouter` / `database.ConnectWithTracer` and every future handler / pgxpool-backed repo inherits span coverage for free. Reserve `tracing.StartSpan(ctx, "pkg.Method", attrs...)` for in-handler business-path spans where finer granularity than the server span is worth the extra attribute payload. For library packages that need request-scoped identity (user, tenant, locale) inside a span without importing pkg/auth, accept a `func(ctx) string` resolver at middleware construction — concrete bindings live at the main.go wiring site so pkg/tracing stays dependency-minimal. Propagator default must be composite `TraceContext{}+Baggage{}`; install it even when tracing is disabled so in-process span authors always get sane propagation defaults. `pgx.QueryTracer` attached at `cfg.ConnConfig.Tracer` BEFORE `pgxpool.NewWithConfig` — every Query/QueryRow/Exec/SendBatch opens a client-kind span automatically. Only attach when tracing.Enabled=true so low-latency reads don't pay span-alloc cost in dev/test.
- Forward-compatible migration invariants (US-275, enforced by `internal/upgrade/forward_compat_test.go`): every `migrations/*.up.sql` must (1) use `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` so migrate up is idempotent, (2) pair any `NOT NULL ADD COLUMN` with a `DEFAULT` so v(N) INSERTs survive after v(N+1) lands the column, (3) avoid `DROP COLUMN`/`DROP TABLE`/`RENAME COLUMN`/`RENAME TABLE` in up.sql — destructive schema ops belong in a later release once every reader is on v(N+1), (4) list any `ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE` in the `allowedNonForwardCompat` allowlist with a paired `docs/upgrade.md` runbook line. Check enforced statically so the whole tree is scanned in single-digit ms inside the default `go test ./...` lane. When a new invariant surfaces a legacy violation, prefer a trivial tightening backport (`IF NOT EXISTS` on old `ADD COLUMN`s) over grandfathering — the fix is byte-identical to a no-op on fresh DBs and an idempotent guard on re-applied DBs.
- Liveness vs readiness route mounting (US-275): mount the conventional `/health/live` alias via the SAME `LivenessHandler` instance as `/health` rather than serving a 30x redirect — kubelet's `httpGet` probes don't follow redirects by default, so a redirect-based alias silently marks every pod unready. Two `r.Method(http.MethodGet, path, shared)` lines is the right shape. Same principle for any future "Kubernetes-conventional alias for a legacy endpoint" surface: mount twice, never redirect.
- Two-process coordination scripts (US-275 rolling-upgrade.sh, future blue/green / shadow-replay): `set -euo pipefail` + one `cleanup()` function attached via `trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM` that no-ops on already-dead PIDs (`kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null`). Capture each spawned PID into a named variable (`OLD_PID` / `NEW_PID`) and blank it after `wait` so cleanup won't retry reaped processes. The trap fires on Ctrl-C too so a cancelled drill never leaves zombies. Dual-probe drills that need "never both unready at once" verification should loop short `curl --max-time 2 http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health/<probe>` polls at 200ms cadence during the handoff window and count any window where neither port returns 200 as a failure — capture the count, fail the script with the specific number so operators know whether it was a single blip or a structural gap.
- jsdom (vitest) does not implement `Element.scrollIntoView` — calling it from a useEffect crashes the test. Guard with `typeof scrollAnchorRef.current?.scrollIntoView === 'function'` BEFORE calling. Canonical fix for any "auto-scroll to bottom of chat / log / feed" pattern in vitest+jsdom; the production browser path is unaffected.
- TanStack Query optional-id pattern: when a `useQuery({queryKey, queryFn, enabled: !!id})` is keyed by an optional id, give the disabled branch a STABLE sentinel queryKey (e.g., `['aip','messages','__none__']`) so the cache hash doesn't churn while disabled. Prior art: `useAIPMessages` in `web/src/hooks/useAIPThreads.ts`.
- Vitest fake timers + ANY interval-driven UI animation (typewriter, polling progress bar, debounced input render): use `vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true })` in `beforeEach` so TanStack Query's internal promise timing still resolves while user-code `setTimeout` is mocked. Without the option mutation `onSuccess` callbacks never fire and the test hangs. Drive animations to completion with `await act(async () => { vi.advanceTimersByTime(500); })`.
- DAG branch-skipping with diamonds (US-281 AIP Logic): per-edge `active []bool` bitmap keyed by edge index, NOT a per-node `skipped` set. A node runs iff at least one incoming edge is active OR it has zero incoming edges; an `if` node deactivates outgoing edges whose `Branch` label doesn't match the taken branch; an unreachable node deactivates all its outgoing edges so dead branches propagate. The naive "mark all downstream of the not-taken edge as skipped" silently breaks reconverging diamonds — the merge node has another live predecessor and should still run, but it's already in the skipped set. ~30 LOC, deterministic across edge orderings, one bit of state per edge. Pattern reusable for any future control-flow node type that gates execution on runtime decisions.
- Subpackage placement for related-but-orthogonal AIP surfaces (US-281): `pkg/aip` (threads / messages) and `pkg/aip/logic` (workflows / runs) intentionally do NOT share types beyond the `aip.Provider` interface. Logic depends on Provider for `llm` nodes via a tiny `ProviderResolver` interface (one method, satisfied implicitly by `*aip.Registry`), but Flow / Run / Node stay independent of Thread / Message so the two domains can version separately. Trying to share a "ChatRequest" abstraction upward cements the wrong shape — flows BUILD a ChatRequest from variable substitution + node config; threads BUILD a ChatRequest from persisted message history.
- `{{node.field}}` placeholder substitution for prompt templates / tool params: a tiny scanner that walks `{{...}}` and resolves via dotted-path lookup beats text/template (Go-only syntax SDK callers won't recognise) or jq (CGO). Empty-string-on-missing-path is the right default — strict "missing-path = error" surfaces every typo as a 422 and frustrates iterative authoring. Apply the same substitution to map values via recursive `substituteVarsAny` so tool params inherit templating without per-tool plumbing.
- React Flow / @xyflow/react v12 in vitest+jsdom: the canvas relies on ResizeObserver, getBoundingClientRect with non-zero size, and a real layout pipeline that jsdom does not provide. The cleanest path is a `vi.mock('@xyflow/react', () => ({...}))` shim that exposes ReactFlowProvider as a passthrough and renders the supplied `nodes` as a `<ul data-testid="rf-mock-nodes">…</ul>` plus forwards `children` so toolbar overlays still mount. Stub `addEdge` / `applyNodeChanges` / `applyEdgeChanges` as identity-ish helpers and pass-through Background / Controls / MiniMap. Production code still uses the real library; the mock only exists to keep RTL tests focused on OUR glue (toolbar buttons, node-config panel, save / execute wiring) rather than xyflow's layout engine. Don't forget `vi.mock('@xyflow/react/dist/style.css', () => ({}))` so the CSS import doesn't break the test resolver.
- Persisting editor-only state inside the wire model without a separate column: stamp it into `node.config.__editorPosition` (or any `__<feature>` prefixed key). The backend's JSONB storage merges unknown keys through unchanged AND `Validate()` doesn't reject them, so canvas layout (x/y), pinned/highlighted state, breakpoints, etc. survive a round-trip without a schema change. Reserve the `__` prefix for editor-private keys (matches the reserved `__primaryKey` / `__rid` convention on WireObject) so future config validators can distinguish "executor input" from "ui scratchpad" if needed.
- Adding a new top-level web route + sidebar entry is a 3-step sync: (1) import the page component into `web/src/App.tsx` and add `<Route path="…" element={…}/>` inside the protected Shell group, (2) add the sidebar nav item to `web/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx` (the always-visible `navItems` slice for non-ontology-scoped pages, or the `activeOntology` ternary branch for ontology-scoped ones), (3) drop a new SVG path constant into the `iconPaths` map at the top of Sidebar.tsx and reference it by name on the nav item. Only step (3) is easy to forget — the icon silently disappears (returns null) without a visible error.
- Catalog-backed plugin tables (US-285 aip_tools, future model registries / connector catalogues): persist (name PK, description, parameters JSONB, handler_function_rid, enabled, created_by, timestamps) with a NAME-format CHECK that mirrors the LLM-API tool-name conventions (`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$`). Registry lifecycle = bootstrap-load + admin-CRUD: `LoadCatalogIntoRegistry(ctx, registry, store, invoker)` walks enabled rows once at boot and the admin handler keeps the in-process registry in sync via `Register` (on Create/Update.Enabled=true), `Unregister` (on Delete or Update.Enabled=false). Same dep-direction trick as aip.Store + featureflags.Store — narrow ToolCatalog interface in pkg/aip, in-memory test impl alongside, PG impl in cmd/server. The "definition + handler indirection" splits cleanly: the wire-visible (Name/Description/Parameters) lives on the catalog row; Execute() routes through a `FunctionInvoker` callback so pkg/aip stays free of any oms / functions dep, and the cmd/server adapter ties it onto `oms.Repository.GetFunction + oms.FunctionExecutor.Execute`. Empty HandlerFunctionRID is a valid "definition-only" state — the LLM can see the tool but `ErrToolHandlerNotConfigured` surfaces at execute-time so operators notice the missing wiring rather than a silent no-op the LLM might loop on.
- Stringifying a FunctionExecutor's `interface{}` return for an LLM-visible string slot: typed switch over the primitive branches (string passthrough, bool/int/float via strconv, json.Number) → `json.Marshal` fallback for maps/slices → `fmt.Sprintf("%v")` last resort. Handles all four runtime shapes the Goja+HTTP executor pair can return without forcing every catalog row to declare its own result-type schema. Specific-before-general matters: int/float64 must be checked before the JSON fallback so `42` doesn't become `"42"` (json-quoted) and `1.5` doesn't become `"1.5"` (same); `nil` must be checked first so it becomes `""` not the literal string `"null"`.
- robfig/cron/v3 parser flag for "5 OR 6 fields + descriptors" (US-289 Pipeline scheduler, future cron-driven feature surfaces): `cron.NewParser(cron.SecondOptional | cron.Minute | cron.Hour | cron.Dom | cron.Month | cron.Dow | cron.Descriptor)`. The default `cron.New()` parser is 5-field-only and silently rejects 6-field schedules; `SecondOptional` is the v3-only flag that accepts both. Construct ONE parser at scheduler-creation time and reuse it inside `cron.New(cron.WithParser(p))` so Validate-time and Register-time agree on the accepted format. Pre-validate with `parser.Parse(spec)` before `cron.AddJob` so a freshly-broken expression fails synchronously at the admin handler instead of inside the cron loop.
- `cron.Stop()` returns a `context.Context` that closes once every running job callback has returned. WAIT on it (`<-c.Stop().Done()`) for strict happens-before between Scheduler.Stop and runner cleanup — under -race, skipping the wait surfaces as data-race noise on shared scheduler state when tests immediately read post-Stop. Same pattern that pkg/audit/retention.Scheduler uses for the captured stop/done channels.
- axe-core a11y smoke-test pattern (US-351): one helper at `web/src/test/axe.ts` (`runAxe` + `expectNoCriticalViolations`), scoped via `runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag21a','wcag21aa'] }` and gated on `impact === 'critical' || 'serious'`. Always disable `color-contrast` for jsdom — no real layout means false-positives on every transparent / OKLCH token. The wcag-tag scope auto-excludes axe's "best-practice" rules (page-has-heading-one, region) so subpages that legitimately ship without an h1 stay clean. Every page under audit needs a parallel `vi.mock` for any realtime / WebSocket / SSE hook (or jsdom hangs on the connect attempt). Validate the assertion is honest by temporarily reverting one fix and confirming the test goes red — placeholder-only inputs DO trip `[critical] label` so the test catches real regressions, not just lints. Decorative svgs get `aria-hidden="true"` + `focusable="false"`; interactive elements get `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-accent-cyan/50` (not `focus:`, which fires on mouse click too); selected nav items use `aria-current="page"` (NOT aria-selected — that needs role=tab/option parent), toggle buttons use `aria-pressed`. SearchBar / FilterBuilder are prior art — copy when adding new search/filter affordances.
- Replace-cron-entry-under-the-same-lock invariant: when re-registering a key in a cron registry (`map[id]EntryID`), the `Remove(old) + AddJob(new) + entries[id] = new` must happen under one mutex hold. A two-phase "remove then add without the lock" briefly lets a concurrent Register see entries[id] empty and double-fire. Generalises to any "replace by key" mutation on a registry where stale entries are observable side-effects (subscriptions, watchers, audit hooks).
- Cron-driven scheduler indirection (`PipelineRunner` interface in pkg/pipeline + `PipelineRunnerFunc` adapter): keep the package free of downstream-runtime imports by accepting an interface in NewScheduler. The wired runner can be a logging placeholder while a future story builds the real dispatcher — ship the lib integration with a placeholder runner in cmd/server so operators can verify the cron path is alive end-to-end. Same dep-direction shape as `aip.ToolCatalog.FunctionInvoker` (US-285) and `pkg/funnel.LinkPropagationResolver` (US-261). Never ship the cron package without a runner indirection: every "swap in the real executor later" story has burned someone who hard-coded the runner inline.
- Adding an MCP method beyond tools/* (US-286 resources/list + resources/read): three-step sync — (1) new case in `pkg/mcp/server.go::Handle`, (2) new handler with the same `(*Server, *Request) *Response` shape returning `NewSuccessResponse` / `NewErrorResponse`, (3) advertise the capability inside `handleInitialize` so spec-compliant clients discover it. Capability shape mirrors `tools` (`{listChanged: false}` + any feature toggles like `subscribe: false`). Optional dependencies (e.g. `ObjectSetCatalog`) follow the same `SetXxx` setter pattern as `SemanticSearcher`: define a narrow interface in pkg/mcp, expose `SetXxx`, and let degraded-mode test routers leave it unset; advertise the capability anyway when at least one resource family is always available (ontologies via the OMS repo). URI scheme is `weave://<kind>/<id>` parsed via a single helper that splits on the first `/` after the authority — multi-slash IDs (future RID shapes) survive the round-trip, empty kind/id reject as InvalidParams. Error code mapping: missing/expired resource → `-32000` CodeToolError (application error), malformed URI → `-32602` CodeInvalidParams, decode failure on params → CodeInvalidParams. Kept consistent with the tools/call dispatch so SDK error handlers don't need a separate branch per method.
- Driver-agnostic database/sql wrappers (US-292 JDBC connector, future "use any pure-Go SQL driver" surfaces): the wrapper package imports NO driver. Operators wire side-effect imports (`import _ "github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib"`) in cmd/server. Two construction paths — `New(cfg)` does `sql.Open` for production, `NewWithDB(db, cfg)` injects a `*sql.DB` for tests and pool-sharing callers. Tests use a hand-rolled fake `database/sql/driver` registered in TestMain (under multiple aliases — one dialect-recognised, one not — so `New()` and `NewWithDB()` paths both run hermetic). ~80 LOC for the fake; avoids a `DATA-DOG/go-sqlmock` dep. Same shape ports to S3-style connectors (US-293), REST pollers (US-294), Kafka consumers (US-295). SQL injection defence belongs at every interpolated identifier (`ValidateIdentifier` per table/column/orderBy/watermark) — single regex `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}$` per dot-separated segment, max 2 segments, covers Postgres+MySQL+SQLite simultaneously. `Quote` helper trusts validated input — double-validating inside `Quote` would invert the contract and slow the read path.
- Keyset vs OFFSET pagination semantics: keyset (`WHERE col > $cursor ORDER BY col ASC LIMIT N`) is mandatory for incremental reads — orders by AND watermarks on the SAME column so writes appended after the read started still surface in later pages. OFFSET (`LIMIT N OFFSET M`) is acceptable for full-table reads only when `OrderBy` is explicit; without ORDER BY the DB returns whatever the scan order produces this pass, causing both duplicates AND skipped rows across calls. `hasMore = (returned rows == PageSize)` is the right cursor signal even though it produces one redundant call when the source has exactly PageSize rows after the cursor — the alternative `COUNT(*)` per page is hot-path expensive.
- Closed-enum DSL with N type-specific evaluators (US-296 quality rules, US-244 control-flow rules, future small-rule-language surfaces): one flat `Rule` struct + all `omitempty` per-type fields beats a discriminated union — JSON decode is allocation-free for unused fields, `Validate` and the per-rule executor each dispatch via a tiny `switch r.Type` calling a named per-variant helper (`evalNotNull` / `evalRange` / ...). Top-level dispatch stays under the gocyclo lint floor (15) regardless of how many variants land. Pair with: (1) an `IsKnownXxx` predicate + `AllXxx` slice for handler validation + admin-UI dropdowns, (2) a CHECK constraint on the persisted column pinning the same identifiers (catches drift between Go and the wire), (3) per-variant compile-time work (regex compile, FK lookup wiring) cached on the Checker at construction so the hot path is allocation-free. Same shape generalises to JSON-Schema-style validators, action-rule executors, alert-condition predicates.
- Read-only DAG visualisation (US-297 PipelineGraph, future Lineage / SchemaGraph monitoring views): prefer a small inline SVG renderer (longest-path column layout + cubic-Bézier edges) over react-flow. SVG nodes as `<g role="button" tabIndex={0}>` with click + Enter/Space activation; data-testid="…-graph-node" + data-node-name + per-edge data-from/data-to so RTL tests assert structure directly without xyflow's mock dance. Reach for react-flow only when the user needs drag-to-rearrange or interactive edge creation (e.g. AIP Logic editor). Layout is `node.column = 1 + max(upstream.column)` for transforms, outputs pinned to `maxTransformColumn + 1` — works for any topologically-ordered DAG validated at create time. Memoise the whole layout in `useMemo([pipeline])` rather than per-node — it's one O(N+E) pass.
- Append-only run-history table for any "X执行/调度" surface (US-298 pipeline_runs, future action / function / quality-check history): `BIGSERIAL id PRIMARY KEY` doubles as the keyset cursor (`WHERE id < $cursor ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT N+1`); fetch limit+1 to compute hasMore in a single round-trip without `COUNT(*)`. FK to the parent table with `ON DELETE CASCADE` so admin deletions drag the history with them — MemoryStore mirrors the cascade by walking `s.runs` and dropping rows whose `PipelineID == id` so re-creating the parent under the same id starts with an empty list. Existence-probe the parent before listing (`SELECT EXISTS(...)`) so the handler can route to 404 vs `200 + []`; the probe is one cheap planar lookup on a primary key. Cross-parent leakage is a real bug — `GetPipelineRun(ctx, parentID, runID)` MUST scope the SELECT to BOTH ids and return RunNotFound when the row exists but lives under a different parent (don't reveal cross-tenant existence). Pagination cursor on the wire is the run id as a decimal string — keeps SDKs from accidentally arithmeticking on it; non-empty NextCursor = more pages remain.
- Force-directed graph rendering on the frontend (US-302 Lineage UI, prior art SchemaGraphPage): codebase has `d3-force` + `@xyflow/react` but NOT `react-force-graph` — when a PRD asks for "react-force-graph" use d3-force + inline SVG instead (matches Dockerfile pure-Go discipline of "use what's already in deps"). Recipe: `forceSimulation<GraphNode>(simNodes).force('link', forceLink<GraphNode, Edge>(simEdges).id(n=>n.id).distance(160).strength(0.5)).force('charge', forceManyBody().strength(-380)).force('center', forceCenter(W/2, H/2)).force('collide', forceCollide(R+16)).stop()` then `for (let i=0; i<300; i++) sim.tick();` — runs the simulation ahead of time, populates a `Map<id, {x,y}>` for render. Memoise on a STABLE STRING SIGNATURE (sorted node ids + sorted edge ids) — `useMemo([nodes, edges])` recomputes on every parent re-render because array references change. Pan/zoom: `<g transform={`translate(${tx},${ty}) scale(${scale})`}>` + `onWheel` updates scale, `onMouseDown` on background `<rect data-pan="true">` records drag start, `onMouseMove` updates tx/ty. Use `data-testid` + `data-rid` on each node so RTL tests can pick them out by RID without measuring positions.
- Click-to-expand graph pattern (any drill-down surface — lineage, lineage cross-set, dependency graph): split state into `data` (TanStack Query result keyed by root params) and `extra` (imperative fetch results merged in). On click of a non-root node, call the same API with that node's id as new root, then `setExtra(prev => { nodes: [...prev.nodes, ...resp.nodes], edges: [...prev.edges, ...resp.edges] })`. Merge in a `useMemo` with edge-key dedup (`from__to__operation__timestamp`) so re-clicking the same node is idempotent. Reset `extra` whenever any of the root-level filters (direction/depth/rootRid) changes — otherwise stale clicks from the previous query contaminate the new result. Don't try to push expansion into the React-Query cache: the queries are keyed by `(rid, direction, depth)` and a single graph view is N+1 of those, with no clean cache key for "the union".
- Controlled `<input type="number">` + RTL `userEvent.clear` + `userEvent.type` is a known footgun (US-302). React rerenders the controlled input with the OLD value before clear "takes effect", so subsequent type appends instead of replacing — `clear → type "3"` on a value-bound `<input value={depth}>` ends up with "13", which fails any min/max bound check and silently keeps state at 1. Fix: keep an unbounded string buffer state for the input (`depthRaw: string`), derive the parsed/clamped numeric value via `useMemo` on `depthRaw`, pass `value={depthRaw}` to the input. The string buffer absorbs the clear/type interleaving honestly. Same shape works for any numeric form input that needs bounded validation.
- Recursive Definition-tree → (nodes, edges) wire shape (US-303 ObjectSet lineage, future ActionRule chain viz / Function dependency graphs / etc.): one tiny recursion (`walk(def) -> string id`) recurses into every input field FIRST, then allocates a synthetic id (`"n" + counter++`) and appends the parent. Edges are emitted as `(childID, parentID, operation=parent.Type)` so leaves precede the root in the slice and callers can render top-down by reverse-iteration without sorting. Type-specific field copy lives in a SEPARATE `populate(node, def)` switch — keeps the recursion under the gocyclo=15 floor and makes "add a new ObjectSet type" a one-case edit. Same shape generalises to any operation-tree surface where each node carries operation-specific metadata.
- Route ordering for chi suffix matching, generalised: any new `GET /{wildcard}/<suffix>` MUST register BEFORE `GET /{wildcard}` in chi, or the wildcard greedily matches the suffix and the new handler never fires. The bug is silent — chi returns the wildcard handler's response (often a 200 with the wrong shape), not a 404. Add an explicit test that mounts the router the SAME way main.go does and hits the suffix URL; any "tested with a one-route mux" assertion is misleading. Prior art: US-224 snapshots route + US-303 lineage route both register the static segment first.
- PRD JSON validation gap: ralph.sh / ralph harness does not currently re-validate `prd.json` after the agent updates it, and a missing `},` between adjacent stories silently passes the bash commit but breaks the next iteration's `python -m json.tool` / `jq` parse. Pre-commit guard worth adding: `jq empty prd.json || exit 1` (or python equivalent) so a syntax break gets caught at the iteration boundary instead of the next read. US-303 hit this and had to repair the US-302 commit's break before continuing — a one-character fix, but discovered hours later.
- Per-connection rolling-window rate limiter (US-308 WebSocket event cap, future per-stream throttles): keep the limiter state on the Connection itself (not a hub-keyed map) so the disabled path is a free pointer-or-zero check (`limit<=0 || window<=0 → allow`) and concurrent calls only touch the connection's own mutex — no contention with other connections. Same FIFO eviction shape as `pkg/functions/quota.Limiter` but with the bucket co-located with its owner. Per-user counters, by contrast, DO live in a hub-keyed map (`userSubs map[string]int`) because the same userID may span multiple connections — that's the natural partition for "across connections" enforcement. When the rate limit fires, fall through to the existing `markOverflow → onOutOfDate` path instead of inventing a new error name; SDKs already resync on overflow so no client surface change is needed. Anonymous (empty userID) connections must bypass the per-user cap entirely so dev-mode + internal tooling that uses `HandleWS` directly stay unaffected — the empty-userID short-circuit is the contract.
- Sub-linear fan-out via key-bucketed routing index (US-306 Hub.subIndex, future tenancy-keyed event routing / org-keyed audit fan-out / ontology-keyed CDC dispatch): replace "iterate every connection × every subscription" with `map[key][]*indexedSub` keyed on the natural partition (objectType, tenant, ontology). Subscribe / unsubscribe / disconnect MUST all maintain the index under the same Hub-level mutex; dispatch snapshots `bucket[:]` under the lock then iterates with the lock released. Lock order: hub.mu → conn.subMu in every mutating handler so HandleObjectChange's bucket lookup never deadlocks against an in-flight subscribe. For composite filters (ObjectSet definitions in our case) collect a SUPERSET of candidate keys via recursive walk and let the precise predicate gate at dispatch time — a false positive costs one wasted match call, a false NEGATIVE drops events silently. Pointer-identity removal (`bucket[i].sub != target`) is allocation-free and unique across the Hub's lifetime; ID-string removal forces every test fixture to stamp unique IDs. Slice in place with `bucket[:0]` + filter-keep + `delete(m, k)` when empty so `len(m[k])` is a clean "anything routed here?" probe.
- cmdk + jsdom test pattern (US-309 CommandPalette, future shadcn/Radix-based components): jsdom does NOT implement `ResizeObserver` or `Element.prototype.scrollIntoView`, both of which cmdk's `Command.Input` calls synchronously on mount (ResizeObserver to track input width, scrollIntoView to scroll the active item into view as selection changes). Without polyfills, every test that mounts a `<Command>` blows up at the effects phase with `ReferenceError: ResizeObserver is not defined` then `TypeError: i.scrollIntoView is not a function` and the entire component tree fails to render. Add no-op stubs ONCE in `web/src/test/setup.ts` (already imported globally by Vitest config). Same polyfill pair applies to any future Radix/Headless-UI/Floating-UI primitive that measures itself on mount.
- React 19 hooks-rules with conditional render (US-309 CommandPalette): when a portal-style component does `if (!open) return null` you cannot legally call `useState` / `useEffect` AFTER the early return, AND ESLint (`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`) will reject any `setState` inside an effect to "reset state when open transitions". The clean fix is the inner-component pattern: outer `Component({open, ...props})` is a thin guard that returns null OR `<ComponentInner {...props}/>`; ALL hooks live in `ComponentInner`, which mounts/unmounts on each open transition so internal state (search query, focus, transient UI) resets naturally without effects. Outer is `<3 lines, pure, no hooks; inner has full freedom. Reusable for any modal/dialog/popover with internal state that should reset on each open.
- Multi-select facet → where clause shape (US-310, future "filter result set by enum-valued field"): the OSv2 `pkg/oss/where` converter has NO `in` operator — `eq`/`and`/`or` only. So same-field multi-select MUST be `{type:"or", value:[{type:"eq",field,value:v1},{type:"eq",field,value:v2}, ...]}`, and cross-field ANDs the per-field disjunctions together (`{type:"and", value:[orForOwner, orForCategory, ...]}`). Empty selections are dropped before composition so a partial state never leaks an empty `or` (which Bleve would reject). Combine with any existing where (FilterBuilder + searchText `containsAnyTerm`) by collecting all clauses into one slice and picking single-entry passthrough vs `and`-wrap based on length — same shape as `whereBuilder.buildWhereClause` but applied at the BrowserPage `useMemo` site. Generalises to any future "checkbox-list-of-values feeds into a Bleve query" surface.
- Auto-deriving facetable fields from ObjectType.properties: walk `objectType.properties` once, keep fields whose `dataType.type` is in {string, boolean, date, datetime, timestamp}, EXCLUDE the primary key (one bucket per row = useless and explodes response size), cap at MAX_FACET_FIELDS=5 so the response stays bounded regardless of schema size. Backend silently returns empty buckets for fields with no data, so over-requesting is safe; under-requesting silently drops a useful facet. Same shape generalises to any UI surface that needs to "pick interesting fields from a heterogeneous schema" — column-mask presets, default-visible-property selection, etc. Note: this client-side heuristic is independent of the backend's `IsSearchable` flag; if a future story wants admin-controlled facet allowlists, plumb a per-property `isFacetable` boolean through to `Property` rather than tightening the UI heuristic.
- Per-user named-state CRUD (US-311 saved searches, future column-visibility presets, dashboard layouts, alert subscriptions): UNIQUE INDEX `(created_by, name)` so different users may pick the same name without colliding; cross-user `Get`/`Update`/`Delete` returns ErrNotFound (NOT 403) so id existence under another user can't be probed; serve admins via the same per-user scope unless the PRD explicitly calls for cross-user visibility — admin override is opt-in, not the default. The wire-form `definition` field is opaque JSONB; the FE owns the schema and the BE round-trips it untouched, so adding new keys (e.g. column visibility) needs zero backend changes. Same dep-direction trick as featureflags / aip / tenants: narrow Store interface in the leaf package, MemoryStore alongside, PG impl in cmd/server. Mounts inside the auth.MiddlewareFull group, gated on `deps.XStore != nil` so degraded-mode (no PG) leaves the routes unmounted and the SPA panel hides itself when the list endpoint 404s.
- react-diff-viewer-continued in vitest+jsdom (US-313, generalises to any third-party React component that pulls in @emotion/react, ResizeObserver, getBoundingClientRect-based measurement, Web Workers): hoist a `vi.mock('react-diff-viewer-continued', () => ({ default: (props) => <pre data-testid="rdv-old">{props.oldValue}</pre>..., DiffMethod: { LINES: 'diffLines' } }))` at the TOP of the test file BEFORE the `import { ObjectDiffPanel }` line — vitest hoists `vi.mock` automatically but the import must be after the mock declaration in the source order so the test's editor / typescript see the mock-shaped module. The mock keeps tests focused on OUR glue (state transitions, version selectors, conditional rendering), production keeps the real lib. Same shape as the @xyflow/react mock in `LogicFlowsPage.test.tsx`. Production opts into `disableWorker={true}` so the worker bundle doesn't have to load in dev/test, and the canonicalise-then-stringify (`JSON.stringify(canonicalize(state), null, 2)`) step is what gives the line-based DiffMethod.LINES "field-level highlighting" — without sorted keys + 2-space indent the same JSON object reorders nondeterministically and every cross-version comparison spuriously diffs every field.
- Saved-view round-trip pattern (US-311 SavedSearchesPanel + BrowserPage): serialise the user-visible filter state (searchText, filters, facets, sort) into a wire envelope at SAVE time, deserialise back into the SAME controlled-state setters at LOAD time. Pure user-state only — derived/server-only values (whereClause, pageTokens, currentPage) are NOT in the envelope; they're recomputed via the existing useMemo + reset on apply. Avoids the "saved view re-injects a stale page token" trap. Apply MUST `setPageTokens([]) + setCurrentPage(1)` so the new filters paginate from page 1; same reset every other filter-change handler does. Frontend hides the panel cleanly on 404/SavedSearchesUnavailable by short-circuiting to `[]` inside the queryFn, so the degraded-mode (no-PG) deployment stays usable.
- Inline-edit "discover the right action" pattern (US-315): inline-edit / inline-delete / inline-link surfaces in OSv2 don't get a generic PATCH endpoint — every mutation has to land in some ActionType. Reusable shape: walk `useActionTypes(ontology)` for an ActionType whose `rules[].type === 'modifyObject'` (or `deleteObject`, `createLink`, ...) targets the current ObjectType AND whose `propertyBindings` cover the field being edited; fall back to read-only when no match exists. Resolve the primary-key parameter via the same precedence as `pkg/actions/rules.go::findPrimaryKey` (`primaryKey` → `<objectType>Id` → `id`). Apply with `{primaryKey, <propParam>: newValue, ...siblingBindings}` — the sibling bindings MUST reuse the WireObject's current values for every other bound property, otherwise the modifyObject rule's `resolveBindings` will blank them out via the missing-param-→-nil branch. Prior art: `BulkActionToolbar.findDeleteAction` (delete) + `findModifyActionForProperty` (modify, US-315). Same trick generalises to inline-link-create, inline-status-toggle, future per-property edit affordances.
- Optimistic-update component shape: small leaf component owns three pieces of state — `editing: boolean` (input vs display mode), `draft: string` (what the user's typing), `optimistic: string | null` (the value to display while the save is in flight). On commit: setOptimistic(draft) BEFORE awaiting the save promise so the display flips instantly. On reject: clear optimistic and surface the error message inline. On parent prop refresh: detect via `if (value !== prevValue)` render-phase check + `setPrevValue(value); setOptimistic(null)` — same render-phase setState pattern progress.txt:109 documents for "reset internal state when a prop changes" without tripping the `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint rule. Generalises to any inline-mutate widget (toggle, dropdown, slider) where the network round-trip should be invisible on the happy path.
- Per-row AbortController cancel for any in-flight async row UI (US-316 upload cancel, future bulk-action cancel, future stream-subscribe cancel): keep the controller as a field on the in-flight item state (`InFlightUpload.controller?: AbortController`) so the cancel handler can locate it via the row id without a parallel `Map<id, controller>`. Detect "cancelled" in the catch branch as `controller.signal.aborted || (err instanceof DOMException && err.name === 'AbortError')` — covers both the XHR-abort path and the signal-already-aborted-at-call edge case. Cancelled rows DISAPPEAR (filter on signal.aborted) rather than convert to error tiles; the user just clicked × so a "failed" tile is noise. After a row finishes (success OR non-abort error) clear `controller: undefined` so UI doesn't keep a stale handle around.
