Tests assert `signal.aborted === true` synchronously after the cancel click — don't rely on the rejected promise (vitest race against React state update); the signal-aborted assertion is deterministic.
- Ontology-scoping a non-ontology-keyed table via JOIN (US-317 action_logs, future audit_logs / lineage_edges / object_history under ontology guards): when the table has no `ontology_rid` column but its parent (e.g. `action_logs.action_type_rid` → `action_types.rid`) does, encode the scope as `JOIN parent ON child.fk = parent.pk WHERE parent.ontology_rid = $1` directly in the store method. Cheaper than a column-add + backfill migration, lets the same SQL serve `ListXxxByOntology` and `GetXxxByOntology` (cross-tenant lookups → ErrNotFound, NOT 403, so id existence under another tenant cannot be probed). Pair with a narrow store interface (Pattern #18) and a setter on the runtime (Executor / OssService / etc.) so degraded-mode test routers leave the hook unset and the handler falls back to empty-page / 404. Generalises to any "this child table inherits its parent's tenancy" surface — same trick will work for `lineage_edges` (via upstream/downstream RID prefix or a JOIN to a parent rid table) and for `object_history` (already keyed by `object_type_rid` which JOINs to `object_types.ontology_rid`).
- Surface "the row id you just wrote" on the response envelope (US-319 actionLogId on SyncApplyActionResponseV2, future "import jobs return jobId on success", "uploaded blob returns mediaRid"): when the write path persists into a side-table the caller will want to address later (revert, drill-down, follow-up action), thread the new row's id through the in-memory result struct and emit it as `<resource>Id` on the response. Cost is three call sites — internal Result struct field (`json:"-"`), wire envelope field (`json:"<resource>Id,omitempty"`), handler that copies one to the other — and zero migrations. omitempty matters: the field is absent when the write was skipped (validate-only, noop, best-effort failure) so SDKs can use presence as a "did the write actually happen?" signal without a separate flag. Don't add a "look up the most recent X for the current user" endpoint to discover the id — the wire is the source of truth for what just happened.
- Minimal in-house toast system pattern (US-319 web/src/stores/toastStore + components/common/Toaster, future generic notifications, future progress-tracking tiles): Zustand store with `Toast{id, message, severity?, actionLabel?, onAction?, ttlMs?}` queue + push/dismiss/clear; React component renders a stacked bottom-right region with per-tile auto-dismiss (default 5000ms, ttlMs=0 disables). Mount once in Shell.tsx so every page can `useToastStore.getState().push(...)` without provider plumbing. Inline action-button click does NOT auto-dismiss — caller pushes follow-up tile on completion (test pins this contract so a future "click ⇒ auto-dismiss" change fails). Beats sonner/react-hot-toast/radix-toast when the requirement is just "tile + optional action + timer" — fewer deps, full control over lifecycle, consumers can extend Toast{} with one optional field instead of fighting third-party hook semantics. Pair with the optional-action-button shape: any feature that needs "show notification with one inline action" (Undo, Retry, Open job page, Download result) reuses the same `pushToast({...actionLabel, onAction})` API.
- Per-user-private + optionally-shareable resource (US-320 action templates, future bookmarks / pinned dashboards / favourite searches): one `shared BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE` column on the existing per-owner table is enough. List/Get widen READ access via `WHERE created_by = $caller OR shared = TRUE`; Update/Delete remain `WHERE created_by = $owner` so `shared` never grants write access. Non-owners always see 404 on private rows (id leak protection); they see the shared row but mutating endpoints still 404 for them — no separate 403 path. Per-owner uniqueness keyed by `(created_by, scope_id, name)` so the same name can be reused across scopes (different ActionTypes, different ObjectTypes, etc.). The wire envelope carries `shared` as a plain boolean and `createdBy` as the visible owner so the SPA can render an "by alice" hint on rows the caller doesn't own. Tri-state pointer field on Update DTO (`Shared *bool`) so partial updates can preserve / set / clear independently. Pattern generalises any time the PRD says "用户私有 + 可分享" / "private with optional sharing".
- Reading optional auth context inside a deeply-mounted page component: prefer `useContext(AuthContext)` directly with a `?.user?.id` chain over `useAuth()` (which throws "must be used within an AuthProvider"). The hook is right for guards / route gates that legitimately can't render without an authenticated user; a page component that wants caller identity for cosmetic purposes (per-row delete affordance, "by alice" hint) should NOT force every test mounting it to grow an AuthProvider wrapper. The render-stable `?.user?.id` chain produces `undefined` when no provider is present, which is the right default for "no caller-specific affordances visible".
- Native HTML5 drag-and-drop in vitest+jsdom (US-326 PivotTable, future kanban / list-reorder / drop-target surfaces): jsdom does NOT instantiate `DataTransfer`, so the drag payload round-trip via `e.dataTransfer.setData(MIME, JSON)` / `.getData(MIME)` returns empty in tests. Supply a tiny stub: `{ setData(k,v): map.set(k,v); getData(k): map.get(k); types: []; effectAllowed: ''; dropEffect: '' }`, hand the SAME object to every `fireEvent.dragStart / dragOver / drop` for one drag gesture so the data survives the transition, and bump `dataTransfer.types = ['<MIME>']` BETWEEN dragStart and dragOver so the drop-target's `types.includes(MIME)` acceptance check fires (otherwise `dragOver` doesn't `preventDefault()` and `drop` is silently ignored). One helper (`dragField(source, target, dt)`) keeps the test DSL flat. Generalises to any feature that needs cross-zone drag without pulling in react-dnd / dnd-kit (~80KB and React-19-compat headaches both bring).
- Cross-tab pivot aggregation: compute row × column cells AND the three total axes (rowTotals, colTotals, grandTotal) by independently aggregating the source rows for each scope — DON'T sum the cell values. sum-of-sums works for `count`/`sum` but `avg`/`min`/`max` are not associative across nested groupings (avg-of-avgs is wrong, min-of-min works only because Math.min is associative — but if the nested cell is null because no rows fell in it, the min skips it where the row total should not). Single source of truth: every aggregate is `aggregate(filteredRows, valueSpec)` over the relevant subset of `data`, not derived from neighbouring cells. ~30 LOC — same shape works for any future bucketed-summary surface where the metric isn't fold-associative. PRD 'react-pivottable' spec was implemented inline via native HTML5 DnD because the lib pulls in react-dnd which only ships React-15/16 batched-update shims (incompatible with React 19). Same anti-dep pattern as US-324 Gantt + US-325 Sankey.
- Route-wrapper pattern for prop-driven pages that need react-router hooks (US-329 dashboards, future shareable saved-searches / objectset-snapshot pages): keep the page component prop-driven (`{id?: string; onSaved?: (id) => void}`) so unit tests can `render(<Page />)` without a `MemoryRouter` wrapper, and put a tiny adapter in App.tsx (e.g. `DashboardEditorRoute = () => { const params = useParams(); const nav = useNavigate(); return <DashboardEditorPage key={params.id ?? '__new__'} id={params.id} onSaved={(id) => nav(\`/dashboards/${id}\`)} /> }`). The `key={id ?? '__new__'}` is load-bearing — without it, react-router DOESN'T remount on `/dashboards/a` → `/dashboards/b` so widget state from dashboard A leaks into dashboard B's view until the next user-driven setState. This decouples 19 prior dashboard tests from any router scaffolding and makes future shareable-resource pages free of MSW-vs-MemoryRouter test pickle.
- `vi.hoisted` + `vi.mock` for adding network calls to a previously-pure component without breaking existing tests (US-329 DashboardEditorPage adding listDashboards/createDashboard/getDashboard): `const apiMocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({ listDashboards: vi.fn(), ... }))` evaluates the factory in vitest's pre-import phase so the mock is registered BEFORE the component imports it. `beforeEach` resets each fn and installs default impls (`listDashboards.mockResolvedValue({dashboards: []})`) so the existing tests that don't care about persistence stay green silently. Per-test overrides (`apiMocks.createDashboard.mockResolvedValue({...})`) exercise the new save path. Beats MSW for unit-level API mocking when the component only calls one or two endpoints — no service worker, no fetch handler registration, just typed vi.fn() over the module boundary.
- Public-share read primitive on a per-user resource (US-329 dashboards, future shareable snapshots / pivot configs): one `is_public BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE` column on the existing per-owner table is enough. Get gate is `row.CreatedBy == createdBy || row.IsPublic`. Update/Delete and List stay strictly `WHERE created_by = $owner` so non-owners can never mutate even on public rows. Get returns ErrNotFound for both "missing" and "private + non-owner" so a leaked id teaches the recipient nothing. PG impl: `getRaw(ctx, id)` is owner-agnostic; the public/private gate happens in Go where it's testable. Beats per-row ACL tables when the surface is just "anyone with the link can VIEW" — those are only worth it once you need scoped sharing (specific users / groups / roles). Compare to US-320 `shared BOOLEAN` which adds public read AND public LIST visibility; US-329 keeps List owner-scoped because share links convey the id explicitly, no need to broadcast public dashboards in everyone's index.
- Foundry V2 `loadObjectSet` requires a non-empty `select` array (US-330 ObjectSet Diff). The handler at pkg/oss/objectset/handler.go:176 returns `SelectRequired` 400 for `len(req.Select) == 0` — the empty case is a deliberate guard, not a permissive default. Any new client-side flow that needs "all properties" must round-trip through `getObjectType(ontology, root)` first to enumerate `Object.keys(objectType.properties ?? {})`. Don't shortcut by sending `select: []`. The hooks-driven `useObjectType(...)` is wrong for click-handler flows (forces render-time async wiring); a plain `async` handler that does sequential `getObjectType` then parallel `Promise.all([loadObjectSet, loadObjectSet])` is ~10 LOC and trivially testable. Same shape applies to ANY future endpoint that wants to compose two ObjectSet reads at the same property shape (diff, intersect-preview, A/B test, drift-monitor).
- PK-string normalization for any cross-set membership check (US-330 diffObjectSets, future setops UI / drift detection / dedup): `__primaryKey` is typed `string | number` per WireObject, and the same row can round-trip through different code paths returning either type. Always coerce with `String(row.__primaryKey)` at the bucket key. Otherwise the same row diffed across two sets that returned `1` vs `"1"` shows as both onlyInA AND onlyInB simultaneously. The envelope keys `__rid` / `__primaryKey` / `__apiName` MUST be excluded from property comparison — they're identity / metadata, not value. Pure recursive `deepEqual` for object/array property values catches structural-equal-but-reference-different cases (`{tags: ['x','y']}` vs `{tags: ['x','y']}`) that `===` would miss.
- localStorage-backed pickers in vitest are seeded directly, not via hooks: `window.localStorage.setItem(localStorageKey(ontology), JSON.stringify(items))` in `beforeEach` + `clear()` in `afterEach`. The `useSavedObjectSets` hook reads on mount via the same key, so seeding the storage IS the input — no need to mock the hook itself. Mirrors how `objectSetBuilder.localStorageKey(ontology)` already namespaces by ontology so cross-test isolation is free if you `clear()` between tests. `within(section).queryByText(...)` is the right scoped negative-assertion shape when distinguishing buckets where the same string can appear in multiple `data-testid` regions (e.g. count "1" vs PK "1") — global `getByText` finds multiple matches and fails opaquely.
- Shareable URL state for any state-bearing page (US-331 ObjectSet `?def=`, future saved searches / dashboard layouts / pivot configs): encode as base64url JSON in a single query param via `btoa` → `replace(/\+/g,'-').replace(/\//g,'_').replace(/=+$/,'')` (no `+/=` chars survive — URL-safe everywhere). Closed-enum guard on the decode path (`KNOWN_TYPES.has(parsed.type)`) is the boundary — decoder returns `null` for malformed base64 / non-JSON / unknown discriminant so a tampered URL falls back to the default state, not a runtime crash in downstream switch dispatch. State restoration uses the **lazy `useState(() => readFromUrl() ?? default)` initializer pattern** — NOT a `useEffect` + setState, which would trip the `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint rule (progress.txt:110) AND force a double render. Auto-execute on URL-restore needs a separate seed for the executeKey-style refetch trigger (e.g. `useState(() => readFromUrl() ? 1 : 0)`) so the first render dispatches the data fetch without the user clicking Execute. Write back via `window.history.replaceState(state, '', `${pathname}?${params}${hash}`)` so existing hash state (e.g. the `#ref=<temp rid>` share mechanism) survives. Tests that exercise URL-restore MUST `window.history.replaceState({}, '', '/?<param>=...')` BEFORE `render(...)` and reset to `/` in `beforeEach` — `MemoryRouter` keeps its own in-memory history but the page reads `window.location.search`, so seeding the URL via the router's `initialEntries` does NOT propagate.
- SheetJS-driven multi-sheet Excel export (US-333, future bulk export / report generators): use `xlsx@0.18.5` (the canonical npm-published SheetJS — newer 0.20.x is CDN-only and breaks `npm install`). Build the Data sheet via `XLSX.utils.aoa_to_sheet(matrix)` where `matrix` is a uniform `(string|number|boolean)[][]` (header row + one row per record, columns padded with `''` for null/undefined and `JSON.stringify(v)` for object/array cells) — `json_to_sheet` re-derives headers from object keys and silently blanks missing cells, which is the wrong default for typed schemas. Append additional sheets with `XLSX.utils.book_append_sheet(wb, sheet, name)` — it mutates BOTH `wb.Sheets[name]` AND pushes onto `wb.SheetNames` (assert ORDER on `SheetNames`, CONTENT on `Sheets[name]`). Emit via `XLSX.write(wb, { type: 'array', bookType: 'xlsx' })` → wrap in `new Blob([buf], { type: 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet' })` → reuse the standard anchor-based download trigger. For "Summary aggregation alongside raw rows": column-wise stats (one row per data column, columns are `count|nonNull|distinct|min|max|sum|avg`) — beats row-wise for wide tables; numeric stats only filled when `objectType.properties[col].dataType.type` ∈ `{integer,long,short,byte,double,float,decimal}` and the value is `Number.isFinite`. `distinct` runs over a `Set<unknown>` with object cells JSON-stringified before adding so structural equality collapses correctly. Round-trip in tests via `XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(sheet, { header: 1 })` to AOA. Reusable surface: `buildXlsxWorkbook(rows, columns, objectType)` + `computeAggregationSheet(rows, columns, objectType)` exported from `web/src/lib/exportObjects.ts`.
- Adding a new query method to a wide repo interface? Don't. Put it on the concrete `*PG<X>Repository` struct directly. `auth.UserRepository` is referenced by ~10 in-memory stubs (refresh / oidc / saml / role-resolver / mfa / api-key tests) — every method added there forces every stub to grow a no-op. Adapters that need the new method type-assert to the concrete type (`pgUser, _ := deps.UserRepo.(*auth.PGUserRepository)`); production hits the assertion, contract / degraded-mode test routers leave nil and the dependent feature degrades gracefully. Same pattern as `auth.UserRoleRevoker` (US-251), `oms.MediaAssetStore` (US-203), `MarkingGrantAdminRepository` (US-259), and now `auth.PGUserRepository.SearchUsers` / `LookupUserByEmailForMention` (US-336).
- Browser-side regex that mirrors a backend extractor (mention emails, citation tokens, slash-command syntax): keep BOTH copies of the regex in sync — one in `pkg/<feature>/extract.go`, one in the React component that highlights or autocompletes the token. If they drift, the SPA highlights things the backend doesn't act on (silent UX bug). Drop a one-line "keep in sync with X" comment on each side so PR reviewers catch the drift; the only durable single-source-of-truth alternative is to ship the regex via the SDK / build step, which costs more than the comment is worth at the current scale.
- Textarea `@`-trigger autocomplete (US-336 mentions, future slash-commands or emoji pickers): single-pass `(?:^|\s)<trigger>([\S]*)$` regex on `value.slice(0, caret)`. Watch BOTH `onChange` (text edits) AND `onSelect` (caret-only moves) so cursor moves into a prior `<trigger>word` re-open the dropdown. Suggestion rows use `onMouseDown` + `e.preventDefault()` (NOT `onClick`) — onBlur fires before onClick so the dropdown unmounts and clicks silently fail; mouseDown fires before blur. Pair with a 100ms onBlur close-defer as belt-and-braces. Empty query right after the trigger should NOT fire the search — wait until the user types one character so the dropdown stays narrow and we don't burn a roundtrip.
- New cross-feature notification surfaces (US-336 mention, future watch / approval / system) reuse `oms.Repository.CreateNotification` directly — no new tables, no new shape. `Type` is the dispatch key the SPA's NotificationCenter switches on; `Link` is a top-level URL like `/<surface>?<query>` (`/mentions?rid=<targetRid>&commentId=<id>`) NOT an ontology-scoped path because the notifier rarely knows the ontology API name from a bare RID. The SPA's notification-click router resolves the deep link to the right page. New surface checklist: (1) define a narrow `<Surface>Notifier` interface in the feature package, (2) cmd/server adapter calls `oms.Repository.CreateNotification` with the right Type tag + deep link, (3) wire through `ServerDeps` so degraded-mode test routers leave it nil and the feature silently no-ops.
- Notification deep-link receiver page (US-340 /mentions, future /watches / /approvals-inbox / similar): when a notifier stamps `Link = /<surface>?...` (per the previous pattern), build a matching SPA route that reads the query params, fetches the underlying entity, and renders it in context. Inbox + thread split is the right v1 layout — the inbox column lists the caller's notifications of that type so they can hop between unresolved items, the thread column renders the focused entity (re-using existing components like `CommentsTab`). Optional `?id=<notificationId>` auto-marks-read on landing so the bell badge clears without a second click. Pair with: (1) the targeted-id receiver passes the entity id through to the renderer (e.g. `<CommentsTab highlightCommentId={...} />`), (2) renderer scrolls the matching row into view + applies a ring-glow class with `data-highlight=true` for testability, (3) jsdom-safe scroll: guard `typeof el.scrollIntoView === 'function'` before calling — vitest's jsdom doesn't implement it (also documented in pattern #199 for chat / log feeds). The notifier-side `Link` stays a constant string the backend can always emit; the receiver page absorbs all the route-resolution complexity.
- NotificationCenter type-aware visual treatment (US-340): when adding a new notification `type` (mention / watch / approval / system / ...), surface the type tag with a small badge component rendered next to the title, and propagate the type onto the row via `data-type={notification.type}` so RTL tests can assert visual differentiation without screenshot diffs. Single switch in `renderTypeBadge(type string)` returns the per-type glyph (`@` for mention, future `◉` watch / `✓` approval / etc.); unknown types render no badge so the pre-existing automation-alert layout stays unchanged. Pair with a click-through link that the backend sets on the notification row — the badge is purely decorative; the deep link is what makes "click jumps to context" work.
- Rendering untrusted user-authored markdown in the SPA (US-341 comments, future PR descriptions / wiki / chat): use `react-markdown` (already pulled transitively via `@uiw/react-md-editor` — declare it in `web/package.json` so the dep is explicit) with NO `rehype-raw` plugin. The default config is the security posture: raw HTML in source is escaped to text rather than rendered as DOM, and `defaultUrlTransform` strips `javascript:` from link/image URLs. Adding `rehype-sanitize` is only needed if you opt INTO `rehype-raw` for some reason — DO NOT add `rehype-raw` for "richer" rendering, that's how XSS sneaks in. Always override the `a` component to stamp `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"` (otherwise linked pages can `window.opener.location = …` or leak referrer). For inline-text decorations (mention badges, citation tokens, etc.) walk the React node tree post-render with a `cloneElement`-based recursive helper that splits string leaves only — react-markdown's `components` prop maps HTML tag names, there is no `text` slot, and pre-processing the source (e.g. `[@x](#mention:x)`) interferes with bare-text inputs. **Skip `remark-gfm`** for any content containing `@email@domain.com` mentions: GFM's autolink-literal extension turns bare emails into mailto links, fragmenting the mention regex's input across two text nodes. CommonMark already covers fenced code blocks; tables/strikethrough/task-lists are rarely needed in comment surfaces. Prior art: `web/src/components/browser/CommentBody.tsx`.
- Global keyboard shortcut registry (US-348, future US-349 help panel / per-page shortcuts): single source of truth in `web/src/hotkeys/registry.ts` — typed `HotkeyId` union + `HOTKEYS` array (id / keys / i18nKey / group). One `useShortcut(id, handler, { enabled? })` call per binding keeps the rules-of-hooks invariant trivial; a parent registers N shortcuts by writing N call sites, never a `Partial<Record<HotkeyId, () => void>>` map looped over inside a hook. Two react-hotkeys-hook v5 traps to bake into any future shortcut hook: (1) the effect deps strip `enabled` / `preventDefault` / `ignoreEventWhen` before comparing, so toggling `options.enabled` after mount does NOT re-subscribe — gate enabled INSIDE the callback closure (and put it in the `dependencies` array so the callback ref refreshes), letting useHotkeys subscribe permanently and the closure decide; (2) jsdom keyboard events MUST carry `code: 'KeyX'` (e.g. `code: 'KeyK'` for `meta+k`) — the library's keydown handler short-circuits when `a.code` is undefined, so a bare `fireEvent.keyDown(document, { key: 'k', metaKey: true })` silently never fires. Sequences use `>` (`g>d`) and a single string can't mix `+` and `>` (library logs and skips). Keep i18n dynamic via `t(def.i18nKey)` and accept the `UNUSED` flag from `extract-i18n.mjs` — the audit is informational, not fatal, and the keys ARE statically defined in zh-CN/en.
- Dual-layer ErrorBoundary pattern (US-352, future SPA-wide guarded surfaces): `react-error-boundary` ships ONE `<ErrorBoundary>` primitive — wire two instances. (1) **GlobalErrorBoundary OUTSIDE the provider tree** (in App.tsx wrapping QueryClientProvider/Router/AuthProvider). Its fallback MUST avoid any hook depending on those providers (no `useTranslation` / `useQueryClient` / `useAuth` / `useNavigate`) — a provider crash means those hooks throw too and the outer boundary has nothing to render. Hardcode bilingual strings ("应用发生错误 / Something went wrong"). (2) **RouteErrorBoundary INSIDE Shell** wrapping `<Outlet />`. Shell stays usable so the user can navigate away; fallback uses `useTranslation()` (i18n is provider-tree-internal, guaranteed available here). Pass `resetKeys={[location.pathname]}` so route changes auto-reset the boundary — without it, navigating away from a crashed page leaves the user stuck on the fallback until they hit Retry. `react-error-boundary@6` widened the `onError(error, info)` first param from `Error` to `unknown` (TS2322 if you keep v5's signature); transparently forward `unknown` to the reporter and let the reporter coerce via `error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error))`. Reporter must NEVER throw upstream — wrap custom reporter calls in `try {} catch {}` and `.catch(() => {})` around fetch/sendBeacon, or you risk a re-entrant boundary catch loop. `navigator.sendBeacon` (with `fetch({ keepalive: true })` jsdom fallback) is the right primitive for fire-and-forget client error POSTs because it survives unload. Prior art: `web/src/components/common/ErrorBoundary.tsx` + `web/src/lib/errorReporter.ts`.

- `pkg/oms/computed_property_test.go` covers `ComputedAggregation.Validate`, `ComputedProperty.CacheTTL`, `ComputedProperty.Validate`.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When adding a brand-new resource type with its own table, DON'T add CRUD methods to the main `oms.Repository` interface unless you're willing to stub them in ~15 mock files (every pkg/{oms,oss,links,actions,index,automate,ai} and test/{northwind,chinook,e2e,fixtures,integration} has at least one inMemoryOmsRepo / mockRepo / mockOmsRepo / stubRehydrateRepo that needs updating). Instead add a narrow interface in the same package and have `*PGRepository` satisfy it implicitly.
  - Injecting a clock via `SetNowFunc(func() time.Time)` is the simplest way to test TTL-cache behaviour deterministically. The convention here mirrors `oms.CachedRepository.nowFunc`.
  - Bleve `DocIDQuery` on per-link target ObjectType still needs `Size = len(targets)` to avoid silent truncation (same learning US-201 called out).
  - `coerceNumeric` is duplicated between `pkg/oss/objectset/executor.go` and now `pkg/oss/computed/resolver.go`. When a third caller appears, hoist it to `pkg/oss/internal/numeric`.
  - The PRD phrase "_computed_at 时戳" is best satisfied by a `Value{Value, ComputedAt}` pair at the resolver layer — downstream HTTP handlers can then decide whether to stamp it on each property or as a sibling map. This keeps the resolver API stable even if the wire format evolves.
  - JSONB round-tripping of structs in pgx uses `[]byte` staging (`var aggJSON []byte` → `json.Unmarshal`). Don't try to pass the struct directly; pgx won't know how to marshal it.
  - Default TTL handling is done in two places (model `CacheTTL()` for the resolver cache path, and repo writes for the column default). Keeping them in sync: the model exposes `DefaultComputedPropertyCacheTTL` as the single source of truth.

## 2026-04-18 - US-203 Media Properties 存储层
- Added `media` as BaseType #22 (`types.Media = "media"`), updated the allBaseTypes map, basetype_test count, and SDK typemap for ts/python/go. Coerce/Validate's default branches handle it as opaque string (media RID).
- Migration `000034_media_assets` creates the new table with the PRD-mandated columns (rid, realm, filename, mime, size_bytes, sha256, path, created_by, created_at), plus a `(realm, sha256)` index for dedup lookups and a `created_by` index for per-user listing.
- New package `pkg/media` with `Store` (content-addressed FS blob store):
  - Layout: `<root>/<realm>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<sha256>` — root is injected by the caller (typically `data/media`) so the PRD path is recovered when WEAVE_DATA_DIR=data.
  - `Put` streams the reader through an `io.MultiWriter(tempFile, sha256.Hasher)` in one pass (no double read of the upload body), then does the dedup check under a single mutex: if the content-addressed path already exists it drops the temp file and reuses the existing blob; otherwise it `os.Rename`s the temp into place atomically.
  - Every Put returns a fresh RID (`ri.media.main.asset.<uuid>`). Dedup happens at the filesystem layer, not at the row layer — the catalog row is the refcount.
  - `Open`/`DeletePath`/`Exists` resolve relPath through a shared guard that cleans the path and verifies the resolved absolute location still lives under root, so a malicious `../etc/passwd` input never hits the filesystem.
  - Clock is injectable via `SetNowFunc` so the yyyy/mm partition is deterministic in tests.
- `pkg/oms.MediaAsset` + `MediaAssetStore` (narrow 5-method interface: Create/Get/Delete/CountBySHA256/ListByCreatedBy) kept OUT of `oms.Repository` — same reasoning as US-202's ComputedPropertyStore, so the ~15 mock repos don't need stubs. `*PGRepository` satisfies it implicitly in `pg_repository_media.go`.
- Tests (13 unit tests in `pkg/media/media_test.go`): content-addressed path shape, identical-bytes dedup (shared path, distinct RIDs, single physical file), different-bytes distinct paths, per-realm isolation (same hash, different paths), invalid realms rejected (path traversal / separators), default MIME, year/month partitioning, Open/DeletePath/Exists happy path + ErrNotFound twice, path-traversal rejection on Open, RID uniqueness + prefix, 16-way concurrent dedup (all 16 get distinct RIDs but exactly one file lands on disk), empty-bytes upload (size=0, canonical sha256). Plus `media_asset_test.go` covers Validate for missing rid/realm/sha256/path and negative size.
- Files changed:
  - `migrations/000034_media_assets.up.sql` (new)
  - `migrations/000034_media_assets.down.sql` (new)
  - `pkg/types/basetype.go` (Media base type, count bumped to 22)
  - `pkg/types/basetype_test.go` (count + slice)
  - `pkg/sdkgen/typemap.go` (Media → string/str/string)
  - `pkg/media/media.go` (new — Store, PutOptions, Asset, path guard)
  - `pkg/media/media_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/oms/media_asset.go` (new — MediaAsset, MediaAssetStore interface)
  - `pkg/oms/media_asset_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/oms/pg_repository_media.go` (new — PGRepository CRUD + CountBySHA256 + ListByCreatedBy)
  - `prd.json` (US-203 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Content-addressed dedup is cheapest done at Put time: hash + write in the same io.Copy (via MultiWriter), then compare-and-swap under a mutex. Do NOT scan the temp file back to rehash after the fact — that doubles I/O and races with concurrent uploads.
  - Always guard relPath → absolute resolution through `filepath.Clean` + `strings.HasPrefix(absResolved, rootAbs+sep)` before opening files. This is the single choke point that prevents `..` and absolute paths from escaping the storage root; duplicate it nowhere, factor it into `resolvePath`.
  - When adding a new BaseType, three places always drift out of sync: (1) `allBaseTypes` map in `pkg/types/basetype.go`, (2) the fixed-length slice in `TestBaseType_AllDefined`, and (3) the three per-language maps in `pkg/sdkgen/typemap.go`. `Coerce`/`Validate` fall through to a sane default so most new BaseTypes don't need code in those files.
  - `Media` is the storage-layer base type (property value = media RID). `MediaReference` is the wire-format base type (property value = Foundry MediaReference object pointing at a mediaSet). They are distinct and both exist: the first keeps ownership of bytes; the second is purely a reference format. Don't collapse them.
  - For new storage-backed packages, the simple-mutex-on-write pattern (`s.mu.Lock()` around the `os.Stat` / `os.MkdirAll` / `os.Rename` sequence) is sufficient for single-machine deployments. Bleve's index and pkg/attachment use the same idiom.

## 2026-04-18 - US-204 Media 上传 API
- Added `pkg/media/handlers.go` (`Handler` struct + `RegisterRoutes`) exposing the three Foundry-style media endpoints:
  - `POST /api/v2/media` — multipart/form-data with required `file` part and optional `realm` form value. Wraps `r.Body` in `http.MaxBytesReader` at `DefaultMaxUploadBytes` (10 MiB) BEFORE calling `ParseMultipartForm`; `errors.As(err, &maxErr)` distinguishes the 10MB cap (returns `MediaUploadTooLarge` 400) from generic multipart parse failure (`InvalidMultipart` 400). On success the bytes are streamed through `Store.Put` (which content-addresses + dedups them) and a row lands in `MediaAssetStore`.
  - `GET /api/v2/media/{rid}` — looks up the row, opens the blob through the path-traversal-guarded `Store.Open`, then writes `Content-Type` + `Content-Length` + `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="..."; filename*=UTF-8''<percent-encoded>` so browsers across vintages recover the original filename verbatim.
  - `DELETE /api/v2/media/{rid}` — fetches the row first (so we still know `(realm, sha256)` after the row is gone), deletes the catalog row, then calls `CountBySHA256`. Only when the count is zero does it call `Store.DeletePath` to reclaim the physical file. Dedup-safe: deleting one of two rows that share a sha256 leaves the blob in place for the survivor.
- `Handler.SetMaxUploadBytes(n int64)` overrides the cap (used by the too-large test to keep allocations small); `n <= 0` is silently ignored so callers can't accidentally disable it.
- `auth.UserFromContext(r.Context()).ID` populates `MediaAsset.CreatedBy` when present; in dev/no-auth mode it stays empty.
- Wired into `cmd/server/main.go`:
  - New `ServerDeps.MediaStore *media.Store` and `ServerDeps.MediaCatalog oms.MediaAssetStore` fields.
  - `deps.MediaStore = media.NewStore(cfg.DataDir + "/media")` next to the attachment store init (always wired — the FS root survives degraded mode).
  - `deps.MediaCatalog = pgRepo` (the bare `*PGRepository`, captured BEFORE wrapping with `oms.NewCachedRepository` — the metadata cache decorator does not wrap MediaAssetStore methods).
  - Inside the auth-protected route group, mounted next to attachments, gated on `deps.MediaStore != nil && deps.MediaCatalog != nil` so degraded-mode test routers silently skip registration.
- Tests (11 cases in `pkg/media/handlers_test.go`):
  - Upload happy path: rid prefix, filename / size / mime / default realm "main", catalog row matches, blob present on disk.
  - Custom realm via form field; invalid realm (`"../escape"`) rejected as 400.
  - Missing `file` field → 400 `MissingFile`.
  - Too-large body (cap shrunk to 64 bytes) → 400 `MediaUploadTooLarge`.
  - `DefaultMaxUploadBytes` is exactly 10 MiB.
  - Download happy path: bytes round-trip, `Content-Type` matches, `Content-Disposition` carries `attachment` + filename.
  - Download / delete on unknown rid → 404 `MediaAssetNotFound`.
  - Delete-last-reference: blob reclaimed from disk after row is the final reference.
  - Delete-deduped-blob-kept: two uploads of identical bytes share the path; deleting one leaves the file; deleting the second reclaims it.
- An in-memory `memCatalog` satisfies `oms.MediaAssetStore` for the handler tests so PostgreSQL is not required (continues the US-202/US-203 narrow-interface pattern).
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/media/handlers.go` (new)
  - `pkg/media/handlers_test.go` (new)
  - `cmd/server/main.go` (import `pkg/media`, ServerDeps additions, init in main(), conditional route registration)
  - `prd.json` (US-204 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - `http.MaxBytesReader` wraps the WHOLE request body — multipart boundaries + form fields count against the cap. If you need exact per-file enforcement, set the limit slightly above the per-file budget OR check `header.Size` after `FormFile` and reject early.
  - `*http.MaxBytesError` is the typed error to look for via `errors.As`; checking `err == io.EOF` or string matching is fragile because Go wraps the error differently across multipart parse vs. body read paths. Both Upload paths (the ParseMultipartForm call AND the streaming Put when the part exceeds the budget) need the same `errors.As` check.
  - When you fetch a row to compute "does the underlying blob still have references after delete", do the GET BEFORE the DELETE — once the row is gone the (realm, sha256) tuple is unrecoverable. The handler order is: Get → Delete row → CountBySHA256 → maybe DeletePath.
  - `oms.CachedRepository` only wraps the metadata `Repository` interface. New narrow stores added on `*PGRepository` (MediaAssetStore, ComputedPropertyStore, etc.) bypass the cache — capture the bare `pgRepo` reference in main.go BEFORE wrapping if you need to hand it to a non-Repository dep.
  - For the multipart test fixture, the exact `Content-Disposition` shape that go-chi/Go's mime/multipart parses correctly is `form-data; name="file"; filename="x.txt"` — `WriteField` won't set per-part headers, so use `mw.CreatePart` with an explicit textproto.MIMEHeader-like map.

Anything that needs multipart OR upload progress MUST bypass it and either use `fetch()` directly (if progress isn't needed) or `XMLHttpRequest` (if it is). Fetch has no upload-progress event in the platform spec — don't add one via polyfill; just use XHR.
  - `useAuthStore.getState().accessToken` is the imperative escape hatch when you can't route through `authedFetch`. The refresh-token interceptor logic is NOT available outside `authedFetch`, so you lose the auto-retry on 401 — acceptable for one-shot uploads but worth noting.
  - `react-dropzone` v15 works under jsdom with two caveats: (1) `DataTransfer` doesn't exist, so drop via `fireEvent.change(input)` + `Object.defineProperty(input, 'files', {...})`; (2) the component internally does `setState` in a microtask, so test asserts on state changes need `await act(async () => { ... })` not just `act(() => ...)`. Without the async wrapper you race past the dropzone's internal dispatch and the spy never sees the File.
  - The backend media API returns the `MediaAsset` row verbatim (pkg/oms.MediaAsset JSON tags). Keeping the TS interface byte-for-byte matched keeps upload → display a one-hop transform; no normalization layer needed.
  - `dev-browser` skill isn't registered in this harness; the PRD "verify in browser" line is covered by the unit/integration tests here + manual QA. Flag this in the PR so reviewers run the dev server once (`make dev`) and confirm drag-and-drop against a Media-typed property.
  - When an acceptance-test mutation hook in `useUploadMedia` throws, React Query marks the mutation as `isError` — but since the component also tracks per-file state in `uploads[]`, the "summary" mutation error is de-duplicated (shown only once all in-flight uploads settled). Don't rely on `mutation.error` alone in tests; assert on the component's own `upload-list` when driving multiple concurrent uploads.

## 2026-04-18 - US-206 Union Types 支持
- Added `Union` as BaseType #23 (`types.Union = "union"`); bumped `allBaseTypes` + `TestBaseType_AllDefined` count to 23. Also exported two well-known keys: `UnionDiscriminatorKey = "__type"` and `UnionValueKey = "value"` so downstream serializers agree on the wire shape.
- Extended `DataType` with `Variants []DataType` (JSON `variants`, `omitempty`). No new DB column — `Property.TypeConfig` is already JSONB, so `{"variants": [...]}` rides along with existing persistence. Schema round-trips via the existing `DataTypeJSON` path.
- Validate: new `validateUnion` branch. If the value is a map carrying `__type`, it is routed directly to the named variant (error if no variant matches that discriminator). Otherwise variants are tried in declared order; first match wins. Empty variants list is an error. Nullable honors `nullable` at the dispatcher level.
- Coerce: new `coerceUnion` branch. If input is tagged, the inner value is coerced against that variant only. Untagged input is attempted against each variant in declared order — Coerce + Validate must both succeed — and the first success is wrapped as `{"__type": "<variant>", "value": <coerced>}`. Nil input passes through unchanged.
- Added `unwrapUnionValue` shared by Validate/Coerce. Supports both wire shapes: the universal wrapper `{__type, value}` (exactly 2 keys → scalar-style unwrap) and the flattened tagged-struct shape `{__type, ...structFields}` (any other key count → struct-style, strip `__type` and pass the rest through).
- sdkgen/typemap.go: Union → `unknown` (ts), `Any` (python), `interface{}` (go) — the one escape hatch for generated types when the concrete variant is not known at codegen time.
- 15 new unit tests in `pkg/types/union_test.go`: BaseType included + wire value, schema JSON round-trip with Variants, validate-first-variant, validate-later-variant, no-variant-match, empty-variants, nil+nullable, discriminator routes to struct variant, discriminator-unknown-variant, discriminator-mismatched-inner-value, wrapped-value-matches, coerce-first-variant-wins, coerce-falls-through-on-first-failure, coerce-honors-hint (coerces 42 → "42" under `__type=string`), empty-variants coerce error, nil pass-through.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/types/basetype.go` (Union constant, allBaseTypes entry, UnionDiscriminatorKey/UnionValueKey exports, Variants field on DataType)
  - `pkg/types/basetype_test.go` (bumped count to 23, added Union to slice)
  - `pkg/types/validate.go` (Union branch + validateUnion + unwrapUnionValue)
  - `pkg/types/coerce.go` (Union branch + coerceUnion + wrapUnionValue helper)
  - `pkg/types/union_test.go` (new, 15 tests)
  - `pkg/sdkgen/typemap.go` (Union entries for ts/python/go)
  - `prd.json` (US-206 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - `DataType` was designed to be extensible via JSON fields (SubType, Fields, Precision, Scale, now Variants). Adding a new parameterized type only needs: (1) a new BaseType constant + allBaseTypes entry, (2) a new `json:"xxx,omitempty"` field on DataType, (3) branches in Coerce + Validate, (4) sdkgen typemap — NO migration required, because `Property.TypeConfig` is JSONB and `DataTypeJSON` already merges unknown keys through.
  - The `{__type, value}` wrapper is the cleanest universal shape for tagged unions because it works for both scalars and structs. The flattened form `{__type, ...fields}` still gets recognized (via the "any key count other than exactly 2" heuristic in `unwrapUnionValue`) so callers that want idiomatic tagged-struct JSON don't need to wrap into a nested `value`. Both are supported on read; write path produces the wrapper form for consistency.
  - When Coerce tries each variant, both Coerce AND Validate must succeed for the variant to be accepted. Coerce alone is too lenient for `Union[string, integer]` — `coerceString(42)` succeeds via `fmt.Sprintf`, which would mean integer input always lands in the first variant if it's string. The Validate pass after Coerce is what makes the "try-in-order" semantic meaningful.
  - Ordering matters: put MORE-specific variants first. For `Union[Integer, String]`, `"42"` coerces to Integer; `"hello"` falls through to String. Reversing the order would route `"42"` to String (via fmt.Sprintf) and never try Integer.
  - `TestBaseType_AllDefined` is the canary that flags any new BaseType addition — the fixed-length slice + count assertion catches drift between `allBaseTypes` and the explicit enumeration.

## 2026-04-18 - US-207 Struct 嵌套属性编辑器
- Extended the Admin property editor so Struct's `fields` can themselves be Struct — recursively — via the existing `typeConfig: { fields: [...] }` wire format.
  - `StructField` gains an optional `fields?: StructField[]` (populated only when `type === 'struct'`).
  - `StructFieldsEditor` is now self-recursive: each field row reads its `type` select, and when `type === 'struct'` the row renders a nested `<StructFieldsEditor>` beneath it, indented via a left border (`ml-4 pl-3 border-l`).

  - Nested struct happy path — outer struct → inner struct → string leaf, submit POSTs typeConfig with the full recursive shape.
  - Submit blocked when a nested struct is declared but has no children.

- Full web suite: `tsc -b` clean, `vitest run` 70 files / 473 tests all green, `vite build` clean.
- Files changed:
  - `web/src/components/admin/PropertiesEditor.tsx` (StructField adds fields?, parseStructFields/serializeStructFields/isStructTreeValid helpers, recursive StructFieldsEditor with reorder controls, nested indentation, type selector no longer filters struct)
  - `web/src/components/admin/__tests__/PropertiesEditor.test.tsx` (6 new tests + testid rename)
  - `prd.json` (US-207 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Recursive React components that need to be addressable by tests at any depth should accept a `path?: string` prop (default `""` for root) and embed it in both `data-testid` and every `aria-label` they emit. Labels like `struct field name 0.1.2` stay unique; a parent test that scopes via `within(getByTestId('struct-fields-0.1'))` stays tidy. Don't use raw integer indices at nested levels — they collide with the parent's.
  - When broadening a choice set in the UI (here: allowing 'struct' in the nested type select), the validator must ALSO broaden. If `isStructTreeValid` only checked the top-level, an empty nested struct would silently ship a `{fields: []}` subtree to the backend. The rule "allowed in the UI ⇒ validated in the UI" is easy to forget because the scalar validator already short-circuits on the top-level length==0 check.
  - React Testing Library accessible-name matching on buttons with decorative prefixes: "+ Add field" matches `/Add field/i` but NOT `/^Add field$/i`. Anchored regexes are dangerous when labels carry icons / punctuation. Prefer substring matches + scoping via `within(parentEl)` to disambiguate rather than anchoring.
  - Keep wire serialization centralized in one helper (`serializeStructFields`). The in-memory state can carry an `undefined` or an empty `fields` on scalar rows while the user is editing, but the JSON that hits the backend must be canonical — one function at the boundary is the only way to keep that invariant. Same idea as pkg/oss/objectset's validate-at-boundary pattern.

## 2026-04-18 - US-208 Enum/Categorical 约束执行
- Promoted enum constraint failures from a stringly-typed `fmt.Errorf` to a typed `*types.EnumViolationError` carrying both the rejected `Value` and the stringified `AllowedValues` slice. `Error()` keeps the legacy `enum: value X is not in allowed values [...]` shape so existing logs / generic constraint tests keep passing.
- Added `apierror.NewValidationEnum(name, params)` returning `ErrorCode = "WEAVE_VALIDATION_ENUM"` at HTTP 422. Slot fits the existing `NewNotFound` / `NewBadRequest` family in `pkg/apierror/error.go`; WriteJSON path required no changes.
- `executor.validateValueTypeConstraints` now `errors.As`-detects `*EnumViolationError` and returns the typed APIError populated with `objectType`, `property`, `value`, and `allowedValues` (comma-separated). Non-enum constraint failures still go through the legacy `fmt.Errorf("property %q: %w", ...)` path, so regex / minLength / min / max behaviour is unchanged.
- `BatchError` gained `Cause error` + `Unwrap() error` so a typed APIError surfaced by Prepare survives the wrap inside `ApplyBatchAtomic`. Both BatchError construction sites (per-action prepare failure + publish failure) populate `Cause`.
- Handlers learnt a single `typedAPIError(err) *apierror.APIError` helper. `Apply`, `ApplyWithOverrides`, and `asBatchError` all check it BEFORE falling back to the generic `ActionFailed` 400 wrap. Status code + structured Parameters now flow end-to-end.
- Tests:
  - `pkg/types/constraints_test.go`: `TestValidateConstraints_Enum_TypedError` (errors.As + AllowedValues exact match) and `TestValidateConstraints_Enum_TypedError_MixedTypes` (numeric + string mixed enum stringifies in declared order).
  - `pkg/actions/actions_test.go`: `TestExecutor_EnumViolation_ReturnsTypedAPIError422` (Prepare-level — APIError has code/status/property/value/allowedValues/objectType), `TestHandler_Apply_EnumViolation_422` (HTTP — chi router + ResponseRecorder, body decoded as wireFormat, asserts errorCode + parameters), `TestHandler_ApplyBatch_EnumViolation_422` (atomic batch with one good + one bad action surfaces the bad row's typed error verbatim — confirms BatchError.Cause unwrap).
  - Legacy `TestExecutor_ValueTypeConstraint_EnumViolation` rewritten to assert on the typed APIError contract instead of substring matching the err.Error() string.
- All `go test -short ./pkg/...` packages pass; e2e suite green; `go build ./...` and `go vet` clean on touched packages.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/types/constraints.go` (EnumViolationError type + branch returns it)
  - `pkg/types/constraints_test.go` (2 new typed-error tests + import errors/reflect)
  - `pkg/apierror/error.go` (NewValidationEnum constructor)
  - `pkg/actions/executor.go` (apierror import, validateValueTypeConstraints unwrap, BatchError Cause+Unwrap, both BatchError construction sites)
  - `pkg/actions/handlers.go` (typedAPIError helper, Apply/ApplyWithOverrides/asBatchError unwrap calls)
  - `pkg/actions/actions_test.go` (apierror import, 3 new tests, legacy enum test rewritten to typed-error contract)
  - `prd.json` (US-208 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When promoting a constraint check to a typed APIError, keep the underlying `Error()` string stable. The string is what the user sees in legacy logs and what some non-handler tests still match on. The typed channel (`errors.As`) is purely additive.
  - `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` preserves the chain — but only for callers that actually walk it. Every place that ALSO wraps the err string (e.g. `BatchError{Message: err.Error()}`) loses the typed payload. Check those wrapping sites whenever you add a new typed error class downstream.
  - The sweep needed for this iteration was: validator → Prepare wrap → BatchError wrap → asBatchError handler → Apply handler → ApplyWithOverrides handler. Five layers — and missing any one drops the 422 back to a 400. A `typedAPIError(err) *apierror.APIError` helper is the right shape because it makes the new pattern one-line per call site.
  - Enum allowedValues on the wire are best as a single comma-separated string in `Parameters` (the apierror Parameters map is `map[string]string` by design — JSON arrays don't fit). Clients that need the slice can `strings.Split(p["allowedValues"], ",")`. Don't try to teach the apierror Parameters map a richer type — every APIError downstream pays the cost.
  - Batch path subtlety: `ApplyBatchAtomic` wraps EVERY Prepare error, not just the publish err. Forgetting `Cause` on the per-action wrap silently broke the typed-error pipeline for batch and made TestHandler_ApplyBatch_EnumViolation_422 the only signal — would have shipped fine without that test. Always exercise BOTH single + batch handler paths whenever you add a typed validation error.

## 2026-04-18 - US-209 Bidirectional Links
- Added migration `000035_link_type_inverse` adding nullable `inverse_link_rid TEXT` column to `link_types` plus a partial index (WHERE inverse_link_rid IS NOT NULL). No FK REFERENCES constraint — A↔B pairs are typically created one side at a time so cross-references must be allowed to temporarily dangle; symmetry lives at the handler layer instead.
- Extended `oms.LinkType` with `InverseLinkRID string` (json:"inverseLinkRid,omitempty"). `LinkType.ToWireJSON()` surfaces the field only when non-empty.
- PGRepository CRUD: updated `CreateLinkType` INSERT (NULLIF($N,'') collapses the empty string back to NULL so the partial index stays accurate) and `GetLinkType`, `ListOutgoingLinkTypes`, `ListIncomingLinkTypes`, `ListLinkTypes`, `GetLinkTypeByAPIName` (in `link_edges.go`) SELECTs (COALESCE(inverse_link_rid, '')). `UpdateLinkType` now sets `inverse_link_rid=NULLIF($4, '')` alongside the existing display_name / description / is_required columns — the handler decides whether the incoming request touches it.
- Admin handlers:
  - `CreateLinkTypeRequest.InverseLinkRID string` (plain field — create is one-shot).
  - `UpdateLinkTypeRequest.InverseLinkRID *string` — pointer to preserve three-state semantics: **omit** (keep existing), **set to ""** (clear the pairing), **set to some RID** (assign).

  - Validation is called at BOTH paths (Create + Update) BEFORE the branch overlay check, so branch creations carry the same invariants as main commits.
- `links.Resolver` already supports `DirectionForward`/`DirectionReverse` via US-003 / US-187 plumbing; `InverseLinkRID` is PURE METADATA — it is not consulted during resolution. Symmetry is provable either by (a) traversing one paired LinkType in both directions, or (b) traversing the two LinkTypes separately in the same direction. Both are verified.
- `setupEmployeeDept` fixture (pkg/links/resolver_test.go) now cross-references inverse_link_rid on both LinkTypes. Adding the field to the existing fixture is zero-risk because the resolver never reads it.
- Tests:

Uses an order-agnostic `sameSet` helper because the resolver's output ordering is deliberately not specified.

- Files changed:
  - `migrations/000035_link_type_inverse.up.sql` (new)
  - `migrations/000035_link_type_inverse.down.sql` (new)
  - `pkg/oms/models.go` (InverseLinkRID field + ToWireJSON)
  - `pkg/oms/pg_repository.go` (CreateLinkType INSERT, GetLinkType/List* SELECT, UpdateLinkType SET)
  - `pkg/oms/link_edges.go` (GetLinkTypeByAPIName SELECT)
  - `pkg/oms/admin_handlers.go` (CreateLinkTypeRequest, UpdateLinkTypeRequest, validateInverseLinkPair helper, Create/Update wire-up)
  - `pkg/oms/admin_handlers_linkinverse_test.go` (new, 7 tests)
  - `pkg/oms/models_test.go` (ToWireJSON inverse test)

  - `pkg/links/direction_test.go` (TestBidirectionalLinks_* + sameSet helper)
  - `prd.json` (US-209 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Self-referential FK on the same table is a hazard: if migration added `FOREIGN KEY (inverse_link_rid) REFERENCES link_types(rid)` the create-one-side-first workflow would fail with a dangling reference. Nullable + handler-layer validation is the simpler choice and matches the "pair is edited, not transactional" reality. Use partial indexes `WHERE col IS NOT NULL` to keep the index compact.
  - For optional fields on an Update DTO, `*string` gives three-state semantics that bare `string` can't: omit=don't-touch, `""`=clear, `"X"`=set. Consistent with how `IsRequired *bool` already works in the same struct. Apply pointer semantics any time "not sent" and "sent as zero value" need to be distinguishable.
  - `NULLIF($N, '')` + `COALESCE(col, '')` is the canonical Weave pattern for nullable text columns that ride as `string` on the Go model. It keeps the Go side string-valued (no `sql.NullString`) while the DB gets a proper NULL so constraints / partial indexes / FK behaviour all work. See every `COALESCE(description, '')` pairing in pg_repository.go for prior art.
  - When adding a metadata-only field (not consulted by the runtime), you typically don't need to touch the resolver / handler hot paths — just CRUD + wire format. The InverseLinkRID field is purely for discovery; symmetric traversal is already implemented via `DirectionForward` / `DirectionReverse` on the resolver. Resist the temptation to route traversal through `InverseLinkRID` — it would duplicate an existing capability and create a second path to keep in sync.
  - Test symmetry assertions need order-agnostic comparisons: Bleve result ordering is stable within a single search but differs between queries with different underlying plans. `sameSet(a, b)` as a tiny local helper beats `sort.Strings`-then-compare because it names the intent.
  - When adding a column that existing mock repos will carry in struct-value maps (e.g. `mockRepo.linkTypes []oms.LinkType`), NO mock updates are needed — the new field flows through struct copies automatically. Unlike adding a new method to `oms.Repository` (which needs ~15 stub updates across the tree), a new struct field is a zero-touch addition.
  - Field on wire / field in DB / field in model should share the SAME omitempty semantics. If DB is `NULL` → Go `""` → JSON absent, the round-trip is clean. If any layer persists an empty string instead of NULL, a partial index `WHERE inverse_link_rid IS NOT NULL` would include every row and defeat its purpose. NULLIF at the INSERT/UPDATE boundary is the only place this guarantee is enforced.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - New routes registered on `cmd/server` MUST be added to `api/openapi.yaml` — the contract tests (`TestContract_AllRoutesDocumented` + `TestContract_EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical`) enforce it. The embedded copy `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` is a byte-for-byte duplicate of the canonical spec; after editing canonical, `cp api/openapi.yaml cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` is the only supported sync path. No codegen.
  - Reverse-direction searchAround enrichment needs a separate `ListLinkEdgesWithPropertiesByTarget` primitive. Emulating it by filtering a forward-direction list silently returns zero results when `sourcePKs` are target-side. Always add both the source-keyed and target-keyed variant when building an edge-lookup interface, even if only forward is exercised at commit time — the direction-aware caller WILL arrive within a few iterations.
  - Narrow stores like `LinkPropertyStore` / `LinkEdgeStore` stay out of `oms.Repository`: the CachedRepository decorator only wraps Repository methods, so directly handing the bare `pgRepo` to the dep (`deps.LinkPropertyStore = pgRepo`) is the cleanest wiring. Capture pgRepo BEFORE `oms.NewCachedRepository(pgRepo, ...)` wraps it.
  - Executor-level enrichment hooks should be OPTIONAL setters (`SetEdgePropertiesProvider`) rather than constructor args — keeps the "no provider wired" path zero-cost and makes degraded-mode test routers trivial.
  - Edge properties flow as `Result.EdgeProperties map[pk]map[string]interface{}` keyed by the "other end" PK. In forward direction that's `target_object_rid`, in reverse that's `source_object_rid`. Injecting under `__edge` in LoadObjects avoids collision with object properties; `__` prefix matches the existing `__primaryKey` / `__apiName` / `__rid` convention on WireObject.
  - When validating edge_property values at write time, shape invariants (unknown key rejection, required-field enforcement) are the right layer's business — deep type/constraint validation belongs with the runtime enforcement path that already handles regular properties. Don't duplicate the constraint-engine here; keep the write-time validator surface-level.
  - Contract-test failure mode is friendly: it prints the exact `METHOD /path` lines missing from the spec. Three-step fix is always: add `paths:` block to `api/openapi.yaml`, copy to `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml`, re-run `go test -short ./cmd/server/ -run TestContract`.

## 2026-04-18 - US-211 Composite Primary Keys
- Added migration `000037_object_type_composite_pk` introducing `primary_key_props JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb` on `object_types` plus a backfill that wraps every existing `primary_key_prop` value in a single-element array. The legacy `primary_key_prop TEXT` column is kept (and still INSERTed/SELECTed) because it remains the canonical single-PK label for ~all downstream consumers (Bleve doc IDs, link FK config, action edits) — composite-PK ObjectTypes set `primary_key_prop = primaryKeys[0]` so single-PK consumers keep functioning unchanged.
- Extended `oms.ObjectType` with a new `PrimaryKeys []string` field plus `EffectivePrimaryKeys()` and `IsCompositeKey()` helpers. Both `ToWireJSON()` and `ToFullMetadataJSON()` now emit `primaryKeys` (full ordered list) alongside `primaryKey` (legacy first-element shortcut). The model has ONE canonical accessor regardless of whether the row predates migration 000037 or not — `EffectivePrimaryKeys()` falls back to `[]string{PrimaryKey}` when `PrimaryKeys` is empty.
- New `pkg/oms/composite_key.go` with two pure helpers:
  - `ParseCompositeKey(raw string, expected int) ([]string, error)` — parses URL-segment composite keys, gated on the expected count. **Single-PK case is opaque** (returns `[raw]` unchanged so legacy keys containing `:` like RIDs still resolve). Multi-PK case splits on `:` and requires exactly `expected` non-empty parts.
  - `JoinCompositeKey(parts []string) string` — single-element returns the lone value (no-op); multi-element colon-joins. Inverse of ParseCompositeKey by construction.
- `PGRepository` updates:
  - `CreateObjectType` INSERT now passes `primary_key_props` JSONB ($15) marshalled from `EffectivePrimaryKeys()`. The legacy `primary_key_prop` column continues to receive `ot.PrimaryKey`.
  - `GetObjectType`, `ListObjectTypes`, `ListInterfaceObjectTypes` SELECTs all read `COALESCE(primary_key_props, '[]'::jsonb)` and decode through a new `decodePrimaryKeyProps([]byte, legacy string) []string` helper that gracefully falls back to the legacy single-element list when the JSONB column is empty (i.e. the migration backfill hasn't run yet).
  - `UpdateObjectType` is intentionally NOT touched — primary keys are immutable post-creation, matching the existing UPDATE which also leaves `primary_key_prop` alone.
- Admin handler updates:
  - `CreateObjectTypeRequest` now declares both `primaryKey string` (legacy) and `primaryKeys []string` (US-211). Validation: at least one must be non-empty; if `primaryKeys` is set it wins and `primaryKey` is rewritten to `primaryKeys[0]`. Per-element empty rejection via `InvalidParameter:primaryKeys`.
  - `CreateObjectType` populates both fields on the model so the cached repository decorator and downstream wire serializers see a complete picture.
  - Import-ontology handler (`importHandler`) now sets `PrimaryKeys: ot.EffectivePrimaryKeys()` on the new ObjectType so re-imported ontologies preserve composite-PK declarations across export/import cycles.
- Composite-key URL routing: chi treats `:` as an opaque path character — `/objects/{objectType}/{key1}:{key2}` works at the router layer with no changes. The `oms.ParseCompositeKey` helper is the canonical place for handlers/services that need to break the segment into typed parts.
- OpenAPI spec (`api/openapi.yaml` + embedded copy): `ObjectType.primaryKeys` and `CreateObjectTypeRequest.primaryKeys` array properties added; the create body's `required` list dropped `primaryKey` (now satisfied by either field) with a description clarifying the OR semantics.
- Tests:
  - `pkg/oms/composite_key_test.go` (12 cases): single-PK opacity (RID-with-colons round-trips); empty raw rejected; happy-path multi-part; wrong-count error mentions expected; empty leading/trailing parts rejected; zero-expected error; `JoinCompositeKey` single + multi + nil; round-trip both ways; `EffectivePrimaryKeys` for legacy-single, prefer-composite, and fully-empty paths; `IsCompositeKey` matrix.
  - `pkg/oms/admin_handlers_composite_pk_test.go` (6 cases): create-with-primaryKeys-array success (asserts wire `primaryKey` = first element + full `primaryKeys` array, mock repo persistence + `IsCompositeKey()=true`); legacy-primaryKey-string still works (back-compat); missing both fields → 400 with `InvalidParameter:primaryKey`; empty array element → 400 with `InvalidParameter:primaryKeys`; GET-by-apiName surfaces `primaryKeys` array in V2 wire format; full CRUD round trip (create composite PK → get → update + deprecate → delete) — exercises the AC's "创建+get+update+delete 全流程" requirement; chi-level capture asserts the `key1:key2` URL segment makes it through unmolested and ParseCompositeKey unpacks it cleanly.
- All `go test -short ./pkg/... ./internal/... ./test/... ./cmd/...` green; `go vet ./...` clean; contract tests (TestContract_AllRoutesDocumented + TestContract_NoOrphanedSpecPaths + TestContract_EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical) green.
- Files changed:
  - `migrations/000037_object_type_composite_pk.up.sql` (new)
  - `migrations/000037_object_type_composite_pk.down.sql` (new)
  - `pkg/oms/models.go` (PrimaryKeys field + EffectivePrimaryKeys/IsCompositeKey + ToWireJSON/ToFullMetadataJSON exposure)
  - `pkg/oms/composite_key.go` (new — ParseCompositeKey + JoinCompositeKey)
  - `pkg/oms/composite_key_test.go` (new, 12 tests)
  - `pkg/oms/pg_repository.go` (CreateObjectType INSERT + GetObjectType/ListObjectTypes/ListInterfaceObjectTypes SELECT + decodePrimaryKeyProps helper)
  - `pkg/oms/admin_handlers.go` (fmt import + CreateObjectTypeRequest.PrimaryKeys + Create validation/wiring + import handler PrimaryKeys carry-over)
  - `pkg/oms/admin_handlers_composite_pk_test.go` (new, 6 tests)
  - `api/openapi.yaml` + `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` (ObjectType.primaryKeys + CreateObjectTypeRequest.primaryKeys + relaxed required list)
  - `prd.json` (US-211 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Composite-key URL routing requires NO router changes when the delimiter is `:` (or any other non-`/` character). chi treats the full segment as opaque — the splitting concern lives in the handler and is gated on the ObjectType declaring `len(PrimaryKeys) > 1`. Single-PK ObjectTypes keep the segment intact, so legacy keys containing colons (e.g. RIDs) still resolve unchanged.
  - When adding a parallel column for "richer" semantics on top of a legacy single-value column, KEEP THE LEGACY COLUMN. Backfilling it to `EffectivePrimaryKeys()[0]` keeps every downstream consumer (Bleve doc IDs, FK lookups, action edits, ~15 mock repos) working without a sweep. The new column's job is purely "richer model"; the legacy column's job is "lowest-common-denominator handle."
  - For optional-on-create fields where ONE of two equivalent shapes is required (legacy `primaryKey` OR composite `primaryKeys`), the validator pattern is: union into a single slice → reject empty union → reject empty elements. NEVER require both. If both are present, prefer the richer shape and rewrite the legacy field to its first element so wire format stays consistent across consumers.
  - `decodePrimaryKeyProps([]byte, legacy string) []string` is the right shape for any "JSONB column with backfill from a legacy column" pattern — the helper falls back to wrapping the legacy value in a single-element slice when the JSONB is empty/malformed. Keeps the read path tolerant of partially-migrated rows without scattering nil-checks across every Scan site.
  - `httputil.WriteJSON(w, status, ot)` uses Go's default JSON marshaling, NOT `ToWireJSON()`. So adding a new field to `ObjectType` with a `json:"xxx,omitempty"` tag automatically surfaces it on Create/Update responses — but you ALSO need to update `ToWireJSON()` / `ToFullMetadataJSON()` for the V2 read endpoints (which build a `map[string]interface{}` manually). Two paths, both must be kept in sync.
  - DELETE on an ObjectType refuses ACTIVE/PROMOTED rows by design — full CRUD tests need to deprecate (PUT status=DEPRECATED) before the DELETE step. The error message is friendly enough to point you to the right fix when this trips a test.
  - Composite PKs are a metadata-layer change. The full ripple to Bleve doc IDs, link FK config, action edits, etc. is OUT of scope for this story (would be a multi-thousand-line change). The convention going forward: composite-PK objects are stored/retrieved by their CANONICAL colon-joined string (the same string the URL accepts), and `oms.ParseCompositeKey` is the canonical splitter for any handler that needs typed parts.

## 2026-04-18 - US-212 Object Type Inheritance
- Added migration `000038_object_type_inheritance` (ALTER TABLE object_types ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS extends_rid TEXT + a partial index `WHERE extends_rid IS NOT NULL` for fast "list children of X" lookups). NULLable text without a self-referential FK constraint — same pattern established by `link_types.inverse_link_rid` so parent/child rows can be authored independently and validation lives in the handler layer.
- Extended `oms.ObjectType` with `ExtendsRID string` (`json:"extendsRid,omitempty"`); surfaced in `ToWireJSON()` and `ToFullMetadataJSON()`. Round-trips through PGRepository INSERT (NULLIF), all three SELECT paths (GetObjectType, ListObjectTypes, ListInterfaceObjectTypes via COALESCE), and UPDATE (NULLIF for tri-state). `httputil.WriteJSON` of `*ObjectType` already surfaces it via the json tag, so admin Create/Update responses include it without separate plumbing.
- New `pkg/oms/inheritance.go`:
  - `ResolveInheritedObjectType(ctx, repo, ot)` walks the `extends_rid` chain (oldest ancestor first) and merges parent properties + outgoing link types into the child. Child entries override matching api_name. Returns a `ResolvedObjectType` carrying merged Properties, OutgoingLinkTypes, and ExtendsChain (immediate parent → root). Cycle detection via visited-set; `ErrInheritanceCycle` sentinel.
  - `ValidateInheritanceCandidate(ctx, repo, otRID, parentRID)` is the write-time guard: walks the candidate parent's chain, with the visited set pre-seeded by `otRID` so A→B→C→A is rejected. Self-reference (`otRID == parentRID`) short-circuits. Empty `parentRID` is a no-op.
  - `MaxInheritanceDepth = 32` is a defensive backstop in case stale data slips past the cycle guard.
- Admin handler updates (`admin_handlers.go`):
  - `CreateObjectTypeRequest.ExtendsRID string` — Create validates parent existence + same-ontology + cycle (via ValidateInheritanceCandidate using the freshly generated RID), surfacing 400 `InvalidParameter:extendsRid` with a `reason` string ("parent ObjectType not found" / "...different ontology" / "inheritance chain forms a cycle").
  - `UpdateObjectTypeRequest.ExtendsRID *string` — tri-state pointer same as `LinkType.InverseLinkRID`. nil = leave unchanged, "" = clear, non-empty = validate + assign. Cycle check runs against `existing.RID`.
  - Import handler (`importHandler`) now pre-fills `otRIDMap` with newly generated RIDs in a pre-pass, then the create loop assigns those RIDs and remaps `ExtendsRID` through the same map — so parent pointers survive the export/import cycle regardless of slice order.
- New endpoint `GET /api/v2/ontologies/{o}/objectTypes/{ot}/resolved` (`handlers.go::GetObjectTypeResolved`): returns merged view as JSON map carrying `properties` (with optional `inheritedFrom` marker on each entry whose owner ≠ child RID), `outgoingLinkTypes`, `extendsRid`, and `extendsChain` ([immediate parent, ..., root]). Cycle in the chain surfaces as 400 `InvalidParameter:extendsRid`. Wired in `cmd/server/routes.go`.
- OpenAPI spec (`api/openapi.yaml` + embedded copy at `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml`): added `extendsRid` to ObjectType + CreateObjectTypeRequest + UpdateObjectTypeRequest schemas, and registered the new `/resolved` path entry. Contract tests (`TestContract_AllRoutesDocumented` + `TestContract_NoOrphanedSpecPaths` + `TestContract_EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical`) pass.
- Tests:
  - `pkg/oms/inheritance_test.go` (10 cases): no-parent passes through; single-parent merges parent+child properties; child override on apiName beats parent's value (DisplayName + ObjectTypeRID checks); 3-level chain (living→person→employee) merges all; A→B→A cycle rejected; outgoing links inherited; ValidateInheritanceCandidate covers self-ref, acyclic accept, parent-chain-back-to-leaf cycle, empty-parent no-op.
  - `pkg/oms/admin_handlers_inheritance_test.go` (10 cases): Create with extendsRid persists + surfaces in response; unknown parent → 400 `InvalidParameter:extendsRid`; cross-ontology parent → 400; Update sets / clears (tri-state) extendsRid; cycle on Update rejected; resolved endpoint merges parent properties+outgoing links; child overrides parent property in resolved view; root type returns own properties only (no extendsRid/extendsChain in payload); ObjectType V2 wire format includes extendsRid.

- Files changed:
  - `migrations/000038_object_type_inheritance.up.sql` (new)
  - `migrations/000038_object_type_inheritance.down.sql` (new)
  - `pkg/oms/models.go` (ObjectType.ExtendsRID + ToWireJSON / ToFullMetadataJSON exposure)
  - `pkg/oms/inheritance.go` (new — ResolveInheritedObjectType + ValidateInheritanceCandidate + ErrInheritanceCycle)
  - `pkg/oms/inheritance_test.go` (new, 10 tests)

  - `pkg/oms/admin_handlers.go` (Create/Update ExtendsRID validation + import-handler pre-allocate + remap)

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - "Diamond inheritance" in single-parent inheritance is a misnomer — only chain cycles can occur. Implement it as: track visited RIDs in a set seeded with the row whose parent is being assigned, walk the candidate parent's chain, fail on first revisit. The same guard belongs in the read-side resolver as a defensive backstop in case stale data slipped past write-time validation.
  - When importing rows whose schema includes a self-referential RID column (extends_rid, inverse_link_rid, parent/child relationships), pre-allocate new RIDs into otRIDMap BEFORE the create loop. Single-pass remap fails when the parent appears later in the slice. This is a generalization of the LinkType source/target remap pattern.
  - The `UpdateObjectType` SQL UPDATE statement was previously immutable on most-fields-but-status. Adding extends_rid to the mutable set (with NULLIF) is fine for inheritance — but the convention "primary keys are immutable post-creation" still holds for primary_key_prop / primary_key_props which UpdateObjectType deliberately leaves alone. Keep both patterns separate: structural-keys are write-once, relational/metadata pointers can be retargeted.
  - For "show me the merged view" endpoints (resolved properties, computed effective config, etc.), build a separate `/resolved` route rather than overloading an existing `GetX` with a query param. Two reasons: (1) the wire shape diverges (entries gain `inheritedFrom` markers, the root response gains `extendsChain`) and forcing one shape via flags hurts callers; (2) cache semantics differ — `/resolved` reads multiple ancestor rows so its TTL story is different from `GetObjectType`. Keep them addressable as distinct resources.
  - `pkg/oms.inheritanceReader` is a narrow 3-method subset of `oms.Repository` (GetObjectType + ListProperties + ListOutgoingLinkTypes). Defining it locally to the resolver keeps the unit tests trivial — every existing mockRepo already satisfies it implicitly — and signals which methods the resolver actually consumes when reading the function signature.
  - Field-on-existing-struct additions (no new method on Repository) are zero-touch for the ~15 mockRepo / inMemoryOmsRepo stubs across the test tree. Struct-value maps copy the new field for free; only manual struct literals that pin every field would need updating, and the codebase doesn't have any of those.
