## 2026-04-18 - US-213 Breaking Change Detection
- New endpoint `GET /api/v2/ontologies/{ontologyApiName}/branches/{branchId}/breaking-changes` returns a `BreakingChangesReport{branchId, changes[]}`. Each entry has `kind` ∈ {PROPERTY_DELETED, PROPERTY_TYPE_NARROWED, PROPERTY_REQUIRED_ADDED, PRIMARY_KEY_CHANGED} plus `objectTypeRid/objectTypeApiName`, `propertyApiName` (when applicable), human-readable `detail`, and two impact slices: `affectedActionTypes` (RIDs) + `affectedSavedObjectSets` (IDs). Ordering inside each slice is sorted+deduped so the wire payload is stable across runs.
- New file `pkg/oms/breaking_changes.go`:
  - `DetectBreakingChanges(ctx, repo, savedSets, ontologyRID, ontologyAPIName, branchID)` is the only entry point. Walks main `ListObjectTypes` then `ListProperties(ot.RID)` for each, indexing branch changes upfront via `indexChanges(all, entityType)` so detection per ObjectType / Property is O(1) lookup.
  - Type narrowing rule: any `BaseType` change OR `IsArray` flip is breaking. The detector deliberately treats every base-type swap as narrowing (rather than building a per-type compatibility lattice) — a String→Integer change is just as risky as String→Boolean for downstream callers, and authors who really need a relaxed migration can bridge by deprecating the old property + adding a new one. Same semantic that Foundry's schema-evolution check uses.
  - Required-added rule: previously `IsNullable=true`, now `IsNullable=false`. Relaxing in the other direction (required→nullable) is NOT breaking — clients that already supply a value keep working.
  - PK change rule: compares `EffectivePrimaryKeys()` (US-211) of main vs branch ObjectType. Single-PK ObjectTypes whose only change is `DisplayName`/`Description` etc. produce zero entries.
- Reference scanning:
  - **ActionTypes**: `actionTypeReferences(at, change)` parses `at.Rules` into a local `actionRule` shape (kept in detector to avoid an `oms→actions→oms` import cycle) and matches on `rule.objectType == change.ObjectTypeAPIName`. For property-level changes the rule must ALSO bind that property in `propertyBindings`; for PK changes any rule on the affected ObjectType counts (because the primary-key derivation in `pkg/actions/rules.go::findPrimaryKey` is shared by every modify/delete on that type).
  - **SavedObjectSets**: `walkSavedSetNode` recursively descends `objectSet`/`objectSets`, plus inspects `properties` (withProperties), `derivedProperties[].field`, and `where` (which is then descended via `walkWhereNode` — handles `and`/`or` arrays + `not` single-child). Matches on `objectType == change.ObjectTypeAPIName` (PK changes only) and on `field == change.PropertyAPIName` (property-level changes). The walker uses generic `map[string]interface{}` rather than typed `objectset.Definition` so the OMS package stays free of an `oss/objectset` import — same dependency-direction reasoning as the ActionType case.
- New narrow types:
  - `oms.SavedObjectSetRef{ID, Definition json.RawMessage}` — minimal projection the detector needs from a SavedObjectSet.
  - `oms.SavedObjectSetLister.ListSavedObjectSets(ctx, ontologyAPIName)` — narrow 1-method interface satisfied by future adapters around `objectset.PGSavedStore`. Kept narrow so `*PGSavedStore` doesn't have to add a method, and so the existing handler test setup doesn't need to mock the full SavedStore CRUD surface.
  - `OMSHandler.SetSavedObjectSetLister(s)` — optional setter, mirroring `SetLinkPropertyStore`/`SetLinkEdgeStore` pattern. When unset (the default in cmd/server right now, since SavedStore isn't wired into routes yet), the detector still runs against ObjectType/Property metadata + ActionTypes; only `affectedSavedObjectSets` is empty.
- New handler `OMSHandler.GetBranchBreakingChanges` in `pkg/oms/handlers_branch.go`: resolves ontology by apiName/RID, verifies branch exists (404 `BranchNotFound`/`OntologyNotFound`), delegates to `DetectBreakingChanges`. No status filter on branch — closed/merged branches still answer (read-only diagnostic).
- Route registration: appended to the existing branches block in `cmd/server/routes.go`. SavedObjectSetLister is NOT wired in `cmd/server/main.go` because the SavedStore is currently only addressable via direct PG access — `objectset.PGSavedStore` exists but no HTTP routes bind it yet. The detector therefore reports zero saved-set impacts in production until that wiring lands; once it does, a 5-line adapter (translating `*PGSavedStore.List` → `[]SavedObjectSetRef`) connects the rest.
- OpenAPI: added `BreakingChange` + `BreakingChangesReport` schemas next to `BranchDiffEntry` and the `/breaking-changes` path entry between `/diff` and `/rebase`. Embedded copy `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` synced via `cp`.
- Tests:
  - `pkg/oms/breaking_changes_test.go` (12 cases): no-op when no branch changes; PROPERTY_DELETED happy path with ObjectType context populated; PROPERTY_TYPE_NARROWED on baseType swap; PROPERTY_TYPE_NARROWED on isArray flip; PROPERTY_REQUIRED_ADDED on nullable→not-nullable; required→nullable is NOT breaking (zero entries); PRIMARY_KEY_CHANGED on PK rename; displayName-only edit produces no PK change false positive; AffectedActionTypes filter (ref'd action vs un-ref'd action); AffectedActionTypes for PK change includes any rule on that ObjectType; AffectedSavedObjectSets filter on `where.field` match; nested `where.and` walks subtree; PRIMARY_KEY_CHANGED hits SavedObjectSets that reference the type via `base`; nil lister still returns property-level changes with empty saved-sets slice.
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_branch_breaking_test.go` (5 cases): HTTP happy path returns 200 + decoded report; missing branch → 404 `BranchNotFound`; missing ontology → 404 `OntologyNotFound`; no-changes returns 200 with `changes:[]`; lister wired surfaces saved-set IDs in the wire payload.
- All `go test -short ./pkg/... ./internal/... ./test/e2e/... ./cmd/...` green; `go vet ./...` clean; contract tests (`TestContract_AllRoutesDocumented` + `TestContract_NoOrphanedSpecPaths` + `TestContract_EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical`) pass.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/oms/breaking_changes.go` (new — types + DetectBreakingChanges + ActionType/SavedObjectSet scanners + sortedUnique/equalStringSlices helpers)
  - `pkg/oms/breaking_changes_test.go` (new, 12 detector tests)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers.go` (savedObjectSetLister field + SetSavedObjectSetLister setter)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_branch.go` (GetBranchBreakingChanges handler)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_branch_breaking_test.go` (new, 5 handler tests)
  - `cmd/server/routes.go` (1 route line)
  - `api/openapi.yaml` + `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` (new schemas + path entry)
  - `prd.json` (US-213 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When an ObjectType (or any other entity) carries a struct-tag `json:"-"` field that the rest of the system relies on (like `Property.ObjectTypeRID`), branch overlay diffs are blind to it — `BeforeState`/`AfterState` are the marshalled JSON. The fix is to walk MAIN's structure (which still has the field set), then index branch changes by RID and look up by main's RID. Don't try to recover the unexported field from the change payload.
  - Detector for "changes against main" should iterate main's view, not the branched view. The branched view applies overlay (DELETED filtered out, etc.) and would silently hide the very rows the detector wants to flag. `BranchedRepository` is the wrong tool for this — talk to the bare `Repository` and consume `ListBranchChanges` directly.
  - When the detector needs to scan a JSON-typed payload (ActionType.Rules, SavedObjectSet.Definition) whose canonical typed shape lives in a downstream package (`pkg/actions`, `pkg/oss/objectset`), define a LOCAL minimal typed shape inside the detector. Importing the downstream package would create a cycle through Repository, and the local copy stays narrow because the detector only consumes a few fields. Same trick as `parseActionRules` here.
  - Walking generic `map[string]interface{}` for SavedObjectSet definitions is noisy but resilient: new `Definition` shapes (added per US-2xx every other iteration) don't break the walker as long as they keep descending via `objectSet`/`objectSets`. The pattern handles withProperties/derivedProperties/where uniformly without the detector growing per-type cases.
  - The "required relaxed is not breaking" semantic is easy to get wrong on first pass — it's tempting to treat ANY isNullable flip as breaking. Always implement breaking-change detectors as DIRECTIONAL: `was X, now Y` matters in only one direction. Add a positive-and-negative test pair (REQUIRED_ADDED breaking + nullable-relaxation no-op) to lock the direction.
  - Adapters between this detector and a real SavedStore (eg. `objectset.PGSavedStore`) belong in `cmd/server/` next to the executor wiring, not inside `pkg/oms/`. Keeps OMS independent of the OSS persistence layer and lets degraded-mode test routers ship without booting the SavedStore.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - "Polymorphic dispatch" against an action registry needs TWO lookup keys: the method rid (for candidacy) AND the target ObjectType apiName (for specialization). Without the second the system can't tell which of N implementations to pick. The shape that works is: filter `ImplementsMethodRID == methodRid`, then parse `Rules` for an `objectType` match. Keep a local minimal rule-parse struct (see also US-213's `actionRule`) to avoid a pkg/actions import cycle through oms.Repository.
  - Adapter-through-narrow-interface (`oms.InterfaceMethodActionDispatcher` wrapping `*actions.Executor` in `cmd/server/`) is the canonical shape for "pkg/oms needs to call into pkg/actions without importing it." The interface lives in oms, the concrete adapter lives in cmd/server. Same reason `pgEdgePropertiesResolver` (US-210) lives in cmd/server: keeps pkg/oms free of downstream deps AND makes degraded-mode test routers trivial — no dispatcher wired → method resolution still works, just doesn't execute.
  - Zero-arg stubs in mockRepo (`AttachInterface(_, _)` → returns createErr) are a trap: they compile fine but the handlers that rely on them (polymorphic invoke, Interface attach/detach chains) silently return empty results. When a new test exercises a handler end-to-end, audit the mockRepo stubs it touches and promote them to real in-memory impls if the handler actually reads the data back. Prior pattern: the `branchChanges` + `actionTypes` slices in mockRepo are real storage; `interfaceAttachments` was not until US-214 needed it.
  - Tri-state pointer fields (`*string` on UpdateActionTypeRequest.ImplementsMethodRID) only disambiguate three states when the handler actually dereferences them differently: nil=preserve, non-nil with "" = clear, non-nil with value = assign. Missing any branch silently collapses the semantics. Ditto on persistence: the UPDATE SQL must use NULLIF($N,'') or the "" case persists as empty string instead of NULL and the partial index stops working. Two places, same invariant — easy to get one right and skip the other.
  - When wiring a new admin handler in cmd/server/routes.go, the contract-test triad enforces: route registered → path entry in `api/openapi.yaml` → embedded copy synced via `cp api/openapi.yaml cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml`. Failing any leg surfaces as a precise `METHOD /path` diff in the test output. Remember the embedded copy — the spec-served-at-runtime IS the embedded copy, not the canonical file.

## 2026-04-18 - US-215 Function Registry (signature + runtime)
- Pre-existing infra (US-089) already shipped the `functions` table + Function model + CRUD handlers + chi routes. US-215 layered the registry-shape extensions:
  - migration 000040: ALTER TABLE functions ADD COLUMN signature JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb, ADD COLUMN runtime TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'goja' + CHECK (runtime IN ('goja','http')) (constraint added via DO-EXISTS guard so the migration is idempotent).
  - `pkg/oms/function.go` (new): FunctionRuntimeGoja/HTTP constants; Function.Validate() (name/sourceCode/runtime + delegated signature shape check); Function.NormalisedRuntime() collapses empty → "goja"; ValidateFunctionSignature() enforces params-array + per-param-name + returns.type. signatureFromBytes / normaliseSignatureForWrite keep the JSONB DEFAULT '{}' contract round-trip-safe (empty/{} stored as '{}' but surfaces as nil JSON so omitempty hides the empty case from clients).

Handler runs Function.Validate() before persisting and emits 400 InvalidParameter:function with reason on failure. existing.Runtime forced through NormalisedRuntime() so mocks see the same value the DB would store.

  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function_us215_test.go` (new, 5 cases): Create round-trips signature+runtime; Create defaults runtime to "goja"; Create rejects unknown runtime; Create rejects bad signature shape; Update preserves signature when omitted; Update rejects unknown runtime.

- `go test -short ./pkg/... ./cmd/... ./internal/...` green; `go vet ./...` clean; contract-tests trio (TestContract_AllRoutesDocumented + TestContract_NoOrphanedSpecPaths + TestContract_EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical) green.
- Files changed:
  - `migrations/000040_function_signature_runtime.up.sql` (new)
  - `migrations/000040_function_signature_runtime.down.sql` (new)
  - `pkg/oms/function.go` (new)
  - `pkg/oms/function_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function_us215_test.go` (new)

  - `prd.json` (US-215 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When adding a NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' JSONB column: the read path must COALESCE(col, '{}'::jsonb) AND the write path must substitute '{}' for nil — pgx encodes nil json.RawMessage as the string "null", which the column accepts but breaks the "empty ⇒ nil-on-the-wire" round-trip the API contract wants. Single normaliseSignatureForWrite + signatureFromBytes choke point keeps both sides honest.
  - Adding a CHECK constraint inside an idempotent migration: wrap with `DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = '...') THEN ALTER ... END IF; END$$;`. ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT alone has no IF NOT EXISTS for CHECKs (unlike COLUMNS), so the naive form double-fires on re-run.
  - Tri-state fields on Update DTO: `Signature *json.RawMessage` works the same way `*string` / `*bool` do — nil = preserve, non-nil = replace (including with empty value). Bare `json.RawMessage` would collapse "absent in JSON" and "present with empty body" into the same zero value, which would silently nuke the schema on every partial update.

## 2026-04-18 - US-216 Function Signature 类型系统
- Added `pkg/oms.ParseFunctionSignature` returning a typed `ParsedFunctionSignature{Params []FunctionParam, Returns *FunctionReturn}`. Empty / null / `{}` raw input collapses to a zero-value parse with `HasContract()==false`. Decode failures surface a generic "invalid signature" error — callers should have already gated through `ValidateFunctionSignature`.
- Added `pkg/oms.ValidateAndCoerceFunctionParams(sig, input)` — the runtime validator the AC calls for. Behaviour:
  - No contract: input copied through verbatim (every key accepted).
  - Per declared param: if missing AND has `default` → JSON-unmarshal the default into the output map; if missing AND `required` → 400 `missing_required`; otherwise the key stays absent.
  - For supplied values: when `type` is declared, run `pkg/types.Validate` against `{Type: BaseType(param.Type)}`; required→non-nullable, optional→nullable. Type failures return 400 `type_mismatch`.
  - Any input key not declared in the signature → 400 `unknown_parameter`. (Empty signatures bypass this rule — see Codebase Patterns entry.)
  - Returns a fresh map (not aliasing input) so handler mutation is safe.
- Added typed `oms.FunctionParamError{Parameter, Code, Reason}` with `Code` ∈ `missing_required` / `type_mismatch` / `unknown_parameter` / `default_invalid`. Handlers consume via `errors.As` and surface the structured payload as the apierror Parameters map; SDKs key off `code`.
- New endpoint `POST /api/v2/ontologies/{ontologyApiName}/functions/{functionRid}/execute` (`pkg/oms/handlers_function.go::ExecuteFunction`):
  - Resolves the function via `GetFunctionByName` (accepts both RID and apiName as the URL segment, same as `GetFunctionV2`).
  - Empty request body is legal — bypasses ReadJSON when `r.ContentLength == 0`. Functions whose params are all-defaults / all-optional invoke without a body.
  - `ParseFunctionSignature` + `ValidateAndCoerceFunctionParams` gate runs BEFORE dispatch. Validation failures emit 400 with `code=apierror.ErrorCode("InvalidParameter:"+paramName)` and `parameters={parameter, code, reason}`.
  - Optional `oms.FunctionExecutor` interface (`pkg/oms/function_executor.go`) consumes the validated map. Wired via `OMSHandler.SetFunctionExecutor(...)`. When unset the endpoint returns `503 ServiceUnavailable` with the coerced parameter map echoed in the body — so degraded-mode test routers (and the current production wiring, which does not yet construct a FunctionExecutor) still exercise the validator surface end-to-end. Same setter-injection convention as US-210's `LinkPropertyStore` / `LinkEdgeStore`.
  - Successful dispatch returns 200 `{functionRid, result}`. Executor errors collapse to 400 `FunctionExecutionFailed` (mirrors `ExecuteQueryType`).
- Route registered in `cmd/server/routes.go`. OpenAPI added the path entry under `/functions/{functionRid}/execute` (200/400/401/404/503 documented including the 503 echo body shape).
- Tests:
  - `pkg/oms/function_param_validator_test.go` (14 cases): empty/null/{}-no-contract; typed-shape parse; pass-through-with-fresh-allocation; happy path; missing-required; required-accepts-zero-values (0, "", false); applies default; default-doesn't-override-explicit; type-mismatch; unknown-parameter; optional-accepts-nil; boolean+array+struct happy; typeless-param-accepts-any; struct-default-deep-decode.
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function_execute_test.go` (10 cases): happy path forwards coerced params + RID to executor; missing-required → 400 with parameter+code; type-mismatch → 400; unknown-parameter → 400; defaults applied before dispatch; no-signature accepts any input shape; empty body works when no required params; function-not-found → 404; no-executor wired → 503 with coerced-params echo; executor error → 400.
- All `go test -short ./pkg/... ./internal/... ./cmd/...` green; `go vet ./...` clean; contract-tests trio (TestContract_AllRoutesDocumented + TestContract_NoOrphanedSpecPaths + TestContract_EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical) green; `go build ./...` clean.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/oms/function.go` (added ParseFunctionSignature + ParsedFunctionSignature/FunctionParam/FunctionReturn types + ValidateAndCoerceFunctionParams + FunctionParamError; added types import)
  - `pkg/oms/function_executor.go` (new — narrow `FunctionExecutor` interface)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers.go` (functionExecutor field + SetFunctionExecutor setter)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function.go` (new ExecuteFunction handler)
  - `pkg/oms/function_param_validator_test.go` (new, 14 tests)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function_execute_test.go` (new, 10 tests)
  - `cmd/server/routes.go` (1 new route under the existing Function block)
  - `api/openapi.yaml` + `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` (new path entry with 200/400/401/404/503 responses)
  - `prd.json` (US-216 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The "runtime validator" for any signature-typed surface (functions, action params, automate effects) follows the same shape: PARSE the signature into a typed Go view → for-each declared param check required/default/type → reject unknown keys → return a fresh map. Don't try to bolt validation onto the shape-checker (`ValidateFunctionSignature`); the shape checker validates the SIGNATURE, the parameter validator validates VALUES against an already-valid signature. Two responsibilities, two functions.
  - When a typed error needs both a structured payload (for handlers to map to 400) AND a legacy Error() string (for log lines / non-handler callers), define a small struct with public fields + a tight Error() method. `oms.FunctionParamError` and `types.EnumViolationError` (US-052) both follow this shape — handlers do `errors.As(err, &pe)` then read `pe.Code` / `pe.Parameter` directly.
  - `apierror.NewInvalidParameter("InvalidParameter:"+paramName, map[string]string{...})` is the canonical shape for "validation rejected the user's value". The ErrorCode carries the parameter name as a suffix so log filters can grep for a specific bad-input by name; the Parameters map carries `parameter`+`code`+`reason` so structured consumers don't have to parse the code suffix.
  - For optional executor-style hooks (`SetFunctionExecutor`, `SetQueryExecutor`, `SetLinkPropertyStore`), the right degraded-mode response is NOT a generic 500 — it's a 503 with whatever pre-execution work IS available echoed in the body. Here the validator runs to completion regardless of executor state, so the 503 response can still tell the caller "your params are valid; we just can't execute right now." Friendly to clients debugging in non-prod environments.
  - Empty body handling in ExecuteFunction: `r.ContentLength == 0` short-circuits before `ReadJSON` so the handler tolerates `POST .../execute` with no body at all (callers MAY pass an empty body when every param has a default). Naive `ReadJSON(r, &body)` against a nil body errors out with "EOF" — guard it.
  - Test the "no contract" / "with contract" boundary explicitly. The "no signature ⇒ accept everything" rule is easy to forget: it's tempting to make the validator strict-by-default, but every legacy Function predates US-215 and has no signature, so a strict-by-default validator silently breaks them all. Two test cases (no-contract pass-through + unknown-rejected-when-contract-declared) lock the right semantics.

## 2026-04-18 - US-217 Function 版本管理
- Migration `000041_function_semver_version` converts `functions.version INTEGER` → `version TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '1.0.0'`. Existing rows backfill as `<n>.0.0` so legacy data stays addressable; the (ontology_rid, name) UNIQUE moves to (ontology_rid, name, version) so multiple semver builds of the same function name coexist. The data-type swap is gated on `data_type = 'integer'` and the constraint adds use a pg_constraint NOT EXISTS guard, so re-running the migration is a no-op.
- `oms.Function.Version` becomes `string` (semver) — the wire JSON for the field flips from integer to string. Tests across `pkg/oms/{handlers_function,handlers_function_us215,handlers_function_execute,execute_query_goja,handlers_import}_test.go` plus `test/integration/{function_action,goja_runtime}_test.go` updated to use `Version: "1.0.0"` literals; the import-handler JSON body in `handlers_import_test.go` updated to send `"version": "1.0.0"` since the JSON Decoder rejects integer ⇒ string. Non-test impact: ~5 production lines (handler default + import carry-over + 4 PG repo Scan/Exec sites).
- New `pkg/oms/function_semver.go`:
  - `Semver{Major, Minor, Patch, Pre}` typed view; `ParseSemver(string)` rejects empty / non-MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH / non-numeric / negative segments. Supports `-PRE` suffix; build metadata is preserved in Pre (no separate field).
  - `CompareSemver(a, b) int` — numeric per-segment, then pre-release `<` no-pre (per semver §11), then lexical pre comparison.
  - `SortFunctionsByVersionDesc([]Function)` — primary key Name asc, secondary key parsed-Version desc. Unparseable versions sort to the bottom of their name group so a malformed row never hides a valid one. Used by both ListFunctions and ListFunctionVersionsByName so latest is always position 0 within a name.
  - `validateFunctionVersion(string)` is the Function.Validate hook (extends the existing runtime + signature gate to also enforce semver shape).
  - `Function.NormalisedVersion()` substitutes empty → `DefaultFunctionVersion` ("1.0.0"). Same shape as `NormalisedRuntime()`.
- `oms.Repository` interface gains two narrow read methods (kept narrow, no batch / cursor / etc.):
  - `GetFunctionByNameVersion(ctx, ontologyRID, name, version)` — exact (name, version) lookup; ErrNotFound when nothing matches.
  - `ListFunctionVersionsByName(ctx, ontologyRID, name)` — every stored semver of the named function, sorted latest-first.
  Existing `GetFunctionByName` now post-sorts by semver desc and returns the LATEST when multiple rows share a name (pre-US-217 callers transparently get latest semantics).
- `*PGRepository`:
  - `CreateFunction` runs `NormalisedVersion()` on the way in so callers can omit the field and the DB still stores the `1.0.0` default.
  - `ListFunctions` orders by `name` at SQL (lexical version sort would put `10.0.0` before `2.0.0`) and re-sorts in Go via `SortFunctionsByVersionDesc`. New helper `scanFunctions(pgx.Rows)` factored out so the per-row signature/runtime decoding stays in one place across the four read paths.
  - `GetFunctionByName` issues one query that may return multiple rows (one per version) and picks the latest after sorting; falls back to RID-equality short-circuit when the URL segment IS a RID.
- Handler updates (`pkg/oms/handlers_function.go`):
  - `CreateFunctionRequest` gains `Version string` (omitempty); handler defaults to `DefaultFunctionVersion` and validates via `Function.Validate()`. Duplicate (ontology, name, version) returns 409 `FunctionAlreadyExists` with `name` + `version` parameters echoed.
  - `UpdateFunctionRequest.Version` becomes `string` (legacy was `int`); empty preserves the existing row's version.
  - `splitFunctionRef("name@1.0.0")` → ("name", "1.0.0", true); `splitFunctionRef("ri.ontology.main.function.f1")` → ("", "", false). RIDs never contain `@`, so the split is unambiguous against the existing "rid or name" paths.
  - `resolveFunctionRef(ctx, ontologyRID, ref)` is the shared "url segment → row" helper. GetFunctionV2 + ExecuteFunction both go through it so `name@version` pinning works on read AND execute paths uniformly.
  - New `ListFunctionVersions` handler: `GET /api/v2/ontologies/{o}/functions/{functionName}/versions` returns `{name, data: [Function...]}` sorted latest-first; 404 when no versions exist for the name.
- Mock-repo plumbing kept consistent across the test tree (~8 files): `mock_functions_test.go` CreateFunction now rejects (ontology, name, version) duplicates with `ErrDuplicate` so the 409 path is exercised in pure-mock tests; the `GetFunctionByName` mock returns latest by SortFunctionsByVersionDesc; new methods stubbed in `pkg/{actions,index,oss,links}/...` and `test/{e2e,northwind,chinook}/mock_link_edges_test.go` plus `pkg/oms/cached_repository_test.go` noopRepo. Pattern: 8 stubs, 2 lines each, return ErrNotFound / nil.

- OpenAPI (`api/openapi.yaml` + embedded `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml`):
  - `Function.version` schema flips from `type: integer` to `type: string` with semver example.
  - `createFunction` request body gains `version` (semver string, defaults `1.0.0`, 409 on duplicate).
  - `updateFunction` request body's `version` flips from integer to string.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When a numeric field on a wire model becomes a typed string (semver, RID, enum-as-string), the migration is the easy half — the cascade is in test literals and JSON bodies. `grep -rn 'Version: 1[,)}]' --include='*.go'` plus a quick `grep -n '"version":' *_test.go` finds them all in one pass; sed-replacing the Go side then hand-fixing the JSON literal (since the decoder distinguishes 1 vs "1") is roughly 15 minutes for a registry-scale field.
  - Lexical version sort is broken for semver: `ORDER BY version` puts "10.0.0" BEFORE "2.0.0". Always re-sort in Go via the parsed Semver after the SQL query (or build a generated-column with major/minor/patch ints if you need the DB to do it). The Go-side sort costs O(n log n) for a tiny n (functions are small) — not worth a generated column.
  - `name@version` URL pinning is a single-character split that requires NO router changes: the `@` is opaque to chi, and RIDs never contain it (they use `.` separators). Centralise the parse in one helper (`splitFunctionRef`) and route both the GET and the EXECUTE handlers through the same resolver — keeps the "pin works on every endpoint" invariant easy to maintain.
  - "List X versions" is a separate endpoint, NOT a query param on the main GetX. The wire shape diverges (it's a wrapper `{name, data: [...]}`, not a single Function), and the cache semantics differ (it reads N rows). Same lesson as US-212's `/resolved` route — when the response shape diverges, the URL diverges.
  - When changing the type of a struct field that's set in 8+ mockRepo stubs, do it in two passes: first the field declaration + production code (compile errors guide you to the call sites), then the per-mock update. The second pass is ~3 lines per mock for the new interface methods. Don't try to add backwards-compat shims (e.g. keeping both `int` and `string` Version) — the cascade is already manageable, and a parallel field would double the maintenance surface forever.
  - Migrations that change a column type need an existence guard on `data_type` so re-running them on an already-migrated DB is a no-op. Combine with `pg_constraint` checks for the constraint adds — both are required to keep the migration idempotent in CI environments where the migration table may run a fresh apply against a partially-migrated schema.

## 2026-04-18 - US-218 Function 执行配额与超时
- Bumped `pkg/functions.DefaultConfig` to the PRD-mandated 5s CPU / 128MiB memory ceilings. The goja runtime already had a heap-poll watchdog on `runtime.MemStats.HeapAlloc` — the change is literally the constant.
- New `pkg/functions/fnerrors` subpackage publishing `ErrTimeout` and `ErrMemoryLimit` sentinel errors. Lives in a sibling subpackage (NOT the main `pkg/functions` package) so `pkg/oms` can import the sentinels for `errors.Is` dispatch without transitively pulling in pkg/oss — the main `pkg/functions` package imports pkg/oss via goja_shim.go and pkg/oss already imports pkg/oms, so a direct pkg/oms ↔ pkg/functions dependency would cycle.
- `pkg/functions.wrapGojaError` translates a `*goja.InterruptedError` into the typed sentinel based on the `vm.Interrupt(...)` tag it carries. Watchdog now tags interrupts with `function.timeout` / `function.memory` constants so the unwrap is discriminated deterministically (was: free-text strings like "execution timeout exceeded" that callers would have had to pattern-match).
- New `pkg/functions/quota` package: a per-key rolling-window `Limiter` (bounded FIFO of timestamps, lazy eviction, injectable clock via `SetNowFunc`). `DefaultLimiter()` returns a 60/minute bucket matching the PRD "每分钟调用配额（按 realm）" wording. Zero-config (`limit=0` or `window=0`) and nil-receiver Allow calls both pass through — degraded-mode test routers without a limiter never silently throttle.
- `pkg/oms` additions: `FunctionQuotaLimiter` narrow interface (single `Allow(key) bool` method), `DefaultFunctionExecutionTimeout = 5 * time.Second` constant, and `OMSHandler.SetFunctionQuotaLimiter` setter wired alongside the existing `SetFunctionExecutor` family. The narrow interface keeps `pkg/oms` free of the quota package dep — production wiring in `cmd/server` will pass `quota.DefaultLimiter()` which satisfies it implicitly.
- `ExecuteFunction` handler (`pkg/oms/handlers_function.go`) adds three new gates in order: (1) per-realm `limiter.Allow(realmFromRID(fn.RID))` → 429 `FunctionQuotaExceeded` with `realm`+`functionRid` in `parameters`; (2) `context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), DefaultFunctionExecutionTimeout)` so the 5s budget applies to every FunctionExecutor implementation (HTTP, remote, in-process Goja, ...); (3) post-exec `errors.Is(err, fnerrors.ErrTimeout) || errors.Is(execCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded)` → 408 `FunctionExecutionTimeout`, `errors.Is(err, fnerrors.ErrMemoryLimit)` → 429 `FunctionMemoryLimitExceeded`. The two 429 cases are distinguishable by `errorName`.
- `pkg/apierror.NewRequestTimeout` is new: constructs `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` / HTTP 408, matching the existing `NewTooManyRequests` / `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` convention. Same one-line addition pattern as NewValidationEnum + NewConflict.
- `realmFromRID(r string) string` centralises the `ri.{service}.{realm}.{resourceType}.{uuid}` parse for the quota key. Falls back to `"main"` when the RID is malformed so even legacy rows that predate strict RID validation stay quota-enforced (not unbounded).
- OpenAPI: the `executeFunction` responses list grows a 408 and a 429 entry documenting `FunctionExecutionTimeout` / `FunctionQuotaExceeded` / `FunctionMemoryLimitExceeded`. Inline APIError shape used instead of `$ref: APIError` because the canonical spec never declared the schema; embedded copy synced via `cp`.
- Tests:
  - `pkg/functions/quota/quota_test.go` (9 cases): within-limit / over-limit / key-isolation / rolling-window-evicts (with injected clock advancing past window) / limit=0 passes through / window=0 passes through / nil-receiver allows / DefaultLimiter matches PRD constants / concurrent Allow from 200 goroutines lands exactly `limit=100` allowed + `100` denied.
  - `pkg/functions/goja_runtime_us218_test.go` (4 cases): timeout→ErrTimeout sentinel but NOT ErrMemoryLimit; memory→ErrMemoryLimit but NOT ErrTimeout; user-thrown error matches neither sentinel; DefaultConfig has 5s/128MiB.
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function_quota_test.go` (6 cases): quota-exhausts-returns-429 with `realm` echoed; limiter-keyed-by-realm (single call → `limiter.seen = ["main"]`); timeout-sentinel→408 with `timeout` parameter; memory-sentinel→429 `FunctionMemoryLimitExceeded`; outer context-deadline propagation→408 (exercises a FunctionExecutor that honours ctx but does not wrap fnerrors.ErrTimeout explicitly); no-limiter-wired = unbounded.

- Files changed:
  - `pkg/functions/fnerrors/fnerrors.go` (new)
  - `pkg/functions/goja_runtime.go` (DefaultConfig bump + tagged interrupts + wrapGojaError)
  - `pkg/functions/goja_runtime_us218_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/functions/quota/quota.go` (new)
  - `pkg/functions/quota/quota_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/apierror/error.go` (NewRequestTimeout)
  - `pkg/oms/function_executor.go` (FunctionQuotaLimiter interface + DefaultFunctionExecutionTimeout)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers.go` (functionQuotaLimiter field + SetFunctionQuotaLimiter)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function.go` (quota check + 5s timeout + 408/429 mapping + realmFromRID)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function_quota_test.go` (new, 6 tests)
  - `api/openapi.yaml` + `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` (408 / 429 response docs)
  - `prd.json` (US-218 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Goja's `*InterruptedError.Value()` is the cleanest signal for differentiating interrupt causes. Tag each `vm.Interrupt(reason)` call with a small set of package-private sentinels (e.g. `"function.timeout"` / `"function.memory"`) and have `wrapGojaError` dispatch on `ie.Value()` — this beats parsing error strings and survives downstream format changes.
  - Cross-package sentinel errors for HTTP dispatch: when two packages need to agree on "this error means 408", put the sentinel in a leaf subpackage with ZERO imports from the rest of the tree. Here `pkg/functions/fnerrors` has no oss/oms/types deps, so both `pkg/functions` (the runtime) and `pkg/oms` (the handler) import it safely. A top-level `pkg/functions.ErrTimeout` would work for the runtime but `pkg/oms` can't import `pkg/functions` without a cycle (functions → oss → oms).
  - Rolling-window quota limiter: a per-key `[]time.Time` FIFO with lazy eviction on every Allow is ~20 lines of Go and uniformly O(expired-entries). Keep it sorted by virtue of append-order; the eviction scan is forward-only. Don't reach for `golang.org/x/time/rate` unless you actually need token-bucket semantics — the sliding window is a better fit for "per minute" PRD language.
  - Zero-value "pass-through" limiter: callers that forget to wire a limiter should NOT be silently throttled. Check `limit <= 0 || window <= 0` at the top of Allow and return true. Pairs with nil-receiver support (Allow on a `*Limiter(nil)` returns true) so both `SetFunctionQuotaLimiter(nil)` and an unset limiter behave identically.
  - Handler-side context deadline: wrapping `r.Context()` with `context.WithTimeout` AROUND the executor call guarantees the 5s CPU ceiling even when the FunctionExecutor is an HTTP dispatcher or a remote runtime that doesn't honour its own config. The runtime-internal watchdog is belt-and-braces for in-process Goja, but the handler's wrap is the portable guarantee.
  - Two distinct 429 reasons (quota vs memory) should be distinguishable by `errorName`, not status code. `FunctionQuotaExceeded` vs `FunctionMemoryLimitExceeded` lets SDKs make retry/backoff decisions without parsing the human-readable reason field. Same lesson US-216 called out for `code` in `FunctionParamError`.
  - Realm extraction from RIDs: the `ri.{service}.{realm}.{resourceType}.{uuid}` format is self-describing, so deriving the quota key from `rid.Parse(fn.RID).Realm` avoids plumbing a separate `realm` column or forcing callers to pass it. Fallback to `"main"` on parse failure means even legacy/malformed rows stay enforceable.

## 2026-04-18 - US-219 Function Result Streaming
- `ExecuteFunction` (`pkg/oms/handlers_function.go`) now branches on `?stream=1`. Pre-execution gates (function lookup, per-realm quota, parameter validation, no-executor 503) stay JSON — the NDJSON contract only kicks in once the executor has been dispatched.
- New `writeFunctionStream(w, fnRID, result, execErr, execCtx)` helper emits the response with `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (so nginx-style proxies don't sit on the body). Each line is one of:
  - `{"item": <element>}` — one per element when `result` is `[]interface{}`, single line for a non-nil scalar, zero lines for an empty slice / nil.
  - `{"error": {"code","reason","functionRid"}}` — terminal line on executor failure. Codes mirror the JSON-mode mapping: `FunctionExecutionTimeout` (errors.Is `fnerrors.ErrTimeout` OR `execCtx.Err()==DeadlineExceeded`), `FunctionMemoryLimitExceeded` (errors.Is `fnerrors.ErrMemoryLimit`), else `FunctionExecutionFailed`.
- `flusher.Flush()` after every line so iterating clients receive items as they're encoded; `enc := json.NewEncoder(w)` keeps trailing newlines per NDJSON convention.
- OpenAPI: `executeFunction` gained the `stream` query param (`enum: ["1"]`) and a second `application/x-ndjson` schema entry under the existing 200 response. Description block calls out the `{"item":...}` / terminal `{"error":...}` line shape and the in-band-error guarantee. Embedded copy synced via `cp`.
- New `pkg/oms/handlers_function_stream_test.go` (9 cases) — array-result emits one line per element, scalar emits single line, empty slice emits zero, executor error → in-band error line with `code=FunctionExecutionFailed`, timeout sentinel → `FunctionExecutionTimeout`, memory sentinel → `FunctionMemoryLimitExceeded`, validation 400 still returns regular JSON 400 (NOT NDJSON), function-not-found still 404, no-executor still 503, request context deadline → in-band timeout line.
- Python SDK additions:
  - `weave_client.functions.FunctionsAPI` — new namespace exposing `client.functions.execute(ontology, function_ref, parameters)` (regular call, returns the deserialized `result`) and `client.functions.execute_stream(...)` (generator yielding each NDJSON `item`; raises `WeaveError` on terminal `{"error":...}` lines with `error_name` mapped to the server-supplied `code`). Pre-execution HTTP errors raise BEFORE the generator yields its first item.
  - `weave_client._http.Transport.stream_lines(method, url, ...)` — returns `(status, headers, line_iterator)` so the SDK can consume large NDJSON responses without buffering. Uses `httpx.Client.send(stream=True)` when httpx is installed; falls back to iterating the urllib response file-handle line-by-line so minimal-deps environments still stream correctly.
  - `weave_client.client.Client.__init__` wires the new namespace alongside `ontologies`/`objects`/`actions`/`objectsets`.
- New `sdk/python/tests/test_functions.py` (9 tests across 2 classes): regular execute returns `result` payload, accepts `name@version` URL-encoded segment, validation/404 errors raise typed exceptions; streaming yields items in order, query string carries `stream=1`, terminal error mid-stream raises `WeaveError` (caller can iterate up to the error then catch), empty result yields nothing, pre-execution 400 raises BEFORE first yield, scalar item is yielded as a value (not wrapped). Streaming tests use a separate stdlib HTTPServer stub that emits `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson` so the iterator contract is exercised end-to-end against a real socket.
- All `go test -short ./pkg/... ./internal/... ./cmd/...` green; `go vet ./...` clean; `go build ./...` clean; contract-tests trio (`TestContract_AllRoutesDocumented` + `TestContract_NoOrphanedSpecPaths` + `TestContract_EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical`) green; `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` 78/78 green.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function.go` (writeFunctionStream + stream branch in ExecuteFunction)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function_stream_test.go` (new, 9 tests)
  - `api/openapi.yaml` + `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` (stream query param + ndjson schema under 200)
  - `sdk/python/weave_client/_http.py` (Transport.stream_lines + Iterator import)
  - `sdk/python/weave_client/functions.py` (new — FunctionsAPI + _consume_ndjson)
  - `sdk/python/weave_client/client.py` (wires FunctionsAPI as `client.functions`)
  - `sdk/python/tests/test_functions.py` (new, 9 tests)
  - `prd.json` (US-219 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - In-band error reporting is the only viable pattern for NDJSON streams. By the time the executor fails, the server has already written `200 OK` headers — flipping to a 4xx/5xx response is impossible. Reserve the JSON status-code path for pre-execution gates (validation, 404, quota, no-executor); all post-execution failures must surface as a terminal `{"error": ...}` line. SDKs MUST handle both: try/except around the generator-returning call to catch HTTP errors, AND try/except inside the loop to catch in-band errors. Document this dual contract explicitly — it's the most common SDK consumer mistake.
  - `enc := json.NewEncoder(w)` writes a trailing newline by default — this is what makes the output NDJSON-compliant. Do NOT manually append `\n` after `json.Marshal`; you'd double-newline and break some strict parsers. Pair every `enc.Encode(...)` with a `flusher.Flush()` call in the same line — the 100ms-ish flush latency users feel between lines comes from the response writer's buffer, not from the encoder.
  - `Cache-Control: no-cache` + `X-Accel-Buffering: no` is the standard NDJSON header pair for streaming through nginx/Cloudflare proxies. Without `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, nginx will buffer the entire response before forwarding — defeating the streaming the SDK iterator depends on. Same trick used by Server-Sent Events endpoints.
  - When designing iterator-based SDK methods, return the generator from a non-generator function (here `execute_stream` is `def`, not just `yield from`). That way the HTTP request fires when the user calls `execute_stream(...)`, not when they pull the first item — which means HTTP errors raise eagerly at the call site, before the user's `for` loop. Lazy generators work but bury HTTP errors inside the iteration which is a worse UX.
  - `http.Flusher` is an OPTIONAL interface on `http.ResponseWriter`. Always do `flusher, _ := w.(http.Flusher)` and guard `if flusher != nil { flusher.Flush() }` — `httptest.ResponseRecorder` and some custom test writers don't implement it. The handler stays correct (no flushing means callers see all lines at end-of-response, which is fine for tests).
  - Python `httpx.Client.send(req, stream=True)` returns a Response whose `iter_lines()` consumes the body line-by-line. Pair it with a `try/finally` that calls `resp.close()` so the socket is returned to the pool — otherwise the test suite's connection cap can leak across runs. The urllib fallback iterates the response object directly (`for raw in r:` yields one line per iteration); both code paths share the same SDK-side `_consume_ndjson` so the iterator contract is identical regardless of transport.
  - `Accept: application/x-ndjson` on the request side is courtesy — the server doesn't content-negotiate (`?stream=1` is the actual switch) — but it makes the wire trace self-documenting and keeps the contract clear if a future server adds explicit content-type negotiation.

## 2026-04-18 - US-220 Function-to-Function 调用
- New leaf subpackage `pkg/functions/fncall` owns the context-propagated call stack + depth/cycle sentinels. Zero imports from the rest of the tree — same reasoning as `pkg/functions/fnerrors` (US-218) — so pkg/oms HTTP handlers (future US-222 Function-backed Actions) can seed a top-level frame via `fncall.WithFrame(ctx, ref)` without risking an import cycle through pkg/oss. Public surface: `MaxDepth = 8`, `ErrDepthExceeded`, `ErrCycleDetected`, `WithStack(ctx, []string) ctx`, `StackFromContext(ctx) []string`, `WithFrame(ctx, ref) ctx` (always allocates a fresh slice so concurrent branches of the context tree stay isolated).
- `pkg/functions/goja_shim_functions.go` (new) defines `FunctionCaller` (single-method interface `CallFunction(ctx, ref, params) (interface{}, error)`) and `Runtime.SetFunctionCaller`. The `registerWeaveShim` method installs a global `weave` object on the VM with `weave.callFunction(ref, params)`. When no caller is wired the global stays absent — matches the `ontology.*` shim pattern (US-066/US-091) so scripts that don't use it see the same sandbox as before.
- Guardrail flow in the shim: on each `weave.callFunction(ref, params)` call the host reads the stack carried by ctx. If `len(stack) >= fncall.MaxDepth` it panics with `fmt.Errorf("%w: depth=... ref=...", fncall.ErrDepthExceeded)`; if `ref` already appears on the stack it panics with `ErrCycleDetected`. Otherwise it constructs `childCtx = fncall.WithFrame(ctx, ref)`, invokes the configured FunctionCaller, and exports the result back into the VM via `vm.ToValue(result)`. Non-object `params` arguments (arrays, strings, ...) are rejected with `weave.callFunction: params must be an object`.
- `pkg/functions/goja_runtime.go` picks up the new shim via `r.registerWeaveShim(vm, execCtx)` (one line added alongside the existing `registerOntologyShim` call) and a new `functionCaller` field on `Runtime`.
- `panic(vm.NewGoError(fmt.Errorf("%w: ...", sentinel)))` is the crucial shape — the `%w` wrap survives goja's `*Exception` wrap AND `wrapGojaError`'s own `"execution error: %w"` wrap, so upstream `errors.Is(err, fncall.ErrCycleDetected)` still returns true. Dedicated tests (`TestWeaveCallFunction_CyclicErrorUnwrapsToSentinel`, `TestWeaveCallFunction_DepthErrorUnwrapsToSentinel`) lock this invariant in.
- Tests: `pkg/functions/goja_shim_functions_test.go` (new, 12 cases):
  - Happy path: A calls `weave.callFunction("doubler", {value:21})` returns `42`, top-level wrapper returns `43`. Arg passes through + single call recorded.
  - Params: capturing wrapper asserts the ref, string/number/bool fields flow through unchanged (goja int64 for whole numbers).
  - Absent shim: `typeof weave === "undefined"` when no caller is wired (matches the degraded-mode shape the ontology shim already establishes).
  - Cycle A↔B: seed top-level with `fncall.WithFrame(ctx, "A")`, then A→B→A throws with `cycle` in the message AND `errors.Is(err, ErrCycleDetected)` true.
  - Self-recursion: with top-level seeded, a function calling itself trips the cycle detector on the first attempt.
  - Depth limit: a 10-deep forward chain rejects at the 9th link (stack would exceed `MaxDepth=8`). Asserts `fncall.MaxDepth == 8` explicitly so the PRD constant never silently drifts.
  - Just-under limit: 8-deep chain completes and returns 42 (confirms the ceiling is inclusive — exactly 8 frames allowed, 9 rejected).
  - Unknown ref: executor failure surfaces as a JS error containing the ref name.
  - Ref required: omitted / empty-string refs both throw.
  - Sentinel round-trips (cycle + depth) — `errors.Is` must match after the full goja + runtime wrap chain.
  - `WithFrame` round-trip: stack reads back in order, parent slice never mutated when a child forks a new frame.
- `go vet ./...` clean, `go build ./...` clean, `go test -short -count=1 ./pkg/... ./internal/... ./cmd/...` all green (~7min), contract-tests trio (AllRoutesDocumented + NoOrphanedSpecPaths + EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical) green.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/functions/fncall/fncall.go` (new)
  - `pkg/functions/goja_shim_functions.go` (new — FunctionCaller + Runtime.SetFunctionCaller + registerWeaveShim)
  - `pkg/functions/goja_shim_functions_test.go` (new, 12 cases)
  - `pkg/functions/goja_runtime.go` (functionCaller field + one-line registerWeaveShim call)
  - `prd.json` (US-220 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Seed the top-level frame BEFORE calling `runtime.Execute`. If the handler / test harness just hands a clean `context.Background()` to the runtime, A→B→A cycles slip through because A isn't on the stack during its own execution — the detector flags at depth 3 (A→B→A→B attempt) instead of depth 2. Seeding is a one-line `ctx = fncall.WithFrame(ctx, fn.RID)` at the boundary; the runtime itself can't do it because it doesn't know its own ref. US-222 (Function-backed Actions) should do the same seeding when action prepare invokes a function.
  - `fncall.WithFrame` MUST allocate a fresh slice on every push. If it were `return WithStack(ctx, append(stack, ref))` the parent's slice header would remain untouched but the backing array could be mutated when an unrelated context branch forks another frame that lands in the same capacity window. Tests locked this in via `WithStackRoundTrip`.
  - Tests that thread `errors.Is` through a sandbox runtime: the wrap chain is Goja `*Exception` → `vm.NewGoError(err)` → `wrapGojaError("execution error: %w")`. As long as every hop uses `%w` the final error still unwraps to the original sentinel. Explicit `errors.Is` tests beat string-matching on `err.Error()` — the message format is cosmetic and can legitimately change in future goja releases.
  - Rejecting the 9th nested call (not the 8th) matches the PRD's "递归深度上限 8" wording. `len(stack) >= MaxDepth` is the correct gate: stack already has 8 frames means 8 calls are in flight, so a new push would make it 9 — and that's the call we reject. `DepthJustUnderLimit` test locks in that exactly 8 frames DO complete.
  - When the FunctionCaller impl lives outside pkg/functions (future cmd/server wiring), it MUST honour the incoming ctx — in particular the stack carried via `fncall.StackFromContext(ctx)`. Any impl that does `context.Background()` or `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` breaks the depth/cycle invariants the shim relies on. The interface doc calls this out.
  - The ontology + weave shims are symmetric: both register a global on the VM only when a client is wired, both use `panic(vm.NewGoError(...))` to surface Go-side failures as JS exceptions, both read ctx via closure. When adding the next host binding (e.g. `weave.now()`, `weave.emit(event)`, `weave.log()`), put a `registerXxxShim(vm, ctx)` method on `*Runtime` and add a one-line call in `Execute` — matches the established pattern.

## 2026-04-18 - US-221 Function 结果缓存
- New leaf subpackage `pkg/functions/cache` (no repo imports — `container/list` + stdlib only) ships a bounded `Cache` with LRU eviction + per-entry TTL plus a `cache.Key(rid, version, params)` helper. Defaults: 10k entries / 5-minute TTL via `NewDefault()` (PRD US-221 mandate). `SetNowFunc` injects a clock so TTL behaviour is deterministic in tests — same convention as `pkg/functions/quota.Limiter` and `pkg/oss/computed.Resolver`.
- Cache key is `<rid>@<version>#<sha256(canonical-params)>`. `canonicalJSON` sorts map keys recursively before encoding, so `{a:1,b:2}` and `{b:2,a:1}` collapse to one bucket. `nil` params and empty `map[string]interface{}{}` hash to the same `sha256("{}")` so the absence-of-params case stays deterministic. Different params and different versions both produce distinct keys.
- Cache is intentionally process-local. The 5-minute TTL is the only invalidation mechanism — there's no cluster pubsub yet, and updating a function's source bumps the row's `version` (US-217), which automatically forks a new cache namespace.
- `pkg/oms.FunctionResultCache` is a narrow Get/Put interface (matches `FunctionQuotaLimiter` shape from US-218). `OMSHandler.SetFunctionResultCache(c)` wires the optional dep; nil/unset cache disables result caching, so degraded-mode test routers without a cache wired keep the legacy "always re-run" semantics.
- `Function.Pure bool` (json:"pure,omitempty") added to the model. Migration `000042_function_pure` adds a `BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE` column with `IF NOT EXISTS` so re-running on a partially-migrated DB is a no-op. `pg_repository.go` updated in 7 spots: INSERT, UPDATE, four SELECT sites (GetFunction / GetFunctionByName / GetFunctionByNameVersion / ListFunctionVersionsByName + ListFunctions), and the shared `scanFunctions` row decoder. Read paths use `COALESCE(pure, FALSE)` so legacy rows decode cleanly.
- `CreateFunctionRequest.Pure bool` accepts an opt-in at create time. `UpdateFunctionRequest.Pure *bool` uses pointer semantics so callers can distinguish "omit ⇒ preserve" from "send false ⇒ disable caching". Same shape as `UpdateFunctionRequest.Runtime *string` (US-217).
- `ExecuteFunction` (`pkg/oms/handlers_function.go`) gates cache lookup on `fn.Pure && !streaming && h.functionResultCache != nil`. Cache hits return `{functionRid, result, cached: true}` and skip the handler-side 5s deadline + executor call entirely. Misses fall through to the existing dispatch; on success the result is written to the cache before responding. Errors are NEVER cached — caller may have raced an external state change (and impure functions don't cache at all, but even pure ones might surface a transient error worth re-running). Streaming responses (?stream=1) skip the cache to keep the in-band-error contract from US-219 intact.
- OpenAPI: `Function` schema gained a `pure: boolean (default false)` field; `createFunction` requestBody picks up `pure` (opt-in at create); `updateFunction` requestBody picks up `pure` (preserve when omitted, toggle when sent). The successful execute response gets a `cached: boolean` field with the US-221 caveat documented. Embedded copy synced via `cp api/openapi.yaml cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml`.
- Tests:
  - `pkg/functions/cache/cache_test.go` (22 cases): hit/miss/TTL-expiry/refresh-on-Put/LRU-eviction/zero-capacity-passthrough/zero-TTL-passthrough/nil-receiver-safe/PRD-defaults/Invalidate/Reset, plus Key stability under map insertion order, nested-map canonicalisation, different-params-different-key, different-versions-different-key, nil-vs-empty-map equivalence, version-omitted determinism, 16-goroutine concurrent stress under capped LRU.
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function_cache_test.go` (8 cases): pure cache miss-then-hit (executor called once, cache populated, hit returns `cached:true`); impure functions never touch the cache; no-cache-wired falls through (every call re-runs); different params produce distinct entries; param map order doesn't matter (`{a,b}` and `{b,a}` share a bucket); cache key prefix is `<rid>@<version>#`; errors NEVER cached (3 failures = 3 executor calls + 0 puts); streaming requests skip the cache entirely (no cache writes after 2 stream calls).
- All `go test -short -count=1 ./pkg/... ./internal/... ./cmd/...` green; `go vet ./...` clean; contract-tests trio (AllRoutesDocumented + NoOrphanedSpecPaths + EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical) green; OpenAPI spec embedding kept in sync.
- Files changed:
  - `migrations/000042_function_pure.up.sql` (new)
  - `migrations/000042_function_pure.down.sql` (new)
  - `pkg/functions/cache/cache.go` (new — LRU+TTL Cache + Key helper + canonicalJSON)
  - `pkg/functions/cache/cache_test.go` (new, 22 cases)
  - `pkg/oms/models.go` (Function.Pure field)
  - `pkg/oms/pg_repository.go` (pure column in INSERT/UPDATE/4 SELECTs/scanFunctions)
  - `pkg/oms/function_executor.go` (FunctionResultCache narrow interface)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers.go` (functionResultCache field + SetFunctionResultCache setter)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function.go` (cache import, Pure on Create/UpdateFunctionRequest, cache hit/miss branch in ExecuteFunction, functionResultCacheKey helper)
  - `pkg/oms/handlers_function_cache_test.go` (new, 8 cases)
  - `api/openapi.yaml` + `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` (Function.pure + createFunction.pure + updateFunction.pure + execute response cached field)
  - `prd.json` (US-221 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Cache key MUST canonicalise nested structures, not just top-level map keys. `json.Marshal` on a `map[string]interface{}` already sorts top-level keys alphabetically, but values that are themselves maps (or slices of maps) inherit Go's nondeterministic iteration order, so `{a:{x:1,y:2}}` can hash differently across runs. The recursive `canonicalJSON` walker fixes this; the `TestKey_NestedMapsCanonicalised` test would have failed otherwise. When reaching for `json.Marshal` as a "canonical" form, walk yourself unless you're sure every value is a scalar.
  - Pointer-typed Update DTO field (`Pure *bool`) is the right shape for ANY boolean toggle on an Update request. Bare `bool` collapses "omit ⇒ preserve" and "send false ⇒ clear" into one, silently disabling the feature whenever a partial update doesn't mention the field. `UpdateFunctionRequest.Runtime *string` and `UpdateLinkTypeRequest.IsRequired *bool` are prior art for this pattern; follow the same shape for any toggleable optional setting.
  - Streaming endpoints + result caches don't mix without extra work. The cached value is a single materialised result, but a streaming response emits items one at a time over an open socket. Reconstituting items from cache would need a `[]interface{}` projection layer plus per-item `flusher.Flush()` calls — strictly more complexity than US-221 calls for. Cleanest answer is to skip the cache on `?stream=1` and document it. If a future story adds per-item streaming-cache, the gate is the single `cacheable := fn.Pure && !streaming && ...` line.
  - Test mocks scattered across `pkg/{oms,oss,links,actions,index,automate,ai}` and `test/{e2e,northwind,chinook,fixtures,integration}` would have needed a stub for any new method on `oms.Repository` — but `Function.Pure` is a struct field on the existing model, not a new method, so there's zero stub-cascade. Same trick used by US-217 (Version field), US-211 (signature/runtime fields). The `narrow-interface-on-PGRepository` rule (US-202/US-203/US-210/US-214) only applies to NEW resource types with their own table.
  - When adding a new optional `OMSHandler.SetXxx` hook, follow the trio established by US-218: (1) define a narrow interface in `pkg/oms` (one or two methods only), (2) put the concrete implementation in a leaf subpackage with no `pkg/oms` import, (3) wire via setter on `OMSHandler`. Production wiring in `cmd/server` passes the concrete impl which satisfies the interface implicitly. Keeps the dep direction clean (`cmd/server → pkg/functions/cache + pkg/oms`, never `pkg/oms → pkg/functions`) so the test routers in `pkg/oms` can run with the hook unset and exercise the degraded-mode path.
  - Never `cp api/openapi.yaml cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` from memory — always run the explicit `cp` after the canonical edit. The contract-tests trio fails with a precise diff if you forget, but it's faster to make the sync part of the same `Edit` step in the tool transcript.

## 2026-04-18 - US-222 Function-backed Actions (executeFunction rule type)
- Added a new `executeFunction` Rule type so a Function can be ONE rule among many, alongside the existing top-level `IsFunctionBacked` mechanism that REPLACES rules entirely. The two paths are intentionally orthogonal: IsFunctionBacked short-circuits Step 6 in `Executor.Prepare`; executeFunction rules participate in Step 8 alongside createObject/modifyObject/etc.
- Rule struct gained a `FunctionRID string` field and an `IsExecuteFunction()` predicate helper (mirrors the IsFormula pattern from US-201). Existing JSON unmarshal handles the new field via `omitempty`, so existing rule rows decode unchanged.
- `ExecuteRules` silently skips executeFunction rules: it's a pure helper without ctx or dispatcher. `Executor.dispatchExecuteFunctionRules(ctx, rules, actionType, params)` walks the same rules list in declaration order and, for each executeFunction entry, shallow-copies the ActionType (`atCopy := *actionType; atCopy.FunctionRID = rule.FunctionRID`) and calls the existing `FunctionDispatcher.Dispatch(ctx, &atCopy, params)`. No new dispatcher interface method needed — GojaDispatcher / HTTPDispatcher / RoutingDispatcher all read at.FunctionRID, so the override is enough.
- Function-derived edits are appended after rule-derived edits in Prepare, then the combined slice is passed through `tagEditsAsUserSource` (so the funnel consumer's user-edit-wins logic from US-021 protects them) and on through link resolution / upsert resolution / interface validation / value-type validation / fetchPrevEdits exactly like rule edits.
- `validateInterfaceRules` was previously indexing `edits[i]` for the rule's resolved ObjectType, which assumed `len(edits) == len(rules)`. Skipping executeFunction breaks that. Refactored to read `resolveObjectTypeParam(params)` directly — same source `executeRule` uses to populate edit.ObjectType for interface rules, so they can never drift. Removed the parallel-slice dependency entirely; validator now takes `params map[string]interface{}` instead of `edits []funnel.Edit`.
- `classifyPrepareError` recognises the new `"execute function rules"` error prefix as `"internal"` (matches the existing `"execute rules"` / `"function dispatch"` branches) so atomic-batch failure reporting carries the right phase label.
- Tests (`pkg/actions/execute_function_rule_test.go`, 9 cases): ParseRules accepts the new type + FunctionRID; ExecuteRules skips executeFunction without error; Executor.Apply dispatches single executeFunction rule and tags edits as user-source; Apply with mixed createObject + executeFunction returns both edits in declaration-then-fn order; Apply with multiple executeFunction rules dispatches each in order with the per-rule FunctionRID; empty FunctionRID surfaces "functionRid is required"; missing dispatcher surfaces "function dispatcher not configured"; dispatcher errors propagate verbatim through the Apply chain; the dispatcher receives the rule's FunctionRID overriding any legacy ActionType.FunctionRID, and the original ActionType pointer is NOT mutated (shallow-copy invariant).
- All `go test -short ./pkg/... ./cmd/... ./internal/...` green; `go vet ./...` clean; `go build ./...` clean. No migration / OpenAPI / mock-cascade work needed (Rule is a Go struct decoded from existing `action_types.rules` JSONB column).
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/actions/rules.go` (Rule.FunctionRID + IsExecuteFunction + ExecuteRules skips executeFunction)
  - `pkg/actions/executor.go` (Step 8b dispatchExecuteFunctionRules + validateInterfaceRules signature change + classifyPrepareError prefix)
  - `pkg/actions/execute_function_rule_test.go` (new, 9 cases)
  - `prd.json` (US-222 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Two coexisting paths for "function provides edits": (a) action-level `IsFunctionBacked=true` short-circuits Step 6, function REPLACES all rules — used when the entire action is a function call. (b) executeFunction rule type runs in Step 8 alongside other rules, function ADDS edits — used when most logic is declarative but ONE step needs a function (audit log, side-effect-driven derivation, etc.). Both share the same FunctionDispatcher infrastructure, just gated differently.
  - When a downstream loop has assumed `len(rules) == len(edits)` (1:1 from ExecuteRules), introducing a rule type that produces 0 or N edits BREAKS THE INVARIANT silently. Hunt callers BEFORE shipping. The fix here was to remove the parallel-slice dependency in `validateInterfaceRules` by reading the source-of-truth (`resolveObjectTypeParam(params)`) instead of `edits[i].ObjectType` — same answer either way for interface rules, but no fragile index alignment. Generalise: when adding a rule type that breaks 1:1, fix the consumers to read from rules + params directly rather than juggling parallel-slice indices.
  - Order convention for mixed rule + executeFunction edit lists: rule-derived edits first, then function-derived edits in rule-declaration order. Keeps the implementation a single append after ExecuteRules, no interleaving needed. Cross-action collapse already enforces "later wins", so a function-emitted MODIFY on the same PK as a rule-emitted CREATE collapses to a single CREATE with the modified properties — same semantics as if both came from rules. If a future story needs strict declaration-position interleaving, walk rules once and dispatch+executeRule on each, but you'll lose the current single-loop simplicity.
  - Shallow-copy ActionType to redirect `FunctionRID` per rule — `atCopy := *actionType; atCopy.FunctionRID = rule.FunctionRID; dispatcher.Dispatch(ctx, &atCopy, params)`. Avoids adding a `DispatchByRID` method to FunctionDispatcher (which would require updating GojaDispatcher / HTTPDispatcher / RoutingDispatcher and every test mock). The original `*oms.ActionType` is never mutated because `*actionType` dereferences and copies the struct value. Verified by an explicit test that re-reads at.FunctionRID after Apply. This trick generalises any time you want to "redirect" an existing dispatcher without changing its interface.
  - `Rule` is decoded from `action_types.rules` JSONB; new fields with `omitempty` are wire-only changes — no migration needed. The Rule shape is shared between admin write paths (which JSON-marshal Go structs) and runtime read paths (which JSON-unmarshal via `ParseRules`), so as long as the field round-trips it Just Works. Same as US-201's Formula on DerivedPropertyDef and many earlier "add a JSONB field" stories.

## 2026-04-18 - US-223 Time-travel Queries (as-of)
- Added migration `000043_object_history_validity_range` introducing `valid_from TIMESTAMPTZ` and `valid_to TIMESTAMPTZ` on object_history. Backfill is wrapped in a `DO $$ ... END$$` guard that only runs the LEAD-window UPDATE when at least one row still has NULL columns, so a re-apply on a partially-migrated DB is a no-op (matches the idempotent-CHECK pattern from US-211 / US-216). New composite index `idx_object_history_valid_range (object_type_rid, valid_from, valid_to)` powers the snapshot scan.
- `pg_repository.go.InsertObjectHistory` now stamps `valid_from = recorded_at` on every insert AND, in a follow-up UPDATE, stamps the prior open version's `valid_to = NEW.recorded_at` so consecutive versions form a half-open contiguous interval. Both branches (caller-supplied RecordedAt and DEFAULT NOW()) are covered. The UPDATE filter on `version < $4 AND valid_to IS NULL` keeps the close-out idempotent for re-runs / late-arriving rows.
- New `*PGRepository.SnapshotObjectsAt(ctx, objectTypeRID, asOf)` returning `[]oms.LatestObjectState` for every PK whose `[valid_from, valid_to)` interval covers `asOf`. DELETE rows + zero-byte new_state are dropped on read so callers see only "live at asOf" objects, never tombstones.
- `pkg/oss/objectset/snapshot.go` declares the narrow `HistorySnapshotProvider` interface (single method `SnapshotObjectsAt(ctx, ontologyAPIName, objectTypeAPIName, asOf)`) + the `ObjectSnapshot{PrimaryKey, Properties}` value type. Lives in pkg/oss/objectset to keep pkg/oms free of any oss-shaped dependencies — same direction as MediaCatalog / ComputedPropertyStore.
- `objectset.Handler` gained `historySnapshots` field + `SetHistorySnapshotProvider(p)` setter. `LoadObjects` now branches on `?asOf=<RFC3339>` BEFORE calling `executor.Execute`: invalid timestamp → `InvalidAsOf` 400; provider unset → `TimeTravelUnavailable` 400; non-base ObjectSet → `TimeTravelUnsupportedObjectSet` 400; missing objectType → `MissingObjectType` 400; provider error → `TimeTravelFailed` 400; happy path returns the snapshot rows after PK-ASC sort + select-filter + pagination + property-visibility filter (US-048 still applies in the time-travel branch).
- `cmd/server/history_snapshot_provider.go` ships `historySnapshotAdapter` — narrow `historySnapshotRepo` (GetOntology + GetObjectTypeByAPIName) for ObjectType API name → RID resolution, narrow `historySnapshotStore` (SnapshotObjectsAt) for the read, plus JSON-decode of object_history.new_state into the `map[string]interface{}` shape WireObject.FormatObject expects. Wired in main.go from the uncached `*PGRepository` (`deps.HistorySnapshotStore = pgRepo`) so the metadata cache decorator never sees the snapshot calls.
- OpenAPI: loadObjectSet now documents the `asOf` query parameter (RFC3339) plus the four error names it can return; description spells out the base-only restriction. Embedded copy synced via `cp api/openapi.yaml cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml`.
- Tests:
  - `pkg/oss/objectset/handler_asof_test.go` (8 unit tests, all green): happy path routes through provider AND skips executor entirely; select drops un-listed properties; 3-PK + pageSize=2 paginates with PK-ASC ordering and a working nextPageToken; invalid timestamp → InvalidAsOf 400 with no provider call; provider unset → TimeTravelUnavailable; composite (filter) ObjectSet → TimeTravelUnsupportedObjectSet with no provider call; provider error → TimeTravelFailed with the underlying message echoed in `parameters.error`; empty snapshot → 200 with totalCount=0 + empty data; live path (asOf absent) NEVER touches the provider even when one is wired.
  - `pkg/oms/object_history_asof_test.go` (3 integration tests, build-gated `//go:build integration`): InsertObjectHistory closes prior valid_to (snapshot at t1+1ns returns v1 with valid_to=t2; snapshot at t2 returns v2 because the interval is half-open `[valid_from, valid_to)`); DELETE tombstone is omitted from snapshots after the delete instant; snapshot before the first version returns zero rows for that PK rather than erroring.
- All `go test -short -count=1 ./pkg/... ./internal/... ./cmd/...` green; `go vet ./...` clean; `go build ./...` clean. Note: `go test -tags integration ./pkg/oms/...` does NOT build cleanly on main due to pre-existing `seedOntology` redeclaration between `repository_test.go` and `admin_handlers_linkinverse_test.go` (verified by stashing my changes and re-running) — the new asof integration tests piggyback on the existing `setupRepo(t)` helper and will activate once that pre-existing breakage is sorted in a future story.
- Files changed:
  - `migrations/000043_object_history_validity_range.up.sql` (new)
  - `migrations/000043_object_history_validity_range.down.sql` (new)
  - `pkg/oms/pg_repository.go` (InsertObjectHistory stamps valid_from + closes prior valid_to; new SnapshotObjectsAt)
  - `pkg/oms/object_history_asof_test.go` (new, 3 integration tests)
  - `pkg/oss/objectset/snapshot.go` (new — HistorySnapshotProvider interface + ObjectSnapshot)
  - `pkg/oss/objectset/handler.go` (asOf branch + loadObjectsAsOf helper + SetHistorySnapshotProvider)
  - `pkg/oss/objectset/handler_asof_test.go` (new, 8 unit tests)
  - `cmd/server/history_snapshot_provider.go` (new — historySnapshotAdapter + narrow store/repo interfaces)
  - `cmd/server/main.go` (HistorySnapshotStore on ServerDeps + wiring + objSetHandler.SetHistorySnapshotProvider)
  - `api/openapi.yaml` + `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` (asOf query param + description + error names)
  - `prd.json` (US-223 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Bitemporal validity range on a write-once history table is the simplest "time-travel" backbone you can ship: one `[valid_from, valid_to)` half-open interval per (key, version) tuple, stamped at write time. The snapshot reader is a single-statement `WHERE valid_from <= asOf AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > asOf)` — no window function at read time. The cost is the extra UPDATE on the prior version inside InsertObjectHistory; for an append-only history table that's still O(1) because the filter `version < $4 AND valid_to IS NULL` matches at most one row.
  - The handler-side asOf branch is the right granularity for v1 time-travel — composite ObjectSet types (filter / union / searchAround / ...) need a per-instant Bleve index that we don't materialise, so rejecting them upfront with `TimeTravelUnsupportedObjectSet` 400 is honest and unblocks future stories. Don't try to filter-in-Go after the snapshot fetch for the v1 — the PRD says "scan history by time", not "scan history then re-apply where clauses". When a future story needs filter+asOf, it can build the composite path on top of this one.
  - DEFAULT can't reference another column in PostgreSQL, so backfilling `valid_from = recorded_at` via `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DEFAULT recorded_at` does not work. Two clean alternatives: (a) trigger on BEFORE INSERT, (b) stamp it at the INSERT site. We chose (b) because the only writer is `InsertObjectHistory` — stamping in Go keeps the trigger surface flat and the migration idempotent (re-running only updates rows that still have NULL columns, never touches already-stamped rows).
  - When pre-existing tests in the same package don't compile (here `seedOntology` is declared twice in different `//go:build integration` files), `go test -tags integration ./pkg/oms/...` fails for ALL tests in the package — including new ones that would otherwise compile in isolation. Verify with a `git stash && go test -tags integration ...` check before claiming the failure is your regression. The new `object_history_asof_test.go` is correctly authored against the existing `setupRepo(t)` helper from `repository_test.go`; it will run cleanly once the pre-existing duplicate is removed.
  - Two-method narrow interface in cmd/server (`historySnapshotRepo` + `historySnapshotStore`) is the right shape when an adapter needs both a *resolver* (ObjectType API name → RID) and a *reader* (the actual query). Splitting them lets contract tests fake one without faking the other, AND it documents the two consumer-distinct roles the *PGRepository plays in this adapter. Same pattern usable for future "X service that wraps a repo + a store" wiring.
  - `?asOf=<RFC3339>` over the wire is the canonical Foundry / Time-Travel idiom — RFC3339 (with Z suffix) is the only format `time.Parse(time.RFC3339, raw)` accepts, so consumers that send RFC3339Nano or "2026-01-01" (no time) get a clean 400 with `InvalidAsOf` rather than a silent zero-time fallback. Document the exact format in the parameter description so SDKs key off the same constant.

## 2026-04-18 - US-224 ObjectSet Versioned Snapshots
- Migration `000044_object_set_snapshots` introduces the new `object_set_snapshots` table with `rid TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, `ontology_api_name TEXT NOT NULL`, `object_type TEXT NOT NULL`, `definition JSONB NOT NULL`, `primary_keys JSONB NOT NULL`, `truncated BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`, `created_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, plus indexes on `(ontology_api_name, created_at DESC)` and `created_by`.
- `pkg/oms.ObjectSetSnapshot` model + `ObjectSetSnapshotStore` narrow interface (Create/Get) — kept OUT of `oms.Repository` per US-202 / US-204 / US-214 convention so the ~15 mock repos don't grow stub methods. `*PGRepository` satisfies it implicitly via `pkg/oms/pg_repository_object_set_snapshot.go` (Create marshals primary_keys to JSONB and substitutes "null" for nil definition; Get scans both columns into `[]byte` then unmarshals, returning `oms.ErrNotFound` on `pgx.ErrNoRows`).

  - `prd.json` (US-224 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When the OMS-side store needs JSONB-encoded data but the handler's narrow interface wants typed Go structs, declare the handler interface with the typed shape (`*Definition`) and put the JSON marshal/unmarshal in the `cmd/server` adapter. The OMS layer never imports the handler package, the handler layer never imports `encoding/json` for the row, and degraded-mode tests can plug a fake using the typed shape directly. This matches the historySnapshotAdapter pattern (US-223) and keeps the domain types un-leaky.
  - Mapping a sentinel across package boundaries: the cmd/server adapter is the right place to translate `oms.ErrNotFound` → `objectset.ErrSnapshotNotFound` so the handler stays pkg/oms-free. A nil-receiver / nil-store branch on the adapter doubles as a defence against degraded-mode wiring footguns ("SnapshotsUnavailable 400" is friendlier than a nil-pointer panic).
  - Frozen membership vs frozen values: v1 of "snapshot" only freezes the PK list. Property values come from the live Bleve index at GET time, so a snapshot of last week's customer set will show today's emails. This is the right tradeoff for v1 because storing a per-row property snapshot is materially more storage and a separate concept ("time-travel object_history" already covers point-in-time property state via US-223). The TestGetSnapshot_FrozenAfterUnderlyingSetMutates test locks in the membership-frozen invariant explicitly.
  - Static path segments must be registered BEFORE wildcard ones for the SAME HTTP method on chi, even though chi v5 generally picks the longer/more-specific match. The new GET `/objectSets/snapshots/{snapshotRid}` shares its prefix with GET `/objectSets/{objectSetRid}`; registering snapshots first is the safest choice and matches the pattern already established by the `loadObjectsMultipleObjectTypes` / `loadObjectsOrInterfaces` POSTs that sit BEFORE the wildcard GET. Different HTTP methods (POST vs GET) don't conflict at the chi tree level so the new POST `/{objectSetRid}/snapshot` doesn't need any reordering.
  - When adding a new optional `OMSHandler.SetXxx` hook, the established trio applies: (1) narrow interface in the handler package (one or two methods), (2) concrete impl in a sibling subpackage / `cmd/server` adapter with no `pkg/oms` import, (3) setter on the handler. Production wiring in `cmd/server` passes the concrete impl which satisfies the interface implicitly; degraded-mode test routers leave the hook unset and exercise the "no store wired" path. Same shape as `SetHistorySnapshotProvider` (US-223), `SetFunctionResultCache` (US-221), `SetFunctionQuotaLimiter` (US-218).
