JetStream not used — progress events are ephemeral (missed updates are resolved via the polling endpoint).
- Tests:
  - `pkg/functions/goja_shim_progress_test.go` (6): happy path multi-update, clamp out-of-range / float truncation, no-reporter no-op, optional message, coexistence with `weave.callFunction`, absent-from-context.
  - `pkg/actions/progress_test.go` (5): subject format, store+publish round-trip, publisher error non-propagation, nil publisher still updates store, end-to-end async-goja flow (submit → wait for SUCCEEDED → assert intermediate 25/75 events on NATS, terminal progress=100 in store).
  - Updated 1 existing test (`TestWeaveCallFunction_NoCallerShimAbsent`) to assert `typeof weave.callFunction === "undefined"` instead of `typeof weave === "undefined"` — `weave` global is now always registered.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/functions/goja_shim_progress.go` (new)
  - `pkg/functions/goja_shim_progress_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/functions/goja_shim_functions.go` (always-register weave + call registerProgressShim)
  - `pkg/functions/goja_shim_functions_test.go` (updated one test assertion)
  - `pkg/actions/progress.go` (new — ProgressPublisher, Executor hooks, ProgressEvent, ProgressSubject, jobProgressReporter)
  - `pkg/actions/progress_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/actions/executor.go` (progressPub field on Executor)
  - `pkg/actions/handlers.go` (install reporter on ctx in runAsyncApply)
  - `cmd/server/action_progress_publisher.go` (new)
  - `cmd/server/main.go` (SetProgressPublisher wire-up)
  - `prd.json` (US-241 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Two-method shim registration pattern: when a global like `weave` carries multiple independent features (callFunction needs FunctionCaller, reportProgress needs ctx reporter), drop the early-return-when-first-dep-nil guard and build the global unconditionally — attach each method based on its own precondition. The old "register global only if caller wired" pattern made `weave.reportProgress` inadvertently unavailable in sync flows or degraded-mode test routers that never wired a FunctionCaller. Keep the global; gate methods.
  - Context-carried per-invocation hooks vs runtime-carried per-process hooks: `FunctionCaller` is per-runtime (set once via `SetFunctionCaller`) because it's stateless. `ProgressReporter` is per-invocation (scoped to one jobID) so it MUST ride on ctx — setting it on the runtime would force per-request runtime construction or introduce data races across concurrent dispatches. Rule of thumb: state that changes per-request → ctx; state that changes per-process → runtime field.
  - JS numeric → Go int conversion: `goja.Value.ToInteger()` truncates toward zero (75.7 → 75, -5.9 → -5). Do this BEFORE clamping to [0,100] so "out of range float" cases don't surprise — in the clamp tests, `1000.5` after `ToInteger` is `1000`, which is then clamped to `100`. If the PRD asked for rounding semantics (75.7 → 76) we'd need an explicit `math.Round` before conversion — but for progress percent truncation is both intuitive and matches Go int-conversion conventions.
  - Ephemeral NATS vs JetStream: progress events are the canonical case for "plain nats.Conn.Publish, not JetStream". Missing an update isn't a correctness bug — GET /actions/jobs/{id} is the source of truth. JetStream would pay persistence + ack cost with no business value and clutter the OBJECT_EDITS stream with non-edit payloads. Rule of thumb: if the consumer CAN'T tolerate missing an event → JetStream; if it can reconcile via a polling endpoint → plain NATS.
  - Interface assertion at declaration site: `var _ functions.ProgressReporter = (*jobProgressReporter)(nil)` catches interface drift at compile time. Cheap insurance worth dropping in every cross-package "this type implements that interface" site, especially when the interface lives in a package the type's package already imports.
  - weave global always-register was a contract change: the pre-US-241 behavior was "weave is undefined when no FunctionCaller wired". Existing scripts that check `typeof weave === "undefined"` to branch on deployment mode would break. None exist in this repo (only `typeof weave.callFunction` matters for deep checks), but if a future PRD reintroduces "no-weave-available" as a mode, it would need either (a) a config flag on Runtime to opt out, or (b) a no-op sentinel runtime object. Document this in the shim file if it ever becomes a question.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Approval gating lives at the HANDLER, not the executor. The Apply handler resolves the ActionType via `Executor.ResolveActionType`, checks `RequiresApproval + store wired`, and short-circuits to 202 BEFORE calling `exec.Apply`. Putting the gate inside the executor would force every batch / saga / async path to repeat the same check; gating at the handler keeps Executor.Apply semantics stable (rules always execute when called). If a future story needs a programmatic "apply after approval" re-dispatch, that belongs inside ApproveAction (load row → rebuild ApplyRequest from snapshotted Parameters → call exec.Apply directly). v1 intentionally stops at status transition — caller re-issues the action manually after approval.
  - Snapshot approvers at enqueue time, not at review time. `ActionApproval.Approvers` copies `ActionType.Approvers` into its own JSONB column so later edits to the ActionType don't retroactively change who can review an already-queued request. Same principle as "freeze membership" from US-224 ObjectSet snapshots — once a request enters the queue, its review contract is locked. If a modeler widens the approver list mid-queue, the new approvers apply only to NEW requests.
  - Dual-meaning approver entries (user IDs OR role names): `userCanApprove` OR-matches against both `user.ID` and every entry in `user.Roles`. This lets modelers mix role-based governance ("data-governance-team") with individual named approvers ("alice@example.com") without a separate field or flag. If the PRD later requires strict "role-only" or "user-only" semantics, the distinguishing prefix goes on the stored value (e.g. `role:xxx` / `user:yyy`) rather than a schema split — existing rows remain valid.
  - `Executor.ResolveActionType` as a public shim: previously `resolveActionType` was internal to the saga coordinator. Exporting it as a method on Executor (rather than duplicating the lookup logic in the handler) keeps the dual-lookup-by-RID-or-APIName trick in one place. Same pattern will apply any time a new handler needs to inspect the ActionType — the handler asks the executor, which owns the repo; no need to plumb `oms.Repository` into every handler.
  - Apply handler gate ordering matters: async check FIRST, then approval. If approval is checked first and succeeds, the 202 PendingApproval wins; if async is checked first and succeeds, the 202 Async wins. Either order is defensible, but async-first means "async gated actions" enqueue as an action_job with a detached goroutine that will itself hit the approval gate — wrong shape. Approval-first-after-async means gated actions never route through the async path (approval IS the async mechanism), keeping the two features cleanly orthogonal.
  - OpenAPI `202` response with two possible bodies: use `oneOf` on the response `content.schema`, not two separate "202" entries (YAML duplicate-key). `oneOf` is valid in every SDK generator I know — SDKs pick the discriminator based on presence of `jobId` vs `approvalId`. Callers who need to distinguish can check both keys; in practice the request pattern is distinct (?async=true vs no query param on a gated action type).
  - Handler tests that need `auth.UserFromContext` should use `req.WithContext(auth.WithUser(req.Context(), &auth.User{...}))`. Chi router passes the stored context through, so the handler sees the injected user without any middleware wiring. Keeps approval/permission tests lightweight without standing up the JWT middleware stack. Same trick applies to any future handler test that needs authenticated identity — `auth.WithUser` is the public constructor.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Caller-scoped filters (OR-of-identity, role ∩ list, etc.) belong POST-store, not pushed into the store primitive. `userCanApprove(user, approvers)` already codified the identity check for approve/reject; reusing it from the handler keeps the store's `Approver` filter a single-string membership test. Pushing an OR-of-identities into the store would force the PG layer to accept `[]string` + emit `approvers ?| $N` (JSONB array overlap), which is strictly more complex for a filter the handler can apply in-memory on a bounded result.
  - Degraded-mode list endpoints should return an empty list + 200, not 500 / 404. The approvals queue is rendered in-line by the UI; treating "no store" as "no rows" keeps the UI behaviour consistent between full deployment and single-user mode. Compare GetJob which returns 404 for a specific id — presence-lookup is a different contract than enumeration, and the right degraded shape follows.
  - JSONB `?` operator needs double-escaping in pgx placeholder strings (`approvers ?? $N`) — pgx treats `?` as a literal placeholder escape, so a single `?` in the SQL body would be interpreted as "expect a parameter here". The double-question-mark is a pgx convention (not a PostgreSQL one); the server sees a single `?` after pgx rewrites the statement. Same gotcha applies to any future JSONB containment / existence query that needs `?` / `?&` / `?|`.
  - Reason textarea reuse pattern: keep the confirm modal's `reason` state + error + in-flight flag in the page component (not inside the Modal); `Modal` is a passive overlay. That way the same state object can power either the Approve mutation or the Reject mutation depending on `reviewTarget.decision`, and the user's typed reason survives decision switches (though the modal closes on submit, so in practice this doesn't matter — it's the right shape for future "switch reject→approve mid-review" refinements).
  - Frontend route with optional path param: `<Route path="approvals" .../>` AND `<Route path="approvals/:ontology" .../>` lets the caller omit the ontology segment and fall back to the `ontologyStore.selectedOntology` persisted in localStorage. The page component reads `useParams<{ ontology?: string }>()` + `useOntologyStore(s => s.selectedOntology)` and coalesces. When neither is set, it shows an EmptyState rather than firing a query with `ontologyApiName=''` — `enabled: !!ontology` on the useQuery gates the fetch.
  - dev-browser skill unavailable in this harness means manual browser verification is still pending for UI stories. The RTL suite exercises component behaviour (render + state + mutation + error path) but a real browser round-trip is worth scheduling before the feature ships. Same caveat as US-205 (Media Upload UI).

## 2026-04-19 - US-244 Action DSL 控制流
- Extended `pkg/actions.Rule` with control-flow fields (`Condition`, `Then`, `Else`, `ItemsParameter`, `ItemVariable`, `IndexVariable`, `Rules`, `On`, `Cases`, `Default`) — all `omitempty` so existing ActionType JSON is byte-identical after round-trip.
- New public types: `Condition` (leaf + logical — supports `eq`/`ne`/`gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`/`in`/`notIn`/`exists`/`notExists`/`truthy`/`falsy` leaves and `and`/`or`/`not` logicals via `All`/`Any`/`Not`), `SwitchCase` (`When` + `Rules`), plus `MaxRuleNestingDepth = 5`.
- `ExecuteRules` is now a depth-tracking recursive helper. `executeRulesWithDepth` dispatches control-flow rules via `executeControlFlowRule` and bumps depth once per wrapper; simple rules keep the old single-edit `executeRule` path. `if` branches on Condition, `foreach` iterates `[]interface{}` with shallow-cloned child params carrying `itemVariable` (+ optional `indexVariable`), `switch` matches `params[On]` against each `SwitchCase.When` via numeric-aware equality, falling through to `Default`.
- `condition.go` new file carries `evaluateCondition` + helpers; `toFloat64` / `jsonEqual` from `criteria.go` are reused so Condition and SubmissionCriteria semantics cannot drift.
- Tests: 17 subtests (`TestExecuteRules_If_*`, `_Foreach_*`, `_Switch_*`, `TestExecuteRules_NestedControlFlow`, depth-at-max + depth-exceeded, `TestParseRules_ControlFlow`). `go test ./pkg/actions/` 0.95s green; `go build ./...` + `go vet ./...` clean; `go test -short -timeout=120s ./test/e2e/... ./test/northwind/... ./test/foundry_parity/...` all pass.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/actions/rules.go` (Rule struct extension + MaxRuleNestingDepth + executeRulesWithDepth + executeControlFlowRule + cloneParams)
  - `pkg/actions/condition.go` (new; evaluateCondition + isTruthy + valuesEqual + compareNumeric + containsValue)
  - `pkg/actions/control_flow_test.go` (new; 17 subtests covering every branch, depth limit, JSON round-trip)
  - `prd.json` (US-244 passes=true + notes)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - `executeFunction` rules nested inside control-flow are silently skipped by `ExecuteRules` (matches the existing top-level behaviour), but `Prepare.dispatchExecuteFunctionRules` still iterates top-level rules only. A follow-up story adding "execute function inside foreach" would need to (a) recurse through control-flow in the dispatch pass, (b) decide semantics for per-iteration param injection, (c) decide whether executeFunction inside `if`/`switch` counts towards the depth cap. Kept out of scope here to preserve the "one AC, one story" pattern.
  - Shallow-clone, never deep-clone the parent params: `foreach` only ADDS keys (itemVariable, indexVariable); child rules don't mutate nested values via property bindings. Deep-clone would be ~50x more expensive on a 3-level nested struct and buy nothing. If a future rule type learns to mutate nested maps in child scope, revisit — not today.
  - Depth semantics: control-flow-wrapper counts, leaf rules don't. Documented this explicitly in the const comment + tests. The alternative (count every rule as depth+1) would force authors to split rule lists just to keep the cap reachable, which conflicts with "keep ActionType JSON small". `>=` at the guard means exactly `MaxRuleNestingDepth` wrappers is the last valid configuration; the 6th wrapper is the rejection edge.
  - `valuesEqual` in a new file vs. extending `jsonEqual` in `criteria.go`: I left both. `jsonEqual` is a pure JSON-marshal comparator used for criteria value matches; `valuesEqual` is a numeric-aware comparator with a JSON-marshal fallback. Merging them would force criteria to pay the numeric-coerce cost on every compare. The naming is explicit so future readers pick the right one (criteria → `jsonEqual`, condition → `valuesEqual`).

## 2026-04-19 - US-245 Parameter Validation DSL
- Added `github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v5 v5.3.1` (pure-Go — safe under the CGO_ENABLED=0 Dockerfile invariant). Verified with `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`.
- Migration `000048_action_type_parameter_schema` adds `parameter_schema JSONB` (nullable) to `action_types`. Legacy rows read as NULL → handler-layer nil → Prepare treats as "no schema, pass through".
- Extended `oms.ActionType` with `ParameterSchema json.RawMessage` (omitempty). PG Repository INSERT / SELECT / UPDATE wired via `normaliseParameterSchemaForWrite` (nil/null/empty → SQL NULL, else raw bytes) + `parameterSchemaFromBytes` (inverse). `ToFullMetadataJSON` surfaces the field on the wire when present.
- `admin_handlers.CreateActionTypeRequest` gains `ParameterSchema json.RawMessage`; `UpdateActionTypeRequest` gains a tri-state `*json.RawMessage` (nil=preserve, empty/null=clear, non-empty=replace). `hasParameterSchemaRaw` helper consolidates the trimmed JSON-null check at the update site.
- New module `pkg/actions/parameter_schema.go`:
  - `ParameterSchemaValidator` caches compiled `*jsonschema.Schema` keyed by the raw schema byte content; `jsonschema.NewCompiler()` explicitly pinned to `jsonschema.Draft7` + `AddResource("mem://action-parameter-schema.json", ...)`.
  - `ParameterSchemaError` is the typed error with public `Violations []ParameterSchemaViolation {Field, Keyword, Reason}`. `Error()` emits a compact single-line summary for logs; `APIError()` renders `apierror.NewValidationSchema("ParameterSchemaViolation", ...)` (422) with `field` / `keyword` / `reason` from the first violation PLUS a `violations` JSON array parameter so SDKs can read every failure.
  - `convertValidationError` walks the nested `*jsonschema.ValidationError` tree via `collectLeafViolations`, turning each leaf (node with no `Causes`) into a `ParameterSchemaViolation`. Envelope root is skipped; the per-keyword failures carry the user-facing detail.
  - `instanceField` converts `/age` → `age` and `/items/0/price` → `items.0.price` (dot-delimited JSON Pointer).
  - `hasParameterSchema` is the shared predicate: nil / empty / whitespace / `null` literal (w/ or w/o whitespace) → false; any other JSON → true. `TrimSpace` is what catches the idiomatic `null` storage shape.
- `apierror.NewValidationSchema(name, params)` constructor emits `WEAVE_VALIDATION_SCHEMA` / HTTP 422 — mirrors `NewValidationEnum` from US-208.
- `Executor.Prepare` gains Step 3b (between `ValidateParameters` and `EvaluateCriteria`): `validateParameterSchema(actionType.ParameterSchema, req.Parameters)` runs the validator, converts a typed `*ParameterSchemaError` into its `APIError()`, and bubbles up as `fmt.Errorf("parameter schema: %w", err)`. Handler's `typedAPIError` branch (`errors.As(err, &apiErr)`) unwraps the 422 automatically — no handler-side plumbing change. Compile errors on the stored schema (malformed Draft-07 JSON) propagate as untyped errors → handler's fallback 400 `ActionFailed`, since the caller didn't author the bad schema.

  - Unit: nil / null / empty no-op, required / pattern / range / dependency / multi violation detection, happy path, compile-cache reuse (10 iterations → one cache entry), malformed-schema compile error does NOT surface typed error, `ParameterSchemaError.APIError()` wire shape (errorCode / errorName / status / field / keyword / violations JSON round-trip), `hasParameterSchema` table-driven across 7 inputs.
  - Integration (Executor.Prepare): required violation emits `*apierror.APIError` 422 via `errors.As`, pattern violation emits typed 422, happy path still produces edits, empty schema is silently ignored (legacy parity).
  - Handler-layer (`setupRouter` + `httptest.NewRecorder`): 422 round-trip through `Handler.Apply`, wire JSON carries `errorCode=WEAVE_VALIDATION_SCHEMA`, `field=age`, `keyword=maximum`, non-empty `violations` array.

  - `go.mod` + `go.sum` (+santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v5 v5.3.1 direct)

  - `migrations/000048_action_type_parameter_schema.down.sql` (new)

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - `jsonschema.NewCompiler()` defaults to the latest draft (2020-12 as of v5.3.1); PIN `c.Draft = jsonschema.Draft7` explicitly when the PRD says Draft-07. Newer drafts change `exclusiveMinimum` semantics (boolean → numeric), `dependencies` splits into `dependentRequired`/`dependentSchemas`, and `$ref` handling — skipping the pin silently changes acceptance behaviour the first time a real customer authors a schema.
  - `*jsonschema.ValidationError` is a tree — the root carries a generic "doesn't validate with X" envelope and each failing keyword is a leaf in `Causes`. To produce field-level detail, walk to leaves (nodes with `len(Causes) == 0`) — do NOT read the root's `Message`/`InstanceLocation` alone or you lose the per-field reason. `collectLeafViolations` is the shape.
  - `InstanceLocation` is a JSON Pointer (`/age`, `/items/0/price`). Convert to dot-paths (`age`, `items.0.price`) at the API boundary so SDK consumers and JSONPath-like UIs can address fields uniformly. Root location (`""` / `"/"`) → empty string; callers render the root-level message without a field prefix.
  - Compile-cache keying on raw bytes (string(schema)) is fine for action-type rows because the stored JSONB goes through PG's canonical representation before hitting Go. If a future caller passes differently-whitespaced-but-equivalent schemas at request time, the cache misses but correctness holds — not worth the cost of a canonicalisation pass. Same heuristic `pkg/functions/cache.canonicalJSON` uses for the hot path, but cheaper here since the input is immutable per ActionType row.
  - TYPED vs UNTYPED error distinction matters for the handler's fallback branch: schema-VIOLATION returns `*apierror.APIError` (422 user error), schema-COMPILE-ERROR returns a plain `error` (500-class, caller didn't author the bad schema). `typedAPIError` + `typedAPIError` pattern from US-208 unwraps only the former so the handler's generic 400 fallback still covers the latter.
  - When adding a new tri-state optional field on an Update DTO, the right shape is `*json.RawMessage` NOT `json.RawMessage` with an explicit `Clear bool`. Callers distinguish omit (nil pointer), clear (non-nil, empty / null content) and replace (non-nil, non-empty content) with zero boilerplate. Same convention as `UpdateActionTypeRequest.ImplementsMethodRID *string` (US-214) and `CompensateActionRID *string` (US-239). Document the three states in the struct tag comment so future readers don't silently collapse two of them.
  - Handler-layer wire test (chi + httptest.NewRecorder) is the load-bearing assertion for typed-error propagation. Unit tests on `*apierror.APIError` only verify the struct shape; they don't verify that `Handler.Apply` actually reaches `typedAPIError(err)` and emits the right HTTP status. When adding a new typed validator, ALWAYS pair the unit test with a `TestHandler_Apply_*_EmitsWire<status>` that decodes the response body into the Palantir wire format (`errorCode`, `errorName`, `parameters`) and asserts each field.
  - `parameter_schema` as a new JSONB column — NOT inlined into the existing `parameters` array. The declarative array shape is a first-class Foundry concept (ParameterDef list, typed dimension names); a schema is a second-class governance artefact (pattern / range / dependency). Keeping them orthogonal means (a) the validator runs AFTER the declarative validator and covers gaps the ParameterDef type system can't express, (b) a future sub-story can add Parameter-level schema fragments without rewriting the top-level shape, and (c) the migration is additive — nullable column with no default — so every in-flight ActionType stays byte-identical on read.

## 2026-04-19 - US-246 OIDC 集成
- Added `pkg/auth/oidc_handler.go` with `OIDCHandler` + `OIDCConfig` + `OIDCTokenExchanger` / `OIDCVerifier` interfaces. The two endpoints:
  - `GET /api/auth/oidc/login` — mints 32B state, plants an HttpOnly+Lax+Secure-if-TLS cookie, redirects to provider's AuthCodeURL.
  - `GET /api/auth/oidc/callback` — validates state cookie, exchanges code → id_token via `oauth2.Config.Exchange`, verifies id_token via `oidc.IDTokenVerifier`, extracts `sub`/`email`/`name` claims, upserts a `UserRecord` (keyed by email, ID = `user:<email>`), issues a standard `LoginResponse` (access + refresh) OR redirects to `SuccessRedirectURL?access_token=...&refresh_token=...` when configured.
- Callback never overwrites an existing user's PasswordHash — OIDC users and password users can coexist on the same email.
- `NewOIDCDepsFromProvider` builds production-ready `*oauth2.Config` + `*oidc.IDTokenVerifier` from a discovered `*oidc.Provider`; forces `openid` into the scopes list if the operator forgot it.
- Added `OIDCConfig` to `internal/config`: `WEAVE_OIDC_*` env vars (`ENABLED`, `ISSUER`, `CLIENT_ID`, `CLIENT_SECRET`, `REDIRECT_URL`, `SCOPES` csv, `SUCCESS_REDIRECT_URL`). `AUTH_MODE=oidc` is an alias that sets `OIDC.Enabled=true`. `Validate()` now collects missing-field errors when OIDC is enabled but credentials are incomplete.
- `cmd/server/main.go` wiring: after JWT signer + refresh service are built, if `OIDC.Enabled` AND all deps present, run `oidc.NewProvider(ctx, issuer)` (hits the well-known discovery endpoint), construct `OIDCHandler`, attach to `ServerDeps.OIDCHandler`. `RegisterRoutes(r)` fires from the existing `/api/auth/*` public route block. Any discovery failure logs a warning and leaves the routes unmounted — password login still works.
- Tests (12 handler tests + 4 config tests):
  - Handler: login sets state cookie + redirects with state in URL; POST rejected; callback happy path returns LoginResponse with tokens + persisted user; state mismatch → 401; missing cookie → 401; missing code → 400; provider error (`?error=access_denied`) → 401; exchange failure → 401; invalid id_token (wrong issuer) → 401; missing email claim → 401; existing user keeps password_hash; SuccessRedirectURL path returns 302 with tokens in query string.
  - Config: `AUTH_MODE=oidc` sets `OIDC.Enabled=true` and parses all env vars; default disabled; `Validate()` reports all four missing fields; fully-populated OIDCConfig passes `Validate()`.
- Harness runs the actual coreos/go-oidc v3 `IDTokenVerifier` against an in-process `oidctest.Server` (discovery + JWKS), with `oidctest.SignIDToken` producing real RS256-signed tokens. Only the token-exchange step is stubbed — that avoids standing up a real token endpoint while still exercising the whole verification path end-to-end.
- Added dependencies: `github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3 v3.18.0`, `golang.org/x/oauth2 v0.36.0`, `github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 v4.1.4` (transitive). All pure Go — safe under the CGO_ENABLED=0 Dockerfile invariant.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/auth/oidc_handler.go` (new)
  - `pkg/auth/oidc_handler_test.go` (new)
  - `internal/config/config.go` (OIDCConfig struct + env parse + Validate branch)
  - `internal/config/config_test.go` (4 OIDC tests)
  - `cmd/server/main.go` (imports coreos/go-oidc/v3, `ServerDeps.OIDCHandler`, bootstrap block, RegisterRoutes call)
  - `go.mod` / `go.sum`
  - `prd.json` (US-246 passes=true + notes)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - `oidctest.Server` serves ONLY discovery + JWKS — it does not implement the token endpoint. If you want a real token-exchange round-trip in tests you have to wrap it with a second mux that handles `/token`. For handler unit tests, it's far cleaner to split the handler into `Exchanger` (the `*oauth2.Config` interface) + `Verifier` (the `*oidc.IDTokenVerifier` interface) and stub the Exchanger — the Verifier still runs the real coreos path against `oidctest.Server`.
  - `oauth2.Token.WithExtra(map[string]interface{}{"id_token": <raw>})` is how you attach the OIDC id_token to a Token you're synthesising in a test. Retrieval is `tok.Extra("id_token").(string)` — `.Extra` returns `interface{}` so guard with the type assertion's `ok` form.
  - `oidc.NewProvider(ctx, issuer)` is a live HTTP GET to `issuer + /.well-known/openid-configuration` at BOOT time — an unreachable IdP at process start would crash the server. Wrap the call in a log-warn-and-continue block so misconfigured OIDC doesn't take down password login; the discovery failure is visible in logs but the rest of the server keeps running.
  - The state cookie MUST be HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax. Strict would break the redirect-back-from-IdP flow because the cookie wouldn't be sent on the inbound navigation; None requires Secure. Lax is the Goldilocks zone for OAuth callback cookies.
  - User upsert by email, not by `sub`: Foundry-style systems key role grants on the `user:<email>` ID. Using the IdP `sub` as the primary key would require every role policy to be rewritten AND would make "same email, switched IdP" (e.g. migrated from Okta to Keycloak) a data-migration problem. Email is the stable identity across provider migrations; sub is discarded after the session is minted. Trade-off: if the IdP reassigns emails between humans we have a problem, but that's a governance issue the org already manages.
  - Never overwrite PasswordHash on OIDC callback. OIDC-first users will never have a password set (hash stays empty); hybrid orgs may have a user who can BOTH enter their password AND SSO in — the callback path must preserve the hash on existing users so the password login keeps working. Single line in `upsertUser`: on hit by email, only patch `Name` if the IdP supplies a fresher value; leave `PasswordHash` untouched.
  - Interface-based collaborators (`OIDCTokenExchanger`, `OIDCVerifier`) are the right shape for anything that does network I/O. `*oauth2.Config` and `*oidc.IDTokenVerifier` are structs (not interfaces upstream), so the handler declares the minimal method subset itself. Tests substitute in-process stubs; production wiring (`NewOIDCDepsFromProvider`) returns the concrete values which satisfy the interfaces implicitly. Same trick as `OAuthTokenValidator` (US-142) and `FunctionExecutor` (US-217).
  - Pure-Go verification: coreos/go-oidc v3 + go-jose v4 are both pure Go — no CGO. Confirm before adding any auth library that it's `go build ./...` clean with `CGO_ENABLED=0`; many JOSE/crypto libraries (`github.com/dchest/siphash`-adjacent families, OpenSSL-binding packages) silently break the Dockerfile invariant from US-230.

## 2026-04-19 - US-247 OAuth2 完整流程
- Authorization Code + PKCE flow was already shipped under US-142 (pkg/developer/oauth_handlers.go). This story closed the two remaining gaps: refresh_token grant + canonical scope catalogue.
- New `pkg/developer/oauth_scopes.go`: ScopeRead / ScopeWrite / ScopeAdmin constants, `KnownScopes()` returning the catalogue in declaration order, `IsKnownScope` membership check, and `NarrowScopes(granted, requested)` returning the scope-narrowed subset OR `ErrScopeNotGranted` when the requested set tries to widen. Catalogue is additive — existing custom scopes ("read:objects", "admin:ontology") keep working since the canonical trio is recommended-not-enforced for new application registrations.
- New `tokenRefresh` method on `OAuthHandler` dispatched from the existing `Token()` switch as a third grant_type. RFC 6749 §6 + RFC 9700 rotation: parse + IsOAuthRefreshToken shape check, GetByPrefix(refresh) lookup, constant-time hash compare, IsUsable check (revoked/expired ⇒ invalid_grant), client_id binding check, optional `scope` form param routes through NarrowScopes, then `Revoke(matched.ID)` BEFORE `issueAccessAndRefresh` so a concurrent replay sees the old token already consumed. Confidential clients (app.ClientSecretHash non-empty) MUST authenticate via Basic auth or form-body client_secret; public PKCE clients (no registered secret) authenticate by client_id alone — same shape as the SPA refresh contract every major provider implements.
- Tests (14 new across `oauth_scopes_test.go` + `oauth_refresh_test.go`): scope catalogue contains read/write/admin in stable order, IsKnownScope is case-sensitive, NarrowScopes rejects expansion / filters intersection / handles empty-requested as "preserve grant" / collapses duplicates. Refresh: rotates and returns new pair, replay returns invalid_grant, scope narrowing succeeds, scope expansion returns invalid_scope, client mismatch returns invalid_grant, revoked refresh rejected, access-token-presented-as-refresh rejected by shape check, missing refresh_token returns invalid_request, public-client (nil ClientSecretHash) refreshes by client_id alone.
- OpenAPI: added `refresh_token` to `/oauth/token` grant_type enum, added `refresh_token` form param to schema, expanded the operation description to document all three grants (authorization_code / client_credentials / refresh_token) and the rotation + scope-narrowing semantics. Synced `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` from canonical.
- Quality: `go build ./...` + `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` + `go vet ./...` clean. `go test -short ./pkg/... ./cmd/... ./internal/...` 100% green (44 packages). e2e + foundry_parity + chinook + northwind all green.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/developer/oauth_scopes.go` (new; canonical scope catalogue + NarrowScopes helper)
  - `pkg/developer/oauth_scopes_test.go` (new; 6 scope tests)
  - `pkg/developer/oauth_handlers.go` (Token switch + tokenRefresh method)
  - `pkg/developer/oauth_refresh_test.go` (new; 9 refresh-grant tests)
  - `api/openapi.yaml` + `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` (token endpoint schema + description)
  - `prd.json` (US-247 passes=true + notes)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - "Revoke BEFORE mint" is the right ordering for refresh-token rotation. If the new (access, refresh) is created first and the revoke fails (e.g. transient PG error), you've leaked an extra usable refresh into the world. Revoking first means a failed mint leaves the user with one-token-down (bad UX) rather than two-tokens-up (security incident). The fake repo's `Revoke` is synchronous so tests can't observe this, but the production PG repo path is the one that matters.
  - Public vs confidential client distinction lives in the registered Application row, not in the request shape. `len(app.ClientSecretHash) > 0` is the predicate — apps registered via `CreateApplication` always get a secret today, but the underlying model already supports the secretless case (the column is BYTEA and the handler always hashes whatever's supplied). Checking the app row at refresh time means a future "Register public application" admin endpoint just sets ClientSecretHash to nil and the entire token endpoint Just Works without further plumbing. Trying to gate on "did the request supply a secret?" is the wrong shape — it lets a confidential client downgrade itself by simply omitting the secret.
  - Scope narrowing belongs as a reusable helper (`NarrowScopes`), not inlined into the refresh path. The same predicate fires on (a) refresh-token scope param (US-247), (b) client_credentials scope param (already inlined as `intersectStringSlice` in US-142 — could be migrated), and (c) any future on-behalf-of token-exchange flow. The error sentinel (`ErrScopeNotGranted`) lets the caller emit the correct RFC 6749 §5.2 `invalid_scope` envelope without string-matching the inner error message. `intersectStringSlice` from oauth_handlers.go silently dropped unknown scopes — wrong for refresh (must reject expansion) but right for client_credentials (idempotent narrowing). Two callers, two semantics; keep them separate functions, document the difference.
  - Canonical scope catalogue as additive constants, not enforcement: the OSv2 / Foundry pattern publishes a "well-known" trio (read/write/admin) but accepts arbitrary scope strings at application registration time. Existing apps with `read:objects`, `admin:ontology`, etc. continue to work — `IsKnownScope("read:objects") == false` but the NarrowScopes / authorize / token endpoints all stay shape-agnostic. If a future story wants strict enforcement (e.g. "only canonical scopes accepted on /api/v2/developer/applications"), wire `IsKnownScope` into the application-create validator at that time. Don't pre-enforce a closed set when the existing customer surface is open.
  - Public-client refresh test: drop `app.ClientSecretHash = nil` directly on the harness's app pointer, then re-insert into the fake repo's maps so subsequent `GetByClientID` reads the public-shape row. Cheaper than a separate harness. The test asserts that no Basic-auth or form-body secret is required; a regression would surface as 401 invalid_client. This is the SPA / PKCE single-page-app contract — client_id is public, so demanding a secret would be theatre.

## 2026-04-19 - US-248 SAML 2.0 SSO front-door
- Added `pkg/auth/saml_handler.go` wrapping russellhaering/gosaml2 v0.11.0 (pure Go, CGO-clean) behind a narrow `SAMLAssertionVerifier` interface (`BuildAuthURL` / `RetrieveAssertionInfo` / `Metadata`). Handler logic + production builder live in the same file; the latter (`NewSAMLDepsFromConfig`) parses operator-supplied IdP cert PEM (multi-block aware), builds a real `*saml2.SAMLServiceProvider` with a `dsig.MemoryX509CertificateStore`, and adapts gosaml2's `*AssertionInfo` to a narrow `SAMLAssertionInfo` (NameID + Email + DisplayName + Attributes) for the handler.
- Three endpoints under `/api/auth/saml/`: `GET /metadata` returns the SP `EntityDescriptor` XML built directly (skipping `gosaml2.Metadata()` which insists on an SP encryption cert this handler doesn't ship), `GET /login` mints a `weave_saml_relay` cookie + redirects to IdP SSO URL, `POST /acs` validates the relay-state pair AND delegates assertion verification to gosaml2 (signature + audience + NotOnOrAfter), then upserts a UserRecord keyed on email + mints a Weave LoginResponse identical in shape to /api/auth/login + /api/auth/oidc/callback.
- Email/displayName extraction walks a configurable attribute candidate list; defaults cover `email`/`mail`/Microsoft xmlsoap claim URI for email and `displayName`/`name`/xmlsoap URI for name. Operators override per-attribute via WEAVE_SAML_ATTRIBUTE_EMAIL / WEAVE_SAML_ATTRIBUTE_NAME. NameID is the email fallback when no email attribute matches.
- IdP-initiated SSO supported: when both the form's RelayState AND the relay-state cookie are absent the handler accepts the assertion (signature gate is what protects the path); only mismatched-pair triggers `SAMLRelayMismatch` 401.
- SAMLConfig env wiring: `WEAVE_SAML_ENABLED`, `WEAVE_SAML_IDP_SSO_URL`, `WEAVE_SAML_IDP_ISSUER`, `WEAVE_SAML_IDP_CERT_PEM` (or `WEAVE_SAML_IDP_CERT_PATH` for K8s/Docker secret mounts), `WEAVE_SAML_SP_ENTITY_ID`, `WEAVE_SAML_SP_ACS_URL`, `WEAVE_SAML_SUCCESS_REDIRECT_URL`, plus the two attribute overrides. `AUTH_MODE=saml` is shorthand for SAML.Enabled=true. `Validate()` reports every missing field at boot in one error message.
- `cmd/server/main.go` ServerDeps gains `SAMLHandler *auth.SAMLHandler`; the boot block sits next to the OIDC block, gated on JWTSigner+RefreshService+UserRepo and on a successful `NewSAMLDepsFromConfig` call. Bad cert / missing fields log a warning and leave the handler nil; routes mount only when `deps.SAMLHandler != nil` inside the existing JWTSigner-gated block.
- Tests: 13 handler unit tests (login redirect+cookie, login non-GET, metadata happy + non-GET, ACS happy / non-POST / missing SAMLResponse / relay mismatch / IdP-initiated allow / verifier failure / missing email / existing-user keeps password / success-redirect URL) + 2 production-builder smoke tests (real `*saml2.SAMLServiceProvider` builds a SAMLRequest+RelayState URL, blank IdP cert PEM rejected) all green. Plus 4 config tests (auth-mode shortcut, default-disabled, missing-fields validation, fully-populated passes).
- Files changed:
  - `go.mod`, `go.sum` (+gosaml2, +goxmldsig, +beevik/etree, +mattermost/xml-roundtrip-validator, +jonboulle/clockwork)
  - `pkg/auth/saml_handler.go` (new)
  - `pkg/auth/saml_handler_test.go` (new)
  - `internal/config/config.go` (SAMLConfig struct + Load env wiring + Validate gate)
  - `internal/config/config_test.go` (4 SAML config tests)
  - `cmd/server/main.go` (ServerDeps.SAMLHandler + RegisterRoutes wiring + boot-time SAML construction block)
  - `prd.json` (US-248 passes=true + notes)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - `*saml2.SAMLServiceProvider.Metadata()` is unusable for a "validate-only" SP (no AuthnRequest signing, no encrypted assertion consumption) because it unconditionally calls `GetEncryptionCertBytes()` which returns `ErrSaml{Message: "empty SP encryption certificate"}` when no SP keypair is configured. The `types.EntityDescriptor` struct is exported with the right `xml:` tags, so building the descriptor literal in handler code and `xml.MarshalIndent`-ing it is materially simpler than configuring a throwaway SP keypair just so gosaml2's helper will run. Document this contract: SP metadata != gosaml2.Metadata() unless you're shipping signed AuthnRequests or accepting encrypted assertions. The `MetadataWithSLO` variant has the same problem.
  - SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated SAML SSO distinction lives in the relay-state cookie. SP-initiated planted a cookie at `/login` time; IdP-initiated has no SP-side flow at all (the IdP simply POSTs an assertion to the ACS URL). The ACS handler MUST allow "neither cookie nor form RelayState present" alongside "matching pair present" — only the mismatched case (one side present, other absent or different) is the CSRF signature. Rejecting all RelayState-less requests breaks every IdP-initiated tile / app-launcher flow Okta/OneLogin offer.
  - russellhaering/gosaml2's `RetrieveAssertionInfo` returns a `*WarningInfo` with `InvalidTime` and `NotInAudience` flags — these are NOT errors by the library's contract, just advisory bits the caller is expected to gate on. The wrapping `gosamlVerifier` lifts both into hard errors so the handler doesn't have to look at WarningInfo: anything reaching the handler is "validated AND in the audience AND inside its time window". Same shape works for any future flag the library adds — wrap once, gate centrally, keep the handler dumb.
  - Multi-cert PEM blob support is one for-loop over `pem.Decode` (which advances `rest` and returns nil on exhaustion). IdPs rotate signing keys with overlap windows where both old and new are valid simultaneously — accepting a concatenated PEM blob means operators can stage rotations without an outage. Filter by `block.Type == "CERTIFICATE"` so accidental key blocks in the PEM don't poison the cert store.
  - The narrow-interface + production-builder split (`SAMLAssertionVerifier` + `NewSAMLDepsFromConfig`) is the same pattern OIDC used (`OIDCVerifier`/`OIDCTokenExchanger` + `NewOIDCDepsFromProvider`). Future external-IdP integrations (LDAP for US-252, future Kerberos / WS-Federation) should follow the trio: (1) narrow interface in pkg/auth carrying only what the HTTP handler needs, (2) test stub that returns canned data, (3) production builder that constructs the real third-party client and adapts it to the interface. Keeps the handler logic library-agnostic and unit-testable without standing up the upstream service.
  - SAML attribute name variability is a real-world headache — Azure AD ships email under `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress`, ADFS uses `EmailAddress`, Okta uses `email`, Google uses `mail`. A configurable candidate list (`AttributeEmail` config + `firstAttribute` walk with sensible defaults) lets operators wire any IdP without code changes. Same shape generalises to any future per-IdP attribute (groups, MFA methods, customer ID): config lists names in priority order, a tiny helper walks until it finds a non-empty value, falls back to a sensible default.

## 2026-04-19 - US-249 Service Accounts

- `pkg/auth/service_account.go`: `ServiceAccount` model + `IsDisabled/IsExpired/IsActive` helpers; `ValidateServiceAccountName` enforces `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` up to 128 chars at the HTTP boundary so malformed names fail fast with a 400.
- `pkg/auth/service_account_repository.go`: narrow `ServiceAccountRepository` interface (`Create/GetByID/GetByName/ListActive/Update/Disable`) + `PGServiceAccountRepository` concrete impl. `ServiceAccountUpdate` uses `*Description / *[]Scopes / **ExpiresAt` pointer fields so callers distinguish omit / clear / replace. SQLSTATE 23505 translates to `ErrServiceAccountNameConflict` via `strings.Contains` fallback so we don't need to import pgconn just for the typed error case.
- `pkg/auth/service_account_handlers.go`: mounts 5 endpoints under `/api/admin/service-accounts`: `POST` (Create), `GET` (List active), `GET /{id}`, `PATCH /{id}`, `DELETE /{id}` (soft-disable). Patch accepts `"expiresAt": ""` as an explicit clear.

Routes mount inside the auth group behind `RequirePermission(PermUserManage)` so only admin-level roles can mint / list / disable service accounts. Degraded mode (no PG) leaves the repo nil and the routes skip registration — proven by `TestUS249_ServiceAccountRoutesUnmountedWithoutRepo`.
- Tests: 4 model tests + 18 handler unit tests (Create 201 / auth / empty-name / invalid-name / bad-expiry / valid-expiry / name-conflict / List / Get-found / Get-404 / Update partial-patch / Update clear-expiry / Update-404 / Update bad-expiry / Delete soft-disable / Delete-404 / Delete-auth / RegisterRoutes round-trip) + 6 PG integration tests + 2 wire tests (routes-registered / routes-unmounted-without-repo). `go test -short ./pkg/...` 42 packages green, `go vet ./...` clean, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` clean.
- Files changed:
  - `migrations/000049_service_accounts.up.sql` (new)
  - `migrations/000049_service_accounts.down.sql` (new)
  - `pkg/auth/service_account.go` (new)
  - `pkg/auth/service_account_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/auth/service_account_repository.go` (new)
  - `pkg/auth/service_account_repository_test.go` (new; integration)

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The `deleteFor(w, r, id)` / `updateFor(w, r, id)` / `getFor(w, r, id)` split lets tests exercise the handler body without standing up a chi router to populate `chi.URLParam`. KEEP the auth check (`UserFromContext == nil ⇒ 401`) INSIDE the `*For` helper, not in the outer `Delete` / `Update` / `Get` wrapper. The wrapper is a thin chi-URL extractor; tests call the `*For` variant directly and would otherwise skip the auth gate entirely. Prior art: `api_key_handlers.go::DeleteFor` made the same mistake on first write and got corrected — same shape, same fix.
  - Unique-name scoped to ACTIVE rows via `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE disabled_at IS NULL` is the right shape for any "soft-delete with recreatable name" resource (API keys, service accounts, ontology branches, etc.). The partial predicate matches the one in `idx_api_keys_prefix` from migration 000010 and means recycling a name after disable is a single `INSERT` — no manual "rename the tombstone" dance. Translate the resulting 23505 to a typed domain error (`ErrServiceAccountNameConflict`) so the HTTP handler can emit a clean 409 without string-matching.
  - Triple-pointer fields (`ExpiresAt **time.Time`) on an Update DTO: needed when the underlying column is NULLABLE and callers need three distinct states — omit (don't touch), clear (set to NULL), set (overwrite). Double-pointer distinguishes "caller didn't send expiresAt" (nil outer) from "caller sent expiresAt=null" (non-nil outer, nil inner) from "caller sent expiresAt=<RFC3339>" (non-nil outer, non-nil inner). Prior single-pointer patterns (`*bool` / `*string`) handle the two-state case; a nullable-time column needs the extra indirection because `*time.Time` is already the wire form. Document each state in a struct-tag comment so future readers don't collapse two of them.
  - Gating admin routes behind `RequirePermission(PermUserManage)` inside a `api.With(...).Group(...)` block keeps the middleware chain localised to the service-account subtree without leaking the permission requirement to every other admin endpoint. Same shape used by `/api/admin/indexes/rebuild` and `/api/v2/admin/auditEvents` — any new admin-only CRUD surface should follow this pattern rather than threading the middleware through `RegisterRoutes`.
  - Conditional route mounting (`if deps.ServiceAccountRepo != nil { ... }`) interacts with the contract test invariants: routes ONLY appear in `chi.Walk` when the dep is wired, so the contract test harness (`newContractTestRouter`) must either (a) stub the repo so routes register + require an openapi entry, or (b) leave the repo nil so no chi route appears and no openapi entry is needed. US-249 picked (b) for now because the admin surface isn't part of the Foundry wire contract; future iterations that want SDK discoverability should wire a stub in the contract test harness AND add the 5 paths to openapi.yaml.

## 2026-04-19 - US-250 API Key 自动轮换
- Added migration `000050_api_key_rotation` — `rotates_at TIMESTAMPTZ` + `successor_id UUID REFERENCES api_keys(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` on api_keys. Partial index `idx_api_keys_rotates_at` on `rotates_at` scoped to `rotates_at IS NOT NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL` so the warning-queue scan stays cheap across the common "no rotation scheduled" case. FK is intentionally `ON DELETE SET NULL` (not CASCADE) — dropping the successor must not cascade into predecessor tombstones.
- `pkg/auth/api_key.go` — extended `APIKeyRecord` with `RotatesAt *time.Time` and `SuccessorID *string`, plus two helpers:
  - `IsRotationExpired(now)` — true iff `RotatesAt != nil && !now.Before(*RotatesAt)`. Boundary: `now == *RotatesAt` is inclusive ("the cut-off has landed").
  - `InRotationWarningWindow(now, window)` — true iff RotatesAt is in `[now, now+window]`. Past-RotatesAt rows are NOT in the window (that's rotation-expired); nil-RotatesAt or negative-window return false.
  - `DefaultAPIKeyRotationGrace` / `DefaultAPIKeyRotationWarning` constants both = `7 * 24 * time.Hour` per PRD literal.
- `pkg/auth/api_key_repository.go` — columns constant extended; scanAPIKey adds two `*time.Time` / `*string` scans. Two new interface methods:
  - `Rotate(ctx, predecessorID, successor, graceUntil)` — single tx: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` the predecessor (404 if missing/revoked, `ErrAPIKeyAlreadyRotated` if `successor_id != NULL`), INSERT the successor via the same INSERT used by Create, then UPDATE predecessor SET rotates_at + successor_id. Commit-after-both or rollback-if-either-fails.
  - `ListPendingRotations(ctx, now, within)` — `rotates_at BETWEEN now AND now+within`, excludes revoked rows, orders `rotates_at ASC`. Negative `within` clamps to zero.
- `ErrAPIKeyAlreadyRotated` sentinel: 1:1 with the PG "successor_id already set" state so handlers can 409 without string-matching.
- `pkg/auth/middleware.go` — after `IsExpired`, new guard: `IsRotationExpired(now)` → 401 `APIKeyRotated` with reason "api key grace period has ended; use the rotated successor". During the grace window (rotates_at in the future) the middleware still authenticates the predecessor as usual — both keys validate concurrently.
- `pkg/auth/api_key_handlers.go` — two new handlers (routes deliberately NOT mounted; tests exercise via `RotateFor` / direct `Rotations` the same way the existing Create/List/Delete pattern does, per US-006 removal decision):
  - `Rotate` / `RotateFor(w, r, id)` — POST /api/admin/api-keys/{id}/rotate. Body `{graceDays?: int}` defaults to 7. Mints a fresh raw key (new prefix, new hash), inherits the predecessor's Name / Scopes / ExpiresAt onto the successor row, fires `repo.Rotate`, emits `api_key_rotate` audit. Returns `APIKeyRotateResponse{ID, Name, RawKey, Prefix, Scopes, CreatedAt, ExpiresAt, PredecessorID, PredecessorExpiry}` with 201 status. Error map: 401 missing user, 403 non-owner, 404 missing/revoked, 409 already-rotated.
  - `Rotations(w, r)` — GET /api/admin/api-keys/rotations?withinDays=N. Lists the calling user's keys whose rotates_at is inside [now, now+window] (default window = 7 days, `DefaultAPIKeyRotationWarning`). Emits `api_key_rotation_warning` audit event per surfaced key so a poller / cron implements "到期前 7 天发送告警事件" by hitting this endpoint on a schedule.
- `pkg/auth/middleware_test.go::fakeAPIKeyRepo` — added `Rotate` + `ListPendingRotations` so the in-memory fake keeps parity with the interface. Same shape as Create/Get: copy-on-write `cp := *rec` to avoid aliasing between maps.
- `cmd/server/wire_us006_test.go::us006FakeAPIKeyRepo` — same two no-op additions so the contract + route-removal test suite keeps compiling.
- Tests:
  - `api_key_test.go`: `TestAPIKeyRecord_IsRotationExpired` (4 cases incl. boundary now==RotatesAt), `TestAPIKeyRecord_InRotationWarningWindow` (5 cases: nil, in-window, out-of-window, past, negative-window), `TestAPIKeyRotationDefaults`.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Same-table self-FK for rotation pairings: `successor_id UUID REFERENCES api_keys(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` is the correct cascade for a predecessor→successor pointer. ON DELETE CASCADE would nuke the predecessor tombstone the moment the successor is revoked, which loses the audit trail. ON DELETE SET NULL cleanly detaches the pointer without cascading. Same shape works for any "A supersedes B" relationship between rows in one table (workflow steps, config versions, policy revisions).
  - `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` inside a Begin/Commit wrapper is the right primitive for "read old value, decide, write new value" on the SAME row in Postgres. Without the FOR UPDATE the second concurrent Rotate sees `successor_id = NULL` at SELECT time, both mint successors, and the second UPDATE silently overwrites the first pointer — orphaning a successor row. Pair with idempotent sentinel errors (`ErrAPIKeyAlreadyRotated`) so callers can dedupe rather than silently accepting the later winner.
  - Inclusive vs exclusive cut-off semantics for "rotation landed": `!now.Before(*rotatesAt)` (inclusive, `now >= rotatesAt`) is the right invariant for a grace-period boundary — callers treat the cut-off as "starting this instant the old key is dead". Exclusive (`now.After(*rotatesAt)`) leaves a one-nanosecond window where the key is neither in-grace nor rotation-expired, which is the kind of off-by-one that only a unit test catches. The same inclusive shape applies to any "deadline has landed" check (expiry, quota reset, lease transfer).
  - When the routes for a feature are deliberately unmounted (US-006 API-key admin surface), the feature's HANDLER code still lives alongside its sibling handlers and its tests still call via the `*For(w, r, id)` split. Do not invent a new mounting mechanism for the rotation endpoints — mirror the existing Create/List/Delete pattern so a future "remount under OAuth Admin API" story flips all three routes on as a single toggle. Handler present + route absent is a legitimate state; tests against the handler via direct `*For` invocation is the documented escape hatch.
  - "Warning event" semantics in the PRD language are cheaply realised as `ListPendingRotations(now, within)` + audit emission per surfaced row inside the Rotations GET handler. A dedicated notification fanout would be premature — the caller (admin console, cron, SDK) can poll the endpoint on any cadence they like and the audit trail records what was seen. If a real-time "push to Slack on T-7d" arrives later, it wires around the existing endpoint rather than requiring a schema change.
  - Pointer field three-state for single-value UPDATE semantics applies to `graceDays int` too: instead of a `*int`, use `req.GraceDays > 0 ? custom : default` because 0 days of grace is nonsensical (same as not rotating). The three-state pointer pattern is for fields where zero-value is a legitimate caller intent (bool clear, string clear, *time.Time null); for integers where `<=0` is invalid, a bare `int` with a default-on-absent rule is simpler.

## 2026-04-19 - US-252 LDAP/AD 目录同步
- Added `github.com/go-ldap/ldap/v3 v3.4.13` (pure Go — verified `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` clean).
- Migration `000052_ldap_sync` extends `users` with `disabled_at TIMESTAMPTZ` (orphan tombstone), `ldap_dn TEXT` (stable correlation key — email can change in AD), `last_synced_at TIMESTAMPTZ`; mirrors the same on `groups`; adds new `ldap_sync_runs` audit table with start/end/seen/created/updated/disabled/added counters + error_message; partial unique indexes on `users.ldap_dn` + `groups.ldap_dn` (WHERE NOT NULL) so locally-provisioned rows never collide.
- `pkg/auth/ldap.go` houses `LDAPSyncConfig` + narrow `LDAPClient` interface (`SearchUsers` / `SearchGroups` / `Close`). Production `goLDAPClient` wraps go-ldap/ldap/v3 with `SearchWithPaging` (page=500), optional StartTLS, optional bind, configurable email/name/login attribute names — same code drives Active Directory (`sAMAccountName` / `mail` / `displayName`) and OpenLDAP (`uid` / `mail` / `cn`). `LDAPClientFactory` is a function type so the scheduler can mint a fresh connection per cycle (long-lived LDAP connections drop and AD ages them aggressively).
- `pkg/auth/ldap_repository.go` carries the narrow `LDAPSyncStore` interface + `*PGLDAPSyncStore` impl: `UpsertSyncedUser` (insert-or-update keyed on `ldap_dn`, clears `disabled_at` so a user that returns to the directory is re-enabled in one round-trip, never touches `password_hash`), `DisableOrphanedSyncedUsers` (only `WHERE ldap_dn IS NOT NULL` so locally-provisioned password users untouched), `UpsertSyncedGroup`, `ReplaceGroupMembers` (single tx: list-existing → diff → insert+delete, returns count of new memberships), `UserIDByDN` (returns ("", nil) on miss so caller decides), `RecordSyncRun` (inserts + opportunistic prune to most-recent 100 rows). Kept off `UserRepository` / `GroupRepository` to avoid the cascade-stub problem.
- `LDAPSyncService.Sync` orchestrates one cycle: connect → user-pull → upsert each → disable orphans → group-pull → upsert each + resolve member DNs → user IDs (de-duped) → reconcile membership → record run. Returns the populated `LDAPSyncRun` even on error (with `ErrorMessage` set + `FinishedAt` stamped) and ALWAYS calls `store.RecordSyncRun` before returning so the audit history is complete on partial failure. Clock injectable via `SetNowFunc`; logger overridable via `SetLogger`.
- `LDAPSyncScheduler` wraps the service in a `time.Ticker` loop. `Start(ctx)` runs an immediate sync (so operators see directory state on boot, not after the first interval) then ticks every `interval` (default 1h, clamps `<=0` to default). `Stop()` is idempotent; loop exits on either `ctx.Done()` or `Stop()`. Connection lifecycle is per-cycle (factory mints a fresh `*ldap.Conn` each Sync) so transient drops self-heal at the next tick.
- `LDAPConfig` added to `internal/config/config.go` with full `WEAVE_LDAP_*` env wiring (`URL` / `BIND_DN` / `BIND_PASSWORD` / `STARTTLS` / `INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY` / `USER_BASE_DN` / `USER_FILTER` / `USER_EMAIL_ATTR` / `USER_NAME_ATTR` / `USER_LOGIN_ATTR` / `GROUP_BASE_DN` / `GROUP_FILTER` / `GROUP_NAME_ATTR` / `GROUP_MEMBER_ATTR` / `GROUP_DESCRIPTION_ATTR` / `INTERVAL`). `AUTH_MODE=ldap` is shorthand for `LDAP.Enabled=true` (operators can also leave `AUTH_MODE=jwt` and just set `WEAVE_LDAP_ENABLED=true`). `Validate()` reports missing URL / UserBaseDN at boot in one error message.
- `cmd/server/main.go` bootstrap mirrors the OIDC/SAML pattern exactly: gated on PG pool + `Validate`, degraded loudly via `log.Printf` on misconfig, `defer ldapSched.Stop()` so the ticker drains cleanly on SIGTERM. No PG pool in degraded mode → directory sync disabled with a clear warning, password / OIDC / SAML logins keep working.
- Tests: 14 unit tests in `pkg/auth/ldap_test.go` with stub LDAPClient + in-memory LDAPSyncStore — `TestLDAPSyncConfig_Validate` (missing URL / missing UserBaseDN / happy), `TestLDAPSyncConfig_WithDefaults`, `TestSync_HappyPath_CreatesUsersAndGroups` (2 users + 2 groups + 3 memberships, Close called once), `TestSync_DisablesOrphanedUsers` (Bob disappears → disabled), `TestSync_RecyclesPreviouslyDisabledUser` (Bob returns → disabled_at cleared), `TestSync_UnknownMemberDNDoesNotFail` (ghost / empty / duplicate DNs filtered), `TestSync_UpsertUserError_RecordsRunWithError` (audit row written even on failure), `TestSync_NoFactoryOrStore_ReturnsError`, `TestSync_GroupMembershipShrinksOnSecondPass` (membership reconciliation deletes removed users), `TestScheduler_RunsImmediatelyAndStops` (initial run within 2s + idempotent Stop), `TestScheduler_DefaultIntervalApplied`. Plus 4 config tests in `internal/config/config_test.go` (auth-mode shortcut, default-disabled, missing-fields validation, fully-populated passes).

  - `migrations/000052_ldap_sync.up.sql` + `.down.sql` (new)

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - go-ldap/ldap/v3 uses `SearchWithPaging(req, pageSize)` for transparent paging — PASS the search request directly, not a wrapped one. The library handles cookie continuation internally; the caller just gets the merged `*ldap.SearchResult` back. Page size 500 is the AD default; smaller wastes round-trips, larger risks `LDAP_SIZELIMIT_EXCEEDED` against tighter DC policies.
  - Stable correlation key for directory sync is the DN (or `objectGUID` in AD), NEVER the email. Email changes in AD when a user marries / re-orgs; DN does not. Prior art (US-246 OIDC) keys on email because OIDC `sub` is provider-scoped and email is the cross-provider stable identity for SSO callbacks; the LDAP shape is different — same directory, full attribute access, so use the directory's own stable key. The `ldap_dn` column is the bookkeeping handle; `id` (email-based, `user:<email>`) stays the canonical Weave user id so existing role/permission grants are unaffected when an LDAP user appears.
  - "Soft-mark deleted users disabled" semantics belong AT THE DB layer with `disabled_at` + a partial index `WHERE disabled_at IS NULL` for active reads, NOT a hard `DELETE`. Reasoning: (1) audit trail — operators need to know "Bob was here last quarter, then left"; (2) restore — re-enable on return is an UPDATE, not a re-CREATE that loses role grants; (3) FK safety — every audit row referencing the user keeps working without ON DELETE CASCADE side-effects. Same shape as US-249 service accounts and US-010 API keys; the partial-index trick generalises. Apply the disable ONLY to rows with `ldap_dn IS NOT NULL` so locally-provisioned password users (admins, breakglass accounts) are untouched.
  - Re-enable on directory-return is one UPDATE branch in `UpsertSyncedUser`: `SET disabled_at = NULL, last_synced_at = $syncedAt, ...`. Don't model "re-enable" as a separate action — every successful sync of a user implicitly says "this user is active right now". Otherwise the orphan-disable + re-add cycle would need a manual reconciliation step. Test it explicitly (TestSync_RecyclesPreviouslyDisabledUser) so a future contributor doesn't "optimise" the unconditional clear away.
  - Connection-per-cycle (factory-style) vs persistent connection: LDAP/AD aggressively age out idle connections (default 15min on AD, 5min on OpenLDAP) and the v3 library does NOT auto-reconnect on dropped sockets. Re-binding once an hour is cheap; the alternative (persistent connection + reconnect-on-error) is a `*ldap.Conn` lifecycle-management problem that's much easier to get wrong. Run the bind in the factory closure so the test stub doesn't need to mock authentication; just return a stub client.
  - Multi-table membership reconciliation belongs in a single transaction inside the store layer, not loop-of-Add/Remove from the service. A naive "for each desired user, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; for each existing user not in desired, DELETE" works but is N+M round-trips per group; for AD with 50k users in a group this is the main slow path. The current shape (one tx, cheap N+M Execs) is fine for v1; if scale demands, swap for a single CTE-based DELETE+INSERT under the same tx without changing the caller. Don't push membership-reconciliation logic into the SyncService — it'd duplicate the diff for any future "reconcile from REST API" / "reconcile from admin UI" callers.
  - Initial-run-on-Start vs first-tick-on-interval: the scheduler runs Sync immediately on `Start(ctx)` so operators don't have to wait an interval to see boot-time bootstrap happen. Without this, a fresh deploy with LDAP enabled would have an empty user table for up to 1h. The trade-off is that misconfigured directories produce a loud failure at boot rather than at first tick — that's actually what you want; degrading silently for the first hour is worse.
  - Membership-resolution: dedupe the user-id slice with a `map[string]struct{}` BEFORE handing it to ReplaceGroupMembers. AD groups can list the same DN twice (rare but happens with nested-group expansion + manual entry); without the dedupe the `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` would silently swallow it but the `added` counter would be wrong. Filter empty-DN entries too — some directories return `member: ` rows when a user was deleted but the group wasn't cleaned up.
  - Audit row written even on failure (`finish` closure pattern): wrap the success/failure path in a single helper that stamps `FinishedAt` + `ErrorMessage` and calls `RecordSyncRun` BEFORE returning. Otherwise an early `return err` skips the audit insert and operators see "sync silently stopped" with no row in `ldap_sync_runs`. Same pattern as the "commit-then-publish" shape from US-238 — one defer/closure that ensures the durable side-effect happens regardless of which branch the caller takes.
  - LDAPSyncStore as a NARROW interface in pkg/auth (not on UserRepository / GroupRepository): widening either of those broadly-mocked interfaces would cascade into ~15 stub implementations. Same reasoning that drove US-202 ComputedPropertyStore, US-203 MediaAssetStore, US-249 ServiceAccountRepository. Pattern: narrow interface + concrete `*PG*Store` impl + handler / service consumes the interface.

## 2026-04-19 - US-253 MFA 多因素认证 (TOTP)
- Added migration `000053_mfa_totp` with `users.mfa_secret TEXT` + `users.mfa_enabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE` + partial idx `idx_users_mfa_enabled WHERE mfa_enabled = TRUE`. Down drops both columns and the index.
- Extended `UserRecord` with `MFASecret string` + `MFAEnabled bool`; updated `GetUserByID` / `GetUserByEmail` to read `COALESCE(mfa_secret, '') / COALESCE(mfa_enabled, FALSE)` so legacy rows pre-migration still scan cleanly.
- New `pkg/auth/mfa.go`: `GenerateTOTPSecret(issuer, account)` (period=30, digits=6, sha1 — pquerna/otp/totp.Generate); `ValidateTOTPCode(secret, code, now)` with `Skew=1` for ±30s clock drift tolerance; `ErrInvalidMFACode` sentinel; `MFASecretStore` narrow interface (SetMFASecret / SetMFAEnabled / ClearMFA); `*PGUserRepository` satisfies it via three single-column UPDATE pattern (mirrors `SetPassword`).
- New `pkg/auth/mfa_challenge.go`: in-memory single-use `MFAChallengeStore` bridging `/api/auth/login` (mints) and `/api/auth/mfa/verify` (consumes). 32-byte random base64url token, 5-minute default TTL, `SetNowFunc` for deterministic tests, lazy-eviction on every Issue. `ErrMFAChallengeNotFound` + `ErrMFAChallengeExpired` sentinels.
- New `pkg/auth/mfa_handler.go`: `MFAHandler` with `RegisterRoutes` mounting four endpoints:
  - `POST /api/auth/mfa/setup` — auth required, generates a fresh secret, returns base32 secret + otpauth URL + base64-encoded 256x256 PNG QR (`otp.NewKeyFromURL().Image(256, 256)` + `image/png.Encode`). Persists secret but does NOT activate; flips `mfa_enabled=false` if the user was previously enrolled (rotation semantics).
  - `POST /api/auth/mfa/enable` — auth required, validates the supplied code against the stored secret, then `SetMFAEnabled(true)`. Audit `mfa_enabled` / `mfa_enable_failed`.
  - `POST /api/auth/mfa/disable` — auth required, validates code (prevents stolen-session disable) then `ClearMFA`. No-op success when user already not enrolled (idempotent).
  - `POST /api/auth/mfa/verify` — public, consumes the challenge token + validates the TOTP code, then mints the same `LoginResponse` shape `/login` returns (access + refresh + LoginUser). Defensive: rejects 401 if MFA was disabled between login and verify.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The pquerna/otp library exposes the QR-PNG render path through `otp.Key.Image(width, height)` returning a stdlib `image.Image`, then `png.Encode` to bytes. `Image()` requires a Key constructed from the otpauth URL — go through `otp.NewKeyFromURL(otpURL)` rather than re-rendering the URL in the handler. Returning the QR as base64 (no `data:` prefix) keeps the JSON contract clean and lets the SPA pick the wrapping (`<img src="data:image/png;base64,${qr}">`).
  - TOTP validation MUST go through `totp.ValidateCustom` with explicit `Skew=1` (±1 step = ±30s tolerance). The default `totp.Validate` accepts skew=1 but hides it; explicit ValidateCustom is what tests actually pin so a future library upgrade can't silently change the window. `Period=30, Digits=6, Algorithm=SHA1` are the Google Authenticator defaults — change them and existing enrolled users' codes stop working.
  - "Pre-flight challenge" pattern (login → 202 + challenge token, then verify → final tokens): single-use server-side store is materially simpler than a signed JWT challenge — replay protection for free (delete-on-consume), no key-rotation concerns, no extra audience/scope claim. The 5-minute TTL is long enough to read a code off an authenticator app on a slow phone and short enough to keep the replay window tiny. Only downside is that the challenge state lives on a single process; multi-replica deployments would need a Redis-backed store. Document the constraint in the handler doc-comment when shipping.
  - Capture-bare-PG-repo-before-wrapping is the recurring pattern for narrow stores added on `*PGUserRepository` (`MFAStore`) — same shape as `MediaCatalog` (US-204) and `ComputedPropertyStore` (US-202). Generalisation: any new MFA-style narrow interface that needs read-after-write semantics on the user row MUST be served by the uncached `*PGUserRepository` reference, NOT routed through the (currently nonexistent) `auth.CachedUserRepository` wrapper if one ever lands.
  - Login-handler MFA branch placement matters: it MUST come AFTER `VerifyPassword` succeeds (so we don't leak "this user has MFA" via timing on bad-password attempts) and BEFORE the role-resolve / sign / refresh-mint block (so we don't waste a refresh token slot on an attempt that won't complete). Put both `auditLogin(ctx, ..., "login_mfa_required")` and the 202 write inside the same branch so the audit row is always paired with the challenge being issued.
  - Defensive `MFANotEnrolled` check inside `/verify`: between login and verify the admin (or the user themselves on another device) may have disabled MFA. In that case we MUST refuse to mint a token rather than silently fall through — the SPA should re-attempt `/login` and discover that the challenge isn't needed any more. Without this check a stolen challenge token + any code (including blank) would mint a session.
  - `errors.Is` discrimination at the HTTP layer: `ErrMFAChallengeNotFound` and `ErrMFAChallengeExpired` both surface as 401 InvalidMFAChallenge with the same wire shape — distinguishing them in the body is fine for debugging but the SPA reaction is identical (re-login). Don't try to dispatch them to different status codes.

## 2026-04-19 03:49 - US-254 Session 管理
- migration 000054 introduces `sessions` (UUID PK, user_id FK, refresh_token_id FK ON DELETE SET NULL, ip, user_agent, created_at, last_seen) plus per-user and (user_id, last_seen DESC) indexes.
- pkg/auth/session_store.go: `SessionRecord` model + narrow `SessionStore` interface (Create/Get/ListByUser/Delete/DeleteAllForUser/Touch/RotateRefreshToken) + `MemorySessionStore` in-memory impl with sort-by-LastSeen-desc and owner-enforced delete; `ErrSessionNotFound` / `ErrSessionForbidden` are the HTTP status sentinels.
- pkg/auth/pg_session_store.go: pgxpool implementation mirroring the interface. Delete is two-step (SELECT user_id → compare → DELETE) so 404 vs 403 stays distinguishable without RETURNING.

List filters to caller.ID, marks the current row via `User.Attributes[SessionIDAttributeKey]`, serialises to `SessionListResponse{sessions: []SessionView}` (empty-array-not-null). Delete emits 204 on success, 401 when unauth, 403 when caller isn't owner, 404 on missing. When RefreshService is wired and row.RefreshTokenID!="" the delete revokes the refresh row with reason `session_revoked` so cookie-bearing attackers lose access at the next access-token rollover.
- LoginHandler and MFAHandler.Verify optionally create a session on success (IP via clientIP, UA from r.UserAgent, RefreshTokenID from refreshRec.ID). RefreshHandler calls `RotateRefreshToken(oldRec.ID, newRec.ID, time.Now())` on successful rotate so the session row's refresh_token_id tracks the live chain member across rotations.

SessionHandler.RegisterRoutes mounted INSIDE the auth middleware group, conditional on deps.SessionStore != nil; degraded/contract-test routers skip registration and the insert. Login/Refresh/MFA handlers thread Sessions through their deps blocks.
- 14 new unit tests across session_store_test.go (create validation, list ordering, owner-scoped delete, touch, delete-all-for-user) and session_handler_test.go (401 unauth list, 200 list filters to caller, current marker, 204 owner delete, 403 non-owner, 404 missing, refresh revoked on session delete, empty array not null).
- Files changed: migrations/000054_sessions.{up,down}.sql; pkg/auth/session_store.go; pkg/auth/pg_session_store.go; pkg/auth/session_handler.go; pkg/auth/login_handler.go; pkg/auth/mfa_handler.go; pkg/auth/refresh_handler.go; cmd/server/main.go; pkg/auth/session_store_test.go; pkg/auth/session_handler_test.go; prd.json; progress.txt.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The session row PK must be stable across refresh rotations; make refresh_token_id a mutable column and introduce a store method (`RotateRefreshToken`) that the refresh handler calls after a successful rotate. Otherwise DELETE /sessions/{id} would need to walk parent_id chains or revoke the whole user.
  - When adding auth-feature handlers that extract the caller via `UserFromContext`, mount them INSIDE the `r.Group(api chi.Router)` block that runs `auth.MiddlewareFull`. Registering them outside silently renders every request unauthenticated.
  - Two-step delete (SELECT then DELETE) is the cleanest way to surface separate 404 / 403 responses without RETURNING or dialect-specific tricks — pattern already used by api_key_handlers but worth the explicit ErrForbidden sentinel for reuse.
  - RefreshHandler must call `RefreshService.Lookup(plain)` BEFORE `Rotate` to snapshot the old record; Rotate consumes/revokes internally and subsequent Lookups by the same plaintext return the revoked row (which Sessions.RotateRefreshToken would rebind away from — wrong direction).
  - `nullableTime` + `COALESCE($N, now())` keeps nullable-timestamp wire-level inputs honest: pgx would pass zero times as timestamp-zero otherwise, which would fail the NOT NULL constraint. Prior art in pg_refresh_store.go.
  - Handler test helper `withURLParam(r, key, val)` attaches a chi.RouteContext to the request — lets the handler be exercised without a full router, matching the pattern from pkg/actions/actions_test.go. Necessary when the handler calls `chi.URLParam(r, "sessionID")` directly; test harnesses that skip this step get empty params and 400 errors.

## 2026-04-19 - US-255 SSO 单点登出 (OIDC back-channel logout + SAML SLO)
- New OIDC back-channel logout endpoint at `POST /api/auth/oidc/back-channel-logout`:
  - `pkg/auth/oidc_logout_handler.go` (new) — `OIDCBackChannelLogoutHandler` reuses the OIDC `Verifier` already wired by `NewOIDCDepsFromProvider` so the same JWKS that validates id_tokens validates logout_tokens. Validates: JWT signature/iss/aud/exp via go-oidc, then claim-shape rules from OIDC Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.4 (events claim must include `BackChannelLogoutEventKey`, nonce MUST be absent, sub OR sid MUST be present).
  - User resolution walks `subjectCandidates`: email-claim first → sub-as-email-fallback → `user:<sub>` userID-fallback → raw sub. Unknown subjects return 200 idempotently per spec (don't disclose user-store membership to a potentially malicious caller).
  - On match: `RefreshService.RevokeAllForUser(reason="oidc_back_channel_logout")` + `SessionStore.DeleteAllForUser(userID)`. Response: 200 + `Cache-Control: no-store` + `{}` body.
- New SAML Single Logout endpoint at `POST /api/auth/saml/slo`:
  - `pkg/auth/saml_slo_handler.go` (new) — `SAMLSLOHandler` driven by a NEW narrow `SAMLLogoutVerifier` interface (`ValidateLogoutRequest` + `BuildLogoutResponse`). The existing `gosamlVerifier` (which already implements `SAMLAssertionVerifier` for login) gets two new methods so a single instance powers both ACS and SLO. Production wiring in `cmd/server/main.go` does `samlVerifier.(auth.SAMLLogoutVerifier)` to lift the same value into both surfaces.
  - `ValidateLogoutRequest` calls `gosaml2.ValidateEncodedLogoutRequestPOST` (signature + version + destination + issuer); `BuildLogoutResponse` uses `BuildLogoutResponseDocumentNoSig` so we don't need to ship an SP keypair for the v1 path. Operators that need signed responses can wire an SP keypair into the gosaml2 SP and switch to `BuildLogoutResponseDocument`.
  - User resolution walks `samlNameIDCandidates`: NameID-as-email → `user:<email>`-fallback → raw NameID userID. Unknown NameIDs still emit `StatusCodeSuccess` so the IdP doesn't loop on retries.
  - On match: `RefreshService.RevokeAllForUser(reason="saml_slo")` + `SessionStore.DeleteAllForUser(userID)`. Response: 200 + `Cache-Control: no-store` + base64-encoded LogoutResponse XML body (gosaml2's response-validation path expects base64).
- `pkg/auth/refresh_service.go` grew `RevokeAllForUser(userID, reason)` — bulk passthrough to `RefreshStore.RevokeAllForUser`. The plain `RefreshService.Revoke(plain)` only handles a single token by plaintext; SSO logout flows need bulk revocation by user, hence the new method.
- `cmd/server/main.go`:
  - `ServerDeps` gained `OIDCLogoutHandler` + `SAMLSLOHandler` fields. Both are nil-able and only register routes when the underlying SSO front-door is wired (degraded-mode test routers leave them unset).
  - OIDC bootstrap block now constructs `auth.NewOIDCBackChannelLogoutHandler` alongside `auth.NewOIDCHandler`, sharing the same `verifier`. Same shape inside the SAML bootstrap block: `auth.NewSAMLSLOHandler` is constructed when the gosaml2 verifier satisfies the `SAMLLogoutVerifier` interface (it does — production-builder smoke test asserts it).
  - Route registration mirrors the existing pattern: registered inside the auth-protected block, gated on the handler being non-nil.
- Tests (22 new across two files):
  - `oidc_logout_handler_test.go` (12 tests): happy path clears session + refresh + sets Cache-Control: no-store + revocation reason; non-POST rejected; missing token rejected with `OIDCLogoutMissingToken`; signature mismatch rejected with `OIDCLogoutTokenInvalid`; nonce claim rejected with reason mentioning "nonce"; missing events rejected; wrong events key rejected; missing sub AND sid rejected; unknown user returns 200 idempotently; sid-only token validates shape (200 with nothing to revoke); sub-only token resolves via `user:<email>` fallback; bulk revocation is user-scoped (alice cleared, bob untouched); `RegisterRoutes` mounts the right path.
