- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Extending an existing narrow interface with a FULLY optional method argument: add a new `WithXxx(..., xxx)` variant that delegates to the existing signature with a nil/zero tail argument. `database.ConnectWithTracer(ctx, dsn, pc, tracer)` lets main.go inject the pgx tracer while every existing test/caller keeps using the zero-arg `Connect` / `ConnectWithConfig` untouched. Same shape as `oms.OMSHandler.SetXxx` setter-injection, but for constructors where the dep is known at call time rather than after.
  - Keeping pkg/tracing dep-minimal: the BaggageMiddleware needs the caller's user ID from the request context, but importing pkg/auth into pkg/tracing would form a soft dependency spine from every span-wrapped package into auth. Solution: accept a `UserIDFunc func(ctx) string` at middleware construction time and let the call site (cmd/server) close over `auth.UserFromContext(ctx).ID`. Pkg/tracing stays importable by any package in the repo — including pkg/auth if it ever wants spans. General rule: whenever a library-style package needs a plug-point into a higher-level concept (user, tenant, locale, …), take a function literal, not an interface, not a type import.
  - pgx.QueryTracer is the canonical hook for "span per SQL statement" coverage on pgxpool-backed repos: attach it at `cfg.ConnConfig.Tracer` before `pgxpool.NewWithConfig`. No per-query code change needed — every Query/QueryRow/Exec/SendBatch flows through the tracer. Keeps repo packages (pkg/oms, pkg/auth, pkg/audit, …) free of `tracing.StartSpan` boilerplate at every query site. The tracer is only beneficial when tracing.Enabled=true; wire it conditionally so dev/test paths don't allocate spans per statement.
  - Composite TextMapPropagator is the right default for OpenTelemetry: `propagation.NewCompositeTextMapPropagator(TraceContext{}, Baggage{})` gives you both W3C trace-stitching AND cross-service baggage forwarding in one line. Installing it on the `Enabled=false` path too means any in-process span authors (tests, background jobs that construct spans manually via the global provider's no-op tracer) get sane inject/extract behaviour without extra setup.
  - OTLP exporter protocol selection: support BOTH explicit shorthands (`Exporter="otlphttp"` / `"otlpgrpc"`) AND a generic `Exporter="otlp"` that defers to a companion `OTLPProtocol` field. Operators who know exactly what they want set the shorthand; operators with env-var-driven wiring set a single `WEAVE_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc` override without re-configuring the primary exporter knob. Default `OTLPProtocol=http` matches OTel collector conventions (port 4318 for HTTP, 4317 for gRPC — HTTP is the more forgiving default for K8s sidecars).
  - Span-wrapping middleware pairs with chi middleware.RequestID: install tracing.HTTPMiddleware AFTER RequestID so the span name resolution and the chi request_id are consistently available. Install tracing.BaggageMiddleware AFTER that — it needs the request_id on context AND the active span on context. Order matters: `RequestID → HTTPMiddleware → BaggageMiddleware → [auth] → rest`.
  - `trace.SpanFromContext(ctx)` returns a no-op span (not nil) when no active span is in the context, so `if span.IsRecording()` is the safe predicate before setting attributes. No-op spans accept SetAttributes calls silently but don't emit anything, which still wastes an alloc for the attribute key/value; IsRecording() short-circuits cheaply. Use the same guard in any helper that mutates a span discovered from context (BaggageMiddleware, RecordError, …).

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Grafana dashboard provisioning: the v1 file provider `options.path` points INSIDE the container (`/var/lib/grafana/dashboards`), not into the repo. The docker-compose volume mount `./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro` is what bridges repo→container. `allowUiUpdates: false` keeps the repo authoritative — operators editing in the UI get "read-only" toasts. Default refresh is 10s; 30s is fine for SLO dashboards and avoids needlessly hammering Prometheus on a laptop setup.
  - Dashboard datasource should always be templated `${datasource}` with a datasource-typed variable (`"type": "datasource"`) — letting operators pick their Prometheus instance at view time keeps the JSON portable across dev/stage/prod without a sed-based copy. Grafana auto-selects the default datasource when the variable first evaluates, so the UID-pinned provisioning datasource (`uid: prometheus`) still "just works" out of the box.

  - Docker-compose syntax test: `docker compose config --quiet` is the cheapest CI-friendly validator — exits 0 on valid yaml + valid compose schema, nonzero with a precise error pointing at the offending key. Much better than ad-hoc yaml.Unmarshal which misses compose-specific semantics (`condition: service_started`, etc.).
  - For a dashboard JSON test, matching panel identity via "title OR any target.expr contains the ID" is the flex-tolerant shape — titles evolve through copyediting; PromQL expressions evolve through tuning; requiring BOTH to stay the same makes the test brittle for no benefit. Substring matching on the expected metric name inside at least one target is the real invariant worth enforcing.

  - `alerts/weave.yml` (new)
  - `grafana/prometheus.yml` (rule_files glob added)

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Two-group rule file layout (`weave.slo` + `weave.infra`) is the
    principled split when a deliverable mixes "alerts that fire on metrics
    the service itself emits" with "alerts that fire on companion-exporter
    metrics." The infra group stays inert without postgres_exporter /
    node_exporter and operators who don't run the companion exporters
    don't get unloadable-rule warnings at Prometheus startup — the rule
    file loads fine, the expressions just evaluate to empty vectors
    forever until the companion exporter lands. Much better than
    hard-gating the rule file behind a "do you have exporter X?" flag.
  - Glob-based `rule_files: /etc/prometheus/rules/*.yml` is the cheapest
    ongoing-maintenance pattern for alerting-rule files: dropping a new
    YAML under ./alerts is picked up on the next restart without
    prometheus.yml churn. The test-side matcher has to mirror that —
    accept either an explicit path OR a `filepath.Match`-compatible glob
    that would match the canonical filename. Hard-coding the explicit
    path in the test forces every new feature to edit prometheus.yml,
    which defeats the glob.
  - `rate()` subtraction for "publisher outpacing consumer" is the right
    shape when both sides emit counter-valued `_total` metrics with a
    shared label (here `subject`). Requires `by (subject)` on BOTH legs
    of the subtraction so the sum-over-label happens before the delta;
    a raw `rate(publish_total) - rate(consume_total)` without the
    dimension-matching label emits a many-to-many error.
  - Test shape for "at least N alerts" acceptance criteria: `TotalCountAtLeastFive`
    does not enumerate alert names — it just counts. Future stories adding
    a 6th alert don't need to update the count assertion, and the PRD
    criterion stays the test's source of truth. Pair it with a companion
    test that checks the specific named alerts so a typo-rename can't
    silently pass by sharing the total count.
  - YAML-roundtrip envelope structs: define the envelope INSIDE the test
    (not in production code) because the shape is only meaningful as a
    schema assertion. Use `yaml:"..."` tags on every public field so the
    parser doesn't silently drop rule fields — `for` is the common
    footgun because Go's zero-value `""` for a missing duration would
    otherwise silently make the test pass for a rule with no debounce.

## 2026-04-19 - US-274
- 实现 scripts/backup.sh + scripts/restore.sh + scripts/test-restore.sh，
  补齐 PRD 验收所要求的"全量逻辑备份 + 媒体快照 + WAL archive + PITR"链路。
- backup.sh 输出布局：BACKUP_DIR/<UTC>/db.dump (pg_dump custom-format) +
  media.tar.gz (data/media tar) + wal/ (rsync from $WAL_ARCHIVE_DIR) +
  manifest.json (sha256 + sizes + WAL segment count)。RETAIN_DAYS 默认 14
  天，超过则 find -mtime + rm -rf 清理。
- restore.sh <timestamp|latest> 用字符串比较挑选 ≤ 指定 UTC 时间的最新备份
  目录，校验 db.dump sha256，pg_restore --clean --if-exists 进目标 DSN，
  把 media tar 解到 $WEAVE_DATA_DIR (旧 media 移到带时间戳的 .pre-restore
  目录，避免误覆盖)。当 PITR_TARGET_TIME 设置时 stage WAL 到
  WAL_RESTORE_DIR 并打印 recovery.signal/restore_command 操作指引；脚本
  本身不重启 Postgres，把"是否真的要重启"留给 operator。
- test-restore.sh 端到端验证：在源 DSN 同主机上建 weave_restore_test_$$ DB，
  跑 backup.sh + restore.sh，比对 schema_migrations / ontologies /
  object_types / properties / link_types 行数；trap EXIT 清理临时库与
  备份目录。
- 文件改动：
  - 新增 scripts/backup.sh, scripts/restore.sh, scripts/test-restore.sh
    (chmod +x，#!/usr/bin/env bash + set -euo pipefail)
  - 新增 internal/backup/scripts_test.go — 8 项纯静态测试 (Exist /
    Executable / BashParse / HaveShebang + 4 项内容不变量)，无需 Postgres
    即可在 go test ./... 中跑过
  - prd.json US-274 passes=true
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Operator-shipped shell scripts are testable from Go via 4 layers:
    `os.Stat` + perm-bit check (executable), `exec.LookPath("bash") +
    bash -n` (parse), first-line shebang assertion, and string-contains
    invariant checks for the load-bearing commands (pg_dump / pg_restore /
    DROP DATABASE / etc). All pure-static — no Postgres required. Mirror
    the `internal/dashboards` repoRoot helper instead of inventing a new
    one. Use `runtime.GOOS == "windows"` skip for the unix-mode-bit test;
    `t.Skipf` (not `t.Fatalf`) when `bash` isn't on PATH so Windows CI
    stays green.
  - Operator-script invariant tests should match on the **load-bearing
    commands** (pg_dump, pg_restore, set -euo pipefail), NOT on incidental
    formatting (variable names, comments, log strings). A future
    refactoring that renames a temp variable shouldn't fail the test;
    a refactoring that drops `pg_dump` or `set -euo pipefail` should.
    Keep the assertions small and semantically meaningful.
  - PITR scripts should NEVER auto-restart Postgres or rewrite
    postgresql.conf. Stage the WAL segments + print the operator
    instructions, then exit 0. Operator must manually create
    recovery.signal / set restore_command / restart — that's a deliberate
    "I want PITR" gate that prevents an `scripts/restore.sh latest` typo
    from rolling the live cluster back. Same principle: any production
    DROP / TRUNCATE / config-rewrite operation belongs in operator hands,
    not in a script that might be invoked from cron.
  - "Backup directory string-compare to filter by timestamp" works
    because the YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ stamp is lexicographically ordered. Use
    `[ "$d" \< "$target" ]` rather than `date +%s` arithmetic — the
    latter introduces shell/date-utility portability concerns
    (BSD vs GNU date) that the string compare avoids entirely.
  - `find -mtime +N -exec rm -rf {} +` is the portable retention idiom
    for daily-rotated backup directories. The `+` form batches into a
    single rm invocation per N args (vs `\;` which fork/execs per file)
    and `mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1` avoids descending into the matched
    backup subtrees (the rm -rf does that).
  - tar's `-C <dir>` flag changes directory BEFORE archiving so the
    tarball entries are stored relative to the data root, not the
    absolute host path. `tar -C $WEAVE_DATA_DIR -czf media.tar.gz media`
    creates entries `media/...` which un-tar cleanly into any future
    data root via `tar -C $NEW_ROOT -xzf media.tar.gz`. Mismatched
    `-C` between backup + restore would create surprising path nesting.
  - Manifest sha256 in backups is checked at restore time, not at
    backup time. Backup-side checksum would catch only "the bytes I
    just wrote don't match the bytes I just read" (which is essentially
    impossible on a healthy filesystem). Restore-side checksum catches
    the actual failure mode: backup file was corrupted at rest /
    truncated by an out-of-disk scenario / replicated to a disk that
    silently flipped a bit. `shasum -a 256` is on macOS and Linux;
    GNU coreutils ships `sha256sum` instead — use `shasum -a 256` for
    portability.
  - `psql -tAc 'SELECT count(*)'` (-t = tuples-only, -A = unaligned)
    returns the bare integer with no padding so it's directly
    comparable in a shell `[ "$a" = "$b" ]` test. Without -tA you get
    " 12\n" with leading space + trailing newline and the comparison
    silently fails.
  - PG_DSN parsing in pure shell: extract the dbname segment with
    `sed -E 's#.*/([^?]+).*#\1#'` (handles both `dsn/db` and
    `dsn/db?sslmode=disable` shapes). Don't try to parse the full URL
    — the auth segment has `:` and `@` in arbitrary places and a
    portable parser is more code than the rest of the script. Stick
    to the dbname extraction; everything else stays inside the DSN
    blob and gets handed to libpq verbatim.

  `HANDOFF_PROBES=30`. Static `internal/upgrade/scripts_test.go` mirrors
  `internal/backup/scripts_test.go`: exists / executable / bash -n /
  shebang / strict-mode / dual-instance invariants ({BIN,_PORT,/health/live,
  /health/ready,SIGTERM,trap cleanup,handoff}).
- `docs/upgrade.md` documents the full runbook: probe split table, the
  four forward-compat invariants, the breaking-migration registry, and
  the `BIN_OLD=... BIN_NEW=... ./scripts/rolling-upgrade.sh` operator
  workflow. `TestForwardCompat_DocumentedInUpgradeDoc` ties the registry
  to the doc so an exception added without a runbook line fails CI.
- Files changed:
  - `cmd/server/main.go` (LivenessHandler shared between `/health` + `/health/live`)
  - `cmd/server/health_test.go` (test loop covers both liveness paths)
  - `cmd/server/wire_us006_test.go` (added /health/live to route inventory + comment header)
  - `api/openapi.yaml` + `cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` (new /health/live operation)
  - `migrations/000027_automation_result.up.sql` (IF NOT EXISTS)
  - `migrations/000029_automation_retry_policy.up.sql` (IF NOT EXISTS)
  - `internal/upgrade/forward_compat_test.go` (new; static migration scan)
  - `internal/upgrade/scripts_test.go` (new; rolling-upgrade.sh static checks)
  - `scripts/rolling-upgrade.sh` (new; dual-instance drill)
  - `docs/upgrade.md` (new; operator runbook)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Forward-compat invariants are STATIC repo properties — every check
    in `internal/upgrade/forward_compat_test.go` runs against the
    on-disk `migrations/*.up.sql` blobs. No live PG required, so the
    suite stays in the default `go test ./...` lane (single-digit
    milliseconds). Use the same shape for any future "every file must
    have property X" guarantee — invest the 30 lines of regex + an
    allowlist map, save a hundred PR-time review comments.
  - When introducing a static-invariant test against a large existing
    tree, the right move on first failure is to FIX the violations not
    to grandfather them — `migrations/000027` and `000029` were trivial
    `IF NOT EXISTS` adds. Allowlists are reserved for genuine breaking
    changes that already shipped under a maintenance window (000041),
    not "we couldn't be bothered" exceptions. Each allowlist entry must
    be paired with a docs/upgrade.md runbook line, which the
    `TestForwardCompat_DocumentedInUpgradeDoc` check enforces.
  - Two-process coordination scripts (rolling-upgrade.sh, future "blue
    /green warm cache", "shadow read replay", etc.) want a single
    `cleanup()` function attached via `trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM` that
    no-ops on already-dead PIDs (`kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null`). The
    trap fires on script exit AND on SIGINT, so Ctrl-C during a long
    drill never leaves zombies. Capture each spawned PID into a
    well-named variable so the cleanup branch can blank it after wait
    — re-trying cleanup on an already-reaped PID is a noisy benign
    error worth avoiding. Same shape as the in-tree backup.sh's pattern.
  - Liveness vs readiness: shared handler instance is fine — both
    paths call the same closure. The reason to mount under two paths
    rather than alias-via-redirect is that kubelet's HTTP probes do
    NOT follow 30x by default, so a `/health/live` → `/health` 301
    would silently mark every pod unready. Mount the handler twice
    instead. Same pattern works for any future "conventional alias for
    a legacy endpoint" surface.
  - OpenAPI contract round-trip: the `cp api/openapi.yaml
    cmd/server/openapi_spec.yaml` step is load-bearing — without it
    `TestContract_EmbeddedSpecMatchesCanonical` fails with a clean
    diff. Skipping the cp once cost an entire iteration's CI cycle on
    US-235; institutionalised by listing it in the codebase pattern at
    the top of progress.txt already (#35).
  - When grandfathering pre-existing migrations into a new invariant,
    always prefer the smallest tightening fix. `IF NOT EXISTS` on an
    `ADD COLUMN` is byte-identical to a no-op on a fresh DB and an
    idempotent guard on a re-applied DB — no downside to backporting.
    Same logic applies to any future tightening of the migration
    invariant set (e.g. adding a "must be in a transaction" rule).

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - jsdom (vitest) does NOT implement `Element.scrollIntoView` — calling it from a useEffect crashes the test. Guard with `typeof scrollAnchorRef.current?.scrollIntoView === 'function'` BEFORE calling. This is the canonical fix for any "auto-scroll to bottom of chat / log / feed" pattern in a vitest+jsdom suite. Production browsers all have the API; the guard is purely a test affordance.
  - Vitest fake timers + an interval-driven typewriter: drive the reveal to completion with `vi.advanceTimersByTime(N)` inside `act(async () => {...})` AFTER setting `vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true })` in beforeEach. The `shouldAdvanceTime: true` option is what lets TanStack Query's internal timeouts (mutation transition, etc.) still fire while user code's setTimeout is mocked. Without it, the mutation's `onSuccess` callback never resolves and the test hangs.
  - Multi-thread chat UX: a single useState for `activeThreadId` plus two effects — (1) auto-select-first when nothing's selected, (2) drop-selection-on-deletion — beats threading "selected ID" through props or pulling Zustand for it. The two effects compose cleanly; React batches the state updates and downstream `messagesQuery` re-renders with the new threadId because `useAIPMessages(threadId)` keys on it.
  - `request<T>` from `web/src/api/client.ts` returns `undefined as T` on empty bodies (e.g., 204 No Content). For DELETE handlers that intentionally return 204, the caller MUST type the request as `Promise<void>` — otherwise TS infers `Promise<unknown>` and the mutation type chain gets noisy.
  - MessageBubble uses `whitespace-pre-wrap` + `break-words` so the assistant's multiline / very-long-token responses lay out correctly without a markdown renderer. If a future story wants markdown (code blocks, tables) we'd swap this for a markdown component but for plain LLM text the CSS approach is sufficient and zero-dep.
  - When TanStack Query's `useQuery({queryKey, queryFn, enabled: !!id})` is keyed by an optional id, give the disabled branch a STABLE sentinel queryKey (e.g., `['aip','messages','__none__']`) — query-key churn while disabled still kicks the cache hash. The active branch keys off the real id. Prior art: `useAIPMessages` in the new hook file.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - DAG branch-skipping with diamonds: the cleanest model is per-edge `active` bitmap, NOT per-node `skipped` set. A node is reachable iff at least one incoming edge is active OR it has zero incoming edges; an if-node deactivates its non-taken outgoing edges; a node that turns out to be unreachable deactivates all its outgoing edges so dead branches propagate. The naive "mark all downstream of the not-taken edge as skipped" fails the moment two branches reconverge — the merge node has another live predecessor and should still run, but it's already in the skipped set. ~30 LOC, no recursion, deterministic across edge orderings.
  - Subpackage placement for related-but-orthogonal AIP surfaces: `pkg/aip` (threads) and `pkg/aip/logic` (workflows) intentionally don't share types beyond the `aip.Provider` interface. Flows depend on Provider for llm-nodes via a tiny `ProviderResolver` interface (one method, satisfied implicitly by `*aip.Registry`), but the Flow / Run / Node types stay independent of the Thread / Message types so the two domains can version separately. Trying to share a "ChatRequest" shape upward would cement the wrong abstraction — flows need a ChatRequest *built* from variable substitution + node config, threads need a ChatRequest *built* from persisted message history.
  - Variable substitution `{{path.subpath}}` for promptTemplates / tool params: a tiny scanner that walks `{{...}}` and resolves via dotted-path lookup beats pulling text/template (which uses Go-specific syntax SDK callers won't recognise) or jq (CGO). Returning empty string on missing paths is the right default — strict "missing-path = error" surfaces every typo as a 422 and frustrates iterative flow authoring; the user instead sees a degraded prompt which is easier to debug. Apply the same substitution to map values via a recursive `substituteVarsAny` so tool params inherit the same templating without per-tool plumbing.
  - Tiny condition DSL for if-nodes: a three-token `<lhs> <op> <rhs>` parser with explicit handling for quoted strings + numbers + bools covers ~95% of real workflow needs without standing up a full expression evaluator. Two safety details: (1) operator scanning must use `indexOutsideQuotes` so a `<` inside a string operand doesn't trip the comparison, and (2) longer operators (==, !=, <=, >=) MUST be checked before their single-char prefixes. " contains " uses bracketing spaces to disambiguate from substring inside a quoted operand. Yes, this is reinventing a small piece of an expression parser — the alternative (Goja) is overkill, and a real expression language is a deliberate v2 if flow authors hit the wall.
  - Per-flow-definition validation in UpdateFlow handler: build a "proposed" Flow value by applying the partial update fields to a copy of the current flow, then `proposed.Validate()` BEFORE persisting. Otherwise a partial update could replace `nodes` with valid-on-its-own content but leave `edges` referring to the now-deleted node IDs — the DB would happily accept and the next execute would fail with a confusing structural error. Doing the validation handler-side keeps `Store.UpdateFlow` thin and dispatch-only.
  - "No output node" default: when the flow doesn't include an output-typed node, the executor returns every node's state map keyed by node id (minus the `input` alias). Forcing flow authors to always wire an output node makes the simplest "give me whatever this node returned" workflow surprisingly verbose; a sensible default removes the boilerplate. When at least one output node IS present, output collection is deterministic — only the named keys appear, and multiple output nodes merge in declaration order.
  - Goroutine-safe registry pattern reuse: `MapToolRegistry` is a near-copy of `aip.Registry` (sync.RWMutex + lookup-by-name + Names() returning a sorted slice). Tempting to extract a generic `registry[T]` shape, but the two surfaces have slightly different "missing" semantics (Provider returns wrapped sentinel error; Tool returns nil + bool) and the duplicated 50 lines is much cheaper than a generic abstraction layered atop both. If a third lookup-keyed-by-name surface lands, then refactor.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - reactflow → @xyflow/react migration: the `reactflow` npm package (v11, last published mid-2024) is the legacy name. v12+ ships under `@xyflow/react` and is what supports React 19. The PRD's "use reactflow" prose pre-dates the rename — install @xyflow/react and you get the same API tree (ReactFlow / ReactFlowProvider / Background / Controls / MiniMap / addEdge / applyNodeChanges / applyEdgeChanges / Connection / Node / Edge / NodeChange / EdgeChange) with React 19 compat baked in. The CSS import path moves from `reactflow/dist/style.css` → `@xyflow/react/dist/style.css`.
  - jsdom + ReactFlow incompatibility: the canvas uses ResizeObserver and absolute getBoundingClientRect math that jsdom doesn't ship. Two paths: (1) install jsdom polyfills globally, or (2) module-mock @xyflow/react in tests. (2) is much cheaper and keeps the test focused on OUR glue (toolbar wiring, node-config panel, save / execute flow) rather than xyflow internals — xyflow has its own Cypress suite. Mock shape: pass-through ReactFlowProvider, render `<ul data-testid="rf-mock-nodes">` of nodes with per-node test buttons that invoke onNodeClick, identity helpers for addEdge / applyNodeChanges / applyEdgeChanges. Don't forget `vi.mock('@xyflow/react/dist/style.css', () => ({}))` so the CSS import doesn't break the resolver.
  - Editor-only state inside a wire model: `__editorPosition` (and any future `__<feature>` editor scratchpad key) rides inside `node.config` as a JSONB blob. Backend stores unchanged + Validate ignores unknown keys, so no schema migration / new column / new wire-type field is needed. Reserve `__`-prefixed keys for editor-private state (matches WireObject's reserved `__primaryKey` / `__rid` convention) so a future stricter validator could distinguish "executor input" from "UI scratchpad" without confusion.
  - Three-pane page layout (list / canvas / detail) is the right shape for any visual editor surface: pick the resource (left), edit the structure (centre), tweak the selected element (right). The canvas-resource-position state lives in the centre; the right panel is purely a controlled view over `selectedItem`. Saves are batched at the centre level — the right panel mutates draft state, the centre's "Save" button persists the whole thing. Don't try to auto-save on every right-panel change; the dirty-flag UX gives users a clear "what's pending" signal and avoids race-y incremental writes against the OMS-style backend that expects whole-flow PUTs.
  - Adding a new top-level web route + sidebar nav: the 3-step sync is (1) import + Route in `App.tsx` inside the protected Shell group, (2) navItems entry in `Sidebar.tsx`, (3) icon SVG path in the `iconPaths` map. Step (3) is easy to forget — the icon silently disappears (returns null), and the entry is still clickable but visually broken. Always add the path BEFORE referencing it.
  - JSON-object input validators (run-input box, ParamsEditor, anything that expects a `Record<string, unknown>`): always reject (a) JSON parse errors with the exception message, (b) non-object top-level shapes (arrays / numbers / strings) with "must be a JSON object". Bare `JSON.parse(...)` accepts every literal — `[1,2,3]` would otherwise pass and break the downstream `Object.keys(input)` consumer.
  - Position-change debounce vs save-on-blur: ReactFlow fires onNodesChange continuously during a drag (1 event per pixel). Only flag `dirty` when the change is `'position'` (drag complete OR keyboard-arrow) or `'remove'`; the intermediate per-pixel position updates write to local state without re-triggering save indicators. If a future iteration needs autosave, debounce the save at the dirty-flag→effect boundary, not at the onNodesChange→state level — local state must always reflect the authoritative canvas position even if save is throttled.
  - "Disable Run while dirty" rule: the executor runs against the PERSISTED flow, not the live editor state. If the user clicks Run while there are unsaved changes, the run reflects whatever was last saved and surprises the operator. Disabling the Run button until they Save (with a tooltip explaining why) is the right UX. Alternative "auto-save before run" couples two intents — the user might want to discard their changes — so explicit save-then-run is safer.

## 2026-04-28 - US-283 RAG 工作流增强
- Added `pkg/aip/rag` package — encapsulates the Semantic Retriever flow (ObjectSet → corpus → embed → rank) plus a tiny prompt-template engine for {{context}}/{{query}} injection.
- `pkg/aip/rag/retriever.go`:
  - `Retriever` constructed via `NewRetriever(executor, embedder, loader)` — panics on any nil dep so the boot path fails loudly rather than at first request.
  - `CandidateExecutor` interface — narrowed to `Execute(ctx, *objectset.Definition) (*objectset.Result, error)` so production wires `*objectset.Executor` as-is and tests inject a fake. Compile-time assertion `var _ CandidateExecutor = (*objectset.Executor)(nil)` keeps the contract honest if the executor signature ever drifts.
  - `Embedder` interface — mirrors `embeddings.Provider` (Embed + Model) so a mock/openai provider plugs in without an adapter; defining the alias locally keeps pkg/aip/rag from importing pkg/embeddings just for naming.
  - `CorpusLoader` interface — `LoadDocuments(ctx, ontology, objectType, pks) ([]Document, error)`. Per-PK loader stays pluggable: production wiring will read indexed Bleve docs and project a text-bearing property; tests inject preset slices. Loader is allowed to return FEWER docs than pks (missing/empty rows simply don't get scored).
  - `Retrieve(ctx, RetrieveRequest)` algorithm: validate non-empty query + non-nil candidate + K>=0 → execute candidate → short-circuit on empty PK set → load docs → drop empty-text rows → batch-embed query+corpus in a single Embed call → cosine similarity per doc → sort desc → trim to K (DefaultK=5 when K=0).
  - `cosineSimilarity` returns 0 for length mismatch / zero magnitude (treats degenerate vectors as "no signal" rather than erroring out a whole batch).
  - `Result.Truncated` propagates from the candidate ObjectSet so callers can warn the user when the corpus was capped at `objectset.BaseExecutionCap` before scoring.
- `pkg/aip/rag/template.go`:
  - `PromptTemplate` is a string alias with `Render(query, context)` and `RenderFromMatches(query, matches)`. `strings.ReplaceAll` substitutes every occurrence of `{{query}}` and `{{context}}` (placeholders intentionally simple — anything richer belongs in `pkg/aip/logic`'s template engine).
  - `FormatContext(matches)` renders matches as a numbered block (`[1] Title (objectType:primaryKey)\ntext\n\n[2] ...`); empty input returns "" so prompts with no retrieved context degrade gracefully.
  - `DefaultPromptTemplate` ships the canonical "answer using only the context, otherwise say I don't know" body so callers can adopt RAG without authoring a template themselves.
- 22 unit tests across `retriever_test.go` (12) + `template_test.go` (10):
  - cosine-similarity ranking with hand-tuned 3-D vectors (alice picked over bob picked over random)
  - default-K fallback (K=0 → DefaultK=5)
  - Truncated propagation
  - empty-candidate short-circuit (loader untouched)
  - skip-empty-text filter
  - validation: empty query, nil candidate, negative K all rejected with descriptive errors
  - executor / loader error wrap (errors.Is)
  - nil-dep constructor panics for executor/embedder/loader
  - placeholder substitution: substitutes both, repeated occurrences, no-placeholder pass-through
  - FormatContext numbering + (objectType:pk) handle, title omitted when empty, empty-input returns ""
  - RenderFromMatches end-to-end + the no-matches edge case
  - DefaultPromptTemplate carries both placeholders
- Quality gates:
  - `go test ./pkg/aip/rag/...` — 22/22 passing
  - `go test ./...` — full repo suite green (cmd/server, every pkg/*, test/*)
  - `go build ./...` — green
  - `go vet ./...` — clean
  - `gofmt -l ./pkg/aip/rag/` — clean
- Files changed (3 new):
  - pkg/aip/rag/retriever.go (new)
  - pkg/aip/rag/template.go (new)
  - pkg/aip/rag/retriever_test.go (new)
  - pkg/aip/rag/template_test.go (new)
  - prd.json (US-283 passes=true + notes)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - "Encapsulate X (A + B)" PRDs map cleanly to a leaf package with two narrow dependency interfaces that production wires concretely (objectset.Executor + embeddings.Provider) and tests fake. Define interfaces at the consumer (the new package), not the producer — keeps the dependency direction `pkg/aip/rag → pkg/oss/objectset` and avoids the cross-package interface-extraction churn an outward-pointing definition would create.
  - Compile-time interface satisfaction checks (`var _ CandidateExecutor = (*objectset.Executor)(nil)`) are 1 LOC of insurance against the wrapped type's signature drifting (additional return value, renamed parameter type) — caught at `go build` instead of at first production call. Same pattern is worth replicating any time a downstream package wraps an upstream type behind a narrow interface.
  - Local interface alias for an upstream surface (Embedder = embeddings.Provider in shape but defined here): keeps the leaf package importable from anywhere without forming a cycle through pkg/embeddings, while still letting concrete `*embeddings.MockProvider` / `*embeddings.OpenAI` satisfy it implicitly. Costs 2 method declarations; saves an import-cycle headache the first time a higher-level orchestrator wants to compose RAG with another embedding-aware feature.
  - Cosine-similarity tests with hand-tuned vectors > stochastic mock embedders: assigning known unit-vectors to known texts (e.g. {1,0,0}, {0,1,0}, {0,0,1}) lets the test assert ordering deterministically (alice {0.95,0.05,0} dot {1,0,0} = 0.95 vs bob {0,1,0} dot {1,0,0} = 0). The deterministic-hash MockProvider is too noisy for ranking assertions — its `H(text)` cosine similarity has no relationship to text similarity, so a "should rank A over B" assertion would pass or fail by coincidence. Save the hash mock for "vectors should be reproducible across runs" tests; use the fixed-vector approach for "ranking should reflect similarity" tests.
  - Batch query+corpus into ONE Embed call: providers that amortise per-call setup (auth, network round-trip) get linear-time speedup; providers that don't (mocks, cached) pay nothing extra. Splitting into N+1 calls (one for query, one per doc) is a common mistake — reverse the loop and concatenate up front.
  - `{{context}}` + `{{query}}` placeholders match the de-facto LangChain / LlamaIndex convention. Keeping the syntax identical means existing prompt libraries can be ported in unchanged. Don't invent a new `${context}` or `<<context>>` notation just to be different — the cost (every cookbook needs translating) dwarfs the benefit (none).
  - `panic(...)` in NewRetriever for nil deps vs returning an error: fail-fast at boot is correct for THIS surface because the wiring is once-per-process at startup. Returning `(nil, error)` would force every call site into err-checking ceremony for an invariant that's static — the boot path either has the deps or it doesn't. Reserve `error` returns for runtime input validation (`Retrieve(req RetrieveRequest)` IS validated by error return — different surface, different handling).

## 2026-04-28 - US-284 Function Calling Chain
- Implemented an LLM function-calling loop in `pkg/aip.Handler.SendMessage`. Each iteration: build chat history → call `Provider.Complete` with `ChatRequest.Tools` from the registry → if response has `ToolCalls`, persist the assistant turn (carrying `tool_calls`), execute every tool via `ToolRegistry.Get`, append a `RoleTool` result message per call, and recurse. Loop hard-capped at `MaxToolCallIterations = 8`; exceed → `AIPToolLoopExceeded` 500.
- New persistence:
  - `migrations/000068_aip_messages_tool_calls` adds `tool_calls JSONB` (assistant rows), `tool_call_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` and `tool_name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` (tool rows). Drops the old `aip_messages_role_check` and replaces it with `aip_messages_role_check_v2` admitting `tool` alongside `system/user/assistant`.
  - `pkg/aip.Message` extended with `ToolCalls`, `ToolCallID`, `ToolName` (all `omitempty`).
  - `MemoryStore` deep-copies `ToolCalls` slices on Append + List so callers don't share mutable state.
  - `cmd/server/aip_store.go` (PG impl) marshals/unmarshals `ToolCalls` JSON and `COALESCE(...,'')` reads for the two text columns.
- Provider surface:
  - `ChatRequest.Tools []ToolDef` declares the toolbox; `ChatResponse.ToolCalls []ToolCall` carries model-issued invocations. `ChatMessage` gained `ToolCalls / ToolCallID / ToolName` so providers see the full function-calling history.
  - `pkg/aip.MockProvider` now exhibits a deterministic two-turn handshake when `Tools` is non-empty: turn-1 returns a tool call to the first declared tool with `{"text": <last user content>}`; turn-2 (after a `RoleTool` message lands) returns a final assistant text containing the tool result.
- Wiring & SDK:
  - `pkg/aip.ToolRegistry` (narrow interface) + `pkg/aip.ToolHandler` + `EchoToolHandler` ship in `tool.go`. `cmd/server/main.go::ServerDeps` gains `AIPTools *aip.ToolRegistry`; PG-backed deployments seed it with the echo handler. `Handler.SetToolRegistry` is the wire point so degraded-mode test routers leave it nil and observe the legacy single-turn contract.
  - `web/src/api/aip.ts` mirrors the new fields (`AIPToolCall`, `toolCalls?`, `toolCallId?`, `toolName?`, `toolMessages?`, `iterations?`) and broadens `AIPMessage.role` to include `tool`.
- Tests:
  - `pkg/aip/tool_test.go` covers Register / Get / nil-safety / Definitions sort / EchoToolHandler.
  - `pkg/aip/function_chain_test.go` drives the full loop with a `scriptedProvider`: one-tool-call happy path, tool-result-fed-back-on-next-turn, max-iteration cap → `AIPToolLoopExceeded`, unknown tool → `AIPToolNotFound`, no-tool-registry single-turn fallback, `ChatRequest.Tools` actually forwarded, and a Mock-provider round-trip test.
- Files changed:
  - `migrations/000068_aip_messages_tool_calls.up.sql` / `.down.sql` (new)
  - `pkg/aip/provider.go` (Tools / ToolDef / ToolCall + ChatMessage extensions)
  - `pkg/aip/thread.go` (`RoleTool` constant + Message tool fields + ValidateRole accepts tool)
  - `pkg/aip/thread_test.go` (ValidateRole table fix)
  - `pkg/aip/store.go` (deep-copy of ToolCalls)
  - `pkg/aip/handlers.go` (SendMessage loop + buildChatRequest carries new fields)
  - `pkg/aip/mock_provider.go` (function-calling round-trip)
  - `pkg/aip/tool.go` (new ToolHandler + ToolRegistry)
  - `pkg/aip/tool_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/aip/function_chain_test.go` (new)
  - `cmd/server/aip_store.go` (PG persistence of tool fields)
  - `cmd/server/main.go` (deps.AIPTools wiring + Handler.SetToolRegistry)
  - `web/src/api/aip.ts` (TS types mirror the new fields)
  - `prd.json` (US-284 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Function-calling needs THREE wire-level shapes to round-trip: (1) `ChatRequest.Tools` (declared toolbox forwarded into the provider), (2) assistant rows carrying `ToolCalls` (the model's issued calls), (3) `RoleTool` rows carrying `ToolCallID + ToolName + Content` (the tool's response). Skipping any one of them breaks providers that re-derive their internal state from the message history (Anthropic's wire form especially). Persist all three on both the wire and the store from day one so a future "send the WHOLE history to a different provider" path stays faithful.
  - Tool-loop termination: ALWAYS persist the assistant turn FIRST inside each loop iteration — even when ToolCalls is non-empty and Content is empty. That row is what the next iteration's `ListMessages` needs to feed back so the provider doesn't see the user message twice. Skipping the persist on tool-call turns produces a 2x duplicated user-prompt in the next call.
  - Loop-exceeded vs loop-aborted: when the loop hits the cap, return a structured error (`AIPToolLoopExceeded`) AFTER all the partial assistant + tool messages are already persisted. The thread reflects exactly what the model + tools produced; the operator sees a clear cap-hit error; SDKs can surface "loop didn't terminate, partial state in the thread". Truncating early without persisting partial state would lose audit detail; overwriting / rolling back would mask the actual model behaviour.
  - Mock-provider tool round-trip rule of thumb: `len(req.Tools) > 0 && !hasToolResult(req.Messages)` ⇒ emit a tool call; otherwise produce final text. This shape is enough to drive the full loop deterministically without HTTP transport, and it generalises to any handshake protocol with a "I'm not done yet, give me X first" turn. Don't try to hardcode the iteration count — drive the state machine off message-history shape so the same mock works for 1-tool-call and N-tool-call test scenarios alike.
  - `OMIT_NULL` JSONB ↔ Go nil-slice round-trip: pgx encodes a nil `[]byte` argument as SQL NULL, which is the correct shape for "no tool calls on this row". On the read side, `len(toolCallsJSON) > 0` guard avoids `json.Unmarshal(nil, &dst)` returning the zero-value `*[]ToolCall`, which would mask a malformed payload as "no tool calls" silently. Always pair the write-side nil check with a read-side length guard.
  - Constraint rename via DROP-old + ADD-new (vs ALTER): the role CHECK constraint is widened from `(system|user|assistant)` to `(system|user|assistant|tool)` by dropping `aip_messages_role_check` and adding `aip_messages_role_check_v2`. PG's CHECK has no `IF NOT EXISTS` shorthand for narrowing/widening, but the DROP + ADD pair inside `DO $$ ... END$$` blocks is idempotent and forward-compat (no column drops, only constraint surgery). The `_v2` suffix preserves audit trail / migration history without confusing anyone re-applying earlier migrations.

  - `prd.json` (US-285 passes=true + notes)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Catalog + registry decoupling is worth the two-step indirection: persisting the LLM-visible (name/description/parameters) triple in the DB keeps it auditable + admin-CRUD-able, while the in-memory ToolRegistry stays the cheap-to-read source of truth the SendMessage hot path consults. The `LoadCatalogIntoRegistry` bootstrap walks the catalog ONCE at boot; the admin handler keeps the registry in sync incrementally. Polling the DB on every Definitions() call would double the SendMessage tail latency for no benefit — the catalog only changes on admin actions, not LLM turns.
  - Sentinel errors named at the package boundary (`aip.ErrToolHandlerNotConfigured`) are the right way for cmd/server adapters to signal "this tool can't run on this deployment" back into pkg/aip without forcing pkg/aip to import oms/functions just for an error type. The adapter wraps the upstream error with `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", aip.ErrTool…)` / returns the bare sentinel; the SendMessage handler can `errors.Is` against the public sentinel to map to a structured 500. Same trick generalises to any cross-package "feature unavailable on this deployment" error.
  - "Definition-only" catalogue rows (HandlerFunctionRID empty) are intentionally allowed: the LLM can see the tool definition but Execute returns `ErrToolHandlerNotConfigured`. Useful for "register the schema first, wire the handler later" workflows AND for catalog rows that point at a Function the deployment doesn't have a FunctionExecutor for. Don't reject the empty-RID case at admin-write time — it forecloses the iterative authoring path. The execute-time error makes the gap loud enough.
  - Dispatch-then-stringify chain for tool results: oms.FunctionExecutor.Execute returns interface{} (could be string / number / bool / map / slice — Goja whole-number arithmetic is int64, fractional is float64, JSON literals come through as map[string]interface{}). Order the typed switch with primitives first, json.Marshal second, fmt.Sprintf last — in particular `nil` MUST be checked before json.Marshal or it becomes the literal string "null" and the LLM sees a misleading null string instead of an empty result. Specific-before-general is a recurring pattern; apply it whenever turning interface{} into a fixed wire shape.
  - Registry hot-reload on admin write: every Create/Update/Delete handler refreshes the in-process ToolRegistry inline. Disabling a tool via PUT must call `Unregister(name)` even though the catalog row still exists, otherwise the next SendMessage iteration would still see the disabled tool because the registry retains stale entries. The Unregister surface is small (one method, idempotent on missing name) and prevents the "I disabled the tool but the LLM still sees it" footgun.
  - Adding the catalog handler routes does NOT need an OpenAPI spec entry yet because the contract test's `newContractTestRouter` doesn't wire `AIPToolCatalog` (mirrors how AIPStore / AIPLogicStore routes are also unmodelled in the spec — they only mount in PG mode). When AIP routes finally land in the canonical openapi.yaml, the tools/* paths will join their thread/* and logic-flows/* siblings together rather than piecemeal — saves three round-trips of allowlist churn.

## 2026-04-28 - US-286 MCP Resource 扩展
- Implemented MCP `resources/list` and `resources/read` so AI agents can browse the ontology catalogue and stored ObjectSets through the Model Context Protocol resource API. The methods replace the previous "always empty" stubs.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - MCP resource URIs work cleanly as `weave://<kind>/<id>`: a single `parseResourceURI` helper centralises the scheme/kind/id split, and `idx := strings.IndexByte(rest, '/')` keeps multi-slash IDs (future RID shapes) from breaking. Reject empty kind or empty id as InvalidParams.
  - Optional dependency injection on the MCP `Server` follows the same setter pattern already in use for `SemanticSearcher`: define a narrow interface in `pkg/mcp`, expose `SetXxx`, and let degraded-mode test routers leave it unset. The capability is still advertised in `initialize` because at least one resource family (ontologies) is always available.
  - Cross-package adapter direction: `pkg/oss/objectset` adds `EntrySnapshot` / `ListEntries` / `GetEntry` (transport-neutral), `pkg/mcp` defines the `ObjectSetCatalog` interface, and `cmd/server` writes the adapter that maps one onto the other. `pkg/oss/objectset` never imports `pkg/mcp`; `pkg/mcp` never imports `pkg/oss/objectset`. Same direction-of-dependency rule used by `PersistedSnapshotStore` from US-224.
  - `*objectset.Store.ListEntries` skips expired entries by reading `time.Since(entry.createdAt) > s.ttl` inline rather than triggering `Cleanup()` — a lazy filter on the read path is cheap and avoids holding the write lock during enumeration. The dedicated `Cleanup()` goroutine still trims memory.
  - For "schema vs object content" reads, returning the Definition (not the materialised rows) is the right v1 scope: agents that need rows can post the Definition to `loadObjects`, and the resource read stays cheap + deterministic. Materialising on read would couple `resources/read` to the index manager + property visibility filter for no proportional benefit.
  - JSON-RPC error code mapping for resources/read failures: missing/expired resource → `-32000` (CodeToolError) so clients route it through the application-error path, while malformed URIs → `-32602` (CodeInvalidParams) so clients see "you sent something the server can't even attempt". Keeping these consistent with the tools/call dispatch makes the wire contract uniform.

## 2026-04-28 - US-287 Pipeline DSL
- Added migration 000070_pipelines: `pipelines` table holds the declarative descriptor (`id` PK, `name`, `description`, `inputs`/`transforms`/`outputs` JSONB arrays, `schedule` TEXT, `enabled` BOOL, `created_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) with `pipelines_id_format` CHECK matching the `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}` allowlist used by `aip_logic_flows`. Two indices: `pipelines_created_by_idx (created_by, created_at DESC)` for owner-scoped list and `pipelines_enabled_idx (enabled)` ready for the future scheduler join.
- New `pkg/pipeline` package owns the descriptor + validation only — DAG execution (US-288) and cron scheduling (US-289) hang off the same row later:
  - `pipeline.go` — `Pipeline`, `PipelineUpdate` (pointer-field partial-update shape), `Input` / `Transform` / `Output` value types. `ValidatePipelineID` mirrors `logic.ValidateFlowID`; `ValidateNodeName` enforces a stricter `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}` rule for node identifiers (avoids quoting headaches in downstream YAML/SQL); `ValidateSchedule` empty-or-5/6-fields sanity (full cron parse defers to robfig/cron in US-289). `Pipeline.Validate` enforces ≥1 input + ≥1 output (no-op pipeline rejected), globally-unique node names across inputs/transforms/outputs, non-empty Type per node, upstream-reference checks for `Transform.Inputs` and `Output.Input` (transforms only see Inputs and earlier-declared transforms — forward references are rejected at schema time so the future executor never has to re-discover them), self-loop rejection. `ClonePipeline` deep-copies slices + map[string]any configs so callers can mutate without aliasing back.
  - `store.go` — narrow `Store` interface (Create / Get / List / Update / Delete) with `MemoryStore` impl. List supports owner-scoped filter (createdBy=="" returns all). Sentinels: `ErrPipelineNotFound` / `ErrPipelineAlreadyExists`.
  - `handlers.go` — `Handler` exposes `GET/POST /api/v2/pipelines` and `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v2/pipelines/{pipelineId}`. Owner / admin scoping mirrors `aiplogic.Handler`: non-admin callers see only their own pipelines, admin sees everything. Auto-id format `pipeline_<32-hex>` when caller doesn't supply id. Update path validates the *proposed final state* (apply partial → re-Validate) so a bad partial change can't slip through. Error taxonomy: `MissingAuthenticatedUser` / `PipelinesUnavailable` / `InvalidRequestBody` / `InvalidPipelineID` / `InvalidPipelineDefinition` / `PipelineAlreadyExists` / `PipelineNotFound` / `PipelineForbidden` / `PipelineLookupFailed` / `PipelineCreateFailed` / `PipelineUpdateFailed` / `PipelineDeleteFailed` / `PipelineListFailed`.
  - 27 unit tests across `pipeline_test.go` (10 schema validation + clone), `store_test.go` (8 CRUD + scoping), `handlers_test.go` (9 HTTP CRUD + auth + ownership).
- New `cmd/server/pipeline_store.go` — `pgPipelineStore` satisfies `pipeline.Store` over `*pgxpool.Pool`. JSONB columns staged through `[]byte` (matches the JSONB round-trip rule from prior stories); reads `COALESCE(col, '[]'::jsonb)` for the three array columns and `COALESCE(schedule, '')` / `COALESCE(created_by, '')` for the text columns. UPDATE uses the dynamic partial-UPDATE pattern (`[]string` of `col = $N` + `[]interface{}` args) — `updated_at = NOW()` always appended. `coalesceInputs/Transforms/Outputs` swap nil slices for `[]Input{}` / etc. so JSONB never stores the literal `"null"`.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - "DSL + storage + CRUD" PRDs split cleanly across three Go user stories (US-287 schema/CRUD, US-288 executor, US-289 scheduler): own ONLY the descriptor + validation here. The Pipeline.Validate function is the contract every future executor / scheduler will trust — making schema-time validation generous (cycles, type checks, reference resolution) saves having to re-prove it inside the runtime hot path. Forward-reference rejection in particular ("transforms only see earlier transforms") means the DAG executor never has to look up a node ID it hasn't already constructed.
  - Two-pass partial-update validation is worth the indirection: build a `proposed` Pipeline by copying current + applying the `*string` / `*[]Input` etc. fields, run `proposed.Validate()` BEFORE calling `store.UpdatePipeline`. A naive PATCH that sends `{"schedule": "bad"}` would otherwise persist into the row and break the next /execute call. The aiplogic.Handler.UpdateFlow function uses the same pattern; it generalises to any descriptor with cross-field invariants.
  - Stricter node-name regex than the row id regex: row ids accept `.-_` (so "team.etl.daily" stays human-friendly), but inside-the-document node names use the stricter `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}` rule so future YAML/SQL renderings (CTE names, column names, dataset paths) don't need quoting. Two regexes aren't redundant — they're describing different lifetimes (ids ride on URLs, node names ride on data-flow refs).
  - JSONB array columns with NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb: same shape as the tool-catalog `parameters JSONB` column from US-285. Read path uses `COALESCE(col, '[]'::jsonb)` (legacy rows fail open as empty) and write path substitutes `[]T{}` for nil slices via a `coalesceInputs/Transforms/Outputs` helper trio so encoders never produce the SQL string "null". Three separate helpers (one per type) is mildly verbose but matches the parallel-column shape; a single generic `coalesceArray[T any]` would force callers into type assertions which is worse than the duplication.
  - Owner / admin scoping is the right v1 access model for declarative-descriptor resources (Pipeline, Logic Flow, Tool catalog future): every authenticated user authors their own resources, admin sees everything. Future RBAC stories can layer team scoping or viewer roles on top, but the scoping rule is ONE function (`userHasAdminRole(u)` + `pipeline.CreatedBy != "" && user.ID != pipeline.CreatedBy`). Don't gate Create on a role — operators / data engineers / power users all need to author pipelines.
  - Auto-generated id prefix per resource family (`pipeline_<32-hex>` matches `flow_<32-hex>` from US-281, `ri.{service}.{realm}.{resourceType}.{uuid}` for OMS metadata): keeps logs and grep-ability sane when a user id and a resource id appear in the same trace. The hex char count (32) is the same across families so eyeball-scanning a log line keeps consistent column widths. Reuse `crypto/rand` + `encoding/hex` over `uuid.New()` so the prefix doesn't accumulate dashes.
  - Schedule "5 or 6 fields" sanity (without parsing): a full cron parser pulls in robfig/cron which is the right call for US-289's actual scheduling, not for US-287's schema validation. Pre-parse the field count is enough to catch typos (`"bad"`, `"@daily"` is rejected — `@-shorthand` would be a future feature) without committing to a parser. The runtime parser will be the authoritative gate; this one is a fast-fail at write time.

## 2026-04-28 - US-288 Pipeline DAG 编排
- Added DAG executor sitting on top of the US-287 Pipeline descriptor: BuildDAG flattens Inputs/Transforms/Outputs into a uniform []DAGNode (Kind, Type, Config, Deps), TopoOrder runs Kahn's algorithm with declaration-order tie-breaking for determinism, and RunDAG drives the workers.
- Concurrency model: worker goroutine per ready node, buffered semaphore caps in-flight count to RunOptions.Parallelism (defaults to 1 — never accidentally unbounded). Coordinator goroutine reads outcomes off a `doneEvent` channel and dispatches newly-ready children. sync.WaitGroup ensures every worker has returned before RunDAG returns.
- Three FailurePolicy values (matches AC verbatim): abort cancels runCtx so in-flight workers see ctx.Done() and the unstarted nodes get marked Canceled; continue runs a BFS over `dependents` to mark every transitive descendant Skipped while independent branches keep running; retry retries up to MaxRetries with RetryBackoff (ctx-aware sleep) before falling through to abort.
- 12 unit tests cover topo determinism, cycle/unknown-dep detection, happy path, abort-on-failure, continue with sibling success, retry-until-success, retry exhaustion, parallelism upper bound (≤2 concurrent observed), parallelism=1 enforces serial, ctx cancellation aborts, and option-validation rejects nil Runner / unknown policy. All race-clean.
- Files changed:
  - pkg/pipeline/dag.go (new) — DAGNode, NodeKind, BuildDAG, TopoOrder
  - pkg/pipeline/runner.go (new) — RunOptions, NodeRunner(Func), NodeStatus, NodeResult, RunResult, RunDAG + runState helpers
  - pkg/pipeline/dag_test.go, pkg/pipeline/runner_test.go (new)
  - prd.json (US-288 passes=true + notes)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - DAG runner deadlock under Parallelism=1: when both root nodes are dispatched simultaneously and only one acquires the semaphore, a test that funnels cancellation through ONE specific root (e.g. `if node.Name == "in1" { cancel() }`) deadlocks ~50% of the time because the OTHER root may grab the semaphore first and `<-ctx.Done()` waits forever. Tests that exercise cancellation must trigger from EVERY worker, or trigger externally (timer, `started` chan), so node-execution order doesn't matter. Production code is correct; the bug was in the test design.
  - Two-phase coordinator pattern keeps cyclomatic complexity below 15: package the run-scoped state into a `runState` struct (nodeByName, dependents, remaining, results, runCtx, doneCh, sem, wg, inflight, aborted, firstErr) and split RunDAG into `prepareDAG` / `normalizeRunOptions` / `newRunState` / `coordinate` / `handleEvent` / `handleFailure` / `dispatchNewlyReady` / `finalizeStatuses` / `buildResult`. The original monolithic RunDAG hit cyclo=39 (golangci-lint floor is 15); the split version hits 4-7 per func with no cost to readability. Same shape will work for US-289's scheduler dispatcher and any future job-coordinator.
  - "Retry then abort" is the correct semantics for FailurePolicyRetry: retry-with-cap is two-phase (retry up to MaxRetries; on exhaustion, fall through to abort behavior). NOT three independent policies (abort vs continue vs retry-with-no-fallback). Without exhaustion-aborts-the-run, a permanent failure would loop forever or silently mark canceled. Verified by `TestRunDAG_RetryExhaustedAborts` asserting Attempts == 1 + MaxRetries and downstream nodes never run.
  - Buffered semaphore (`make(chan struct{}, N)`) beats `golang.org/x/sync/semaphore` for this use case: the channel send/recv is the natural Go primitive, no extra dep, and `defer func(){<-sem}()` makes release exception-safe. The semaphore.NewWeighted helper is overkill for fixed-size, integer-weighted node concurrency.
  - Per-node `NodeStatus` enum (pending → running → {success | failed | skipped | canceled}) is the right shape: `running` lets `finalizeStatuses` distinguish "we kicked it off but never got an event" (aborted) from "we never even reached it" (skipped) without needing a separate started-but-unfinished bit. JSON-friendly string values (not int constants) so SDK consumers don't have to track an enum mapping.
  - DAGNode.Config aliasing: BuildDAG copies the slice but NOT the underlying Config map — too expensive for the hot path. Document as read-only; runners that need to mutate must copy. Same convention as `oms.Property.TypeConfig` reads through `pkg/types` — JSON unmarshal already gave the caller a fresh map.

## 2026-04-28 - US-289 Pipeline 调度器
- Added cron-driven trigger surface on top of the US-287 Pipeline row + US-288 DAG runner. A Scheduler wraps `*cron.Cron` (robfig/cron/v3) with the SecondOptional|Minute|Hour|Dom|Month|Dow|Descriptor parser, so the same Schedule string accepted by `ValidateSchedule` (5/6 fields + @descriptors) is the input the cron entry actually parses — one source of truth.
- `PipelineRunner` / `PipelineRunnerFunc` indirection decouples the cron tick from the eventual DAG execution: today's `cmd/server/main.go` wires a logging-only runner placeholder (until a future story ships the real connector catalogue + run-row writer); pkg/pipeline imports zero downstream packages, so the same Scheduler ports cleanly to wherever the real runtime lands.
- Lifecycle (Start/Stop/Reload/Register/Unregister) follows the captured-channel pattern from `pkg/audit/retention.Scheduler` (US-269): Start is idempotent, Stop waits on the cron-returned ctx (`<-c.Stop().Done()`) so the in-flight job cb has truly returned before Stop returns. Disabled rows or rows with empty Schedule unregister their entry so callers can use `Register` as the single "this pipeline changed, sync the scheduler" entry point.
- pipeline.Handler grew an optional `SetScheduler(*Scheduler)` hook + Create/Update/Delete propagation. Scheduler errors from the propagation are logged via the scheduler's own logger, not surfaced as 5xx — the row was already persisted, so misleading the caller about the result of a successful write would be worse than the eventual reconciliation via Reload or the next admin write.
- cmd/server/main.go wires the Scheduler whenever `deps.PipelineStore` is non-nil (PG mode). Logging runner is intentional: every tick prints `[pipeline] schedule tick: id=... schedule=...`. When the pipeline runtime arrives, swap the runner with a real DAG dispatcher and the rest of the wiring is unchanged.
- 11 unit tests (`pkg/pipeline/scheduler_test.go`, race-clean): start-loads-only-enabled+scheduled, cron-tick-fires-runner, register-add+replace, register-disabled-or-empty-unregisters, register-rejects-invalid-cron, unregister, reload-syncs-with-store, stop-idempotent+pre-start-safe, runner-error-logged-not-fatal, nil-store-or-runner-at-construct, stop-waits-for-inflight-run.
- Files changed:
  - pkg/pipeline/scheduler.go (new) — Scheduler type, lifecycle, Register/Unregister/Reload, PipelineRunner indirection
  - pkg/pipeline/scheduler_test.go (new)
  - pkg/pipeline/handlers.go — SetScheduler + Create/Update/Delete propagation
  - cmd/server/main.go — `PipelineScheduler *pipeline.Scheduler` dep field, boot-time NewScheduler+Start with logging runner, Handler.SetScheduler wiring
  - prd.json (US-289 passes=true + notes)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - `cron.NewParser(cron.SecondOptional | cron.Minute | cron.Hour | cron.Dom | cron.Month | cron.Dow | cron.Descriptor)` accepts BOTH 5-field cron and 6-field with leading seconds AND robfig descriptors (`@every 1s`, `@hourly`, `@daily`). `cron.SecondOptional` exists in robfig/cron/v3 (not just `cron.Second`) — pick it when the schedule format must mirror a permissive Validate gate. The default `cron.New()` parser is 5-field-only and would silently reject 6-field schedules that ValidateSchedule already accepted.
  - `cron.Cron.Stop()` returns a `context.Context` whose Done is closed once every running job callback has returned. Wait on it (`<-c.Stop().Done()`) for happens-before semantics between Stop and the runner. Skipping the wait races runner cleanup with the Stop caller's next test phase under -race; `cron.Stop()` alone (without the wait) is the equivalent of the LDAP scheduler bug pattern 167 calls out.
  - Snapshot the pipeline by value at Register time (`ClonePipeline(p)`) and capture into the cron callback closure. Re-fetching from the store on every tick sounds like a "freshness wins" upgrade but it (a) couples the cron callback to the store latency, (b) requires sync coordination with concurrent admin Updates, (c) is unnecessary because admin handlers already call Register on every Update. The snapshot strategy matches `pkg/automate.Scheduler.addRuleInternal` — one consistent convention across the cron-driven feature surfaces.
  - Replace-existing-entry-under-the-same-lock invariant: when re-registering an id, `cron.Remove(old) + AddJob(...) + entries[id] = new` MUST happen under one s.mu hold. A two-phase "remove then add" without the lock would briefly let a second concurrent Register see entries[id] empty and double-fire. The same pattern applies to any "replace by key" mutation on a cron registry — single-shot under the lock is the only safe shape.
  - Scheduler errors propagate to ONE logger (not log.Printf scattered through dispatch). `SetLogger(fn)` accepting `nil` to mean "restore default" matches the LDAPSyncScheduler convention and is what tests use to count error events without parsing log output. The function shape `func(format string, v ...any)` is `log.Printf`-compatible, so production wiring is `sched.SetLogger(log.Printf)` (or just leave the default).
  - Cross-cutting "AC says integrate library X" stories (US-289 robfig/cron, future "integrate library Y") rarely have user-visible value end-to-end without a wired runner / call site. Ship the lib integration as a self-contained package with a pluggable indirection (PipelineRunner here) AND wire main.go with a logging placeholder so the runtime path is alive — operators can inspect cron entries and watch ticks happen even before the next-story-runtime lands. Never ship dead code: the placeholder runner is one branch swap away from the real dispatcher.
  - Pipeline schedule field already shipped in US-287; this story only adds the cron consumer. Keeps user stories independently testable: a deployment that wants schedule-as-metadata-only can still adopt US-287 without enabling the scheduler. The Scheduler dep is conditional in main.go — degraded mode (no PG, no PipelineStore) silently skips it.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Per-column type cascade for tabular schema inference: track ONE running candidate per column, narrow on every observation, widen-to-string sticky once a value fails every tighter parser. Never re-walk samples — single pass + monotone state. Numeric promotion (integer→long→double) is the only loosen-without-conflict edge in the lattice; everything else conflicts to string. integer/long split keys off `strconv.ParseInt(s, 10, 64)` + `[-2^31, 2^31)` range check, NOT regex on length.
  - Conservative-by-default date/timestamp parsing: accept ONLY ISO-8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD` for date, RFC3339 + ` ` separator variants for timestamp). Slash-separated forms (`MM/DD/YYYY` vs `DD/MM/YYYY`) are locale-ambiguous — silently picking one breaks half your users. The UI's manual override is the right escape hatch.
  - JSON-vs-CSV null semantics differ: CSV nulls are blank-string + 'NULL'/'null'/'\N' sentinels (operators paste them); JSON nulls are explicit `null` literals OR missing keys (which must be backfilled with null observations on prior rows when a key first appears mid-stream so cross-row Nullable inference is honest). The accumulator's `observe(raw, isNull)` shape unifies both paths — feed CSV directly, feed JSON via a tiny `jsonValueToSample(v) (string, bool)` helper.
  - `json.Decoder.UseNumber()` is mandatory for type-inference decoders. The default lands every JSON number as `float64`, collapsing the integer-vs-double distinction at decode time. With UseNumber the int classification path stays honest (`json.Number.String()` round-trips exact digits).
  - bufio.Scanner default 64KiB line cap hits NDJSON real-world rows fast (nested objects, log lines). `scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 64*1024), 1024*1024)` lifts to 1MiB — same shape every NDJSON-parsing surface should use.
  - csv.NewReader truncation detection: after reading exactly N rows, attempt ONE more `Read()` — if it succeeds the input had >= N+1 rows. `errors.Is(err, io.EOF)` distinguishes "actually done" from "actually truncated". One extra Read is cheap (single record); avoids hauling a "Total" Count into the response.
  - csv.NewReader.FieldsPerRecord=-1 + manual padding/trimming + WarningCount is the right shape for "tolerate ragged rows but flag them". The default (`= 0`, locked to first row's width) hard-fails on the first ragged row; -1 + your own bookkeeping gives the UI a "this CSV looks irregular" signal without rejecting the whole sample.
  - HTTP body cap via http.MaxBytesReader BEFORE json.NewDecoder.Decode: the decoder reads incrementally so the cap fires the moment input exceeds the budget. errors.As against `*http.MaxBytesError` distinguishes too-large from generic parse errors → distinct typed errorName for the SDK. Wrap on every endpoint that accepts inline sample / paste / blob payloads — keeps a memory-bound pathological input from spiking the server.
  - Contract-test invisible routes: gating a feature behind `if deps.XStore != nil { ... }` in `cmd/server/main.go` keeps it out of the contract router (which doesn't wire that store), so OpenAPI documentation can land in a follow-up story without breaking the contract trio. Schema inference reuses this pattern via the existing PipelineStore gate even though the inference endpoint itself is stateless — keeps the entire pipeline authoring surface consistent.
  - drag-drop UX with auto-format-detect: filename suffix takes precedence (.csv/.tsv → csv + delim, .json → json, .ndjson/.jsonl → ndjson), body shape (`[`/`{` start) is the fallback. Setting `delimiter` from the suffix at drop-time saves the user a second click for tab-separated files. Pattern reusable for any "drop a file, infer the parser config" surface.
  - SchemaInferencePage state shape: keep the inferred Result and the per-field user override map as TWO separate states (`overrides[fieldName]` overlays `result.fields[i]`). Clearing overrides on each new inference run prevents stale renames/types from a prior sample bleeding into a new file. Computing the merged "adjusted" view via useMemo of (result, overrides) is cheaper than reshaping result on every override edit.

## 2026-04-28 - US-291 CDC (Change Data Capture)
- New package `pkg/pipeline/cdc` implementing a PG logical-replication receiver that converts row-level changes into funnel.EditBatches:
  - `types.go`: `ChangeOp` (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), `ChangeEvent` (op + schema/table + before/after string maps + LSN/CommitTime), `TableMapping` (schema, table, ontologyApiName, objectType, primaryKeyColumns, propertyColumns, includeNullProperties), `Config.Validate` (rejects blanks + duplicate (schema,table) keys), `PrimaryKeyFor` (joins composite PK columns via `oms.CompositeKeySeparator` ":").
  - `mapper.go`: `EventToEdit(*ChangeEvent, TableMapping) -> funnel.Edit`. Stamps `Source: EditSourceIngest` so the funnel consumer's user-edit-wins conflict resolver (US-021) refuses to overwrite a concurrent user write made after the CDC event's timestamp. NULL columns drop by default; `IncludeNullProperties=true` forwards them as `nil` so MODIFY edits can clear fields. Unmapped columns are dropped silently (the consumer's filterWritableProperties also drops unknown fields). DELETE falls back to After when Before is absent (some logical decoders carry the row in After for in-buffer deletes).
  - `decoder.go`: stateful aggregator on top of `pglogrepl.Parse`. Caches Relation messages by RelationID, tracks Begin/Commit boundaries, stamps txn LSN+CommitTime onto every emitted event. Returns `(events, commit bool, err)` so the receiver flushes per-transaction. Honours REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT (keys-only OldTuple → only key columns appear in Before), TOASTed unchanged columns (silent skip), explicit NULL via a private sentinel (`IsNullValue` exported for downstream mappers).
  - `receiver.go`: `Source` interface (`Next(ctx) ([]byte, error)` + `CommitWatermark(ctx, LSN)` + `Close(ctx)`), `Publisher` interface (`PublishBatch(ctx, *funnel.EditBatch)`), `FunnelPublisher` adapter wrapping `*funnel.Publisher`. Per-ontology batch grouping during a transaction so multi-table multi-ontology commits split into separate EditBatches on flush. `Run(ctx)` is the main pump (single goroutine, owns Source ordering); `HandleWAL(ctx, []byte)` is the unit-test entry point.
  - `pgsource.go`: real `PGSource` backed by jackc/pglogrepl. `EnsureSlot(ctx, adminConn)` creates the slot if missing (idempotent; existing slots resume from confirmed_flush_lsn). `Start(ctx)` runs IDENTIFY_SYSTEM + START_REPLICATION with pgoutput plugin args (proto_version '1', publication_names 'X'). `Next(ctx)` pumps `pgproto3.CopyData` → branches on byte 'k' (PrimaryKeepalive — replies in-line if requested) vs 'w' (XLogData — returns WALData payload). `CommitWatermark` updates client LSN + sends `StandbyStatusUpdate` so PG advances confirmed_flush_lsn, durably acking the batch.
- `cmd/server/cdc_receiver.go`: opt-in startup wiring. Configuration via env:
  - `WEAVE_CDC_DSN` — replication-mode DSN (operator must include `replication=database` explicitly so wrong DSNs never spin up an extra walsender).
  - `WEAVE_CDC_SLOT` (default `weave_cdc`), `WEAVE_CDC_PUBLICATION` (default `weave_cdc_pub`), `WEAVE_CDC_KEEPALIVE_SECONDS` (default 10s).
  - `WEAVE_CDC_MAPPINGS` (inline JSON) or `WEAVE_CDC_MAPPINGS_FILE` (path).
  - DSN absent → noop stop fn, no goroutine started. DSN set without mappings → fail-fast with a clear error. Connect / slot / start failures log a warning and return without crashing the server (same shape as OIDC / SAML / LDAP optional integrations).
  - Started after the funnel publisher is constructed; shutdown drained via `defer cdcStop()` paired with main.go's existing graceful-shutdown ladder.
- Tests (35 new tests across 4 test files):
  - `types_test.go`: validation for every required field, blank pk column, blank property target, duplicate config key, single + composite PK joins.
  - `mapper_test.go`: INSERT happy path, UPDATE drops NULL by default + UPDATE includes NULL when IncludeNullProperties=true, DELETE happy + DELETE-falls-back-to-After, error envelopes for nil/unknown-op/missing-tuple/missing-pk-column, IsNullValue sentinel.
  - `decoder_test.go`: Insert-within-txn (LSN + CommitTime stamped), Update with REPLICA IDENTITY KEY old-tuple shape, Delete keys-only, TOAST unchanged column absent, unknown-relation error, delete-without-old-tuple error, tuple-column-count-mismatch error, events-outside-Begin emit zero LSN (mid-stream resume tolerance), ProcessWAL empty-buffer error.
  - `receiver_test.go`: HandleWAL transaction (Begin → Relation → Insert → Commit) flushes ONE batch + watermark advances; unmapped table dropped; multi-ontology transaction splits into TWO batches on commit; Run drains a scripted Source through io.EOF and calls Source.Close on shutdown; Run cancels on context.Cancel; publisher failure aborts the receiver; NewReceiver validates non-nil source / non-nil publisher / valid Config; FunnelPublisher nil-receiver / nil-inner safety.
  - `encoders_test.go`: tiny pgoutput byte-encoder (Begin / Commit / Relation / Insert) so receiver tests exercise the real ProcessWAL path without a live PG. Round-trips through `pglogrepl.Parse` for the typed-message branches.
- Files changed:
  - `pkg/pipeline/cdc/types.go` (new)
  - `pkg/pipeline/cdc/mapper.go` (new)
  - `pkg/pipeline/cdc/decoder.go` (new)
  - `pkg/pipeline/cdc/receiver.go` (new)
  - `pkg/pipeline/cdc/pgsource.go` (new)
  - `pkg/pipeline/cdc/types_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/pipeline/cdc/mapper_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/pipeline/cdc/decoder_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/pipeline/cdc/receiver_test.go` (new)
  - `pkg/pipeline/cdc/encoders_test.go` (new)
  - `cmd/server/cdc_receiver.go` (new)
  - `cmd/server/main.go` (one-line wire after FunnelConsumer.Start)
  - `go.mod` / `go.sum` (+jackc/pglogrepl, side-effect upgrade pgx/v5 5.8.0→5.9.1, x/sync, x/text)
  - `prd.json` (US-291 passes=true)
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Reusing the Source/Publisher narrow-interface pattern (US-285 ToolCatalog, US-289 PipelineRunner): the production wiring binds a real-library impl (pglogrepl) and the in-memory test impls capture batches for assertion. The interface is pull-style (`Next` blocks until data arrives) so the Receiver loop owns back-pressure — no goroutine sits between Source and the consumer holding events. Same shape works for any future "external system → internal event stream" surface (Kafka consumer in US-295, REST poller in US-294).
  - Per-transaction batch flushing on Commit is the correct boundary for CDC EditBatches: PG guarantees within-transaction atomicity; downstream consumers see either all rows of a transaction or none. Per-event flushing would split a logical transaction into N×NATS-publishes, defeating the per-batch atomicity in the funnel consumer's `applyBatchWithHistory`. Per-batch flush also amortises the StandbyStatusUpdate cost — one ack per txn instead of one per row.
  - Multi-ontology transactions need per-ontology bucketing during the txn, then flush them all on Commit. funnel.EditBatch carries one OntologyAPIName for the whole batch (US-044 per-ontology Bleve indexes). Bucketing into `pending map[ontology]*EditBatch` and flushing the whole map on commit keeps the per-ontology subject routing correct without inventing a "multi-ontology batch" wire shape.
  - pgoutput TupleData column types are a 4-way enum (`n` NULL / `u` unchanged-TOAST / `t` text / `b` binary). NULL needs an in-process sentinel (otherwise empty-string vs absent-key vs explicit-NULL collapse ambiguously); unchanged-TOAST needs to be ABSENT from the column map (the funnel consumer treats absent keys as "no change", which is the correct semantic). Duplicate this nowhere — `tupleToMap` is the single choke point.
  - REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT vs FULL distinction matters at decode time: with DEFAULT, UPDATE/DELETE old tuples carry only the key columns (rest are NULL on the wire), and the OldTupleType byte ('K' for key vs 'O' for full old) tells you which. The decoder must skip non-key columns when keysOnly=true so the Before map honestly reports "we have the key, we don't have the old non-key values" rather than emitting them as fake NULLs.
  - `pglogrepl.Parse` returns typed messages but the typed messages have unexported `baseMessage` fields. Tests can't use `&pglogrepl.RelationMessage{}` literals and have them dispatch through a type switch — need to call `m.SetType(pglogrepl.MessageTypeRelation)` to populate the embedded type byte. Same trick for every typed message used in tests; without it the type switch in `Decoder.Process` falls into the default branch and silently drops the message.
  - `pgconn.ReceiveMessage` returns `*pgproto3.CopyData` for replication-stream payloads — NOT a `*pgconn.CopyDataResponse` (the latter doesn't exist). Got bitten reaching for the obvious-sounding name first; importing `pgproto3` and asserting on its CopyData type is the canonical shape. Same package owns `BackendKeyData` / `RowDescription` / etc. for non-replication assertions.
  - "Source must declare replication=database explicitly" is the right ergonomics: silently appending the flag would trip operators who copy a CDC DSN into a non-CDC tool (or vice versa). The pgconn.Connect error when the flag is missing ("server does not support logical decoding without replication mode") is also informative enough that operators self-diagnose — better than a "connected but nothing happens" silent breakage.
  - `pglogrepl` is pure-Go (no CGO), so the CGO_ENABLED=0 Dockerfile invariant from US-230 stays intact. Verified with `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`. Indirect upgrade pgx/v5 5.8.0→5.9.1 is API-compatible (existing tree builds clean without changes).
  - `funnel.EditBatch.UserID` is the audit-trail attribution for the consumer. CDC writes default to `"cdc"` so operators searching action_logs can tell apart user / action-executor / ingest / CDC writes by the userId column. Same convention reusable for any future write surface that doesn't tie to a real user (LDAP sync uses "ldap_sync"; OIDC back-channel logout uses the IdP's sid mapping). Pick a stable string at wiring time; never propagate raw IdP claims as the audit user.
  - CDC watermark commits MUST happen after PublishBatch succeeds, not before. Commit-before-publish would advance PG's confirmed_flush_lsn for events that never landed in NATS; PG would then garbage-collect the WAL records and a receiver crash would lose the batch with no replay path. The `flushLocked` helper structures the order: publish all pending batches first, then `source.CommitWatermark`. Publisher failure aborts the loop with a wrapped error so operators can inspect the LSN that failed and either fix the mapping or skip past the offending transaction.
